laws.content:
§ 8-2-15

trade or an assumed name that was provided under Section 120.2 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of license; work prohibited where license expired or revoked
laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of an Awning and Canopy Erector License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division prior to expiration each year.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Awning and Canopy Erector License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation as an awning and canopy erector until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) An Awning and Canopy Erector License that is issued under Section 120.5 of this code shall expire one year from the date of issuance and, unless renewed within 60 days thereafter, is deemed revoked.

(d) An Awning and Canopy Erector License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Awning and Canopy Erector License has not been renewed to erect, repair, or re-cover any awning or canopy, or to engage in the business of erecting, repairing, or re-covering awnings or canopies, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(f) An Awning and Canopy Erector License that is issued under this section may be renewed or reinstated only by submitting a completed application and paying the non-refundable fee as required, respectively, in Section 120.2 and Section 120.3 of this code to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division.

laws.title: Suspension or revocation
laws.content:
(a) The Building Official may send a Notice to Appear to the holder of an Awning and Canopy Erector License, where facts exist regarding any of the following reasons:

(1) An allegation of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under Section 120 of this code;

(2) An allegation of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under Section 120 of this code;

(3) Failure of the licensee to comply with any notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department regarding the improper erection, repairing, or re-covering of any awning or canopy;

(4) Failure of licensee to comply with the conditions under which a permit was issued;

(5) Failure of the licensee, or its partner or officer, or his authorized agent, to appear at the hearing;

CD8:49
§ 8-2-15

DETROIT CITY CODE

(6) Inability to locate the licensee, or its partner or officer, after a diligent search at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department records; or

(7) Failure of the licensee to comply with any other requirement of this code or the 2019 Detroit City Code.

(b) The Notice to Appear shall:

(1) Be in writing to the holder of the license at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department records to appear before a hearing officer at a stated date and time to show cause why the license should not be suspended or revoked;

(2) State the reason or reasons therefor that the license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at the hearing; and

(3) Be sent, via first class and certified mail, at least seven days before the scheduled hearing date.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearing officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the officer may suspend or revoke an Awning and Canopy Erector License through the entry of an order, which reflects his or her decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearing officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearing officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearing officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Awning and Canopy Erector License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee; and

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm or corporation whose Awning and Canopy Erector License has been suspended or revoked to erect, repair, or recover any awning or canopy that requires such license for its performance until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated or reissued.

120.9 Review of adverse decision. In the event that the decision of the hearing officer is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the hearing officer remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: Additions to Section 3303 of 2015 Michigan Building Code, Demolition
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 3303 of the 2015 Michigan Building Code, Demolition, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

3303.4 Vacant lot. Where a structure has been demolished or removed, the vacant lot shall be filled and maintained in accordance with Sections 3303.8 through 3303.8.5 of this code.

3303.6 Utility connections. Service utility connections shall be discontinued and capped in accordance with Sections 3303.8 through 3303.8.5 of this code.

3303.8 Wrecking operations. Wrecking operations shall include the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, along with the removal, of any building or structure. All wrecking operations shall be conducted in accordance with these provisions to ensure the safety of workers and the general public.

3303.8.1 Wrecking permits.

(a) A wrecking permit shall be obtained from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department before the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and the removal, of any building or structure, except for those which are one-story frame buildings or structures

The provisions of this section shall not apply to the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, of 50 percent or less of any building or structure incidental to, or necessary in connection with, the repair, alteration, or enlargement of such building or structure.

(b) A permit shall not be issued for the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, of a building or structure, unless:

(b) All roof structures, all signs and other exterior appurtenances shall be removed before wrecking operations are started.

(c) The holder of the wrecking permit shall be responsible for compliance with this section, with the applicable provisions of this code, and with other laws covering this subject. The methods to be used in demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, shall not involve undue hazards to the public or unnecessary danger to the workers, and shall be in accordance with good practice. All persons who are actively engaged in wrecking operations on the job site shall wear personal protection equipment.

(d) A cable, chain, clam bucket, crane, demolition ball, or other similar mechanical devices shall not be used to demolish, disassemble, dismantle or dismember, and remove, any building or structure, unless detailed plans and proposed procedures are submitted with the application for a wrecking permit and are approved by the Building Official.

(e) Suitable provision shall be made for the disposal of solid waste, as defined in Section 42-1-1 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, which results from the wrecking operations. No part of the structure shall be overloaded by excessive storage of materials or debris, chutes, and scaffolds. Derricks and hoists shall be strong, substantial, and safe for the purpose for which they are intended. Materials, which when removed, would cause any excessive amount of dust shall be wetted down to prevent the creation of a nuisance. Open fires or other sources of flame, except necessary cutting torches, shall neither be permitted on the inside of the building or structure, which is being demolished, disassembled, dismantled or dismembered, and removed, nor in close proximity to flammable materials outside of the building or structure, and every precaution shall be taken to prevent the possibility of fire.

laws.title: Wrecking requirements
laws.content:
(a) The wrecking operation that is performed in accordance with a permit issued under Section 3303.8.1 of this code shall be performed, or executed:

(1) By the employees of the licensed wrecking contractor, while acting under his or her supervision and direction, and shall not be done by an independent contractor or subcontractor; or

(2) By the homestead-property owner and shall not be done by any licensed or unlicensed wrecking contractor.

(b) No individual, partnership, firm, or corporation shall conduct, or carry on, a wrecking operation under a wrecking permit that is issued to some other individual, partnership, firm, or corporation.

(c) It shall be the responsibility of the holder of the wrecking permit to complete the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, of any and all buildings or structures within the scope of said permit, including the filling to grade of all excavations.

(d) In any wrecking operation for the demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, of any building or structure, it shall be the responsibility of the holder of the wrecking permit for demolition, disassembling, dismantling or dismembering, and removal, of the building or structure to undertake the following measures at the site:

(1) Dismantle and remove all basement or cellar walls and floors, footings, and foundations;

CD8:59
§ 8-2-20

DETROIT CITY CODE

(2) Fill all open holes to grade level with backfill that shall be clean earth and is composed of mineral soil such as crumbling yellow clay, sand, or loam;

(3) Cap all water mains and sewer pipes;

(4) Remove all existing private sidewalks, driveways, walls, and other miscellaneous concrete slabs to full depth;

(5) Remove all pole and monument signs, dumpster enclosures, and other miscellaneous structures; and

(6) Remove all excess solid waste, as defined in Section 42-1-1 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, from the site above grade.

3303.8.5 Wrecking site restoration. Whenever a building or structure is demolished, disassembled, dismantled or dismembered, and removed, the holder of the wrecking permit shall ensure that the site is free from all unsafe or hazardous conditions, all public sidewalks and curbs that have been damaged replaced, all established grades restored, and all necessary retaining walls and fences erected in accordance with this code and the 2019 Detroit City Code.

laws.title: Additions to Appendix H, Signs, Section H101 of 2015 Michigan Building Code, General
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Appendix H, Signs, Section H101 of the 2015 Michigan Building Code, General, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

H101.1.2 Permit

H101.1.2.1 Required. No individual, partnership, firm, or corporation shall erect, install, re-face, remove, or re-hang any sign without first securing a permit from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

H101.1.2.2 Licensure a prerequisite. A permit for the erection, installation, re-facing, removal, or re-hanging of any sign shall not be issued, except to an individual who, or partnership, firm or corporation which, has obtained and holds a Sign Erector License that authorizes the erection, installation, re-facing, removal, or re-hanging of signs under Section 121 of this code.

H101.1.2.3 Surety bond for each permit. In addition to the requirements under Section 105 of this code, before a permit may be issued, the contractor who, or which, is licensed as a sign erector, shall file with the Office of Chief Financial Officer a surety bond in the sum of $5,000.00, which has been approved by the Corporation Counsel, indemnifies the City of Detroit and the individual who, or partnership, firm or corporation which, may be injured or damaged by or through the erection, installation, re-facing, removal, or re-hanging of such sign, and is to remain in full force and effect during the time that such sign is maintained. The surety bond shall be conditioned on the erection, installation, re-facing, removal, or re-hanging of the sign in accordance with the provisions of this code and shall protect and hold harmless the City of Detroit from any and all claims or demands for damages by reason of any negligence of the licensed sign

CD8:60

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-3-2

erector, or his or her agents, or by reason of the defects in the erection, installation, re-facing, removal or re-hanging of the sign, or from damages resulting from the collapse or failure of the sign, or part thereof.

**H101.1.2.4 Necessary Permit from Department of Public Works.** A permit for a sign, which projects over public property, shall not be issued until any necessary permit and approval has been obtained from the Department of Public Works.

**H101.1.2.5 Identification of sign erector.** For identification purposes, the name and address of the licensed sign erector shall be placed in a permanent legible and inconspicuous form on the interior or underside of each sign.

laws.title: Additions to Article 80 of 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Administration and Enforcement
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Article 80 of the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Administration and Enforcement, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

80.1.4. Certain advertising, signs and statements prohibited. It is unlawful to publish, state, indicate or imply, for advertising purposes, in any medium, that the City of Detroit, or the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department or its Electrical Division, have approved any product, device, fixture or material for installation or use.

80.14.2. Identification with official badge. The Code Official shall cause to be issued for him or herself and all electrical inspectors a badge of office, which shall be carried and displayed as proper identification when inspecting buildings, structures, or premises in the performance of duties under this code.

R 408.30811

80.14.2.1. Inspections. The Code Official, and his or her authorized assistants, are authorized to:

(a) To inspect all electrical equipment which requires an installation or alteration permit under the provision of this code;

(b) To inspect all equipment and systems covered by this code which, due to their condition, may be dangerous to life or property;

(c) To make or cause to be made such other inspections and tests as are deemed necessary for the purpose of safety and the enforcement of this code; and

(d) To issue orders for repairs and the correction of unsafe conditions and violations of this code.

80.14.2.2. Pre-approval for overtime inspection. Pre-approval of overtime inspection shall be obtained for all services provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours.

80.14.3.1. Reports of inspectors. The electrical inspectors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall make a written report of each inspection and file same in the records of the Department.

80.14.3.2. Interference with Department personnel prohibited. Any person who refuses to comply with this code, or assists in the violation of this code, or, in any manner, hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents or interferes with the electrical inspectors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in the

CD8:64

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-3-3

performance of any duty imposed by this code, or does not permit an electrical inspector to perform their duty by refusing entrance at reasonable times to buildings or places for the purpose of enforcing this code, shall be subject to the fines and penalties as provided for in Section 80.23.2 of this code.

laws.title: Means of appeal
laws.content: An interested person, or the person's authorized agent, aggrieved by a decision, determination, or order of the Code Official, also known as the Building Official, as defined in this code, which refuses to grant an application for a permit or makes any other decision pursuant or related to this code, may appeal in writing for a variance to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Board of Appeals for Construction*, and this section. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the code or the rules governing construction have been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of the code do not apply, or an equal or better form of construction is proposed. The decision of the Board of Appeals may be appealed to the Construction Code Commission in accordance with the act and time frames.

laws.title: Exception
laws.content:
As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a variance where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., *Government Organization and Employees*; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally

CD8:65
§ 8-3-3

DETROIT CITY CODE

chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

R 408.30812

80.18. Maintenance of existing wiring and equipment; wiring or equipment found unsafe. Every building, structure, or part thereof shall be kept in good electrical repair by the owner. Where, upon inspection of a building or structure, or part thereof, any existing wiring or equipment covered by this code is found to be in an unsafe condition, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve upon the owner and, where applicable, the holder of a permit, a written notice of the findings that states a date and time when repairs must be completed.

R 408.30815

80.18.1. Disconnection of dangerous electrical equipment. If the use of any electrical equipment is found imminently dangerous to human life or property, the enforcing agency may condemn the equipment or disconnect it from its source of electric supply, except that the enforcing agency shall not disconnect the service entrance equipment or utility service drop wires unless the entrance equipment or utility wires in themselves constitute a hazard to life or property. If the enforcing agency condemns or disconnects dangerous equipment, then the agency shall place a notice, in the form of a red sticker, on the equipment listing the causes for the condemnation or disconnection and the penalty under the act for the unlawful use of the equipment. The agency shall give written notice of the condemnation or disconnection and the causes for condemning or disconnecting the equipment to the owner or the occupant of the building, structure, or premises. A person shall not remove the red sticker or reconnect the electrical equipment to its source of electric supply, or use or permit the use of electrical current in the electrical equipment, until the causes for the condemnation or disconnection are remedied and a permit for the electrical repairs of the equipment is obtained from the enforcing agency.

R 408.30817

80.19. Permits and certificates. A person shall not equip a building with electrical conductors or equipment or make an alteration of, change in, or addition to, electrical conductors or equipment without receiving a written permit to do the work described. If the electrical installation or alterations of, changes in, or addition to, electrical conductors or equipment are found to be in compliance with the provision of the code and if the work has passed the inspection of the enforcing agency, then the enforcing agency shall, upon the request of the permit holder to whom the permit was issued, issue A certificate of final electrical inspection. The certificate certifies that the provisions of the code have been complied with. This section does not apply to installations that are referred to in section 7(3)(a), (b), (c), (d), (e), (f), (h), (k), (l), (m), or (o) of the Electrical Administrative Act, MCL 338.887. A permit is required for all installations of a temporary nature that are governed by Article 590 of this code, Temporary Installations. A permit for inspection of electrical equipment for a carnival, convention display, parade, or street fair shall be issued and approval of the electrical equipment obtained prior to commencing of the carnival, convention display, parade, or street fair.

R 408.30818

laws.title: To whom permits are issued
laws.content:
(1) A permit for any type of electrical installation may be secured by one of the following:

(a) A holder of an electrical contractor license or the qualifying master for the electrical contractor when authorized by the electrical contractor to secure a permit.

(b) A homeowner who occupies or will occupy a single-family dwelling and other accessory structures located on the same lot intended for use by the homeowner for which the permit is obtained and who will install the electrical equipment as certified by the homeowner on the permit application pursuant to the act. A homestead-property owner of a single-family residence which is, or will be on upon completion, his or her own place of residence, and no part of which is used for rental or commercial purposes or is now contemplated for such purpose, provided, that the owner shall:

(1) Sign an affidavit on a form furnished by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division showing that the applicant is the homestead-property owner and occupant, or will be the occupant on upon completion of the residence and that the applicant will personally install the equipment therein for which the permit is required; and

(2) Apply for and secure the required permit.

(2) A permit for a fire alarm system may be secured by the holder of a fire alarm specialty contractor license or the qualifying fire alarm specialty technician qualifying the fire alarm specialty contractor when authorized by the fire alarm specialty contractor to secure a permit.

(3) A permit for an electrical sign or outline lighting, as defined in Section 1b(1) and (2) of 1956 PA 217, the Electrical Administrative Act, MCL 338.881b(1) and (2), may be secured by the holder of a Sign Specialty Contractor License of the sign specialty technician qualifying the sign specialty contractor when authorized by the sign specialty contractor to secure a permit.

(4) A permit for electrical wiring associated with the installation, removal, alteration, or repair of a water well pump on a single-family dwelling to the first point of attachment in the house from the well, may be secured by a registered pump installer under part 127 of the public health code, 1978 PA 368, MCL 333.12701 to 333.12771.

(5) A permit for wiring associated with existing mechanical and plumbing systems referenced in section 7(3)(i) of the electrical administrative act, 1956 PA 217, MCL 338.887(3)(i), may be secured by the following:

(a) A holder of a mechanical contractor license issued pursuant to section 6(3)(a), (b), (d), (e), and (f) of the Forbes mechanical contractors act, 1984 PA 192, MCL 338.976(3)(a), (b), (d), and (f).

(b) A holder of a plumbing contractor license issued pursuant to the state plumbing act, 2002 PA 733, MCL 338.3511 to 338.3569.

(6) Any person requesting or requiring an inspection of electrical equipment for a carnival, convention display, parade, or street fair.

R 408.30818

laws.title: Application for permit; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) Each application for a permit, with the required fee, shall be filed with the Code Official on a form furnished for that purpose and shall contain a general description of the proposed work and its location. Pertinent data relating to the work to be done, which cannot be adequately described on the application for a permit, shall be shown on plans accompanying same. The permit application shall contain all applicable information pursuant to with the act and shall include the signature of the applicant in compliance with Section 80.19.1 of the code.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a permit where the

(d) A person against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the person can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

R 408.30818

laws.title: Action on application for permit
laws.content: The Code Official shall examine, or cause to be examined, applications for permits and amendments thereto within a reasonable time after filing. If the application or the construction documents do not conform to the requirements of pertinent laws, the Code Official shall reject such application in writing, stating the reasons therefor. If, based upon the approval of the applicable electrical inspector through the affixing of his or her respective signature on the application, the Code Official is satisfied that the proposed work conforms to the requirements of this code, other state construction codes and laws and the 2019 Detroit City Code applicable thereto, the Code Official shall issue a permit therefor as soon as practicable.

laws.title: Additional work under permit prohibited
laws.content: After a permit has been issued and the fee paid, no additional work shall be included under the permit. Where additional work is to be installed, a new permit shall be secured and the required fee paid.

laws.title: Fee refunds
laws.content: Except for a permit that is fraudulently obtained, a permit issued under the provisions of this article may be canceled by the Building Official on the written request from the holder of such permit, provided, that such request is made within 180 days from the date of issuance of the permit and prior to any inspection or other action taken under the permit, including any exercise of privileges granted by the permit. In the event that any permit is canceled, the City Treasurer, upon notification in writing from the Building Official, shall make a refund of 80 percent of all fees paid in connection with the issuance of such unused permit, provided, that where a permit expires, a refund shall not be granted but the permit may be reinstated in accordance with Section 80.19.3 of this code.

laws.title: Annual permit
laws.content:
In place of an individual permit for each alteration to an already approved electrical installation, the enforcing agency may issue an annual permit upon application to any person who, or firm or corporation which, employs a full-time licensed master electrician, or a full-time licensed electrical journeyperson, to actively supervise the installation of electrical equipment on a premises owned or occupied and used by the applicant in the conduct of his or her business, and at which premises the licensed master electrician or the licensed electrical journeyperson performs his or her duties, provided, that:

(1) Said licensed electrical journeyperson has held his or her license for at least two full years; and

(2) Both the employer and the licensed journeyman execute an affidavit on a form furnished by the Electrical Division, which is kept on file in the Electrical Division.

The applicant shall be licensed pursuant to the Electrical Administrative Act, 1956 PA 217, MCL 338.881 to 338.892.

R 408.30818

laws.title: Approval of construction documents
laws.content: When the Code Official issues a permit, the construction documents shall be approved, in writing or by stamp, as "Reviewed for Code Compliance." One set of three sets of construction documents so reviewed shall be retained by the Code Official. The second and third sets shall be returned to the applicant. The second set shall be kept by the applicant at the work site and be open to inspection by the Code Official or a duly authorized representative while the third set shall be retained by the applicant for his or her records.

laws.title: Inspection requests
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the permit, or his or her duly authorized agent, shall notify the Code Official when work is ready for inspection. A notice, which contains this requirement, shall be printed on all permits that are issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The permit holder shall

CD8:69
§ 8-3-3

DETROIT CITY CODE

provide access to, and means for, inspections of work that is required by this code. The Code Official shall perform the inspection within a reasonable period of time after the request for inspection is made.

(b) Where it is found during an inspection that any electrical equipment does not conform to the provisions of this code, the electrical inspector:

(1) Shall attach a red sticker, which states "NOT APPROVED", and document any reason therefor on the sticker; and

(2) Notify the person installing or responsible for installing such electrical equipment in writing of such defect, misuse, or violation and that all such defects, misuses, or violations of said electrical equipment shall be corrected within a reasonable length of time. When such corrections have been made, such person shall notify the Electrical Division, in writing, at least 24 hours prior to the time re-inspection is desired.

(c) Where it is found during an inspection that the electrical equipment conforms to the provisions of this code, the electrical inspector shall attach a green sticker, which states "APPROVED", and notify the person installing or responsible for installing such electrical equipment in writing of the same.

(d) Any sticker that is attached to the electrical equipment by an electrical inspector shall only be altered or removed by an electrical inspector.

80.22.3. Final inspection. The final inspection shall be made after all work required by the electrical permit is completed. Confirmation of completion of work under the permit is validated by the issuance of a Certificate of Approval.

80.23. Notice of Violation. Where it is found that any electrical equipment does not conform to the provisions of the code, the Code Official is authorized to serve, via first class mail, a Notice of Violation or order on the person who installs, or who is responsible for installing, the electrical equipment, in accordance with this act, of the defect, misuse, or violation. Such order shall direct the discontinuance of the illegal action or condition and the abatement of the violation. Any portions that do not comply shall be corrected and this portion shall not be covered or concealed until authorized by the enforcing agency.

R 408.30826

80.23.1. Prosecution of violation.

(a) Where a Notice of Violation or order is not complied with by the date specified therein or by the date specified in any extension that is granted for no longer than 28 days, the Code Official is authorized to request that the Corporation Counsel:

(1) Represent the City electrical inspector in the prosecution of the misdemeanor ordinance violation that has been filed with the court; or

(2) Institute appropriate proceedings at law or in equity to correct or to abate such violation or to require the removal or termination of the unlawful use of the building or structure in violation of the provisions of this code or of the order or direction made pursuant thereto.

(b) The total elapsed time from issuance of the Notice of Violation or order to the filing of a misdemeanor ordinance violation shall not exceed six months.

80.23.2. Violation penalties.

(a) It is unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation to violate a provision of the code or fail to conform with any of the requirements thereof, or cause work to be performed or done, in conflict with or in violation of the approved construction documents or directive of the Code Official, or a permit or certificate issued under this code.

(b) In accordance with Section 10 of the Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.890, a person licensed or registered under the act who commits a violation of the act that is not a minor violation as

CD8:70

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-3-3

described in Section 8c of the Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.888c, or a person not licensed or registered under the act who is performing any activity regulated by the act and is not exempt from licensure or registration under the act, is guilty of a civil violation:

(1) Punishable for a first violation by a fine of not less than $1,000.00 per day for each day the violation occurs, provided, that such fine shall not exceed $5,000.00 in total per violation; or

(2) Punishable for a second or subsequent violation by a fine of not less than $2,000.00 per day for each day the violation occurs, provided, that such fine shall not exceed $10,000.00 in total per violation.

(c) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, upon conviction, all other persons who are not governed by Subsection (b) of this section shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court. Each day that the violation continues, or is permitted to exist, without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable, upon conviction, in the manner prescribed by this subsection.

(d) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, as the administrating and enforcing agency that prosecutes a violation of this code, the City shall retain any fine that is imposed upon conviction.

laws.title: Establishment and approval of fees; payment of fees required before work begins
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Sections 10(1) and 22(1) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1510(1) and 125.1522(1), and Section 9-507 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of appeals, examinations, certificates, permits, inspections, re-inspections, and other fees that are required by the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code and by Chapter 8, Article III, of 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs, which are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) In accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish and collect necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of licenses that are required by this article.

(c) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(d) The fees prescribed by this section shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department before a permit to begin work for new construction, alteration, removal, demolition, or other building operation may be issued. In addition, an amendment to a permit necessitating an additional fee shall not be approved until the additional fee is paid.

Addition of Article 81 to 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Electrical Contractor License
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Article 81, Electrical Contractor License, to the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

81. ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR LICENSE

81.1. Definitions. For purposes of Article 81 of this code, the following terms have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section:

*Electrical contractor* means an individual, firm, or corporation engaged in the business of erecting, installing, altering, repairing, servicing, or maintaining electrical wiring, devices, or equipment.

*Electrical wiring* means all wiring, generating equipment, fixtures, appliances, and appurtenances in connection with the generation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, within or on a building, residence, structure, or properties, and including service entrance wiring.

81.2. Required; exceptions.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as an electrical contractor in the installation, maintenance, repairing, servicing or altering of electrical equipment for light, heat, fire alarm, or power purposes where the electromotive force exceeds 50 volts, except for fire alarms, in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, without having first obtained an Electrical Contractor License as provided for in this article.

(b) No license is required for the repair of electrical wiring whose valuation is not in excess of $100.00, the replacement of lamps, or the connection of portable electrical equipment to suitable permanently-installed receptacles.

(c) An individual who holds: 1) a valid Electrical Contractor License and a valid Master Electrician License, or 2) a valid Electrical Contractor License and employs a full-time individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License, is not required to hold an Electrical Journeyperson License, a Fire Alarm Contractor License, a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License, a Sign Specialty Contractor License, or a Sign Specialist License in order to perform work that is permitted under such licenses.

(d) In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), a person who holds a valid Electrical Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses is not required to obtain an Electrical Contractor License from the City of Detroit, but is required to register under Article 81.50 of this code.

81.3. Requirements.

The Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue an Electrical Contractor License to a person who does all of the following:

(1) Holds a Master Electrician License or has at least one mas-

laws.title: Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Article 81 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon compliance with Sections 81.4 through 81.6 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue an electrical contractor license to the applicant.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

(c) An electrical contractor shall not allow their license to be used by any other individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

laws.title: Posting and displaying of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon issuance, the current, original Electrical Contractor License shall be conspicuously posted in the licensee’s principal place of business.

(b) After issuance, the current, original wallet-size Electrical Contractor License shall be carried when acting as an electrical contractor and displayed when requested.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content:
(a) Every holder of an Electrical Contractor License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division any change of the address that was provided under Section 81.4 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

(b) Every holder of an Electrical Contractor License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division any change of partners, officers, or a trade or an assumed name that was provided under Section 81.4 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of license; work prohibited where license expired or revoked
laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of an Electrical Contractor License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division prior to January 1st.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Electrical Contractor License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued

operation as an electrical contractor until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) An Electrical Contractor License that is issued under Section 81.7 of this code shall expire on December 31st and, where not renewed 60 days after the date of expiration, the license is deemed revoked.

(d) An Electrical Contractor License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Board of Electrical Examiners and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose Electrical Contractor License has not been renewed or has been revoked to engage in the business of installing, maintaining, repairing, servicing, or altering electrical equipment in or on any building structure or part thereof, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such expired or revoked license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration by the Board of Electrical Examiners.

(f) An Electrical Contractor License that is issued under this section may be renewed or reinstated only by submitting a completed application and paying the fee as required, respectively, under Section 81.4 and Section 81.5 of this code to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division.

81.11. Suspension and revocation.

(a) The Building Official may send to the holder of an Electrical Contractor License a Notice to Appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners, where facts exist regarding any of the following reasons:

(1) An allegation of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under Article 81 of this code;

(2) An allegation of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under Article 81 of this code;

(3) An allegation of incompetence;

(4) An allegation of an act of willful or gross negligence;

(5) An allegation of deliberate misrepresentation;

(6) Failure of the licensee to comply with any notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department regarding the improper erection, installation, alteration, repair, servicing, or maintenance of electrical wiring, devices, or equipment;

(7) Failure of the licensee to comply with the conditions under which a permit was issued; or

(8) Failure of the licensee to comply with any other requirement of this code, the 2019 Detroit City Code, or applicable state law.

(b) The Notice to Appear shall:

(1) Be in writing to the holder of the license at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division records to appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners at a stated date and time to show cause why the license should not be suspended or revoked;

(2) State the reason or reasons therefor that the license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at the hearing; and

(3) Be sent, via first class and certified mail, at least seven days before the scheduled hearing date.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the Board of Electrical Examiners is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the Board may suspend or revoke an Electrical Contractor License through the entry of an order, which reflects the Body’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the Board shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the Board decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the Board shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the Board of Electrical Examiners; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Electrical Contractor License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee;

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, which shall correct its records; and

(c) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department

Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Electrical Contractor License has been suspended or revoked to erect, install, alter, repair, service, or maintain electrical wiring, devices, or equipment requiring such license for its performance in the City, or to arrange for the performance of such work on a contractual basis, until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated or reissued.

81.12. Review of adverse decision. In the event that the decision of the Board of Electrical Examiners is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the Board remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: Required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), it shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is not within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as an electrical contractor in the installation, maintenance, repairing, servicing, or altering of electrical equipment for light, heat, fire alarm, or power purposes where the electromotive force exceeds 50 volts, except for fire alarms, in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, or to act in the capacity of an electrical contractor within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. A Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall not be issued to any such person unless the person holds a valid Electrical Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses.

(b) No Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor is required for the repair of electrical wiring whose valuation is not in excess of $100, the replacement of lamps, or the connection of portable electrical equipment to suitable permanently-installed receptacles.

laws.title: Application required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the appropriate individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required registration fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The name, address of their principal place of business, and telephone number of the business;

(2) Where the applicant is an individual:

    (a) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years; and

    (b) The applicant’s current mailing address and e-mail address; and

(3) If applicant is a corporation:

    (a) Full and accurate corporation name;

    (b) The state and date of incorporation; and

    (c) The full names and addresses of officers, directors, managers, and other individuals with authority to bind the corporation;

(4) If applicant is a partnership:

    (a) Names of members thereof; and

    (b) Current mailing address and email address of members thereof.

(5) If the applicant conducts business under a trade or assume name:

(a) Complete and full trade name and date of registration with County Clerk; and

(b) The name of the individual or individuals doing business under such trade or assumed name; and

(6) The name and business address of the statutory agent, or other agent, who is authorized to receive service of process.

(b) An application shall be accompanied:

(1) By a true copy of the applicant’s valid Electrical Contractor License issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, for retention by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division; and

(2) By payment of the non-refundable registration fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(c) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

81.54. Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of certificate.

(a) Upon compliance with Section 81.53 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor to the applicant.

(b) A Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

(c) An electrical contractor shall not allow their Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor to be used by any other individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

81.55. Updating certain information required.

Every registrant shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division any change of the address that was provided under Section 81.53 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

81.56. Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration.

(a) Prior to the expiration of a current Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor, a registrant shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the certificate. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the registration fee before the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall allow to operate as an electric contractor in the City of Detroit until such time that the Certificate of Registration renewal application is denied, or the Certificate of Registration is deemed void.

(b) In order to make the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor commensurate with the expiration date of the license that is issued by the Michi-

§ 8-3-5

DETROIT CITY CODE

gan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, each Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall expire on December 31st, provided, that such Certificate of Registration shall expire annually and not on a three-year cycle.

(c) In order to make the renewal date of the Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor commensurate with the renewal date of the license that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, each Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall be renewed no later than March 1st, provided, that such Certificate of Registration shall be renewed annually and not on a three-year cycle.

(d) Commensurate with Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, where a license that was issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, is not renewed by March 1st and, therefore, is deemed void, the Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor shall not be renewed until the license is reinstated.

81.57. Certification of Registration deemed void; unlawful to perform or arrange performance of work.

(a) Where an Electrical Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, expires, or is suspended or revoked by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Electrical Contractor Licenses, the Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor issued under Section 81.54 of this code is deemed void and the holder thereof shall not engage in the business, or act in the capacity, of an electrical contractor in the City of Detroit.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any individual whose Certificate of Registration for an Electrical Contractor is void to erect, install, alter, repair, service, or maintain electrical wiring, devices, or equipment requiring such Certificate of Registration for its performance, or to arrange for the performance of such work on a contractual basis, until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated or reissued.

laws.title: Required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any individual whose legal address is within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage in the trade or occupation of master electrician in the installation, alteration, maintenance or repair of electrical wiring equipment, apparatus or fixtures for light, heat, power or medical purposes in or about buildings or structures within the City of Detroit without having first obtained a Master Electrician License as provided for in this article.

(b) An individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License is not required to hold an Electrical Journeyperson License, a Fire Alarm Contractor License, a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License, a Sign Specialty Contractor License, or a Sign Specialist License in order to perform work that is permitted under such licenses.

(c) A holder of a Master Electrician License shall not qualify for more than one Electrical Contractor License.

(d) In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), an individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Master Electrician Licenses is not required to obtain a Master Electrician License from the City of Detroit, but is required to register under Article 82.50 of this code.

laws.title: Requirements; failure to pass examination; license limitation
laws.content:
(a) The Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Master Electrician License to an individual who is not less than 22 years of age and does all of the following:

(1) Files a completed application form provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division;

(2) Files a written statement from present or former employers to the effect than the applicant has not less than 12,000 hours of practical experience obtained over a period of not less than six years related to electrical construction or maintenance of buildings, or electrical wiring or equipment under the supervision of a master electrician;

(3) Provides documentation that he or she has held an Electrical Journeyperson License for not less than two years;

(4) Pays the non-refundable examination fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code and passes an examination provided for by the Board of Electrical Examiners and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division;

(5) Obtains the approval of the Board of Electrical Examiners; and

(6) Pays the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(b) Upon failure to pass the master electrician examination two times within a period of two years, an applicant shall be ineligible to sit for another examination until a period of not less than one year from the date of failure of the second examination, at which time he or she shall present documentation to the Board of Electrical Examiners of the successful completion of a state-approved course on code, electrical fundamentals, or electrical theory in order to become eligible to sit again for an examination.

82.4. Application; supplementation of information required.

(a) An application for a Master Electrician License shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The application shall be considered complete when the individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required license fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

(2) The applicant’s current mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number;

(3) Written proof of age in the form of a driver’s license, or a picture identification document containing the applicant’s date of birth issued by a governmental agency, or a copy of a birth certificate accompanied by a picture identification document issued by a governmental agency; and

(4) The period of time during which said applicant has been engaged in the business.

(b) An application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(c) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

82.5. Written examination required.

(a) The Board of Electrical Examiners shall determine the qualifications of each applicant. The Board shall make its decision based upon the completed application and the written examination.

(b) The written examination shall be conducted once each month in accordance with the examination schedule that is posted at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division for the current calendar year. A completed application to take the examination, including any request for special-needs accommodation, along with the required fee, shall be received at the Department no later than 14 days before the examination.

(c) As the Board of Electrical Examiners determines, the examination shall consist of a written test. The examination for a Master Electrician License shall include, but not be limited to, questions designed to test an individual’s knowledge of this code, the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1501 et seq., and any other applicable law, as well as the theory relative to those codes and laws.

laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of a Master Electrician License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division prior to January 1st. During or after those years that this code is updated or changed by adoption into the 2019 Detroit City Code, the master electrician is required, as a condition of renewal of his or her Master Electrician License, to present with their application documentation of the successful completion of a state-approved course concerning any update or change in the code prior to or within 12 months after the adoption of the update or change in this code.

laws.title: Addition of Article 82.50 to 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Master Electrician Registration
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Article 82.50, Master Electrician Registration, to the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

82.50. MASTER ELECTRICIAN REGISTRATION

82.51. Definitions. For purposes of Article 82.50 of this code, the following terms have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section:

*Electrical wiring* means all wiring, generating equipment, fixtures, appliances, and appurtenances in connection with the generation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, within or on a building, residence, structure, or properties, and including service entrance wiring.

*Master electrician* means an individual who has the necessary qualifications, training, experience, and technical knowledge

to supervise the installation of electrical wiring and equipment in accordance with this code.

82.52. Required.

In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), it shall be unlawful for any individual whose legal address is not within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as a master electrician in supervising the installation of electrical wiring and equipment, or to act in the capacity of a master electrician within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration for a Master Electrician from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. A Certificate of Registration for a Master Electrician shall not be issued to any such individual unless the individual holds a valid Master Electrician License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Master Electrician Licenses.

82.53. Application required.

(a) An application for a Certificate of Registration for a Master Electrician shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required registration fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The name, address of his or her principal place of business, and telephone number of the business;

(2) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years; and

(3) The applicant’s current mailing address and e-mail address.

(b) An application shall be accompanied:

(1) By a true copy of the applicant’s valid Master Electrician License issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Master Electrician Licenses, for retention by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division; and

(2) By payment of the non-refundable registration fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(c) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

82.54. Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of certificate.

(a) Upon compliance with Section 82.53 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Certificate of Registration for a Master Electrician to the applicant.

(b) A Certificate of Registration for a Master Electrician that is issued un-

(b) While on active duty as a member of the armed forces, served as an interior electrician or in an equivalent job classification; was honorably discharged from that military service in the one-year period preceding the date the license application is filed; and has, and provides with his or her application an affidavit signed by a commanding officer, supervisor, or military superior with direct knowledge of the applicant’s service that states that he or she has at least 8,000 hours of entry-level experience in and basic knowledge of each of the following:

(3) Knowledge of circuit classifications and ratings and design and use requirements for circuits, including branch circuit loads;

(4) The determination of ampacity, type of insulation, usage requirements, methods of installation, protection, support, and termination;

(5) Knowledge regarding the installation of motors and control circuits;

(6) The calculation of electrical loads and determination of proper size, rating, and type of service and feeder conductors;

(7) Knowledge regarding fuses, circuit breakers, and all types of protective devices for conductors and equipment;

(8) Knowledge of all types of raceways and their uses, including determining proper size, conductor fill, support, and methods of installation;

(9) Knowledge of circuits and equipment characterized by usage and electrical power limitations, including differentiating them from electric light and power circuits; and

(3) Pays the non-refundable examination fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code and passes an examination provided for by the Board of Electrical Examiners and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division;

(b) Where an applicant who otherwise meets the requirements of Subsection (a)(2)(b) of this section has not attained 8,000 hours of entry-level experience or does not have basic knowledge in each of the areas described in Subsection (a)(2)(b)(1) to (10) of this section, he or she may provide with his or her application an affidavit signed by a commanding officer, supervisor, or military superior with direct knowledge of the applicant’s service that states the amount of experience the applicant has attained and of which of the areas described in Subsection (a)(2)(b)(1) to (10) of this section

the applicant has basic knowledge, and the Department may in its discretion grant the applicant credit toward the 8,000-hour experience requirement of Subsection (a)(2)(a) of this section based on the applicant's experience.

(c) Upon failure to pass the electrical journeyperson examination two times within a period of two years, an applicant shall be ineligible to sit for another examination until a period of not less than one year from the date of failure of the second examination, at which time he or she shall present documentation to the Board of Electrical Examiners of the successful completion of a state-approved course on code, electrical fundamentals, or electrical theory in order to become eligible again to sit for an examination.

83.4. Application; supplementation of information required.

(a) An application for an Electrical Journeyperson License shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required license fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The applicant's full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

(2) The applicant's current mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number;

(3) Written proof of age in the form of a driver's license, or a picture identification document containing the applicant's date of birth issued by a governmental agency, or a copy of a birth certificate accompanied by a picture identification document issued by a governmental agency; and

(4) The period of time during which said applicant has been engaged in the business.

(b) An application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(c) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

83.5. Written examination required.

(a) The Board of Electrical Examiners shall determine the qualifications of each applicant. The Board shall make its decision based upon the completed application and the written examination.

(b) The written examination shall be conducted once each month in accordance with the examination schedule that is posted at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division for the current calendar year. A completed application to take the examination, including any request for special-needs accommodation, along with the required fee, shall be received at the Department no later than 14 days before the examination.

(c) As the Board of Electrical Examiners determines, the examination shall consist of a written test. The examination for an Electrical Journeyperson License shall include, but not be limited to, questions designed to test an individual's knowledge of this code, the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1501 et seq., and any other applicable law, as well as the theory relative to those codes and laws.

(d) An applicant who passes the written examination is eligible for issuance of his or her license at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, provided, that the applicant complies with Section 83.6 of this code.
