laws.title: Addition of Article 85 to 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Fire Alarm Contractor License
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Article 85, Fire Alarm Contractor License, to the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

85. FIRE ALARM CONTRACTOR LICENSE

85.1. Fire alarm contractor defined. For purposes of Article 85 of this code, the term "fire alarm contractor" means an individual, firm, or corporation engaged in the business of erecting, installing, altering, repairing, servicing, or maintaining the wiring, devices, appliances, or equipment of a fire alarm system.

85.2. Required; exceptions.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as a fire alarm contractor in the installation, maintenance, repairing, servicing or altering of electrical equipment for fire alarm systems or appurtenances thereof in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, without first having obtained a Fire Alarm Contractor License as provided for in this article.

(b) No license will be required for the repair of electrical wiring whose valuation is not in excess of $100.00, the replacement of lamps, or the connection of portable electrical equipment to suitable permanently-installed receptacles.

(c) An individual is not required to hold a Fire Alarm Contractor License in order to perform work that is permitted under such license where:

(1) The individual holds both a valid Electrical Contractor License and a valid Master Electrician License; or

(2) The person holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and employs a full-time individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License; or

(3) The individual holds a valid Electrical Journeyperson License and works under the supervision of an individual who holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and an individual who holds valid Master Electrician License.

(d) In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), a person who holds a valid Fire Alarm Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Fire Alarm Contractor Licenses is not required to obtain a Fire Alarm Contractor License from the City of Detroit, but is required to register under Article 85.50 of this code.

(d) A Fire Alarm Contractor License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Board of Electrical Examiners and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Fire Alarm Contractor License has not been renewed or has been revoked to engage in the business of installing, maintaining, repairing, servicing, or altering electrical equipment in or on any building structure or part thereof, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such expired or revoked license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration by the Board of Electrical Examiners.

(f) A Fire Alarm Contractor License that is issued under this section may be renewed or reinstated only by submitting a completed application and paying the fee as required, respectively, under Section 85.4 and Section 85.5 of this code to the Build-

ings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division.

85.11. Suspension and revocation.

(a) The Building Official may send to the holder of a Fire Alarm Contractor License a Notice to Appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners, where facts exist regarding any of the following reasons:

(1) An allegation of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under Article 85 of this code;

(2) An allegation of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under Article 85 of this code;

(3) An allegation of incompetence;

(4) An allegation of an act of willful or gross negligence;

(5) An allegation of deliberate misrepresentation;

(6) Failure of the licensee to comply with any notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department regarding the improper erection, installation, alteration, repair, servicing, or maintenance of the wiring, devices, appliances, or equipment of a fire alarm system;

(7) Failure of the licensee to comply with the conditions under which a permit was issued; or

(8) Failure of the licensee to comply with any other requirement of this code, the 2019 Detroit City Code, or applicable state law.

(b) The Notice to Appear shall:

(1) Be in writing to the holder of the license at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division records to appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners at a stated date and time to

CD8:102

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-3-11

show cause why the license should not be suspended or revoked;

(2) State the reason or reasons therefor that the license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at the hearing; and

(3) Be sent, via first class and certified mail, at least seven days before the scheduled hearing date.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the Board of Electrical Examiners is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the Board may suspend or revoke a Fire Alarm Contractor License through the entry of an order, which reflects the Body’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the Board shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the Board decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the Board shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the Board of Electrical Examiners; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Fire Alarm Contractor License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee;

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, which shall correct its records; and

(c) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Fire Alarm Contractor License has been suspended or revoked to erect, install, alter, repair, service, or maintain the wiring, devices, appliances or equipment of a fire alarm system requiring such license for its performance in the City, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated or reissued.

85.12. Review of adverse decision. In the event that the decision of the Board of Electrical Examiners is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the Board remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: Required
laws.content: In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), it shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is not within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as a fire alarm contractor in the erecting, installing, altering, repairing, servicing, or maintaining the wiring, devices, appliances or equipment of any fire alarm system in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, or to act in the capacity of a fire alarm contractor within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. A Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor shall not be issued to any such person unless the person holds a valid Fire Alarm Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Fire Alarm Contractor Licenses.

laws.title: Application required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the appropriate individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required registration fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(2) Where the applicant is an individual:

 (a) The applicant's full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years; and

 (b) The applicant's current mailing address and e-mail address; and

(3) If applicant is a corporation:

 (a) Full and accurate corporation name;

 (b) The state and date of incorporation; and

 (c) The full names and addresses of officers, directors, managers, and other individuals with authority to bind the corporation;

(4) If applicant is a partnership:

 (a) Names of members thereof; and

 (b) Current mailing address and email address of members thereof.

(5) If the applicant conducts business under a trade or assume name:

 (a) Complete and full trade name and date of registration with County Clerk; and

 (b) The name of the individual or individuals doing business under such trade or assumed name; and

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
(a) Prior to the expiration of a current Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor, a registrant shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the certificate. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the registration fee before the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor shall allow for the continued engagement as a fire alarm contractor until such time that the Certificate of Registration renewal application is denied, or the Certificate of Registration is deemed void.

(b) In order to make the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor commensurate with the expiration date of the license that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Fire Alarm Contractor Licenses, each Certificate of Registration for a Fire Alarm Contractor shall expire on December 31st, pro-

laws.title: Addition of Article 86 to 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Article 86, Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License, to the 2014 Michigan Electrical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

86. FIRE ALARM SPECIALTY TECHNICIAN LICENSE

86.1. Fire alarm specialty technician defined. For purposes of Article 86 of this code, the term "fire alarm specialty technician" means an individual other than a fire alarm contractor who, as his or her principal occupation, is engaged in the practical installation or alteration of fire alarm system wiring.

86.2. Required; exceptions.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any individual whose legal address is within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage in the occupation or trade of fire alarm specialty technician in the City without first having obtained a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License as provided for in this article.

CD8:106

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-3-12

(b) An individual is not required to hold a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License in order to perform work that is permitted under such license where:

(1) The individual holds both a valid Electrical Contractor License and a valid Master Electrician License; or

(2) The person holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and employs a full-time individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License; or

(3) The individual holds a valid Electrical Journeyperson License and works under the supervision of an individual who holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and an individual who holds valid Master Electrician License.

(c) The holder of a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License shall not qualify for more than one Fire Alarm Contractor License.

(d) In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), an individual who holds a valid Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs is not required to register as a fire alarm specialty technician in order to work in the City of Detroit.

laws.title: Requirements
Application; supplementation of information required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required license fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

(2) The applicant’s current mailing address, e-mail address, and telephone number;

(3) Written proof of age in the form of a driver’s license, or a picture identification docu-

DETROIT CITY CODE

ment containing the applicant's date of birth issued by a governmental agency, or a copy of a birth certificate accompanied by a picture identification document issued by a governmental agency; and

(4) The period of time during which said applicant has been engaged in the business.

(b) An application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

(c) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

86.5. Board of Electrical Examiners to determine qualifications of applicants; written examination required.

(a) The Board of Electrical Examiners shall determine the qualifications of each applicant. The Board shall make its decision based upon the completed application and the written examination.

(b) The written examination shall be conducted once each month in accordance with the examination schedule that is posted at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division for the current calendar year. A completed application to take the examination, including any request for special-needs accommodation, along with the required fee, shall be received at the Department no later than 14 days before the examination.

(c) As the Board of Electrical Examiners determines, the examination shall consist of a written test. The examination for a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License shall include, but not be limited to, questions designed to test an individual's knowledge of this code, the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1501 et seq., and any other applicable law, as well as the theory relative to those codes and laws.

(d) An applicant who passes the written examination is eligible for issuance of his or her license at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, provided, that the applicant complies with Section 86.6 of this code.

86.6. Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage.

(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Article 86 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual.

(c) A fire alarm specialty technician shall not allow his or her license to be used by any other individual.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of license; condition of renewal; work prohibited where license expired or revoked
laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division prior to January 1st. During or after those years that this code is updated or changed by adoption into the 2019 Detroit City Code, the fire alarm specialty technician is required, as a condition of renewal of his or her Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License, to present with their application documentation of the successful completion of a state-approved course concerning any update or change in the code prior to or within 12 months after the adoption of the update or change in this code.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation as a fire alarm specialty technician until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) A Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License that is issued under Section 86.7 of this code shall expire on December 31st and, where not renewed 60 days after the date of expiration, the license is deemed revoked.

(d) A Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Board of Electrical Examiners and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual whose Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License has not been renewed or has been revoked to engage in the business of installing, maintaining, repairing, servicing, or altering electrical equipment in or on any building structure or part thereof, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration by the Board of Electrical Examiners.

86.11. Suspension and revocation.

(a) The Building Official may send to the holder of a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License a Notice to Appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners, where facts exist regarding any of the following reasons:

(1) An allegation of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under Article 86 of this code;

(2) An allegation of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under Article 86 of this code;

(3) An allegation of incompetence;

(4) An allegation of an act of willful or gross negligence;

(5) An allegation of deliberate misrepresentation;

(6) Failure of the licensee to comply with any notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department regarding the improper installation or alteration of fire alarm system wiring;

(7) Failure of the licensee to comply with the conditions under which a permit was issued; or

(8) Failure of the licensee to comply with any other requirement of this code, the 2019 Detroit City Code, or applicable state law.

(b) The Notice to Appear shall:

(1) Be in writing to the holder of the license at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division records to appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners at a stated date and time to show cause why the license should not be suspended or revoked;

(2) State the reason or reasons therefor that the license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at the hearing; and

(3) Be sent, via first class and certified mail, at least seven days before the scheduled hearing date.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the Board of Electrical Examiners is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the Board may suspend or revoke a Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License through the entry of an order, which reflects the Body’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the Board shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the Board decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the Board shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the Board of Electrical Examiners; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Fire Alarm Specialty Technician License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee;

laws.title: Required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as a sign specialty contractor in the installation, maintenance, repairing, servicing or altering of electrical equipment for signs and appurtenances thereof in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, without first having obtained a Sign Specialty Contractor License as provided for in this article.

(b) No license will be required for the repair of electrical wiring whose valuation is not in excess of $100.00, the replacement of lamps, or the connection of portable electrical equipment to suitable permanently-installed receptacles.

(c) An individual is not required to hold a Sign Specialty Contractor License in order to perform work that is permitted under such license where:

(1) The individual holds both a valid Electrical Contractor License and a valid Master Electrician License; or

(2) The person holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and employs a full-time individual who holds a valid Master Electrician License; or

(3) The individual holds a valid Electrical Journeyperson License and works under the supervision of a person who holds a valid Electrical Contractor License and an individual who holds valid Master Electrician License.

(d) In accordance with Section 5 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), a person who holds a valid Sign Specialty Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or by a Michigan municipality that regulates Sign Specialty Contractor Licenses is not required to obtain a Sign Specialty Contractor License from the City of Detroit, but is required to register under Article 88.50 of this code.

laws.title: Board of Electrical Examiners to determine qualifications of applicants; written examination required
laws.content:
(a) The Board of Electrical Examiners shall determine the qualifications of each applicant. The Board shall make its decision based upon the completed application and the written examination.

(b) The written examination shall be conducted once each month in accordance with the examination schedule that is posted at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division for the current calendar year.

A completed application to take the examination, including any request for special-needs accommodation, along with the required fee, shall be received at the Department no later than 14 days before the examination.

(c) As the Board of Electrical Examiners determines, the examination shall consist of a written test. The examination for a Sign Specialty Contractor License shall include, but not be limited to, questions designed to test an individual’s knowledge of this code, the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1501 et seq., and any other applicable law.

(d) An applicant who passes the written examination is eligible for issuance of his or her license at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, provided, that the applicant complies with Section 88.6 of this code.

laws.title: Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Article 88 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the appli-

cant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

88.7. Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of license.

(a) Upon compliance with Sections 88.3 through 88.6 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Sign Specialty Contractor License to the applicant.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

(c) A sign specialty contractor shall not allow their license to be used by any other individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

88.8. Posting and displaying of license.

(a) Upon issuance, the current, original Sign Specialty Contractor License shall be conspicuously posted in the licensee’s principal place of business.

(b) After issuance, the current, original wallet-size Sign Specialty Contractor License shall be carried when acting as a sign specialty contractor and displayed when requested.

88.9. Updating certain information required.

(a) Every holder of a Sign Specialty Contractor License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division any change of the address that was provided under Section 88.4 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

(b) Every holder of a Sign Specialty Contractor License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division any change of

partners, officers, or a trade or an assumed name that was provided under Section 88.4 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

88.10. Expiration and renewal of license; work prohibited where license expired or revoked.

(a) An application for renewal of a Sign Specialty Contractor License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division prior to January 1st.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Sign Specialty Contractor License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation as a sign specialty contractor until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) A Sign Specialty Contractor License that is issued under Section 88.7 of this code shall expire on December 31st and, where not renewed 60 days after the date of expiration, the license is deemed revoked.

(d) A Sign Specialty Contractor License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Board of Electrical Examiners and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Sign Specialty Contractor License has not been renewed or has been revoked to engage in the

laws.title: Suspension and revocation
laws.content:
(a) The Building Official may send to the holder of a Sign Specialty Contractor a Notice to Appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners, where facts exist regarding any of the following reasons:

(1) An allegation of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under Article 88 of this code;

(2) An allegation of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under Article 88 of this code;

(3) An allegation of incompetence;

(4) An allegation of an act of willful or gross negligence;

(5) An allegation of deliberate misrepresentation;

(6) Failure of the licensee to comply with any notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department regarding the improper manufacturing, installation, maintenance, connecting, or repair of electric sign wiring or devices, including directly-related wiring for electric signs that is electrically dedicated as a sign circuit beginning at the load side of the sign circuit disconnect;

(7) Failure of the licensee to comply with the conditions under which a permit was issued; or

(8) Failure of the licensee to comply with any other requirement of this code, the 2019 Detroit City Code, or applicable state law.

(b) The Notice to Appear shall:

(1) Be in writing to the holder of the license at the address shown on Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division records to appear before the Board of Electrical Examiners at a stated date and time to show cause why the license should not be suspended or revoked;

(2) State the reason or reasons therefor that the license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at the hearing; and

(3) Be sent, via first class and certified mail, at least seven days before the scheduled hearing date.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the Board of Electrical Examiners is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the Board may suspend or revoke a Sign Specialty Contractor License through the entry of an order, which reflects the Body’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the Board shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the Board decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the Board shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the Board of Electrical Examiners; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Sign Specialty Contractor License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee;

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division, which shall correct its records; and

(c) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Sign Specialty Contractor License has been suspended or revoked to manufacture, install, maintain, connect, or repair electric sign wiring or devices, including directly-related wiring for electric signs that is electrically dedicated as a sign circuit beginning at the load side of the sign circuit disconnect, requiring such license for its performance in the City, or to arrange for the performance of such work on a contractual basis, until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated or reissued.

the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. In accordance with Section 6(5) of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.886(5), it shall be unlawful for any person whose legal address is not within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit to engage as a sign specialty contractor in manufacturing, installing, maintaining, connecting, or repairing electric sign wiring or devices, including directly-related wiring for electric signs that is electrically dedicated as a sign circuit beginning at the load side of the sign circuit disconnect in or on any building structure or part thereof, or premises, or to act in the capacity of a sign specialty contractor within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. 88.53. Application required.

(a) An application for a Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor shall be made on a form that is approved by the Board of Electrical Examiners and provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division. The application shall be considered complete when the appropriate individual has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required registration fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The name, address of their principal place of business, and telephone number of the business;

(2) Where the applicant is an individual:

    (a) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years; and

    (b) The applicant’s current mailing address and e-mail address; and

(3) If applicant is a corporation:

    (a) Full and accurate corporation name;

    (b) The state and date of incorporation; and

    (c) The full names and addresses of officers, directors, managers, and other individuals with authority to bind the corporation;

(4) If applicant is a partnership:

    (a) Names of members thereof; and

    (b) Current mailing address and email address of members thereof.

(5) If the applicant conducts business under a trade or assume name:

    (a) Complete and full trade name and date of registration with County Clerk; and

    (b) The name of the individual or individuals doing business under such trade or assumed name; and

(6) The name and business address of the statutory agent, or other agent, who is authorized to receive service of process.

(b) An application shall be accompanied:

(1) By a true copy of the applicant’s valid Sign Specialty Contractor License issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Fire Alarm Contractor Licenses, for retention by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Electrical Division; and

(2) By payment of the non-refundable registration fee that is established and approved under Section 80.24 of this code.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
(a) Prior to the expiration of a current Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor, a registrant shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the certificate. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the registration fee before the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor shall allow for the continued engagement as a sign specialty contractor until such time that the Certificate of Registration renewal application is denied, or the Certificate of Registration is deemed void.

(b) In order to make the expiration date of the Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor commensurate with the expiration date of the license that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Sign Specialty Contractor Licenses, each Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor shall expire on December 31st, provided, that such Certificate of Registration shall expire annually and not on a three-year cycle.

(c) In order to make the renewal date of the Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor commensurate with the renewal date of the license that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Sign Specialty Contractor Licenses, each Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor shall be renewed no later than March 1st, provided, that such Certificate of Registration shall be renewed annually and not on a three-year cycle.

(d) Commensurate with Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, where a license that was issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 3 of the Michigan Electrical Administrative Act, being MCL 338.883, or by a Michigan municipality which regulates Sign Specialty Contractor Licenses, is not renewed by March 1st and, therefore, is deemed void, the Certificate of Registration for a Sign Specialty Contractor shall not be renewed until the license is reinstated.

Building Construction and Property Maintenance
Restrictions for appointees, employees, and independent contractors
laws.content:
All appointees, employees, and independent contractors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall not engage in, or directly or indirectly be connected with, the furnishing of labor, materials, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building or structure, or the preparation of plans or of specifications therefor, unless he or she is the owner of the building or structure, or engage in any work which conflicts with his or her official duties or with the interests of the Department. Employees and independent contractors shall not make inspections or perform any other Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department responsibility on property or equipment that is wholly or partially owned by the employee or independent contractor, or by a member of the employee’s or independent contractor’s immediate family.

(Code 1964, § 12-11-11.6; Code 1984, § 12-11-11.6; Ord. No. 290-H, § 1(12-11-11.6), eff. 11-15-1978; Ord. No. 15-88, § 1(12-11-11.6), eff. 9-21-1988)

laws.title: Certain advertising, signs and statements prohibited

**Sec. 8-4-6. Additions to Section 106 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Permits.**

In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 106 of the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, *Permits*, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

**106.1 Permits required.**

(a) A contractor licensed under 1984 PA 192, MCL 338.971 to 338.988, who desires:

(1) To erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert, or replace a mechanical system, the installation of which is regulated by this code, or cause such work to be done, shall first make application in accordance with the requirements of the act; or

(2) To install, alter, or repair a boiler or a pressure vessel, the installation of which is regulated by this code, or cause such work to be done, shall first make application in accordance with the requirements of this code.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person having control or management of any building or structure to use, or allow to be used, therein any equipment or system requiring a permit without a permit having been obtained from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

**106.3 Application for a permit; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions.**

(a) Each application for a permit, along with the required fee, shall be filed with the Code Official on a form furnished for that purpose and shall contain a general description of the purposed work or location. The contractor who is performing the work shall sign the application. Unless authorized to do so by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, no person shall use the name of another person to obtain a permit. The permit application shall indicate the proposed occupancy of all parts of the building and of that portion of the site or lot, if any, not covered by the building or structure and shall contain the information required by the act.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a permit where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

(i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

(ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

(iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

(iv) Is a financial institution with power:

A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

laws.title: Establishment and approval of fees; payment required before work begins
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Sections 10(1) and 22(1) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1510(1) and 125.1522(1), and Section 9-507 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of appeals, examinations, certificates, permits, inspections, re-inspections, and other fees that are required by the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code and by Chapter 8, Article IV, of 2019 Detroit City Code, Mechanical Code. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs that are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) In accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish and collect necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of licenses that are required by this article.

(c) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(d) The fees prescribed by this section shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department before a permit to begin work for new construction, alteration, removal, demolition, or other building operation may be issued. In addition, an amendment to a permit necessitating an additional fee shall not be approved until the additional fee is paid.

106.5.4 Fee for failure to obtain permit before starting work. Any person who commences installation of any mechanical system for which a permit is required by this code, without first having obtained a permit, shall pay, if legally authorized and subsequently allowed to obtain a permit, in addition to the permit fee specified by this code for such installation, a supplemental inspection fee to cover the cost of the services rendered by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that this requirement shall not apply to emergency work or installation when proved to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, or the Detroit Health Department, that such work or installation was urgently necessary, and would have been impractical to have awaited the time required for application and issuance of the permit, provided further, that, even in such emergencies, the required permit shall be obtained without unreasonable delay after installation starts, and in no case more than three days during which the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is open for business, or a supplemental inspection fee shall be charged in addition to the permit fee.

106.5.5 Fee refunds. Except for a permit that is fraudulently obtained, a permit issued under the provisions of this code may be canceled by the Building Official on the written request from the holder of such permit, provided, that such request is made within 180 days from the date of issuance of the permit and prior to any inspection or other action taken under the permit, including the exercise of any privilege granted by the permit. Where the permit is canceled, the City Treasurer, upon notification in writing from the Building Official, shall make a refund of 80 percent of all fees paid in connection with the issuance of such unused permit, provided, that, where a permit expires, a refund shall not be granted but the permit may be reinstated in accordance with Section 106.4.3 of this code.

laws.title: Additions to Section 107 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Inspections and Testing
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 107 of the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Inspections and Testing, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

107.1 General. The code official is authorized to conduct such inspections as are deemed necessary to determine compliance with the provisions of this code. In addition, a person who inspects equipment under Chapter 10 of this code, Boilers, Water Heaters and Pressure Vessels, is required under the Michigan Boiler Rules to hold, as applicable, a Certificate of Competency from the Director of the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs or a valid Commission as an inspector of boilers and pressure vessels that was issued by the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors, or both. Construction or work for which a permit is required shall be subject to inspection by the code official, and such construction or work

§ 8-4-7

shall remain assessable and exposed for inspection purposes until approved. Approval as a result of inspection shall not be construed to be an approval of a violation of the provisions of this code or of other ordinances of the jurisdiction. Inspections presuming to give authority to violate or cancel the provisions of this code or of other ordinances of the jurisdiction shall not be valid.

laws.title: Required inspections and testing
laws.content:
The Code Official, upon notification from the permit holder or the permit holder’s agent, shall make the following inspections and other such inspections as necessary, and shall either release that portion of the construction or shall notify the permit holder or the permit holder’s agent of violations that must be corrected. The holder of the permit shall be responsible for the scheduling of such inspections.

1. Underground inspection shall be made after trenches or ditches are excavated and bedded, piping installed, and before backfill is put in place. When excavated soil contains rocks, broken concrete, frozen chunks and other rubble that would damage or brake the piping or cause corrosive action, clean backfill shall be on the job site.

2. Rough-in inspection shall be made after the roof, framing, fireblocking and bracing are in place and all ducting and other components to be concealed are complete, and prior to the installation of wall or ceiling membranes.

3. Final inspection shall be made upon the completion of the mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel. After completion of the final inspection for installation of a boiler or a pressure vessel requiring periodic inspections under this code, the inspector shall affix to the boiler or the pressure vessel a metal tag, which contains a City serial number for permanent identification of the boiler or pressure vessel. Each metal tag for a boiler shall contain a four-digit serial number with a five-pointed star immediately before and after the serial number, while each metal tag for a pressure vessel shall contain a five-digit serial number with a five-pointed star immediately before and after the serial number. Such metal tag shall identify that the equipment was inspected by the City of Detroit and shall be applied only by duly authorized inspectors from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The location of the metal tag on the boiler or pressure vessel shall be recorded on the inspection report. The City’s metal tag, as well as other stampings required for identification on equipment, shall not be concealed, altered, made illegible, or removed, except by, or under the direction, of an inspector from the Department.

**Exception.** Ground-source heat pump loop systems tested in accordance with Section 1210.10 of this code shall be permitted to be backfilled prior to inspection.

The requirements of this section shall not be considered to prohibit the operation of any heating equipment or appliances installed to replace existing heating equipment or appliances serving an occupied portion of a structure, provided, that a request for inspection of such heating equipment or appliance has been filed with the Department not more than 48 hours after such replacement work is completed, and before any portion of such equipment or appliances is concealed by any permanent portion of the structure.

laws.title: Accident inspections
laws.content:
The user of any system or equipment governed by the code shall immediately notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department of any accident involving personal injury, or damage to equipment, on or about or in connection with such system or equipment and shall afford the Department every facility for investigating such accident or damage. Where an accident involves the failure, breakage, damage or destruction of any part of the system or equipment, it shall be unlawful to use such system equipment until after an examination by a representative of the Department and approval of such system

CD8:137
§ 8-4-7

DETROIT CITY CODE

or equipment is granted by the Department for continual use, provided, that, when such system or equipment is repaired and placed in safe operating condition by a person deemed qualified by the Department to do so, such as an applicable licensed contractor, the system may be used pending such inspection where notice is given by such person to the Department not later than the next business day following the repair. It shall be the duty of the Department to make a prompt examination into the cause of such accident and to file in the Department records a full and complete report thereof.

107.2.2.1 Pre-approval for Overtime Inspection. Pre-approval of overtime inspection shall be obtained for all services provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours.

107.3.4 Special Hydrostatic Pressure Tests. All high-pressure boilers, that are 25 years or older and have longitudinal lap seams, or that are 30 years or older, shall be subject to a special hydrostatic pressure test as described in the National Board Inspection Code, followed by an internal inspection, in the presence of an inspector from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. Thereafter, where determined necessary by the Department, the special hydrostatic pressure test shall be conducted approximately every three years.

107.7 Reports of inspectors. The inspectors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall make a written report of each inspection and file same in the records of their Department. A copy of such report shall be mailed to the owner and, if applicable, to the contractor.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.3, 4.0, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 5.2, 5.3, 801.3, 801.9; Ord. No. 705-G, § 1(3.3, 4.0, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 5.2, 5.3), eff. 7-4-1972; Ord. No. 390-H, § 1(801.3, 801.9), eff. 10-19-1980)

laws.title: Additions to Section 108 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Violations
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act,

being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 108 of the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Violations, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

108.1 Unlawful acts. It shall be unlawful for a person, firm, or corporation to erect, construct, alter, repair, remove, demolish or utilize a mechanical system, or cause same to be done, in conflict with or in violation of any of the provisions of this code, or to render ineffective any safety device or alarm for a boiler or pressure vessel under this code or cause same to be done, or to abuse any boiler or pressure vessel to render the equipment unsafe under this code or cause same to be done.

108.1.1 Interference with Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department personnel. Any person who refuses to comply with or who shall assist in the violation of any of provision of this code, or who hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents, or interferes in any manner with any inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in the performance of any duty imposed by this code, or refuses to permit such inspectors to perform their duties, shall be subject to the penalties and fines provided for in Section 108 of this code.

108.4 Violation penalties.

(a) Any person, or anyone acting on behalf of said person, who violates a provision of this code, who fails to conform with any of the requirements thereof, or who erects, installs, alters, or repairs mechanical work in violation of the approved construction documents or directive of the enforcing agency, or a permit or certificate issued under the provisions of this code shall be fined, or imprisoned, or both, in accordance with Subsection (b) of this section. (b) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, upon conviction, a person shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500, or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90

laws.title: Unsafe mechanical systems, boilers, and pressure vessels
laws.content: A mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel that is unsafe, constitutes a fire or health hazard, or is otherwise dangerous to human life, as regulated by this code, is hereby declared as an unsafe mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel. Use of a mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel regulated by this code constituting a hazard to health, safety or welfare by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard, disaster, damage or abandonment is hereby declared an unsafe use. Such unsafe equipment and appliances are hereby declared to be a public nuisance and shall be abated by repair, rehabilitation, demolition or removal.

laws.title: Authority to condemn mechanical systems, boilers, and pressure vessels
laws.content:
Whenever the code official determines that any mechanical system, boiler or pressure vessel, or portion thereof, regulated by this code has become hazardous to life, health, property, or has become insanitary, the code official shall order in writing that such system either be removed or restored to a safe condition. A time limit for compliance with such order shall be specified in the written notice. A person shall not use or maintain a defective mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel after receiving such notice.

Where such mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel is to be disconnected, written notice as prescribed in Section 108.2 shall be given. In cases of immediate danger to life or property, such disconnection shall be made immediately without such notice.

laws.title: Authority to place mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel out of service
laws.content:
A mechanical system, or a boiler or pressure vessel, which is governed by this code, may be placed out of service for the reasons that:

(1) The mechanical system has not been registered under Section 111 of this code, or the boiler or pressure vessel has not been registered under Section 112 of this code;

(2) There is a willful failure to comply with a notice issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for correction of any violation; or

(3) The owner has requested that the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department take such action due to non-use of the mechanical system or the boiler or pressure vessel.

laws.title: Red Tag required; defacing or removing Red Tag prohibited
laws.content: Any mechanical system, or boiler or pressure vessel, that is shut down by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department either as condemned under Section 108.7.1 of this code or as out of service under Section 108.7.1.1 of this code, shall be conspicuously labeled with a Red Tag, which indicates the reason for the shut down, and any defacing, tampering, or removal of such Red Tag without the approval of the Department shall constitute a violation of this section.

laws.title: Unlawful to use mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel, labeled with Red Tag
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person having control or management of any mechanical system, boiler, or pressure vessel that is governed by this code, which is labeled with a Red Tag as condemned under Section 108.7.1 of this code or as out of service under Section 108.7.1.1 of this code, to use or permit to be used such system, or part thereof, until the causes for the shutdown have been eliminated and the system, or part thereof, has been put in a safe condition and approved as such by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that a Mechanical Contractor who is registered under

laws.title: Addition of Section 112 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Boiler and Pressure Vessel Registration
laws.content:

**112 BOILER AND PRESSURE VESSEL REGISTRATION**

**112.1 Registration of boilers and pressure vessels required.** No person shall use, or cause to be used, any boiler or pressure vessel, which is subject to inspection in accordance with Section 102.3.2 of this code, without first registering the equipment at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that a system installed and previously inspected by the Department will be registered by the Department.

laws.title: Addition of Section 113 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Mechanical Contractor Registration
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Section 113, Mechanical Contractor Registration, to the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

**113 MECHANICAL CONTRACTOR REGISTRATION**

**113.1 Certificate of Registration required.** It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of or to act in the capacity of a contractor in any of the work classifica-

tions set forth in Section 6(3) of the Michigan Forbes Mechanical Contractors Act, being MCL 338.976(3), within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that, in the case of Fire Suppression Contractors, such Certificate of Registration shall be obtained from the Office of the Fire Marshal. A Certificate of Registration shall not be issued to any person unless such person is licensed as a mechanical contractor by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs in one or more of the work classifications set forth in Section 6(3) of the Michigan Forbes Mechanical Contractors Act, being MCL 338.976(3).

**113.2 Installation, alteration, and service; homeowner installations.**

(a) Except as provided for in Subsection (b) of this section, a person who is not registered with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department as a Mechanical Contractor under the provisions of this division shall not install, alter or service any of the equipment or systems specified in this code, or arrange to alter or service the latter on a contractual basis, provided, that:

(1) This may be done where a clause is made part of the contract, designating the registered contractor and stating that the contractor will obtain the necessary permits and perform the contracted-for work; and

(2) A person who is licensed as a First-Class Stationary Engineer, a Second-Class Stationary Engineer, or a Third-Class Stationary Engineer may make operational adjustments to the gas burners, oil burners or appurtenances thereof in boiler facilities, where they have been employed to operate.

(5) If the applicant conducts business under a trade or assume name:

 (b) The name of the person or persons doing business under such trade or assumed name.

laws.title: Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any Certificate of Registration that is required by Section 113 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be

CD8:143
§ 8-4-12

DETROIT CITY CODE

the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A Certificate of Registration shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

113.5 Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of Certificate of Registration.

(a) Upon compliance with Sections 113.3 and 113.4 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Certificate of Registration for a Mechanical Contractor to the applicant.

(b) A Certificate of Registration that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

(c) A mechanical contractor shall not allow their Certificate of Registration for a Mechanical Contractor be used by any other individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or other legal entity.

113.6 Updating certain information required.

Every holder of a Certificate of Registration for a for a Mechanical Contractor shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engi-

neering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided under Section 113.3 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

113.7 Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration.

(a) Commensurate with the expiration date of their state license under Section 10(2) of the Michigan Forbes Mechanical Contractors Act, being MCL 338.980(2), each Certificate of Registration as a mechanical contractor shall expire on August 31st every third year.

(b) Commensurate with the renewal of their state license under Section 10(2) of the Michigan Forbes Mechanical Contractors Act, being MCL 338.980(2), each Certificate of Registration as a mechanical contractor shall be renewed no later than October 31st every third year.

(c) Commensurate with Section 10(2) of the Michigan Forbes Mechanical Contractors Act, being MCL 338.980(2), where a license that is not renewed by October 31st every third year is deemed void and may be reinstated only by reapplying and paying the licensing fee, the Certificate of Registration as a mechanical contractor shall not be renewed until the license is reinstated.

laws.title: Required
laws.content: The actual work necessary to install, alter, or service any refrigerating systems, which are governed by this code, may be done under the supervision of a licensed and registered Mechanical Contractor by persons who are registered with the City of Detroit either as a Refrigeration Apprentice or as a Refrigeration Journeyman.

laws.title: General
laws.content: There shall be a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice and a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman. The applicable designation shall be indicated on the face of the certificate. The holder of a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice is limited to perform the installation, alteration, or servicing of unit or self-contained refrigerating systems that do not exceed one and one-half horsepower while under the supervision of a Mechanical Contractor by whom employed. The holder of a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman may install, alter, or service refrigerating systems while under the supervision of a Mechanical Contractor by whom employed.

laws.title: Application with required references
laws.content: An application for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. Each application shall contain the full name, address, and telephone number of two personal references who are acquainted with the character and habits of the applicant. Documentary evidence of professed experience that is required under Section 114.6 of this code shall be submitted with the application for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman. The completed application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

laws.title: Age requirement
laws.content:
(a) An applicant for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice shall have attained a minimum of 18 years of age.

(b) An applicant for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall have attained a minimum of 20 years of age.

laws.title: Experience requirements
laws.content:
An applicant for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall meet either of the following experience requirements:

CD8:145
§ 8-4-13

DETROIT CITY CODE

(1) An applicant for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice shall have at least two years of experience, while an applicant for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall have at least four years of experience, in the actual installation, alteration, or servicing of refrigerating systems; or

(2) The applicant is registered as a professional engineer, or possesses a Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical, electrical, civil or chemical engineering, or is a graduate of an approved refrigeration trade school, and has at least one year of experience as a refrigeration apprentice, or at least two years of experience as a refrigeration journeyman, in the actual installation, alteration or servicing of refrigerating systems.

114.6 Substantiation of experience. The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall require substantiation of professed experience:

(1) By means of a communication from present or previous employers that is prepared on business letterhead and signed by an authorized person in the presence of a notary public; or

(2) By other acceptable documentary evidence.

114.7 Examinations required.

A written examination for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman to be issued by the City shall be administered by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department or his or her authorized assistants. No Certificate of Registration shall be issued to an applicant unit he or she has passed the required examination.

114.8 Content of examinations.

(a) The written examination for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall be practical in character and shall relate to those matters which fairly test the ability of the applicant to install, alter, or service refrigerating systems in a safe and proper manner. The applicant shall attain a predetermined score in the examination, as set by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, to qualify for a Certificate of Registration.

(b) An applicant who fails the examination shall wait at least 90 days before re-applying for examination. The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall have the authority in specific cases to make such modification of the waiting period between examinations as will not be contrary to the public interest and so that the spirit of Section 114 of this code shall be observed.

114.9 Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage.

(a) Upon application and before any Certificate of Registration that is required by Section 114.1 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax, or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A Certificate of Registration shall not be issued or renewed by the

laws.title: Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of certificate

(b) A Certificate of Registration that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual.

(c) A refrigeration apprentice or a refrigeration journeyman shall not allow his or her Certificate of Registration to be used by any other individual.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content: Every holder of a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or a Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided under Section 114.3 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
(a) Each Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall expire one year from the date of issuance.

(b) Each Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Refrigeration Journeyman shall be renewed before its expiration date.

laws.title: Certificate of Registration expired; unlawful to perform or arrange performance of work
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person whose Certificate of Registration for a Refrigeration Apprentice or for a Refrigeration Journeyman has not been renewed to install, alter, or service any refrigerating systems, which are governed by this code, until such expired Certificate of Registration has been renewed or reinstated.

laws.title: Required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for refrigerating systems, the largest of which contains more than 250 pounds of refrigerant but not more than 500 pounds of refrigerant or is driven by motors or engines that are in excess of 50 horsepower but not in excess of 125 horsepower as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate or as calculated using acceptable engineering methods, that is governed by this code to be operated without the presence of a licensed operator in responsible charge acting as an attending licensed oper-
