ator who, at a minimum, is licensed by the City as a third-class refrigeration operator.

(b) Refrigerating systems, the largest of which contains not more than 250 pounds of refrigerant and is driven by motors or engines that are not in excess of 50 horsepower as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate or as calculated using acceptable engineering methods, that is governed by this code is not required to have a licensed operator in responsible charge or an attending licensed operator present during operation.

(c) A refrigerating system, which employs only water as a refrigerant as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate, that is governed by this code is not required to have a licensed operator in responsible charge or an attending licensed operator present during operation.

115.2 Application with required references. An application for a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. Each application shall contain the full name, address, and telephone number of two personal references who are acquainted with the character and habits of the applicant. Documentary evidence of professed experience that is required under Section 115.5 of this code shall be submitted with the application for a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License. The completed application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

115.3 Age requirement. An applicant for a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall have attained a minimum of 19 years of age.

115.4 Experience requirements. An applicant for a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall meet one of the following experience requirements:

(1) He or she shall have had at least three months of experience in the operation of non-domestic refrigeration equipment; or

(2) He or she shall have satisfactorily completed an acceptable course in the operation, servicing, installation, repair or maintenance of non-domestic refrigerating systems, as established by completion letters or certificates.

115.5 Substantiation of experience. The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall require substantiation of professed experience:

(1) By means of a communication from present or previous employers that is prepared on business letterhead and signed by an authorized person in the presence of a notary public; or

(2) By other acceptable documentary evidence.

A written and an oral examination for a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall be administered by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department after payment of the examination fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code. laws.content:
(a) Upon compliance with Sections 115.2 through 115.8 of this code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License to the applicant.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of license
laws.content:
(a) A Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall expire one year from the date of issuance and, unless renewed within 60 days thereafter, is deemed revoked.

(b) A Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and a showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has not been renewed to operate any equipment that is governed by this code until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated.

115.13 Suspension and revocation of license.

(a) Upon recommendation of the Code Official, the Director may take action to suspend or revoke a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License. The causes for which such license may be suspended or revoked are any of the following:

(1) The practice of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under this code;

(2) The practice of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under this code;

(3) An act of gross negligence;

(4) Engaging in advertising contrary to Section 105.6 of this code;

(5) An act which demonstrates incompetence;

(6) Neglect of duty;

(7) Failure to keep apparatus in safe working order;

(8) Turning over operating equipment to a non-licensed or improperly licensed person; and

(9) A violation of this code.

(b) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall promulgate procedural administrative rules for hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of Third-Class Refrigeration Operator Licenses. Among others, such rules shall provide that the Director is required, at least seven days before the hearing, to send, via first class and certified mail, to the licensee a Notice to Appear, which contains the reason or reasons therefor under Subsection (a) of this section, that his or her license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at a hearing provided before a designated hearing officer. Pending the hearing,

the Director may forthwith suspend such license where, in his or her judgment, the circumstances warrant such action.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearing officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the hearing officer may suspend or revoke a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License through the entry of an order, which reflects the hearing officer’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearing officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearing officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the hearing officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which, in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearing officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee; and

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has been suspended or revoked to operate equipment that

laws.title: Second-class Refrigeration Operator License
laws.content:
**116.1 Required.** It shall be unlawful for refrigerating systems, the largest of which contains more than 500 pounds of refrigerant but not more than 1,000 pounds of refrigerant or is driven by motors or engines that are in excess of 125 horsepower but not in excess of 250 horsepower as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate or as calculated using acceptable engineering methods, that is governed by this code to be operated without the presence of a licensed operator in responsible charge who, at a minimum, is licensed by the City as a second-class refrigeration operator.

**116.2 Application with required references.** An application for a Second-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. (a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Section 116.1 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Section 117.1 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

partment shall issue a First-Class Refrigeration Operator License to the applicant.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual.

(c) A first-class refrigeration operator shall not allow his or her license to be used by any other individual.

117.10 Posting of license. Upon issuance, the current, original First-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall be conspicuously posted in the area containing the equipment that is operated by the licensee.

117.11 Updating certain information required.

Every holder of a First-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided under Section 117.2 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

117.12 Expiration and renewal of license.

(a) A First-Class Refrigeration Operator License shall expire one year from the date of issuance and, unless renewed within 60 days thereafter, is deemed revoked.

(b) A First-Class Refrigeration Operator License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and a showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant's license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has not been renewed to operate any equipment that is governed by this code until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated.

117.13 Suspension and revocation of license.

(a) Upon recommendation of the Code Official, the Director may take action to suspend or revoke a First-Class Refrigeration Operator License. The causes for which such license may be suspended or revoked are any of the following:

(1) The practice of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under this code;

(2) The practice of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under this code;

(3) An act of gross negligence;

(4) Engaging in advertising contrary to Section 105.6 of this code;

(5) An act which demonstrates incompetence;

(6) Neglect of duty;

(7) Failure to keep apparatus in safe working order;

(8) Turning over operating equipment to a non-licensed or improperly licensed person; and

(9) A violation of this code.

(b) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall promulgate procedural administrative rules for hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of First-Class Refrigeration Operator Licenses. Among others, such rules shall provide that the Director is required, at least seven days before the hearing, to send, via first class and certified mail, to the licensee a Notice to Appear, which contains the reason or reasons therefor under Subsection (a) of this section, that his or her license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at a hearing provided before a designated hearing officer. Pending the hearing,

the Director may forthwith suspend such license where, in his or her judgment, the circumstances warrant such action.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearing officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the hearing officer may suspend or revoke a First-Class Refrigeration Operator License through the entry of an order, which reflects the hearing officer’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearing officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearing officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the hearing officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which, in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearing officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue First-Class Refrigeration Operator License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee; and

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has been suspended or revoked to operate equipment that is governed by this code until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated.

117.14 Review of adverse decision. In the event that the decision of the hearing officer is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the hearing officer remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: Required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a low-pressure boiler facility that has an aggregate heating surface of more than 300 square feet and less than 5,000 square feet as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate, or that has hot water heating and hot water supply boilers of 1,000 or less square feet of aggregate heating surface as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate, which is governed by this code, to be operated without the presence of a licensed operator in responsible charge acting as an attending licensed operator who, at a minimum, is licensed by the City as a low-pressure boiler operator.

CD8:157
§ 8-4-17

DETROIT CITY CODE

(b) A low-pressure boiler facility that has 300 or less square feet of aggregate heating surface as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate, which is governed by this code, is not required to have a licensed operator in responsible charge or an attending licensed operator present during operation.

(c) A low-pressure boiler facility that has hot water heating and hot water supply boilers with each boiler having 1,000 or less square feet of heating surface as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate, which is governed by this code, is not required to have a licensed operator in responsible charge or an attending licensed operator present during operation.

118.2 Application with required references. An application for a Low-Pressure Boiler Operator License shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. Each application shall contain the full name, address, and telephone number of two personal references who are acquainted with the character and habits of the applicant. Documentary evidence of professed experience that is required under Section 118.5 of this code shall be submitted with the application for a Low-Pressure Boiler Operator License. The completed application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

118.3 Age requirement. An applicant for a Low-Pressure Boiler Operator License shall have attained a minimum of 19 years of age.

118.4 Experience requirements. An applicant for Low-Pressure Boiler Operator License shall have been actively employed for a minimum of one year in connection with the operation or maintenance of low-pressure boilers, high-pressure boilers, steam prime movers, and their auxiliaries.

118.5 Substantiation of experience. The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall require substantiation of professed experience:

(1) By means of a communication from present or previous employers that is prepared on business letterhead and signed by an authorized person in the presence of a notary public; or

(2) By other acceptable documentary evidence.

118.6 Examination required. An examination for a Low-Pressure Boiler Operator License, which consists of written and oral portions, shall be administered by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department after payment of the examination fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code. No license shall be issued to an applicant until he or she has passed the examination. An applicant who fails this examination shall wait at least 90 days before reapplying for the examination, provided, that the Department is authorized in specific cases to make modification of the waiting period between examinations, which is not contrary to the public interest, so that the spirit of Section 118 of this code is observed.

118.7 Content of examination. The examinations shall cover boilers, steam prime movers and their appurtenances, accessories and auxiliaries, fuels and fuel burning equipment, basic electricity, controls and instrumentation, feed water treatment, piping, safety measures, and other subjects relating to the safe and proper care and the operation of boiler facilities and steam prime mover facilities.

laws.title: Second-class Stationary Engineer License
laws.content:
121.1 Required. It shall be unlawful for a boiler facility that has an aggregate of more than 7,500 and not more than 20,000 square feet of heating surface, and an aggregate of more than 100 and not more than 200 steam engine-turbine horsepower as determined from data on the manufacturer’s nameplate or as calculated using acceptable engineering methods, which is governed by this code, to be operated without the presence of a licensed operator in responsible charge who, at a minimum, is licensed by the City as a second-class stationary engineer.

121.2 Application with required references. An application for a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Build-

CD8:167
§ 8-4-20

DETROIT CITY CODE

ings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. Each application shall contain the full name, address, and telephone number of two personal references who are acquainted with the character and habits of the applicant. Documentary evidence of professed experience that is required under Section 121.5 of this code shall be submitted with the application for a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License. The completed application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

**121.3 Age requirement.** An applicant for a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall have attained a minimum of 19 years of age.

**121.4 Experience requirements.** An applicant for Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall meet one of the following experience requirements:

(1) He or she shall possess a Third-Class Stationary Engineer License and shall have had at least one year of experience as such a stationary engineer;

(2) He or she shall be an engineering graduate of a college of recognized standing and have been actually employed in the engineering or research division of a steam-electric power generating plant for at least one year;

(3) He or she shall have at least four years of experience in the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler facility having an aggregate heating surface of more than 7,500 square feet, as established by documentary evidence from present and previous employers;

(4) He or she shall have at least one year of experience in the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler facility having an aggregate heating surface or more than 7,500 square feet, plus sufficient experience in the actual operation of steam prime movers in excess of 100 horsepower to make a total of at least four years, as established by documentary evidence from present and previous employers; or

(5) He or she shall have at least one year of experience in the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler facility having an aggregate heating surface of more than 7,500 square feet, plus sufficient experience in the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler facility having an aggregate heating surface of more than 4,000 square feet to make a total of at least four years, as established by documentary evidence from present and previous employers.

**121.5 Substantiation of experience.** The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall require substantiation of professed experience:

(1) By means of a communication from present or previous employers that is prepared on business letterhead and signed by an authorized person in the presence of a notary public; or

(2) By other acceptable documentary evidence.

**121.6 Examinations required.** A written and an oral examination for a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall be administered by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department after payment of the examination fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code. No license shall be issued to an applicant until he or she has passed both examinations. The applicant shall attain a predetermined score in the written examination as set by the Department before he or she becomes eligible for the oral examination. An applicant who fails either the written exam-

ination or the subsequent oral examination shall wait at least 90 days from the date of the written examination before reapplying for the examinations, provided, that the Department is authorized in specific cases to make modification of the waiting period between examinations, which is not be contrary to the public interest, so that the spirit of Section 121 of this code is observed.

laws.title: Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Section 121.1 of this code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Posting of license
laws.content: Upon issuance, the current, original Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall be conspicuously posted in the area containing the equipment that is operated by the licensee.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content: Every holder of a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided under Section 121.2 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of license
laws.content:
(a) A Second-Class Stationary Engineer License shall expire one year from the date of issuance and, unless renewed within 60 days thereafter, is deemed revoked.

(b) A Second-Class Stationary Engineer License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and a showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant's license is revoked for more than three years,

DETROIT CITY CODE

the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has not been renewed to operate any equipment that is governed by this code until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated.

121.13 Suspension and revocation of license.

(a) Upon recommendation of the Code Official, the Director may take action to suspend or revoke a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License. The causes for which such license may be suspended or revoked are any of the following:

(1) The practice of fraud or deceit in obtaining a license under this code;

(2) The practice of fraud or deceit in the performance of work for which a license is required under this code;

(3) An act of gross negligence;

(4) Engaging in advertising contrary to Section 105.6 of this code;

(5) An act which demonstrates incompetence;

(6) Neglect of duty;

(7) Failure to keep apparatus in safe working order;

(8) Turning over operating equipment to a non-licensed or improperly licensed person; and

(9) A violation of this code.

(b) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall promulgate procedural administrative rules for hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of Second-Class Stationary Engineer Licenses. Among others, such rules shall provide that the Director is required, at least seven days before the hearing, to send, via first class and certified mail, to the licensee a Notice to Appear, which contains the reason or reasons therefor under Subsection (a) of this section, that his or her license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at a hearing provided before a designated hearing officer. Pending the hearing, the Director may forthwith suspend such license where, in his or her judgment, the circumstances warrant such action.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearing officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the hearing officer may suspend or revoke a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License through the entry of an order, which reflects the hearing officer’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearing officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearing officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the hearing officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which, in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearing officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Second-Class Stationary Engineer License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

(a) To the licensee; and

(b) To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has been suspended or revoked to operate equipment that is governed by this code until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated.

laws.title: Review of adverse decision
laws.content:
In the event that the decision of the hearing officer is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the hearing officer remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: Application with required references
laws.content: An application for a First-Class Stationary Engineer License shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The applicant shall complete the form in ink or type, shall provide information as deemed pertinent in determining the eligibility of the applicant for examination, and shall sign the form in the presence of a notary public. Each application shall contain the full name, address, and telephone number of two personal references who are acquainted with the character and habits of the applicant. Documentary evidence of professed experience that is required under Section 122.5 of this code shall be submitted with the application for a First-Class Stationary Engineer License. The completed application shall be accompanied by payment of the non-refundable license fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

laws.title: Age requirement
laws.content: An applicant for a First-Class Stationary Engineer License shall have attained a minimum of 19 years of age.

laws.title: Experience requirements
laws.content:

(1) He or she shall possess a Second-Class Stationary Engineer License and shall have had at least two years of experience as such a stationary engineer;

(2) He or she shall have at least six years of experience in the actual operation of boilers in a high-pressure boiler facility having an aggregate heating surface of more than 20,000 square feet, as established by documentary evidence from present and previous employers;

laws.title: Addition of Section 123 of 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, Special Inspectors Registration
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds Section 123, Special Inspectors Registration, to the 2015 Michigan Mechanical Code, which provisions were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

123 SPECIAL INSPECTORS REGISTRATION

123.1 Certificate of Registration required. It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of or to act in the capacity of a special inspector for an insurance company under Rules 75, 79, and 81 of the Michigan Boiler Rules, being R408.4075, R408.4079, and R408.4081 in the Michigan Administrative Code, as promulgated by the Director of the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 4 of the Michigan Boiler

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-4-22

Act of 1965, being MCL 408.754, within the corporate limits of the City of Detroit without first obtaining a Certificate of Registration for a Special Inspector from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. A Certificate of Registration for a Special Inspector shall not be issued to any person unless such person is licensed as a special inspector by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs.

laws.title: Application required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a Certificate of Registration for a Special Inspector shall be made on forms furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. In addition to other information, the application, in affidavit form, shall contain the following:

(1) Name, birthdate, and business address of applicant; and

(2) Name, address, and telephone number of insurance company that employs the applicant.

(b) A completed application shall be accompanied:

(1) By a true copy of the applicant’s valid Special Inspector License, issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, for retention by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department; and

(2) By payment of the non-refundable registration fee that is established and approved under Section 106.5 of this code.

laws.title: Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of Certificate of Registration

(c) A special inspector shall not allow his or her Certificate of Registration for a Special Inspector to be used by any other individual.

laws.title: Updating certain information required

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:

(b) A Certificate of Registration Certificate of Registration for a Special Inspector shall be renewed commensurate with the renewal date of their state license under Rule 79 of the Michigan Boiler Rules, being R408.4079 in the Michigan Administrative Code, as promulgated by the Director of the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs under Section 4 of the Michigan Boiler Act of 1965, being MCL 408.754.

laws.title: General
laws.content: Except as otherwise permitted in Section 1012 of this code, the presence of an attending licensed operator, or a licensed operator in responsible charge acting as an attending licensed operator, who continuously maintains the post of duty as specified in Section 1012 of this code shall be required when a boiler and its steam prime mover are in operation. A boiler and its steam prime mover shall be considered in operation unless the fuel supply has been permanently disconnected so that no additional fuel will be introduced, either automatically or manually, into the firing chamber, the air supplied to the firing chamber is below that used under normal conditions, and the pressure in the boiler continues to approach atmospheric pressure.

laws.title: Operation of low-pressure steam boilers and low-pressure hot water boilers outside normal business hours
laws.content:
The presence of an attending licensed operator shall not be required when the premises served by a low-pressure steam boiler or boilers, or a low-pressure hot-water boiler or boilers, is not normally occupied or is not in use to conduct business or industry, such as during nights, weekends and holidays, when the premises is closed to operations or public usage, provided, that the following requirements are met:

(1) The aggregate heating surface of the boiler facility shall not exceed 1,500 square feet;

(2) Steam boilers shall be equipped with approved safety valves set and stamped to relieve at not more than 15 psi, and hot water boilers shall be equipped with approved safety relief valves set and stamped to relieve at not more than 160 psi;

(3) An approved automatic means of feeding water into the boilers shall be provided;

(4) Boilers shall be equipped with an approved pressure control with a maximum setting not to exceed 90 percent of the setting of the safety valves or safety relief valves and, in addition, hot water boilers shall be equipped with an approved temperature control with a maximum setting of 250 degrees Fahrenheit;

(5) An approved control, requiring manual re-setting, shall be installed which will shut off the fuel and air supply in the event of low water;

(6) During this period, the boilers shall be used only for space heating, indirect hot water supply heating, or the maintaining of temperatures of idle processes; and

(7) Such method of operation shall not be put into effect until written request is submitted to, and written

CD8:177
§ 8-4-23

DETROIT CITY CODE

permission has been granted by, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

**1012.4 Licensed operator in responsible charge required.** Except as provided for in Section 1012.3 of this code, it shall be unlawful to operate a boiler facility or a steam prime mover facility as specified in Section 1012 of this code without a licensed operator in responsible charge thereof who possesses the required license, or a higher classification of the required license, commensurate with the designated classification of the boiler facility or the steam prime mover facility.

**1012.5 Post of duty for licensed operator in responsible charge.** The post of duty of the licensed operator in responsible charge of a boiler facility or a steam prime mover facility shall be within the actual facility. When he or she must also serve as attending licensed operator, his or her post of duty shall be maintained as specified in Section 1012 of this code. When other operators, serving as attending licensed operators, are on duty under the licensed operator in responsible charge, the latter may absent himself or herself from his or her post of duty for the purpose of performing his or her regularly assigned duties for reasonable periods, provided, that the time absent is not more than two hours at a time and not more than a total of four hours in any eight-hour period and that, in the opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, his or her absence does not jeopardize the safe operation of the facility.

**1012.6 Attending licensed operator for boiler facilities.** A person serving as attending licensed operator of a boiler facility under the direction of the licensed operator in responsible charge may operate a boiler facility covered by the license of the latter, provided, that the attending licensed operator possesses at least a Low-Pressure or a High-Pressure Boiler Operator License, which is commensurate with the designated classification of the boiler facility.

**1012.7 Attending licensed operator for steam prime mover facilities.** An attending licensed operator of a steam prime mover facility who serves under the direction of the licensed operator in responsible charge may monitor the steam prime mover covered by the license of the licensed operator in responsible charge, provided, that the attending licensed operator possesses at least a Third-Class Stationary Engineer License.

**1012.8 Post of duty for high-pressure steam boiler and high-pressure hot water boiler facilities.** The post of duty of the attending licensed operator of high-pressure steam boiler and high-pressure hot-water boiler facilities shall be in the room where the boiler or boilers are located and in immediate adjoining rooms, if so arranged, which contain the auxiliaries pertinent to the operation of said boilers, provided, that, in the opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the wall openings between the auxiliary and boiler rooms are readily accessible for passage, visibility, and audibility.

**1012.9 Post of duty for low-pressure steam boiler facilities.** The post of duty of the attending licensed operators of low-pressure steam boiler facilities shall be as follows:

(1) In facilities having an aggregate of more than 1,000 square feet of heating surface, the post of duty of the attending licensed operator shall be in the room where the boiler or boilers are located and in immediate adjoining rooms, if so arranged, which contain the auxiliaries pertinent to the operation of said boiler or boilers, provided, that, in the opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the wall openings between the auxiliary and boiler rooms are readily accessible for passage, visibility, and audibility;

(2) In facilities having an aggregate of more than 750 but not more than 1,000 square feet of heating surface, the post of duty of the attending

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:

licensed operator shall be as described in Subsection (1) of this section, provided, that he or she may be absent from the room where the boiler or boilers are located for not more than 60 consecutive minutes when, in the opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the safety of the facility is not jeopardized by his or her absence;

(3) In facilities having an aggregate of more than 300 square feet but not more than 750 square feet of heating surface, the post of duty of the attending licensed operator shall be on the premises, provided, that, in the opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the absence of the attending licensed operator from the boiler room does not jeopardize the safe operation of the facility; and

(4) In facilities having an aggregate of 300 or less square feet of heating surface, no attending licensed operator is required.

laws.title: Post of duty for low-pressure hot water boiler facilities
laws.content: The post of duty of the attending licensed operator of low-pressure hot water boiler facilities with an aggregate of more than 1,000 square feet of heating surface shall be on the premises.

laws.title: Unapproved change in floor plan or unsuitable duty assignment
laws.content: Where the floor plan of the building or structure that houses boilers, steam prime movers and their accessories, auxiliaries and regulating equipment is changed without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, or the assigned duties of the required licensed operating personnel are inconsistent with Section 1012 of this code, a violation may be issued and correction of the offending conditions shall be made in a manner acceptable to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

laws.title: Prohibited actions
laws.content:
(a) An attending licensed operator or a licensed operator in responsible charge shall not leave his or her post of duty, except as otherwise permitted in Section 1012 of this code, or relinquish his or her responsibilities for the operation of boilers or steam prime movers to a person who is not licensed in accordance with the requirements of this code.

(b) A person having control or management of a boiler facility or a steam prime mover facility shall not operate or cause to be operated such apparatus contrary to the requirements of this code, or allow or require the necessary licensed personnel to leave their post of duty except as permitted in Section 1012 of this code.

laws.title: Definitions
laws.content:
For purposes of Section 1110 of this code, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them by this section:

*Attending licensed operator* means the person who:

(1) Is licensed under this code, commensurate with the designated classification of the refrigerating system, as a third-class refrigeration operator under Section 115 of this code,

CD8:179
§ 8-4-24

DETROIT CITY CODE

a second-class refrigeration operator under Section 116 of his code, or a first-class refrigeration operator under Section 117 of this code;

(2) Is designated by the person having control or management of the equipment, property, or premises to operate equipment covered by this code; and

(3) Is physically available to fulfill the post of duty requirements of Section 1110 of this code.

*Licensed operator in responsible charge* means the person who:

(1) Is licensed under this code, commensurate with the designated classification of the refrigerating system, as a third-class refrigeration operator under Section 115 of this code, a second-class refrigeration operator under Section 116 of his code, or a first-class refrigeration operator under Section 117 of this code; and

(2) Is selected and designated by the person having control or management of the equipment, property, or premises to assume full charge while on duty for the complete and safe operation of equipment covered by this code.

*Post of duty* means the station or place to be occupied by a person who is licensed under this code, commensurate with the designated classification of the refrigerating system, as a third-class refrigeration operator under Section 115 of this code, a second-class refrigeration operator under Section 116 of his code, or a first-class refrigeration operator under Section 117 of this code while carrying out his or her assigned duties and responsibilities.

1110.2 General. Except as otherwise permitted in Section 1110 of this code, the presence of an attending licensed operator, or a licensed operator in responsible charge acting as an attending licensed operator, who continuously maintains the post of duty as specified in Section 1110 of this code shall be required when refrigerating systems are in operation. The three classes of licenses, which cover the operation of refrigeration systems, are designated in ascending order of precedence as Third-Class Refrigeration Operator, Second-Class Refrigeration Operator, and First-Class Refrigeration Operator.

1110.3 Operation of refrigerating system outside normal business hours. The presence of an attending licensed operator, or a licensed operator in responsible charge, shall not be required when the premises served by a refrigerating system is not normally occupied or is not in use for the conduct of business or industry, such as during nights, weekends and holidays, when closed to operations or public usage, provided, that such method of operation shall not be put into effect until written request is submitted to, and written permission has been granted by, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

1110.4 Licensed operator in responsible charge required. Except as provided in Section 1110.3 of this code, it shall be unlawful to operate a refrigerating system as specified in Section 1110 of this code without a licensed operator in responsible charge thereof possessing the required license, or a higher classification of license, for the specific refrigerating system.

1110.5 Post of duty; refrigerating systems requiring third-class refrigeration operators. The post of duty for an operator of a refrigerating system, which requires a third-class refrigeration operator as the licensed operator in responsible charge thereof, shall be on the premises where the system is located.

1110.6 Post of duty; refrigerating systems requiring second-class or first-class refrigeration operators. The post of duty for an operator of a refrigerating system, which requires a second-class or first-class refrig-

CD8:180

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-4-50

eration operator as the licensed operator in responsible charge thereof, shall be as follows:

(1) *Licensed operator in responsible charge.* The post of duty of the licensed operator in responsible charge of a refrigerating system shall be within the room or area containing such system. When he or she must also serve as attending licensed operator, his or her post of duty shall be maintained as specified in Subsection (2) of this section. When other operators, serving as attending licensed operators, are on duty under the licensed operator in responsible charge, the latter shall be on the premises but may absent himself or herself from his or her post of duty for the purpose of performing his or her regular assigned duties for reasonable periods, provided, that:

(a) The time absent is not more than two hours at a time or more than a total of four hours in any eight-hour period; and

(b) In opinion of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, his or her absence does not jeopardize the safe operation of the equipment; and

(2) *Attending licensed operator.* The post of duty of the attending licensed operator of a refrigerating system shall be within the room or area containing such system, provided, that the operator may be absent for a period of not more than 15 consecutive minutes during any one hour for the purpose of checking or adjusting parts, auxiliaries, or appurtenances of the system.

1110.7 Attending licensed operator may serve under license of licensed operator in responsible charge. An attending licensed operator of a refrigerating system who serves under the direction of the licensed operator in responsible charge may monitor the refrigerating system covered by the license of the licensed operator in responsible charge, provided, that the attending licensed operator possesses at least a Third-Class Refrigeration Operator License.

1110.8 Unapproved change in floor plan or unsuitable duty assignment. Where the floor plan of the building or structure that houses a refrigerating system and its accessories, auxiliaries, and regulating equipment is changed without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, or the assigned duties of the required licensed operating personnel are inconsistent with Section 1110 of this code, a violation may be issued and correction of the offending conditions shall be made in a manner acceptable to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

1110.9 Prohibited actions.

(a) An attending licensed operator or a licensed operator in responsible charge shall not leave his or her post of duty except as otherwise permitted in Section 1110 of this code, or relinquish his or her responsibilities for the operation of a refrigerating system to a person who is not licensed in accordance with the requirements of this code.

(b) A person having control or management of a refrigerating system shall not operate or cause to be operated such apparatus contrary to the requirements of this code, or allow or require the necessary licensed personnel to leave their post of duty except as permitted in Section 1110 of this code.

(Code 1964, §§ 2.1, 2.11, 2.15, 5.0, 5.1, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.10, 5.11; Ord. No. 706-G, § 1(2.1, 2.11, 2.15, 5.0, 5.1, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.10, 5.11), eff. 7-4-1972)

laws.title: Additions to Section 102 of 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Applicability
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 102 of the 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Applicability, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

102.10 Code requirements to be cited. Any agreement, contract, subcontract or purchase, which includes or covers any installation of plumbing or a drainage system in the City, or permanent physical connection therewith or thereto, shall clearly state that the installation and its supervision shall be in accordance with the provisions of this code.

(Code 1964, § 401.1.2; Ord. No. 256-H, § 1(401.1.2), eff. 6-23-1978)

laws.title: Additions to Section 103 of 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Department of Plumbing Inspection
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 103 of the 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Department of Plumbing Inspection, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

103.4 Duties of employees. The employees of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Plumbing Division shall perform any proper assignment of duties made by the Building Official in the administration and enforcement of this code, or any work which may demand their services in an emergency.

103.5 Restrictions for appointees, employees, and independent contractors. All appointees, employees, and independent contractors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall not engage in, or directly or indirectly be connected with, the furnishing of labor, materials, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building or structure, or the preparation of plans or of specifications therefor, unless he or she is the owner of the building or structure, or engage in any work which conflicts with his or her official duties or with the interests of the Department. Employees and independent contractors shall not make inspections or perform any other Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department responsibility on property or equipment that is wholly or partially owned by the employee or independent contractor, or by a member of the employee’s or independent contractor’s immediate family.

(Code 1964, §§ 601.7, 12-11-11.6; Code 1984, § 12-11-11.6; Ord. No. 256-H, § 1(601.7), eff. 6-23-1978; Ord. No. 290-H, § 1(12-11-11.6), eff. 11-15-1978; Ord. No. 15-88, § 1(12-11-11.6), eff. 9-21-1988)

laws.title: Application for a permit; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) Each application for a permit, along with the required fee, shall be filed with the Code Official on a form furnished for that purpose and shall contain a general description of the purposed work or location. The application shall be signed by the owner or an authorized agent. Unless authorized to do so by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, no person shall use the name of another person to obtain a permit. The permit application shall indicate the proposed occupancy of all parts of the building and of that portion of the site or lot, if any, not covered by the building or structure and shall contain the information required by the Code Official.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a permit where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

(i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

(ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

(iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

(iv) Is a financial institution with power:

A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

(a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

(b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

(c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(c) A person against whom any fee is assessed is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until payment of the outstanding fee is made to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(d) A person against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the person can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

106.3.1.1 Field information on existing premises; inapplicable to new construction; charged as special inspection service.

(a) The plumbing contractor who has been assigned, hired, or contracted with by the owner, or his or her agent, or by the lessee, of any existing premises, may request the Plumbing Division to send an inspector or supervisor to the job after an information permit has been obtained. The inspector shall review the conditions of the structure or premises and submit a report to the plumbing contractor regarding the proposal. Where the plumbing contractor desires a variance from this code regarding his or her proposal, he or she may file an appeal to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Board of Appeals for Construction.

(b) The information permit and service therefor are not applicable to new construction for which plans are filed with, and accepted by, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(c) An information inspection, which by its nature is not an installation inspection, shall be classified as a special inspection service and shall be charged in accordance with Section 107.2.2.1 of this code.

laws.title: Fraudulent application for permit illegal
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for any person to present any fraudulent information in making application for any permit from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. Furthermore, it shall be unlawful to use the name of another person in order to secure a permit unless proper legal authorization is granted by the person whose name is used by his or her agent.

laws.title: Prior approval of certain plans and specifications required
laws.content: Prior to submission to the Building Official, plans and specifications that involve new connections to the public sewer, public water main, or both, shall be approved by the Water and Sewerage Department.

laws.title: Notification of quitting installation required
laws.content: Where a plumbing contractor, to whom a permit has been issued for an installation and inspection of plumbing or a drainage system, quits the installation for any reason, he or she shall provide notification of the action to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in the form of a letter that he or she has signed and dated in the presence of a notary public.

laws.title: Inspection of partially completed installation required upon plumbing contractor quitting
laws.content: Where an installation has been partially completed, the plumbing contractor to whom a permit has been issued shall notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department upon quitting the installation and request an inspection. Acceptance of, or violations against, the work installed shall be recorded by the inspector on the permit record according to his or her findings. No refund shall be granted to the plumbing contractor of the fee paid for the permit.

laws.title: Inspection of partially completed installation where plumbing contractor fails to notify Department of quitting or is terminated by owner
Transfer of permit from plumbing contractor to plumbing contractor
laws.content:
(a) Where the original permit holder gives written permission through a notarized letter, the permit shall be transferred, upon approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, to the latter plumbing contractor, provided, that a transfer fee is paid. The transfer of the permit by the original permit holder does not transfer any pending criminal charge to the new permit holder.

(b) Where permission is not granted by the original permit holder, the plumbing contractor who completes the installation shall secure a permit covering the work he or she is to do, and the latter contractor shall be responsible for work done under his or her supervision as well as proper and satisfactory operation of the entire plumbing or drainage system done by either or both of the contractors.

106.6 Establishment and approval of fees; payment required before work begins.

(a) In accordance with Sections 10(1) and 22(1) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1510(1) and 125.1522(1), and Section 9-507 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of permits, inspections, re-inspections, certificates, appeals, and other fees that are required by the 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code and by Chapter 8, Article V, of 2019 Detroit City Code, Plumbing Code. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs that are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) The fees prescribed by this section shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department before a permit to begin work for new construction, alteration, or other building operation may be issued. In addition, an amendment to a permit necessitating an additional fee shall not be approved until the additional fee is paid.

106.6.4 Fee for failure to obtain permit before starting work. Any person who shall commence installation of any plumbing or any drainage system for which a permit is required by this code, without first having obtained a permit, shall pay, if legally authorized and subsequently allowed to obtain a permit, in addition to the permit fee specified by this code for such installation, a supplemental inspection fee to cover the cost of the services rendered by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that:

(1) A supplemental inspection fee is not required for emergency work or installation when proved to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, or the Detroit Health Department, that such work or installation was urgently necessary, and would have been impractical to have awaited the time required for application and issuance of the permit; and

(2) In such an emergency, the required permit shall be obtained without unreasonable delay after installation starts, but not later than 72 hours while the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is open for business, or a supplemental inspection fee shall be charged in addition to the permit fee.

106.6.5 Fee refunds. laws.title: Types of buildings and structures requiring an annual Certificate of Plumbing Inspection
laws.content: All buildings and structures, including those used for public assembly, schools, halls, clubs, armories, theatres, sports arenas, auditoriums, office buildings, buildings used or designed for manufacturing or commercial purposes, hotels, hospitals, jails, prisons, convalescent homes, orphanages, homes for the aged, apartment houses, rooming houses, parking decks, garages, passenger stations, and all other buildings occupied or used by large numbers of persons or which use water for processing or manufacturing or which create and discharge to the drainage system noxious, toxic, harmful, hazardous, or deleterious industrial or commercial wastes shall be required to have a Certificate of Plumbing Inspection.

laws.title: Annual Inspection and Certification
laws.content:
The Building Official shall cause, as nearly as possible, all buildings and structures of the types mentioned in Section 107.1.1 of this code to be inspected annually by the Plumbing Division for compliance with this code. After inspection, the Plumbing Division shall notify the owner, the agent of the owner, lessee, occupant, or other person legally responsible for maintenance of the building or structure of any violation of this code, and shall apply all legal measures necessary to effect reasonable compliance. Following inspection, the Licenses and Permits Division shall submit an invoice covering the fee for issuance of a Certification of Plumbing Inspection as prescribed in Section 106.6 of this code to the owner, agent of owner, lessee, tenant, occupant, or other person responsible for maintenance of the building or structure.

After a building or structure is found to comply with the provisions of this code, and after receipt of payment of the fee for issuance of a Certification of Plumbing Inspection as prescribed in Section 106.6 of this code, the Licenses and Permits Division shall issue a Certificate of Plumbing Inspection to the owner, or his agent, the lessee, or manager of the premises. Upon receipt of the Certificate, the owner, or his agent, the lessee, or manager of the building or structure shall post and maintain the Certificate in a conspicuous place within the building or structure.

laws.title: Inspection requests
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of the holder of the permit or their duly authorized agent to notify the Code Official when work is ready for inspection. It shall be the duty of the permit holder to provide access to and means for inspections of such work that are required by this code. Unless the holder of the permit proves to the satisfaction of the Code Official that inability to have the installation ready for inspection was due to unforeseen or unusual circumstances, which demonstrate no willful negligence or carelessness on the part of the holder of the permit or his or her workers, the holder of the permit shall pay a fee for re-inspection of the work as prescribed in Section 106.6 of this code.

laws.title: Special inspection service
laws.content: Where an installation, or part thereof, of any plumbing or drainage system necessitates the presence of a plumbing inspector for extended periods of time or at frequent intervals during the installation process in order to ensure that proper inspection is made, the permittee shall be charged for a special service. Where the original cost of the permit is insufficient to cover the cost of the special inspection service, the fee for the service shall be based on the hourly rate as established under Section 106.6 of this code.

laws.title: Pre-approval for overtime inspection
laws.content: Pre-approval of overtime inspection shall be obtained for all services provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours.

laws.title: Approval required
laws.content: Work shall not be done beyond the point indicated in each successive inspection without first obtaining the approval of the Code Official. The Code Official, upon notification, shall make the requested inspections and shall either indicate the portion of the construction that is satisfactory as completed, or notify the permit holder or his or her agent wherein the same fails to comply with the code. Any portions that do not comply shall be corrected and such portion shall not be covered or concealed until authorized by the Code Official. Where any plumbing or drainage system, or part thereof, which is installed, altered, or repaired, is covered before being inspected, tested and approved, as prescribed in this code, it shall be uncovered for inspection after notice to uncover the work has been issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to the responsible person, firm, or corporation.

laws.title: Suspension and revocation
laws.content:
The Code Official is authorized to, in writing, suspend or revoke a Certificate of Approval issued under the provisions of this code whenever the notice is issued in error, or on the basis of incorrect information supplied, or where it is determined that the building or structure, premise or portion thereof is in violation of any provisions of this code or of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

(Code 1964, §§ 501.3, 501.4, 501.6, 601.9.1, 601.9.3, 602.6, 602.7; Ord. No. 256-H, § 1(501.3, 501.4, 501.6, 601.9.1, 601.9.3, 602.6, 602.7), eff. 6-23-1978; Ord. No. 471-H, § 1(601.9.3), eff. 4-14-1982)

laws.title: Unlawful employment, hiring, and subcontracting
laws.content: It is unlawful to employ, hire, or subcontract with any person, firm, or corporation other than through a licensed plumbing contractor to install, or supervise the installation of, plumbing or a drainage system within the City.

laws.title: Unlawful for plumbing contractor to transfer responsibility
laws.content: It is unlawful for any licensed plumbing contractor who agrees to, or is hired to install, or who contracts, or subcontracts to install any plumbing or drainage system in the City to transfer the duties and responsibilities for such work, for securing any permit, and for requesting inspection of any installation either to the person with whom he or she has contracted to install the plumbing or drainage system or to any subcontractor.

laws.title: Unlawful for plumbing contractor to fail to register or show Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
It is unlawful for any plumbing contractor who is in the act of supervising, installing, or receiving an inspection of plumbing or drainage system work, except an owner who is working under a permit in his or her own residence, to fail to carry a Certificate of Registration that is required under Section 111 of this code, or to show such Certificate when requested to do so by a City inspector, engineer, or police officer.

CD8:190

laws.title: Unlawful for master plumber, journey plumber, or apprentice to not carry credentials
laws.content:
(a) Any person who as licensed by the state as a master plumber or a journey plumber shall carry his or her current state license, while employed or engaged in the task of supervising the installation of plumbing or a drainage system within the City.

(b) Any person who as registered by the state as an apprentice plumber shall carry his or her current state registration, while engaged in learning and assisting in the installation of plumbing or a drainage system under the direct on-site jobsite supervision of a master plumber or a journey plumber within the City.

laws.title: Unlawful for master plumber or journey plumber to misrepresent status of apprentice plumber
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for a master plumber or a journey plumber while employing an apprentice plumber to represent the apprentice plumber as a licensed master plumber or a licensed journey plumber.

laws.title: Failure to comply within 72 hours of issuance of Notice of Violation
Failure to comply within 35 days of issuance of Notice of Violation
laws.content: Where a Notice of Violation is issued for any provision of this code that is not delineated in Section 108.2.2 of this code, including one which requires issuance of a permit under Section 108.2.2(1) of this code and, upon investigation, the Plumbing Division determines that compliance has not been made within 35 days after issuance of the Notice of Violation, the owner and the permit holder may be issued a misdemeanor violation.

laws.title: Prosecution of violation
laws.content:
Where a Notice of Violation or order is not complied with by the date specified therein or by the date specified in any extension that is granted for no longer than 28 days, the Code Official is authorized to request that the Corporation Counsel:

(1) Represent the City plumbing inspector in the prosecution of the misdemeanor ordinance violation that has been filed with the court; or

(2) Institute the appropriate proceedings at law or in equity to restrain, correct or abate such violation, or to require the removal or termination of the unlawful occupancy of the building or structure in violation of the provisions of this code or of the order or direction made pursuant thereto.

laws.title: Violation penalties; separate offenses; retention of fines by City
laws.content:
(a) A person who violates a provision of this code, who fails to conform with any of the requirements thereof, or who erects, installs, alters, or repairs any plumbing work, or any drainage system, in violation of the approved construction documents or directive of the enforcing agency, or a per-

CD8:191
§ 8-5-8

DETROIT CITY CODE

mit or certificate issued under the provisions of this code shall be assessed a fine in accordance with Subsections (b) and (c) of this section.

R 408.30718

(b) In accordance with Section 49 of the State Plumbing Act, being MCL 338.3559, a person licensed or registered under the act who commits a violation of the act, or a person not licensed or registered under the act who is performing any activity regulated by the act and is not exempt from licensure or registration under the act, is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than $1,000.00 per day for each day the violation occurs, provided, that a fine shall not exceed $5,000.00 in total per violation or punishable by imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or both.

(c) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, upon conviction, all other persons who are not governed by Subsection (b) of this section shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court. Each day that the violation continues, or is permitted to exist, without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable, upon conviction, in the manner prescribed by this subsection.

(d) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, as the administrating and enforcing agency that prosecutes a violation of this code, the City shall retain any fine that is imposed upon conviction.

108.5 Stop work orders. Notice shall be in accordance with this act. A person who is served with a stop work order, except for work that the person is directed to perform to remove a violation or unsafe condition, is subject to the penalty provisions prescribed in Section 108.4 of this code. laws.title: Additions to Section 109 of 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Means of Appeal
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 109 of the 2015 Michigan Plumbing Code, Means of Appeal, the following provision, which was contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

109.1 Means of appeal.
