laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 105 of the 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, Permits, the following provision, which was contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concerns administration and enforcement:

[A] 105.3 Application for permit; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions.

(a) To obtain a permit, the applicant shall first file an application therefor in writing on a form furnished by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for that purpose. Such application shall:

1. Identify and describe the work in accordance with Chapter 3 to be covered by the permit for which application is made.

2. Describe the land on which the proposed work is to be done by legal description, street address, or similar description that will readily identify and definitely locate the proposed building or work.

3. Indicate the use and occupancy for which the proposed work is intended.

4. Be accompanied by construction documents and other information as required in Section 106.3.

5. State the valuation of the proposed work.

6. Be signed by the applicant, or the applicant’s authorized agent.

7. Give such other data and information as required by the code official.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a permit where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

(i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

(ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

(iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

(a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(c) A person against whom any fee is assessed is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until payment of the outstanding fee is made to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(d) A person against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the person can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

[A] 105.3.1 Action on application. The Code Official shall examine, or cause to be examined, applications for permits and amendments thereto within a reasonable time after filing. If the application or the construction documents do not conform to the requirements of pertinent laws, the Code Official shall reject such application in writing, stating the reasons therefor. If, based upon the approval of all applicable building inspectors through the affixing of their respective signatures on the application, the Code Official is satisfied that the proposed work conforms to the requirements of this code, other state construction codes and laws and the 2019 Detroit City Code applicable thereto, the Code Official shall issue a permit therefor as soon as practicable.

**Sec. 8-6-7. Additions to Section 106 of 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, Construction Documents.**

In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 106 of the 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, *Construction Documents*, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

**106.1 Submittal of documents.** Construction documents, special inspection and structural observation programs, investigation and evaluation reports, and other data shall be submitted in three sets with each application for a permit. The construction documents shall be prepared by, or under the direct supervision of, a registered design professional when required by 1980 P.A. 299, MCL 339.101 to 339.2721. When special conditions exist, the Building Official is authorized to require additional construction documents to be prepared by a registered design professional.

*Exception:* The Building Official is authorized to waive the submission of construction documents and other data not required to be prepared by a registered design professional if it is found that the nature of the work applied for is such that reviewing of construction documents is not necessary to obtain compliance with this code.

R 408.30562

**106.3.1 Approval of construction documents.** When the Code Official issues a permit, the construction documents shall be approved, in writing or by stamp, as "Reviewed for Code Compliance." One set of the three sets of construction documents so reviewed shall be retained by the Code Official. The second and third sets shall be returned to the applicant. The second set shall be kept by the applicant at the work site, and be open to inspection by the Code Official or a duly authorized representative while the third set shall be retained by the applicant for his or her records.

**Sec. 8-6-8. Additions to Section 108 of 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, Fees.**

In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 108 of the 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, *Fees*, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

**108.1 Establishment and approval of fees; payment of fees required before work begins.**

(a) In accordance with Sections 10(1) and 22(1) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1510(1) and 125.1522(1), and Section 9-507 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of appeals, certificates, permits, inspections, re-inspections, and other fees that are required by the 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings and by Chapter 8, Article VI, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings*. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs that are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

laws.content: Except for a permit that is fraudulently obtained, a permit that is issued under the provisions of this article may be canceled by the Building Official on the written request from the holder of such permit, provided, that such request is made within 180 days from the date of issuance of the permit and prior to any inspection or other action taken under the permit, including any exercise of privileges granted by the permit. laws.content:
Any person who commences work for which a permit is required by this code, without first having obtained a permit, shall pay, if legally authorized and subsequently allowed to obtain a permit, in addition to the permit fee specified by this code for such installation, a supplemental inspection fee to cover the cost of the services rendered by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that this requirement shall not apply to emergency work or installation when proved to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that such work or installation was urgently necessary, and would have been impractical to have awaited the time required for application and issuance of the permit, provided further, that, even in such emergencies, the required permit shall be obtained without unreasonable delay after installation starts, and in no case more than three days during which the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is open for business, or a supplemental inspection fee shall be charged in addition to the permit fee.

laws.title: Notice of violation
laws.content: The Code Official is authorized to serve, via first class mail, a Notice of Violation or order on the person responsible for the repair, alteration, extension, addition, moving, removal, demolition, or change in the occupancy of a building in violation of the provisions of this code, or in violation of a permit or certificate issued under the provisions of this code. Such order shall direct the discontinuance of the illegal action or condition and the abatement of the violation.

laws.title: Prosecution of violation
laws.content:
(a) Where a Notice of Violation or order is not complied with by the date specified therein or by the date specified in any extension that is granted for no longer than 28 days, the Code Official is authorized to request that the Corporation Counsel:

(1) Represent the City building inspector in the prosecution of the misdemeanor ordinance violation that has been filed with the court; or

(2) Institute the appropriate proceedings at law or in equity to restrain,

correct, or abate such violation, or to require the removal or termination of the unlawful occupancy of the building or structure in violation of the provisions of this code or of the order or direction made pursuant thereto.

(b) The total elapsed time from issuance of the Notice of Violation or order to the filing of a misdemeanor ordinance violation shall not exceed six months.

113.4. Violation penalties.

(a) It is unlawful for any person, partnership, firm, or corporation to violate a provision of this code or fail to conform with any of the requirements thereof, or erect, construct, alter, extend, repair, move, remove, demolish, or occupy any building, structure, or equipment regulated by this code, or cause work to be performed or done in conflict with or in violation of the approved construction documents or directive of the Code Official, or a permit or certificate issued under this code.

(b) A violator shall be assessed a fine in accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, and, upon conviction, shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court. Each day that the violation continues, or is permitted to exist, without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable, upon conviction, in the manner prescribed by this subsection.

R 408.30571

(c) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, as the administrating and enforcing agency that prosecutes a violation of this code, the City shall retain any fine that is imposed upon conviction.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content: Every registrant shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of address that was provided under Section 118.4 of this code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
(a) Commensurate with the expiration date of their state license under Section 2404(5) of the Michigan Occupational Code, being MCL 339.2404(5), each Certificate of Registration as a residential builder or a residential maintenance and alteration contractor shall expire on the termination of the three-year cycle of their license.

(b) An application for renewal of a Certificate of Registration shall be made on a form furnished for such purpose by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and be accompanied with the correct fee. Proper submission of a renewal application shall grant said applicant permission to operate within the City of Detroit unless the Certificate of Registration is deemed void under Section 118.8 of this code.

laws.title: Certification of Registration deemed void; unlawful to perform or arrange performance of work
laws.content:
(a) Where a Residential Builder License or a Residential Maintenance and Alteration Contractor License that is issued by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs expires, or is suspended or revoked by the Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs, the Certificate of Registration issued under Section 118 of this code is deemed void and the holder thereof shall not engage in the business, or act in the capacity, of a residential builder or a residential maintenance and alteration contractor.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any individual, partnership, firm, or corporation whose Certificate of Registration is void to install, alter, or service equipment requiring such Certificate of Registration for its performance, or to arrange for the performance of such work on a contractual basis.

laws.title: Addition to Section 1301 of 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, General
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section 1301 of the 2015 Michigan Rehabilitation Code for Existing Buildings, General, the following provision, which was contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concerns administration and enforcement:

1301.2 Conformance. Buildings and structures moved into or within the jurisdiction shall comply with the provisions of Chapter 8, Article XIV, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Moving of Buildings and Structures. The building shall be safe for human occupancy as determined by Chapter 18, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Detroit Fire Prevention and Protection Code, and Chapter 8, Article XV, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Property Maintenance Code. Any repair, alteration, or change of occupancy undertaken within the moved building or structure shall comply with the requirements of this code applicable to work being performed. Any field-fabricated elements shall comply with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article II, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Building Code, or Chapter 8, Article VII, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Residential Code, as applicable.

(Code 1964, § 12-11-42; Code 1984, § 12-11-42; Ord. No. 290-H, § 1(12-11-42), eff. 11-15-1978; Ord. No. 15-88, § 1(12-11-42), eff. 9-21-1988)

laws.title: Additions to Section R103 of 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Department of Building Safety
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section R103 of the 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Department of Building Safety, the following provision, which was contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concerns administration and enforcement:

R103.2 Restrictions for appointees, employees, and independent contractors. All appointees, employees, and independent contractors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental

Department shall not engage in, or directly or indirectly be connected with, the furnishing of labor, materials, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building or structure, or the preparation of plans or of specifications therefor, unless he or she is the owner of the building or structure, or engage in any work which conflicts with his or her official duties or with the interests of the Department. Employees and independent contractors shall not make inspections or perform any other Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department responsibility on property or equipment that is wholly or partially owned by the employee or independent contractor, or by a member of the employee’s or independent contractor’s immediate family.

laws.title: Additions to Section R104 of 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Duties and Powers of the Building Official
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section R104 of the 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Duties and Powers of the Building Official, the following provision, which was contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concerns administration and enforcement:

R104.5 Identification with official badge. The Building Official shall cause to be issued for him or herself and all building inspectors a badge of office, which shall be carried and displayed as proper identification when inspecting structures or premises in the performance of duties under this code.

laws.title: R105.3 Application for permit; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) To obtain a permit, the applicant shall first file an application therefor in writing on a form furnished by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for that purpose. Such application shall:

1. Identify and describe the work to be covered by the permit for which application is made.

2. Describe the land on which the proposed work is to be done by legal description, street address, or similar description that will readily identify and definitely locate the proposed building or work.

3. Indicate the use and occupancy for which the proposed work is intended.

4. Be accompanied by construction documents and other information as required in Section R106.1.

5. State the valuation of the proposed work.

6. Be signed by the applicant, or the applicant's authorized agent.

7. Give such other data and information as required by the building official.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a permit where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

R105.3.1 Action on application. The Building Official shall examine, or cause to be examined, applications for permits and amendments thereto within a reasonable time after filing. If the application or the construction documents do not conform to the requirements of pertinent laws, the Building Official shall reject such application in writing, stating the reasons therefor. If, based upon the approval of all applicable building inspectors through the affixing of their respective signatures on the application, the Building Official is satisfied that the proposed work conforms to the requirements of this code, other state construction codes and laws and the 2019 Detroit City Code applicable thereto, the Building Official shall issue a permit therefor as soon as practicable.

laws.title: Additions to Section R106 of 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Construction Documents
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section R106 of the 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Construction Documents, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

R106.1 Submittal documents. Construction documents, special inspection and structural program and other data shall be submitted in three sets with each application for a permit. The construction documents shall be prepared by, or under the direct supervision of, a registered design professional when required by 1980 PA 299, MCL 339.101 to 339.2919 and known as the Michigan Occupational Code. Where special conditions exist, the Building Official may require additional construction documents to be prepared by a registered design professional.

R106.3.1 Approval of construction documents. When the Building Official issues a permit, the construction documents shall be approved in writing or by stamp, which states "REVIEWED FOR CODE COMPLIANCE." laws.title: R108.1 Establishment and approval of fees; payment of fees required before work begins
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Sections 10(1) and 22(1) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1510(1) and 125.1522(1), and Section 9-507 of the 2012 Detroit City Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of appeals, certificates, permits, inspections, re-inspections, and other fees that are required by the 2015 Michigan Residential Code and by Chapter 8, Article VII, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Residential Code. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs that are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) The fees prescribed in this section shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department before a permit to begin work for new construction, alteration, removal, demolition, or other building operation may be issued. In addition, an amendment to a permit necessitating an additional fee shall not be approved until the additional fee is paid.

R 408.30508

laws.title: R108.7 Fee refunds
laws.content: Except for a permit that is fraudulently obtained, the holder of a permit that is issued under this code may make a written request that the Building Official cancel the permit, provided, that such request is made within six months from the date of issuance of the permit and prior to any inspection or other action taken under the permit, including the exercise of any privilege granted by the permit. Where the permit is canceled, the City Treasurer, upon notification in writing from the Building Official, shall make a refund of 80 percent of all fees paid in connection with the issuance of such unused permit.

laws.title: R108.8 Fee for failure to obtain permit before starting work
laws.content:
Any person who commences work for which a permit is required by this code, without first having obtained a permit, shall pay, if legally authorized and subsequently allowed to obtain a permit, in addition to the permit fee specified by this code for such installation, a supplemental inspection fee to cover the cost of the services rendered by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, provided, that this requirement shall not apply to emergency work or installation when proved to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that such work or installation was urgently necessary, and would have been impractical to have awaited the time required for application and issuance of the permit, provided further, that, even in such emergencies, the required permit shall be obtained without unreasonable delay after installation starts, and in no case more than three days during which the Buildings,

R109.1.6 Final inspection. Final inspection shall be made after the permitted work is complete and prior to occupancy. Confirmation of completion of work under the permit is validated by the issuance of a Certificate of Approval.

laws.title: Additions to Section R113 of 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Violations
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 8b(11) of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1508b(11), the City adds to Section R113 of the 2015 Michigan Residential Code, Violations, the following provisions, which were contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code prior to July 31, 2001, and concern administration and enforcement:

R113.2 Notice of violation. The Building Official is authorized to serve, via first class mail, a notice of violation or order on the person responsible for the erection, construction, alteration, extension, repair, moving, removal, demolition or occupancy of a building or structure in violation of the provisions of this code, or in violation of a detailed statement or a plan approved thereunder, or in violation of a permit or certificate issued under the provisions of this code. Such order shall direct the discontinuance of the illegal action or condition and the abatement of the violation.

R113.3 Prosecution of violation.

(a) Where a Notice of Violation or order is not complied with by the date specified therein or by the date specified in any extension that is granted for no longer than 28 days, the Building Official is authorized to request that the Corporation Counsel:

(1) Represent the City building inspector in the prosecution of the misdemeanor ordinance violation that has been filed with the court; or

(2) Institute the appropriate proceedings at law or in equity to restrain, correct, or abate such violation, or to require the removal or termination of the unlawful occupancy of the building or structure in violation of the provisions of this code or of the order or direction made pursuant thereto.

(b) The total elapsed time from issuance of the Notice of Violation or order to the filing of a misdemeanor ordinance violation shall not exceed six months.

R113.4. Violation penalties.

(a) It is unlawful for any person, partnership, firm, or corporation to violate a provision of the code or fail to conform with any of the requirements thereof, or erect, construct, alter, extend, repair, move, remove, demolish, or occupy any building, structure, or equipment regulated by the code, or cause work to be performed or done, in conflict with or in violation of the approved construction documents or directive of Building Official, or a permit or certificate issued under this code.

(b) A violator shall be assessed a fine in accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, and, upon conviction, shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court. Each day that the violation continues, or is permitted to exist, without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable, upon conviction, in the manner prescribed by this subsection.

R 408.30511

(c) In accordance with Section 23 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1523, as the administrating and enforcing agency that prosecutes a violation of this code, the City shall retain any fine that is imposed upon conviction.

(Code 1964, §§ 12-11-6.1, 12-11-26.2, 12-11-26.3, 12-11-26.4, 12-11-45; Code 1984, §§ 12-11-26.3, 12-11-26.4; Ord. No. 290-H, § 1(12-11-6.1, 12-11-26.3, 12-11-26.4, 12-11-45), eff. 11-15-1978; Ord. No. 23-85, § 1(12-11-26.3), eff. 6-14-1985; Ord. No. 15-88, § 1(12-11-26.4), eff. 9-21-1988)

laws.title: Existing elevator installations; alteration requirements
laws.content:
(a) Where in good repair, existing elevator installations, including solid bumpers, may be continued in their present state, provided, that the installation does not present an apparent safety hazard due to the method of installation, its operation, or its design.

(b) Where an alteration is proposed or made, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to require that such alteration be made in accordance with the ASME Code and this article. The Department is authorized to prohibit any alteration where the alteration is not practical due to cost or creates a hazardous condition, or to require other alterations as the Department deems necessary for the safe operation of such altered equipment.

(c) Where, in the opinion of the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or his or her designee, an existing installation is found to be in a dangerous condition, or where the design or method of operation in combination with devices used is considered inherently dangerous, or where there is an immediate hazard to those riding on or using such equipment, the Department shall make or order such tests or inspections as are deemed necessary to determine the condition of the equipment and to administratively issue written orders for any alteration or addition as are deemed necessary to eliminate any existing dangerous condition.

(Code 1964, § 1.3; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(1.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Application of other codes and requirements
laws.content: Unless otherwise specified in this article, additions, alterations, and repairs to all elevators, escalators, dumbwaiters and moving walks, including their hoistways and associated spaces, and platform lifts and stairway chairlifts, as required, installed, and used in all structures and premises within the City of Detroit covered by this article shall be done in accordance with the applicable rules promulgated pursuant to Section 4 of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1504.

laws.title: Electric Elevators: Five-Year Test, Only One Elevator on Standby Power Supply
laws.content: As outlined in Item 1.17.2.1 of this code, have the elevator placed on standby power. Place the rated load on the elevator (125 percent rated load for passenger elevators that are permitted to carry passengers) and operate the elevator observing for safe operation. Use a tachometer in the machine room to verify that the overhauling load does not cause a speed increase in excess of 125 percent of rated speed or the governor tripping speed.

laws.title: Electric Elevators: Five-Year Test, More Than One Elevator Operating Simultaneously on Standby Power Supply
laws.content: Have the elevators placed on standby power supply operation and loaded with the rated load (125 percent rated load for passenger elevators and freight elevators that are permitted to carry passengers) and operate all of the elevators simultaneously while observing that they operate normally and will safely lower, stop, and hold. Use a tachometer to check the speed of each elevator when operating simultaneously in both directions. Verify that each elevator stops at or near the terminal landing and before the final terminal stopping device operated. The speed should not exceed 125 percent of the rated speed or the governor tripping speed.

laws.title: Hydraulic Elevators: Five-Year Test, Only One Elevator on Standby Power Supply
laws.content: As outlined in Item 1.17.2.2 of this code, have the elevator placed on standby power. Place the rated load on the elevator (100 percent rated load for passenger elevators that are permitted to carry passengers) and operate the elevator observing for safe operation. Use a tachometer to verify that the rated load does not cause a speed increase.

laws.title: Hydraulic Elevators: Five-Year Test, More Than One Elevator Operating Simultaneously on Standby Power Supply
laws.content:
Have the elevators placed on standby power supply operation and loaded with the rated load (100 percent rated load for passenger elevators and freight elevators that are permitted to carry passengers) and operate all of the elevators simultaneously observing that they operate normally and will safely lower, stop, and hold. Use a tachometer to check the speed of each elevator when operating simultaneously in both directions and to verify that the rated load does not cause a speed increase.

laws.title: Authorization and enforcement; issuance of notices, orders, and violations; conflict of interest
laws.content:
(a) The Building Official, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, through designated local officials, is authorized to administer and enforce the provisions of this article.

(b) In accordance with state law and the prescribed procedures of the City, the Building Official shall have the authority to designate inspectors who are authorized to enforce and to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article, to conduct inspections and re-inspections, and to issue and serve upon a person a written notice, order, or violation where the authorized local official has reasonable cause to believe that there has been a violation of this article.

(c) A City official or employee who is connected with the enforcement of this article shall not engage in, or directly or indirectly be connected with, the furnishing of labor, materials or appliances for the construction, alteration or maintenance of an elevator, escalator, or any associated equipment, unless that person is the owner of the building, premises or structure, or is engaged in any work that conflicts with official duties or with the interests of the City.

laws.title: Right of entry for inspection
laws.content:
(a) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this article, the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner or an authorized agent of the owner of any building in the City where any equipment covered under this article is installed, or any building, premises or structure that is owned, operated, and/or maintained by the City, shall permit and assist the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or any designated inspector of the Department, to enter the building to make inspections of any equipment during reasonable hours, subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures.

(b) Where access to the location of equipment covered under this article is denied by the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment, or where

CD8:236

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-9-29

access is otherwise not obtained, the Department may pursue recourse, as provided by law, to conduct an investigation pursuant to this article. Accordingly, the holder of the Certificate of Registration, or the owner of the equipment, shall be responsible for making arrangements for access to the site and equipment, including review of surveillance video, to facilitate the completion of any inspection.

(Code 1964, § 4.0; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Holder of Certificate of Registration or owner of equipment to notify City of accident
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment, shall notify the Department within one business day after receiving a report of an accident as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code.

(b) Upon reasonable notice from the Department, the holder of the Certificate of Registration, or the owner of the equipment, shall provide the Department access to facilitate an investigation of the equipment that was involved in the accident as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 6.1; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(6.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Accident inspection
laws.content: Upon notification of the Department of an accident, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, by the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or owner of such equipment, an inspection shall be made of the equipment.

laws.title: Unlawful to use equipment following accident until approval
laws.content:
Where an accident, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, involves the failure, breakage, damage, or destruction of any part of the apparatus or mechanism of the device that affects the safe operation of the equipment, it shall be unlawful to repair or service, or use, the equipment until after an investigation, inspection and approval by a designated inspector of the Department for the continued use of such equipment.

(Code 1964, § 6.2; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(6.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Interference with Department inspection personnel as violation
laws.content:
Any person who shall refuse to comply with or who shall assist in the violation of any of the provisions of this article, or who, in any manner hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents or in any manner interferes with the inspection personnel of the Department, including the failure to permit a designated inspector of the Department to perform his or her duty by refusing entrance to a building or place at reasonable hours for the purpose of enforcement of this article, shall be deemed in violation of this article and subject to the penalties that are contained in Section 8-9-28 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 8.1; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(8.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Violations; penalties
laws.content:
(a) Any person, or anyone acting on behalf of a person, who violates any provision of this article shall be subject, upon conviction thereof, to a fine of not more than $500.00, or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

(b) Each day that a violation of this article continues or is permitted to exist without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable upon conviction in the manner prescribed in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1964, § 8.0; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(8.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Appeals from decisions, determinations, or orders; exception
laws.content:
(a) An interested person, or the person’s authorized agent, aggrieved by a decision, determination, or order of the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this code, which refuses to grant an application for a permit or makes any other decision pursuant or related to this code, may appeal in writing for a variance to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Board of Appeals for Construction*. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the code or the rules governing construction have been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of the code do not apply, or an equal or better form of construction is proposed. As provided for in Section 8-1-15 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, the decision of the Board of Appeals is final and neither the City nor the applicant may appeal the decision.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a variance where the person, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(Code 1964, § 1.4; Code 1984, § 9-2-5; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(1.4), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 24-16, § 1(9-2-5), eff. 8-1-2016)

laws.title: Subdivision A. Permits
laws.content:
**Sec. 8-9-41. Permit required; emergency alterations; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions; application; exceptions.**

(a) No person shall construct, install, alter, or decommission any elevator, escalator, dumbwaiter or moving walk, including their hoistways and associated spaces, or any platform lift or stairway chairlift, covered under this article in any structure or premises within the City without first having obtained a permit from the Department for such construction, installation, alteration or decommission, provided, that, in the case of any emergency alteration, the required permit for the work shall be obtained within 72 hours from the time of the emergency alteration.

(b) A permit that is required by this section may be issued only to a person licensed by the Department as an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor pursuant to this article upon the filing of a permit application on a form approved by the Department.

(c) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor is not eligible to apply for a permit where the an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(d) An unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor against whom any fee is assessed is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until payment of the outstanding fee is made to the Department.

(e) An unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the unlimited-elevator contractor or limited-elevator contractor can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

(f) An application for a permit shall include plans and specifications that provide details for the proposed construction or alteration and the payment of the applicable permit fee.

(g) Payment of the required permit fee shall include no more than two inspections, which shall include a final inspection. Failure to cancel a scheduled final inspection with appropriate notice to the Department, or where the designated inspector of the Department determines that circumstances prevent the inspection, shall result in an additional inspection fee.

(h) Where the device to be constructed or altered pursuant to the permit is not completed in accordance with this article, the unlimited-elevator contractor or the limited-elevator contractor shall be responsible for the payment of any follow-up inspection or inspections fees.

(i) Ordinary repairs and replacements may be made in accordance with the provisions of this article without the filing of a permit application with the Department.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.0, 602.7; Code 1984, § 9-2-5; Ord. No. 256-H, § 1(602.7), eff. 6-23-1978; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.0), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 24-16, § 1(9-2-5), eff. 8-1-2016)

laws.title: Contractor license required for the issuance of permits and to perform work
laws.content:
(a) Permits issued under this subdivision shall be issued by the Department only to a person licensed by the Department as an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor.

(b) No person, except an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the Department, shall be allowed to enter into a contract to maintain, repair, adjust, inspect, or decommission elevators or devices covered under this article. Such licenses shall be issued by the Department to qualified applicants in accordance with Subdivision B of this division.

(c) No person shall be issued a permit for the construction, installation, or alteration of any equipment covered under this article unless all prior fees for permits, Certificates of Registration for an Elevator, and inspections including overtime have been paid to the City.

(Code 1964, § 3.1; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Payment of fees for permits and inspections
laws.content:
Any fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-9-21 of this Code for the issuance of a permit, or for a required inspection, under this subdivision shall be paid to the Department at the time that the permit is issued or the inspection is made. Where the fee is paid by check or money order, it shall be made payable to the "Treasurer, City of Detroit."

CD8:240

laws.title: License required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) All installation, inspection, maintenance, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting, testing or decommission of any elevators, including their hoistways and associated spaces, and other equipment covered by this article, shall be arranged by an individual who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator contractor.

(b) All installation, alteration, maintenance, repair, servicing, adjusting, testing, and removal of platform lifts and stairway chairlifts only under this article shall be arranged by an individual who is licensed by the City as a limited-elevator contractor.

the limited-elevator journeyperson regularly employed by the applicant to supervise all contract work, to engage in the work of installation, alteration, repair, servicing and maintenance of elevating devices in the City in accordance with this article.

(e) Where a license has been issued based upon the qualifications of a limited-elevator journeyperson regularly employed by the applicant, the termination of employment of such regular employee shall act as an immediate suspension of such a license until the applicant is again qualified in accordance with the provisions of this article, provided, that a 30-day period may be allowed for the employer, with the approval of the Department, to replace him or her by another qualified individual. The Department shall be notified, in writing, by both the employed limited-elevator journeyperson and the employer when such termination of employment takes place.

(Code 1964, § 3.2; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Investigation required to confirm no City tax or assessment in arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by Section 8-9-51 of this Code shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessment are unpaid, outstanding, or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon compliance with either Section 8-9-52 or Section 8-9-53 of this Code, and with Section 8-9-54 of this Code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue an Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License to the applicant.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual.

(c) An unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor shall not allow his or her license to be used by any other individual.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content: Every holder of an Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided either under Section 8-9-52 of this Code or under Section 8-9-53 of this Code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of contractor licenses; work prohibited where license expired or revoked
laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of an Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division prior to January 1st in each year.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or Limited-Elevator Contractor License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation as an unlimited-elevator contractor or a limited-elevator contractor until such time that the renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) An Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License that is issued under Section 8-9-55 of this Code shall expire on December

CD8:243
§ 8-9-57

DETROIT CITY CODE

31st following the issuance of the license and, where not renewed 60 days after the date of expiration, the license is deemed revoked.

(d) An Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Department and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) An Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License that is issued under this section may be renewed or reinstated only by submitting a completed application and paying the non-refundable fee as required either in Section 8-9-52 of this Code or in Section 8-9-53 of this Code to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division.

(f) It shall be unlawful for any person whose Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or Limited-Elevator Contractor License that has not been renewed to construct, install, alter, maintain, repair, adjust, inspect or decommission, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, elevators or devices covered under this article until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration by the Department.

laws.title: Suspension and revocation of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon recommendation of the Building Official, the Director may take action to suspend or revoke an Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License. The causes for which such license may be suspended or revoked are any of the following:

(1) Gross incompetence;

(2) Gross neglect;

(3) Deliberate misrepresentation;

(4) Failure to pay any required fees or assessed penalties under this article; or

(5) Willful failure to comply with any requirement of this article.

(b) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall promulgate procedural administrative rules for hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of Unlimited-Elevator Contractor Licenses or a Limited-Elevator Contractor Licenses. Among others, such rules shall provide that the Director is required, at least seven days before the hearing, to send, via first class and certified mail, to the licensee a Notice to Appear, which contains the reason or reasons therefor under Subsection (a) of this section, that his or her license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at a hearing provided before a designated hearings officer. Pending the hearing, the Director may forthwith suspend such license where, in his or her judgment, the circumstances warrant such action.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearings officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the hearings officer may suspend or revoke an Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or a Limited-Elevator Contractor License through the entry of an order, which reflects the hearings officer’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearings officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearings officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the hearings officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which, in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearings officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Unlimited-Elevator Contractor License or Limited-Elevator Contractor License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

a. To the licensee; and

b. To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has been suspended or revoked pursuant to this section to construct, install, alter, maintain, repair, adjust or inspect, or to perform such work on a contractual basis,

elevators or devices covered under this article until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated upon reconsideration by the Director.

(Code 1964, § 3.5; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Review of adverse decision
laws.content: In the event that the decision of the hearing officer is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the hearing officer remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

laws.title: License required; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) All installation, inspection, maintenance, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting, testing or decommission of any elevators, including their hoistways and associated spaces, and other equipment covered by this article, shall be performed by, or under the immediate supervision of, an individual who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson.

(b) All installation, alteration, maintenance, repair, servicing, adjusting, testing, and removal of platform lifts and stairway chairlifts only under this article shall be performed by, or under the immediate supervision of, an individual who is licensed by the City as a limited-elevator journeyperson.

(c) An inspector employed by an insurance company authorized to do business in this state may inspect devices covered under this article without being licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson, provided, that the inspector has been issued a certificate of competency and an active commission by the State of Michigan for the inspection of elevators, and that an official copy of each of these documents has been submitted to the Department for its retention.

(Code 1964, § 3.3; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Application for Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License; supplementation of information required; other requirements
laws.content:
(a) An application for an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License shall be made on a form that is provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The application shall be considered complete when the appropriate person has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has provided an affidavit that attests to their experience and is signed in the presence of a notary public, has paid the non-refundable fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-9-21 of this Code, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) Name, date of birth, and address of applicant;

(2) Name and address of current or previous employer;

(3) Number of years that the applicant has been employed in elevator work and a description of such work;

(4) The signature of two character references who have knowledge of relevant character, habits, and work experience of the applicant; and

(5) Letter from a trade representative.

(b) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

(c) An applicant for an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License is required to successfully pass a written and an oral examination. A prerequisite to taking the written examination shall be a minimum of four years’ employment in the elevator industry as a constructor, service person, maintenance person, or repair person. The Department shall have the authority to require documentation or substantiation of professed experience by means of affidavits from current or previous employers and trade representatives, or by other acceptable means concerning the applicant’s experience in the elevator industry as determined by the Department. A degree in electrical or mechanical engineering from a college or university recognized by the Department or a certificate or diploma of completion from a recognized elevator educational program may be considered the equivalent of one year’s employment in the elevator industry as a constructor, service person, maintenance person, or repair person.
