(d) The examination for an unlimited-elevator journeyperson shall be practical in nature and shall fairly test the fitness of the applicant to perform the duties of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson in a competent and safe manner. Examinations shall be given at such place and times as determined by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 3.4; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Application for Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License; supplementation of information required; other requirements
laws.content:
(a) An application for an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License shall be made on a form that is provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. The application shall be considered complete when the appropriate person has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has provided an affidavit that attests to their experience and is signed in the presence of a notary public, has paid the non-refundable fee that is established and approved under Section 8-9-21 of this Code, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) Name, date of birth, and address of applicant;

(2) Name and address of current or previous employer;

(3) Number of years applicant has been employed in the installation of platform lifts and stairway chairlifts, and a description of such work; and

(4) The signature of two character references who have knowledge of relevant character and habits of the applicant.

(b) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

(c) The examination for a limited-elevator journeyperson shall be practical in nature and shall fairly test the fitness of the applicant to perform the duties of a limited-elevator journeyperson in a competent and safe manner. Where required, examinations shall be given at such place and time determined by the Department.

(d) An applicant for a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License is required to successfully pass a written and an oral examination. A prerequisite to taking the written examination shall be a minimum of three years of experience in the platform lifts and stairway chairlifts industry as a constructor, service person, maintenance person, or repair person. The Department shall have the authority to require documentation of any required experience by means of the submission of an affidavit or affidavits from current or previous employers, or by other acceptable means as determined by the Department concerning the applicant's experience.

(e) A Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License may be issued without written examination to a person who has been engaged as a constructor, service, maintenance, or repair person related to platform lifts and stairway chairlifts for a period of not less than three years before the effective date of this article, provided, that the application for the license is made within 12 months after the effective date of this article. The Department shall have the authority to require documentation of any required experience by means of the submission of an affidavit or affidavits from current or previous employers, or by other acceptable means as determined by the Department concerning the applicant's experience.

(Code 1964, § 3.4; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Director of Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department to take action upon application; non-transferability of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon compliance either with Section 8-9-72 of this Code or with Section 8-9-73 of this Code, and with Section 8-9-74 of this Code, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall issue an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License to the applicant.

(b) A license that is issued under Subsection (a) of this section is not transferable to another individual.

(c) An unlimited-elevator journeyperson or a limited-elevator journeyperson shall not allow his or her license to be used by any other individual.

laws.title: Updating certain information required
laws.content: Every holder of an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License shall report to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department any change of the address that was provided either under Section 8-9-72 of this Code or under Section 8-9-73 of this Code within 30 days after the change has occurred.

laws.title: Expiration and renewal of journeyperson licenses; work prohibited where license expired or revoked
laws.content:
(a) An application for renewal of an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License shall be filed annually with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division prior to January 1st in each year.

(b) Prior to the expiration of a current Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay a non-refundable fee for renewal of the license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the non-refundable fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson or a limited-elevator journeyperson until such time that the renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(c) An Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License that is issued under Section 8-9-75 of this Code shall expire on December 31st following the issuance of the license and, where not renewed 60 days after the date of expiration, the license is deemed revoked.

(d) An Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License that is revoked under this section may be renewed upon application to the Department and the showing of good cause. An applicant whose license is revoked is required to pay a late fee for each year and, where the applicant’s license is revoked for more than three years, the applicant is subject to retesting and the payment of the examination fee.

(e) An Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License that is issued under this section may be renewed or reinstated only by submitting a completed application and paying the non-refundable fee as required either in Section 8-9-72 of this Code or in Section 8-9-73 of this Code to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division.

(f) It shall be unlawful for any individual whose Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License has not been renewed to construct, install, inspect, maintain, alter, repair, service, adjust, test, or, as the case may be, decommission or remove elevators or devices covered under this article, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, until such expired license has been renewed or reinstated upon reconsideration by the Department.

laws.title: Suspension and revocation of license
laws.content:
(a) Upon recommendation of the Building Official, the Director may take action to suspend or revoke an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License. The causes for which such license may be suspended or revoked are any of the following:

(1) Gross incompetence;

(2) Gross neglect;

(3) Deliberate misrepresentation;

(4) Failure to pay any required fees or assessed penalties under this article; or

(5) Willful failure to comply with any requirement of this article.

CD8:247
$\S 8-9-78$

DETROIT CITY CODE

(b) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall promulgate procedural administrative rules for hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson Licenses or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson Licenses. Among others, such rules shall provide that the Director is required, at least seven days before the hearing, to send, via first class and certified mail, to the licensee a Notice to Appear, which contains the reason or reasons therefor under Subsection (a) of this section, that his or her license will be suspended or revoked unless good cause is shown to the contrary at a hearing provided before a designated hearings officer. Pending the hearing, the Director may forthwith suspend such license where, in his or her judgment, the circumstances warrant such action.

(c) Where the reason or reasons stated in the Notice to Appear are substantiated by the facts presented at the hearing or the hearings officer is not satisfied that the defects complained of will be properly remedied, the hearings officer may suspend or revoke an Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or a Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License through the entry of an order, which reflects the hearings officer’s decision. In the event that the licensee prevails, the hearings officer shall enter an order of dismissal and provide a true copy to the licensee. In the event the hearings officer decides that the license shall be suspended or revoked, the hearings officer shall enter, as the case may be, an order of suspension with the beginning and ending dates of the suspension or an order of revocation with the effective date, which, in either instance, shall be transmitted to the Director for implementation.

(d) The Director shall:

(1) Receive the order of the hearings officer; and

(2) Prepare a notice that the at-issue Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License or Limited-Elevator Journeyperson License has been suspended, including the term of the suspension, or has been revoked, along with a copy of the order, which shall be sent:

a. To the licensee; and

b. To the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Licenses and Permits Division, which shall correct its records.

(e) It shall be unlawful for any person whose license has been suspended or revoked pursuant to this section to construct, install, alter, maintain, repair, adjust or inspect, or to perform such work on a contractual basis, elevators or devices covered under this article until such suspended or revoked license has been reinstated upon reconsideration by the Director.

(Code 1964, § 3.5; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Review of adverse decision
laws.content:
In the event that the decision of the hearing officer is adverse to the licensee, the licensee may pursue review of the adverse decision in accordance with the Michigan Court Rules by appeal to the circuit court within 21 days of entry of an order. Where said licensee seeks judicial review, the decision of the hearing officer remains in effect until enjoined or reversed by the circuit court.

Secs. 8-9-80—8-9-90. Reserved.

laws.title: Certificate of Registration required; renewal; posting requirement
laws.content:
(a) A person shall not use, or cause to be used, any equipment covered under this article that requires a periodic inspection without first securing a Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, from the Department.

(b) Where equipment is installed under current installation permit requirements and has not been subject to a periodic inspection by the Department, a Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, will be issued by the Department without a fee after inspection and approval of the equipment. The Certificate of Registration shall be renewed in accordance with Subsection (c) of this section.

(c) The Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, shall be renewed annually on or before May 31st upon payment of the non-refundable fee that is established and approved in accordance with

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-9-104

Section 8-9-21 of this Code. Where the fee is paid by check or money order, it shall be made payable to the "Treasurer, City of Detroit."

(d) Upon issuance, the current, original Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, shall be posted in a conspicuous place inside the elevator control room, the elevator machine room, or an office that is accessible during business hours for observation by an authorized representative of the Department.  
(Code 1964, § 6.0; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(6.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Certificate of Registration fee required for equipment placed out of use by owner
laws.content: Unless the elevator meets all of the requirements for being placed out of service pursuant to Section 8-9-131 of this Code and is placed out of service by the Department, equipment placed out of use by the owner, or agent of the owner, shall be considered billable and payment of the non-refundable fee for the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, is required. Where the fee is paid by check or money order, it shall be made payable to the "Treasurer, City of Detroit."

laws.title: Inspections and tests required; frequency
Presence of inspector
laws.content:
The inspections and tests that are required by Section 8-9-91 of this Code shall be made by, or in the presence of, a designated inspector of the Department.  
(Code 1964, § 4.2; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Overtime inspections
laws.content:
An unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City, or the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment, shall submit a letter to the Department requesting overtime inspection of any equipment under

this article for all inspection services provided by the Department during periods other than the Department’s regular business hours.

(Code 1964, § 3.7; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(3.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

Secs. 8-9-105—8-9-110. Reserved.

laws.title: Temporary Certificates of Use for permanent elevators during construction or renovations
Temporary use of altered or rebuilt elevator by building employees, residents, and other occupants
laws.content:
(a) Elevators covered under this article being altered or rebuilt for permanent use in a building may be used before completion on a temporary basis for the transport of employees, residents, or other occupants of the building during the period of alteration or renovation upon the issuance of a certificate for temporary use by the Department.

(b) The Department is authorized to issue temporary certificates where the elevator has been altered for continuous use and has passed all tests required by this article in the presence of a designated inspector of the Department. Installations of equipment other than ele-

CD8:250

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
Qualifications of operators of temporary elevators; authority to order removal; action taken for violation of section
laws.content:
(a) An operator of a temporary elevator shall be an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. The operator shall be free from physical or mental impairments that limit his or her ability to safely operate the elevator and selected with consideration for their ability to perform their duties in a careful and competent manner.

(b) The Department shall have the authority to order the removal of any temporary elevator operator found operating an elevator in a manner dangerous to life, or while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or in any manner contrary to this article.

(c) It shall be a violation of this article for any individual removed from the position of temporary elevator operator pursuant to this section to operate a temporary elevator in the City, unless the individual has been approved by the Department for such position.

(d) Unless reinstated by the Department, it shall be a violation of this article to re-employ any individual so dismissed after written notice by the Department of such dismissal has been served upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment. A violation of this

section shall result in action being taken under Section 8-9-78 of this Code to suspend or revoke the person's Unlimited-Elevator Journeyperson License.

(Code 1964, § 5.5; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Instructions to temporary elevator operators
Equipment found unsafe; notice
laws.content:
(a) Where inspection by the Department of any equipment covered under this article is found to be in an unsafe condition, the Department shall serve a written notice of such a finding upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment or the owner's agent, which states a date and time when required repairs or service must be completed, provided, that, where the required repairs or service are in the nature of an emergency and the their neglect would endanger human life, the subject equipment shall be sealed out of use as provided for in this subdivision and the required repairs or service shall be ordered to be completed immediately.

(b) After the service of a notice under this section, it shall be the duty of the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner or his or her agent, to proceed within the specified time to make the required repairs or services necessary to place the equipment in a safe condition.

(c) It shall be unlawful to operate a device or equipment after the date and time stated in a notice issued under this section unless the specified repairs and service have been made and the device or equipment accepted and approved for use by the Department or where a written extension of time for repair or service has been secured from the Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.6; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance

§ 8-9-140

(b) Where in the case of an emergency and the continued use of equipment creates the possibility of danger to the public, a written notice shall be served stating that the equipment has been taken out of use and the reason or reasons for such actions.

(Code 1964, § 4.8; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.8), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Additional authority to seal equipment out of use; notice
laws.content:
(a) In addition to the authority provided for in Sections 8-9-121 and 8-9-122 of this Code, the Department shall have the authority to seal out of use any equipment covered under this article for any of the following reasons:

(1) Failure to secure a Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or to renew such Certificate;

(2) When in case of emergency, in the opinion of the designated inspector of the Department, any equipment covered under this article is in such condition as to render it unsafe for operation; or

(3) The willful failure to comply with recommendations issued by the Department for the correction of violations.

(b) It shall be unlawful to operate equipment that has been taken out of use by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.7; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Out of use sign or tag; unlawful to deface or remove
laws.content:
(a) Any device covered under this article that has been sealed out of use by the Department shall be plainly marked with a sign or tag indicating the reason or reasons for such action.

(b) It shall be unlawful to deface any sign or tag that has been affixed to any device covered under this article that has been sealed out of use by the Department.

(c) It shall be unlawful to remove, without the approval of the Department, any sign or tag that has been affixed to any device covered under this article that has been sealed out of use by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.9; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(4.9), eff. 3-2-1979)

Secs. 8-9-125—8-9-130. Reserved.

laws.title: Equipment placed out of service
laws.content:
(a) In addition to the requirements of Section 8.11 of the ASME Code, equipment covered by this article placed out of service shall mean equipment that has had its power-feed lines disconnected from the mainline disconnect switch, and:

(1) For an electric elevator or dumbwaiter, the suspension ropes have been removed, whose car and counterweight rest at the bottom of the hoistway, and whose hoistway doors have been permanently barricaded or sealed in the closed position on the hoistway side;

(2) For a hydraulic elevator or dumbwaiter, where the car rests at the bottom of the hoistway, where provided with suspension ropes and counterweight, the suspension ropes have been removed and the counterweight rests at the bottom of the hoistway, where the pressure piping for the equipment has been disassembled and a section removed from the premises and the hoistway doors are permanently barricaded or sealed in the closed position on the hoistway side; and

(3) An escalator or moving walk where entrances have been permanently barricaded.

(b) For equipment to be deemed placed out of service, it is not required that the power-feed lines be removed from the motor or the oil removed from a hydraulic elevator tank.

laws.title: Equipment to be placed out of service
laws.content:
(a) The holder of a Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment shall contact the Department to place equipment out of service.

(b) Where the requirements of Section 8-9-131 of this Code have been met, the equipment shall be sealed out of service by the Department.

(c) Periodic inspections, tests, and fees shall not be required for equipment placed out of service.

Secs. 8-9-133—8-9-140. Reserved.

laws.title: Access to hoistway
laws.content:
(a) In addition to the requirements of Section 2.12.7 of the ASME Code, hoistway access switches shall be provided for each electric elevator in accordance with this section. Access switches shall be for the sole use of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, any individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, and designated inspectors of the Department.

(b) The hoistway access switch shall be provided at one upper landing and an additional switch shall be installed at the lowest landing, provided, that, where the only access to the pit is by means of the lowest hoistway door, the switch shall allow the elevator to run the full length of the hoistway. Minimum car speed shall be 50 feet per minute for top of car inspection station on traction elevator. Switches shall not be mounted over 72 inches and less than 60 inches from the floor level, and more than 12 inches horizontally from the door opening. Unless authorized by the Department, switches shall not be installed at any other landing.

(c) The switch installed at the upper landing may permit up and down car operation but shall not permit the car to be operated above this landing, and shall be so zoned as to prevent the car from being lowered beyond a point where the car top is more than three feet below this landing, unless the physical dimensions of the car and building accomplish the same result.

(d) An emergency hoistway door unlocking device shall be installed at all landings. All other hoistway door unlocking devices are prohibited.

(Code 1964, § 7.1; Code 1984, § 7.1; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.1), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(7.1), eff. 3-10-1997)

laws.title: Requirements for hydraulic oil line
laws.content: For new hydraulic elevator installations, hydraulic oil line supply piping that is installed outside the elevator machine room or hoistway shall not exceed 30 feet in length and shall be properly marked every ten feet.

laws.title: Elevators in structures where flammable liquids are stored or handled
laws.content:
(a) Elevators installed in garages or buildings where flammable liquids are stored or handled, as determined by the Detroit Fire Marshal, shall be provided with mechanical ventilation, ramping, and electrical equipment as specified in this article. (b) Continuous mechanical ventilation adequate to provide at least six air changes per hour shall be carried from the lowest portion of the pit to the outer atmosphere by means of a fire resistant vent or duct in accordance with the following table:
Volume of Pit Cubic Feet Cubic Feet per Minute Discharge Area of Vent or Duct in Square Inch
Up to 500 50 50
Up to 1,000 100 110
Up to 1,500 150 150

(c) A ramp having at least a six-inch rise and forming an angle not greater than 30 degrees from the horizontal, or other approved means, shall be provided at each hoistway door entrance at each floor of the building where flammable liquids are used or stored. (d) All electrical equipment, including electrical equipment on the car, which is less than 18 inches above the bottom terminal floor shall be of a type approved for use in Class 1, Group D, locations as defined in Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. (Code 1964, § 7.2; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Signs and plates
laws.content:
(a) Signs and plates for elevators shall be provided and posted as required by Section 2.16 of the ASME Code, except that the requirements in Subsections 2.16.1.2 and 2.16.1.3 of the ASME Code shall apply in lieu of Subsections 2.16.3.3, 2.16.5.1.1, and 2.16.5.2 of the ASME Code.

(b) Signs and plates shall be of metal and shall have letters and figures stamped, etched in or cast on the surface in such a manner as to be readily legible. The height of the figures shall be not less than one-half inch, except that figures no less than one-eighth inch high may be used for data plates.

CD8:254

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-9-151

(c) Capacity plates for passenger elevators shall have indicated thereon the capacity in pounds and the City serial number. Existing passenger elevators not conforming to the loading requirements of Section 2.16 of the ASME Code shall also have indicated on the plate the allowable number of passengers as determined by the Department, which shall be 160 pounds per passenger.

(d) In addition to the wording required by Section 2.16.5 of the ASME Code, capacity plates for freight elevators shall have indicated thereon the capacity in pounds and the City serial number.

(e) Capacity plates shall be furnished by the Department without charge, provided, that the non-refundable fee as established and approved in accordance with Section 8-9-21 of this Code shall be charged for duplicate plates to replace those that are lost, mutilated, or destroyed.

(f) An additional plate containing the information required by Section 2.16.3 of the ASME Code shall be provided by the installer on all new elevators.

(Code 1964, § 5.4; Code 1984, § 5.4; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.4), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(5.4), eff. 3-10-1997)

laws.title: Classes of loading for freight elevators
laws.content:
All freight elevators shall be designed for Class A loading, Class B loading, or Class C loading as specified in Section 2.16 of the ASME Code.

(Code 1964, § 7.3; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Car lighting and ventilation circuits
laws.content:
A separate circuit for car lighting and ventilation circuits for each elevator shall be fed individually from a branch circuit panel, circuit breaker, or fused switch used for no other purpose and located in the elevator machine room or control room. A test switch or other acceptable means shall be provided inside the elevator to activate the emergency lighting system.

(Code 1964, § 7.4; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Venting of hoistways; exceptions
laws.content:
Hoistways of elevators, new or altered construction, that serve more than three floors above or below grade, or more than 36 feet of rise, shall be furnished with the means to vent smoke and hot gases into the outer air in the event of fire, provided, that for occupancies of other than Use-Groups R-1, R-2, I-1, I-2 and similar occupancies with overnight sleeping quarters, venting of the hoistway is not required where the building is equipped throughout with approved sprinkler heads that are installed at the top of the hoistway.

(Code 1984, § 7.4.1; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(7.4.1), eff. 3-10-1997)

laws.title: Machine room or control room ventilation
laws.content:
(a) Elevator machine rooms or control rooms, new or altered, shall be provided with an independent means of ventilation or air-conditioning to protect against the overheating of the electrical equipment. The system shall be capable of maintaining temperatures within the range established by the manufacturer’s recommendation for the elevator equipment.

(b) Where the elevator machine room is not equipped with an approved automatic sprinkler system, an approved smoke control system shall be provided in accordance with Chapter 8, Article II, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Building Code, to vent smoke into the outer air in the case of fire. The aggregation capacity of smoke exhaust fans shall be determined by the following equation: Capacity Equals Area x 300 (C = A x 300).

laws.title: Minimum size for elevator control room; elevator control spaces prohibited
laws.content:
(a) An elevator control room shall not be less than ten square feet to ensure safe clearance by authorized personnel while engaged in the servicing, maintenance, or repair of elevator equipment.

(b) All elevator control spaces are prohibited.

laws.title: Electric contacts for top emergency exits
laws.content:
In addition to Section 2.14.1.5 of the ASME Code, top emergency exits, where required, shall be provided with car door electric contacts conforming to Section 2.26.2.18 of the ASME Code that are located as to be inaccessible from the inside of the car. An approved means shall be provided to prevent the contacts from being accidentally closed.

(Code 1964, § 7.5; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Glass enclosed elevators
laws.content:
Elevators with glass enclosed cars or glass enclosed hoist ways may be installed only with the specific permission of the Department.

(Code 1964, § 7.6; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Protection of hydraulic cylinders and piping; additional requirements
Test gage connection and relief valve for hydraulic elevators
laws.content:
(a) All new hydraulic elevators, and all existing hydraulic elevator installations undergoing cylinder replacement, shall be provided with a one-fourth-inch pipe size snap-on valve connection between the pump and the check valve for attaching a pressure gage to determine the discharge pressure of the pump. All new hydraulic elevators, and all existing hydraulic elevator installations undergoing cylinder replacement, shall be provided with an approved relief valve in accordance with Section 3.19.4.2.1 of the ASME Code. The relief valve shall be preset to open at a full flow not greater than 125 percent of the working pressure.

(b) When the relief valve for the hydraulic system is incorporated into a compound valve which provides control functions, the adjustment of which affect the setting or operation of the relief valve, a separate and independent relief valve shall be installed in accordance with Section 3.19.4.2.1 of the ASME Code, excluding Subsection (b) of the section.

(Code 1964, § 7.8; Code 1984, § 7.8; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.8), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(7.8), eff. 3-10-1997)

laws.title: Hydraulic elevator safeties
laws.content:
Hydraulic elevator safeties of a type other than those prescribed by the ASME Code, such as those which grip the piston, may be installed only with special permission of the Department.

(Code 1964, § 7.9; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.9), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Car doors or gates for power dumbwaiters
laws.content:
Car doors or gates equipped with electric contacts shall be provided on all power dumbwaiters.

(Code 1964, § 7.10; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.10), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Location of platform lifts and stairway chairlifts
laws.content:
Platform lifts and stairway chairlifts may be installed in locations other than private residences by special permission of the Department, which may require such

CD8:256

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-9-158

additional features as the Department deems necessary in the interests of safety. Such platform lifts and stairway chairlifts installed in other than private residences shall be subject to annual inspection and the payment of the fee for a Certificate of Registration as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 7.12; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.12), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 568-H, § 1(7.12), eff. 11-9-1983)

laws.title: Electrical requirements
laws.content:
(a) All electrical equipment and wiring for lighting of the elevator machine room, machinery space, control room, hoistway and pit, including the main line disconnect switch located in the elevator machine room or control room, shall be installed in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*, Section 2.26 of the ASME Code, and this article.

(b) Main line disconnect means for new and altered elevators shall be an enclosed externally operable fused circuit switch, heavy-duty type and feature a dual cover interlock, or a circuit breaker capable of being locked in the open position.

(c) Where circuit breakers are used as a disconnecting means, they shall not be opened automatically by a fire alarm system.

(d) Where there is more than one driving machine, the disconnect switches or circuit breakers shall be numbered to correspond to the number of the driving machine which it controls in accordance with Section 2.29 of the ASME Code.

(e) Conductors and optical fibers, including low-voltage signal equipment applications, that are located in hoistways, machine rooms, machinery space, control rooms, or control spaces in or on a car, excluding traveling cables that connect the car and hoistway wiring, shall be installed in rigid metal conduit, intermediate metal conduit, electrical metallic tubing, rigid non-metallic conduit, or wireways, or shall be Type MC, MI, or AC cable.

laws.title: Operating devices and controls; electrical protective devices
laws.content:
Electrical protective devices shall be provided in accordance with the following:

(1) *Slack-rope switch.* Winding drum machines shall be provided with a slack-rope device equipped with a slack-rope switch of the enclosed manually reset type which shall cause the electric power to be removed from the elevator driving machine motor and brake where any hoisting rope becomes slack.

(2) *Motor-generator running switch.* Where generator-field control is used, means shall be provided to prevent the application of power to the elevator driving machine motor and brake unless the motor generator set connections are properly switched for the running condition of the elevator. It is not required that the electrical connections between the elevator driving machine motor and the generator be opened in order to remove power from the elevator.

(3) *Compensating-rope sheave switch.* Compensating-rope sheave shall be provided with a compensating-rope sheave switch or switches mechanically opened by the compensating-rope sheave before the sheave reaches its upper or lower limit of travel to cause the electric power to be removed from the elevator driving machine motor and brake.

(4) *Motor field sensing means.* Where direct current is supplied to an elevator armature and shunt field or a driving machine motor, a motor field current sensing means shall be provided, which shall cause the electric power to be removed from the motor armature and brake unless current is flowing in the shunt field of the motor, except for static control elevators provided with a device to detect an overspeed condition prior to, and independent of, the operation of the governor overspeed switch. This device shall cause the power to be removed from the elevator driving machine motor armature and machine brake.

(5) *Emergency signaling device.* An audible signaling device shall be provided and operable from the emergency stop switch and from a switch or button identified as "ALARM", which shall be provided in or adjacent to each car's operating panel in accordance with Section 8-9-192 of this Code.

(6) *Emergency stop switch.* On all elevators, an emergency stop switch shall be provided in the car. Emergency stop switches shall be located in or adjacent to each car operating panel. When opened, the stop switch shall cause the electrical

DETROIT CITY CODE

power to be removed from the elevator driving-machine motor and brake. In addition, the emergency stop switch shall:

a. Be of the manually opened and closed type;

b. Have red operating handles or buttons;

c. Be conspicuously and permanently marked "STOP" and indicate the stop and run positions;

d. Be positively opened mechanically and its opening not solely dependent on springs;

e. Have push/pull type switch that is arranged to operate: push to run, pull to stop; and

f. Be an audible signal device.

(7) Broken rope, tape, or chain switches used in connection with machine room normal terminal stopping switches. Broken rope, tape, or chain switches, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.26.2.6 of the ASME Code, shall be provided in connection with normal terminal stopping devices located in machine rooms or traction elevators. Such switches shall be opened by a failure of the rope, tape, or chain.

(8) Stop switch in pit. A stop switch, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.26.2.5 of the ASME Code, shall be provided in the pit of every elevator. See Section 2.26.2.7 of the ASME Code.

(9) Stop switch on top of car. A stop switch, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.26.2.28 of the ASME Code, shall be provided on the top of every elevator car.

(10) Car-safety mechanism switch. A switch, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.17.7 of the ASME Code, shall be required where a car safety is provided.

(11) Governor overspeed switch. A governor overspeed switch shall be provided when required by Section 2.18.4 of the ASME Code.

(12) Final terminal stopping devices. Final terminal stopping devices, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.25.3 of the ASME Code, shall be provided for every electric elevator.

(13) Emergency terminal speed limiting devices. Where reduced stroke oil buffers are provided, as permitted by Section 2.22.4.1.2 of the ASME Code, emergency terminal speed limiting devices conforming to the requirements of Section 2.25.4.1 of the ASME Code shall be provided.

(14) Buffer switches for oil buffers used with Type C car safeties. Oil-level and compression switches, conforming to the requirements of Sections 2.17.8.2.7 and 2.17.8.2.8 of the ASME Code shall be provided for all oil buffers used with Type C safeties. See 2.17.5.3 of the ASME Code.

(15) Hoistway-door interlocks or hoistway-door electric contacts. Hoistway-door interlocks or hoistway-door electric contacts, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.102 of the ASME Code, shall be provided for all elevators.

(16) Car-door or gate electric contacts. Car-door or gate electric contacts, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.14.4.2 of the ASME Code, shall be provided for all elevators.

(17) Emergency terminal stopping devices. Emergency terminal stopping devices, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.25.4.2 of the ASME Code, shall be provided for all elevators where static control is used unless exempted by Section 2.25.4.2 of the ASME Code.

(18) Car side-emergency-exit door contact switches. A car-door electric contact, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.14.1.10.2 of the ASME Code, shall be provided on every car side-emergency-exit door.

(19) Motor-generator overspeed protection. Means shall be provided to cause the electric power to be removed automatically from the elevator driving-machine motor and brake should a motor generator set, driven by a direct-current motor, overspeed excessively.

(20) Electric contacts for hinged car-platform sills. Hinged car platform sills, where provided, shall be equipped with electric contacts conforming to the requirements of Section 2.15.16 of the ASME Code.

(21) In-car stop switch. On passenger elevators, a stop switch, either key operated or behind a locked cover, may be provided in the car and located in or adjacent to the car operating panel. The switch shall be clearly and permanently marked "Stop" and shall indicate the stop and run positions. The switch shall be positively

opened mechanically and its opening shall not be solely dependent on springs. When opened, this switch shall cause the electric power to be removed from the elevator driving-machine motor and brake.

(22) *Buffer switches for gas spring-return oil buffers.* Buffer switches, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.22.4.5 of the ASME Code, shall have contacts which are positively opened mechanically and their opening shall not be dependent solely on springs.

(23) *Stop switch in remote machine and control rooms.* A stop switch, conforming to the requirements of Section 2.26.2.5 of the ASME Code, shall be provided in remote machine and control rooms where required by Section 2.7.3.5 of the ASME Code.

laws.title: Installation of pipes or ducts conveying gases, vapors, or liquids in hoistways, machine rooms, or machinery spaces
laws.content:
(a) Steam and hot water pipes are permitted to be installed in hoistways, machinery spaces, machine rooms, or control rooms for the purpose of heating these areas only, subject to the following:

(1) Heating pipes shall convey only low pressure steam [15 PSI (100 kPa) or less] or hot water [212 degrees Fahrenheit (100 degrees Celsius) or less];

(2) All risers and return pipes shall be located outside the hoistway; and

(3) Traps or shutoff valves shall be provided in readily accessible locations outside the hoistway.

(b) Ducts for heating, cooling, ventilation, and venting these spaces are permitted to be installed in the hoistway, machine spaces, machinery room, or control room. Other pipes or ducts conveying gases, vapors or liquid, and not used in connection with the operation of the elevator, shall not be installed in any hoistway, machinery space, machine room, or control room.

laws.title: Installation of sprinkler protections in hoistways, machinery spaces, machine rooms, or control rooms
laws.content:
(a) Sprinkler protection that conform to the requirements of the NFPA 13 may be installed in hoistways, machinery spaces, machine rooms or control rooms, subject to the following:

(1) All risers and returns shall be located outside these spaces;

(2) Branch lines in the hoistway shall supply sprinklers at not more than one floor;

(3) Electronically supervised shut-off valves shall be provided in readily-accessible locations outside the hoistway, machine room or control room, provided, that, where an electronically pre-active sprinkler system, or similar type, is installed in accordance with NFPA 13, a shut-off valve is not required; and

(4) Means shall be installed in the machine or control room to automatically disconnect the main-line power supply to the affected elevator prior to the application of water, but not until the elevator car has reached the designated landing and the car doors have opened and remain open, provided, that the means shall not be self-resetting and that the activation of sprinklers outside of the hoistway, machine room, or control room shall not disconnect the main-line power supply.

(b) A separate fuse circuit breaker for heat sensors shall be installed in the elevator machine or control room and used for no other purpose.

(c) An indicator light for the shunt trip operation shall be installed and located in the machine or control room for testing purposes.

(d) Fire alarm initiating devices, or combination-type fire alarm initiating devices, shall not be used to activate shunt-trip operations in these spaces or to disconnect the main-line power supply.

(e) Only rate-of-rise, fixed-temperature type fire alarm initiating devices are permitted in elevator pits, hoistways, machinery spaces, machine rooms, or control rooms.

laws.title: Drains and sump pumps
laws.content:
New or altered elevators provided with Firefighters’ Emergency Operation shall be provided with a drain or

sump pump as required by Sections 2.2.2.4 through 2.2.2.6 of the ASME Code. Installation of drains and sump pumps required under this section shall comply with Chapter 8, Article V, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Plumbing Code.

laws.title: Limited-use/limited-application elevators
Building Construction and Property Maintenance
Elevators required; exceptions
laws.content:
In buildings where a required accessible floor is four or more stories above or below a level of exit discharge, at least one required accessible means of egress shall be an elevator that complies with this article as specified in Section 1009.2.1 of the 2015 Michigan Building Code.

Secs. 8-9-164—8-9-170. Reserved.

laws.title: Responsibility for care, operation, and maintenance of equipment; reporting of defects or violations; licensed individual to perform work
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the Certificate for Temporary Use issued by the Department for equipment covered under this article shall be responsible for the care, maintenance, and proper operation of the equipment. The inspections and tests that are required pursuant to Division 3, Subdivision B, of this article shall be performed by the Department.

(b) Any maintenance or service that is required by this division shall be made pursuant to a contract that is entered into between the holder of Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, and an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly use, or to permit or cause the use of, any device or equipment covered under this article, which is defective,

CD8:262

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-9-173

is otherwise not in compliance with this article, or creates a condition that affects the safe operation of the device or equipment.

(d) It shall be the duty of any person who is employed as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, is an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, or is an inspector employed by an insurance company authorized to do business in this state to promptly notify the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the Certificate for Temporary Use, the building owner, or the individual in charge of any equipment covered under this article, and the Department, regarding any defect known to the person that may affect the safe operation of the equipment.

(e) Only an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, or an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under this article, shall perform work in an elevator hoistway, including the cleaning of the elevator pit and machine room.

(f) It shall be unlawful for any unlimited-elevator journeyperson to alter, repair, service or maintain any elevator, escalator, dumbwaiter or moving walk, including their hoistways and associated spaces, while the equipment is being used by any individual other than the journeyperson.

(Code 1964, § 5.0; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Inspection and service; elevators to remain in operation when building occupied; notice of elevator out of use
laws.content:
(a) In addition to the periodic tests required by this article, all power elevators, escalators and moving walks shall be inspected and serviced at such periods as may be necessary to maintain the equipment in a safe operating condition, but not less than once every 30 days, by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. This interval may be extended to periods not exceeding 90 days by special permission of the Department upon a written request from the holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, provided, that the Department deems the frequency of use of the relevant equipment is so low as to not require servicing at 30-day intervals. All other equipment covered under this article, except private residence elevators, and private residence platform lifts and stairway chairlifts, shall be similarly inspected and serviced at least quarterly.

(b) In buildings where passenger elevators are used, at least one passenger elevator, or one elevator in each bank or group of elevators, shall be maintained in operation at all times by the building owner or manager when the building is occupied, provided, that a building equipped with only one elevator shall be permitted to have the elevator temporarily out of use for a reasonable amount of time for testing or servicing.

(c) Where an elevator is placed temporarily out of use by the building owner for a period in excess of 30 days, the building owner shall notify the Department with such information.

(Code 1964, § 5.1; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Elevator service record
laws.content:
(a) An elevator service record shall be posted in the elevator machine or control room.

(b) For electric elevators, the record shall:

(1) Comply with the maintenance and test checklist from Sections 8.7.1.64 through 8.7.1.66, Sections 8.6.4.1 through 8.6.4.9, and Sections 8.6.11.4 through 8.6.11.4.6 of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, A17.1—2010/CSA B44-10;

(2) Memorialize the date of each service maintenance or test; and

(3) Be signed by the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City and performed each service or test.

(c) For hydraulic elevators:

(1) Comply with the maintenance and test checklist from Sections 8.6.5.1 through 8.6.5.12 of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, A17.1—2010/CSA B44-10;

(2) Memorialize the date of each service maintenance or test; and

(3) Be signed by the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City and performed each service or test.

laws.title: Maintenance of fire service
laws.content: All elevators provided with Firefighters' Emergency Operation shall be subjected to Phase I recall by use of the key switch and a minimum of one floor operation on Phase II at least once every 30 days. A written record of test results shall be maintained in the machine room or control room. The holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment, shall notify the Department of any deficiencies in the Firefighters' Emergency Operation, any completed correction, and necessary updating of the maintenance record.

laws.title: Maintenance of hydraulic cylinders with corrosion protection and monitoring systems
laws.content: In addition to the requirements of Section 3.18.3.8 of the ASME Code, the methods for monitoring the hydraulic cylinders for corrosion and other underground conditions shall be tested not less than once every 30 days by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. A written record of the results of each test shall be kept in the machine room or control room.

laws.title: Maintenance of emergency signaling devices
laws.content:
(a) All elevators provided with emergency signaling devices shall be tested at least once every 30 days to verify that the emergency devices meet the requirements and operate in accordance with Section 2.27 of the ASME Code.

(b) A written record of the test of the emergency devices shall be maintained in the elevator machine room or control room.

laws.title: Periodic test of car and counterweight safeties, governors, and oil buffers
laws.content:
(a) Car and counterweight safeties, governors, and oil buffers shall be periodically tested in accordance with Section 8.10.2.2.2(ii) of the ASME Code by holder of the Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, the owner of the equipment or his or her agent, or an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City, provided, that such tests shall be performed by, or under, the immediate supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. Unless requested by the designated inspector of the Department, a test that is conducted under this section does not have to be performed in the presence of a designated inspector of the Department.

(b) Car and counterweight safeties, governors, and oil buffers of all elevators, except private residence elevators, shall be tested at least once every 30 months, the tests alternating between no load in the car at one time and full load in the car at the other time using approved test weights.

(c) The results of the test required under this section, including any defects found, shall be reported to the Department on a form furnished by the Department within 30 days of completion of the test. The report shall be signed by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson person who licensed by the City and is performing the test or under whose direct supervision the test is performed. The Department shall keep a record of all such tests.

(d) It shall be unlawful for the holder of a Certificate of Registration as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of the equipment, to fail to have any test that is required to be performed under this section. (Code 1964, § 5.2; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.2), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 568-H, § 1(5.2), eff. 11-9-1983)

laws.title: Acceptance and periodic test of hydraulic cylinder and relief valve; test requirements
laws.content:
(a) Hydraulic cylinders and relief valves shall be tested during the acceptance inspection and at least once every 30 months. The relief valve setting shall be in compliance with Section 3.19.4.2 of the ASME Code.

(b) Where the relief valve setting is altered or the seal is broken, the relief valve shall be resealed. Hydraulic cylinders that are more than 35 years old shall be tested every 12 months. Each test shall be performed either by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of this Code, or by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of this Code. Unless requested by the designated inspector of the Department, by the holder of the Certificate of Registration as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or by the owner of the equipment a test conducted under this section need not be performed in the presence of a designated inspector of the Department.

(c) Procedures for static load tests shall be as follows:

(1) Put rated load in the car;

(3) For cylinders that are not completely exposed, after a minimum of 120 minutes, note the position of the platform with respect to the chosen reference. For cylinders that are completely exposed, after a minimum of 60 minutes, note the position of the platform with respect to the chosen reference. A change in the car position during a cylinder test that cannot be accounted for by visible oil leakage or temperature change of the oil indicates a failure of some type requiring further inspections, tests, or repairs. An accessible written record of all oil levels and all oil added shall be maintained in the machine room or control room.

(d) The results of the test required under this section, including any defects found, shall be reported to the Department on a form furnished by the Department within 30 days of completion of the test. The report shall be signed by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson person who licensed by the City and is performing the test or under whose direct supervision the test is performed. The Department shall keep a record of all such tests.

laws.title: Frequency of reshacking drum-type machines
laws.content:
In lieu of Section 8.6.4.10.1 of the ASME Code, the reshacking of car hoisting ropes of drum-type machines shall be performed at the following frequencies:

(1) Machines with 1:1 roping located over the hoistway shall be reshacked:

a. Concurrently, with the no-load testing of the car and counterweight safeties, governors, and oil buffers required by Section 8-9-177 of this Code;

b. Concurrently, with the rated-load testing of the car and counterweight safeties, governors, and oil buffers required by Section 8-9-177 of this Code; and

c. At such other times as the condition of the ropes warrants reshacking as directed by the Department.

(2) Machines with 1:1 roping located below or at the side of the hoistway, and all machines with other than 1:1 roping, shall be reshacked when the condition of the ropes warrants, as directed by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 5.8; Code 1984, § 5.8; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(5.8), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(5.8), eff. 3-10-1997)

Secs. 8-9-180—8-9-190. Reserved.

laws.title: Firefighters’ emergency operations
laws.content:
(a) In addition to the requirements of Section 2.27.3 of the ASME Code, elevator fire alarm initiating devices shall be installed in all of the following locations:

(1) Each floor served by the elevator;

(2) Associated elevator machine rooms, machine spaces, and control rooms; and

(3) Elevator hoistway and pits where sprinklers are located.

(b) Where fire alarm initiating devices are installed in the elevator pit, the activation of the device shall cause the elevator to be sent to the higher of the two designated or alternate recall levels.

(c) If by-pass key switch operations are used, the three position key-operated switch located in the operating panel in each elevator or at the designated level, as described in Sections 2.27.3.1 and 2.27.3.3 of the ASME Code, shall be of single- or double-cut type.

(d) The activation of the fire alarm initiating device in any elevator lobby, machine room and hoistway, or in any other space associated with the operation of the elevator equipment, other than at the designated floor, shall cause all elevators to return non-stop to the designated floor.

(e) Where the fire alarm initiating device at the designated floor is activated, the elevator shall return to an alternate floor approved by the Department.

(f) When the fire alarm initiating device located in the elevator machine room, control room, hoistway, or machinery space is activated, the Phase II emergency in-car operations shall be inoperable.

(g) A separate fire alarm initiating device circuit for the elevator, or groups of elevators, shall be fed individually from a branch circuit panel. Circuit breakers or a fused switch, used for no other purpose, shall be provided and located in the elevator machine room or control room.

(h) The requirements of Section 2.27.3 of the ASME Code shall apply to elevators installed in buildings designated as "high-rise" by the Michigan Building Code. Such elevators, and their hoistways and associated spaces, shall comply with Chapter 8, Article II, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Building Code*.

(i) Elevator fire alarm initiation systems shall be of a stand-alone type and shall be installed by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City or by an apprentice who is under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City.

(j) Elevator fire alarm initiation devices shall be audible.

(k) Elevator fire alarm initiating devices required by Section 2.27 of the ASME Code and Subsection (a) of this section shall be monitored by the building’s fire alarm panel. A supervisory signal shall be provided where the building’s fire alarm panel is located in an attended location that is staffed at all times by authorized personnel.

(l) Where the building’s fire alarm panel is installed in a non-attended location, or monitored from a location outside of the building, the elevator’s fire alarm initiating devices shall be connected to the building’s fire alarm panel and the activation of the devices shall place the building in a general alarm condition.

(m) Where only alterations to any elevator in an existing building are being made:

(1) New building fire alarm initiating devices may be installed and located adjacent to the elevator’s fire alarm initiating devices in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section; and

(2) The elevator’s fire alarm system is not required to be connected to the panel.

(n) Where an elevator is, or elevators are, independent of a building’s fire alarm system, a mechanism shall be installed to bypass the system during monthly testing of Phase I and II Operations.

(Code 1964, § 7.14; Code 1984, § 7.14; Ord. No. 307-H, § 1(7.14), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 568-H, § 1(7.14), eff. 11-9-1983; Ord. No. 03-97, § 1(7.14), eff. 3-10-1997)

Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:

ically transfer to a source of standby or emergency power after the normal power supply fails. The power source shall be capable of providing for the operation of the audible signaling device and illumination of the alarm switch for at least one hour, and the means of two-way conversation for at least four hours.

(c) In buildings where an attendant, such as a building employee or security guard, is not continuously available to take action when the required emergency signal is operated, the elevators shall be provided with a means within the car for communication with or signaling to a service that is capable of taking appropriate action when a building attendant is not available. A standby or emergency power system that conforms to the requirements of Subsection (b) of this section shall be provided.

laws.title: Elevator evacuation and generator power procedures
laws.content:
(a) Elevator evacuation procedures shall be governed by Sections 8.6.11.4 through 8.6.11.4.6 of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, A17.1—2010/CSA B44-10, and the American Society of Mechanical Engineers Guide for Emergency Personnel, A17.4—1999 (Reaffirmed 2009), which have been adopted by referenced pursuant to Section 8-9-2(a)(4) of this Code.

(b) The holder of a Certificate of Registration, as defined in Section 8-9-11 of this Code, or the owner of a building shall prepare both written elevator evacuation procedures and generator power procedures, which shall be submitted to, and approved by, the Department.

(c) The Department shall consult with necessary Fire Department personnel regarding the written elevator evacuation procedures and generator power procedures that are approved in Subsection (b) of this section.

Secs. 8-9-194—8-9-200. Reserved.

laws.title: Purpose, scope, and applicability
laws.content:
(a) In order to provide for the safety of life, limb and property, this article covers the design, construction, installation, registration, alteration, inspection, testing, maintenance, operation, and repairing of manlifts and their runways in the City of Detroit. Where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of this article will result in unnecessary hardship or involve practical difficulties, the Board of Appeals shall have the authority, upon appeal in specific cases, to authorize a variance, or to modify the requirements of this article so that the results will not be contrary to the public interest and so that the intent of this article shall be observed, public safety secured, and substantial justice done.

(b) No manlift shall be installed after March 1, 1979, in any building or structure in the City other than those used exclusively as cement manufacturing plants, flour mills, granaries, or parking garages.

(Code 1964, §§ 1.0, 1.2, 3.10; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(1.0, 1.2, 3.10), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
(a) Any person, or anyone acting in behalf of said person, who violates any provision of this article, shall be subject, upon conviction thereof, to a fine or not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

(b) Each day that a violation of this article continues or is permitted to exist without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable upon conviction in the manner prescribed in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1964, § 6.0; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(6.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

Secs. 8-10-4—8-10-10. Reserved.

Subdivision B. Additions to ASME Standard to Meet Needs of City of Detroit

laws.title: Construction
laws.content: The rails shall be standard guardrails with toeboards meeting the provisions of ANSI A12.1. On those sides not used as a landing, the guardrails shall be extended to a minimum height of 66 in. (1,675 mm) when less than 24 in. (610 mm) away from the edge of the floor opening. In lieu of the 66 in. (1,675 mm) high guardrail, a wall, wire mesh, expanded metal, or solid panels may be used. This minimum 66 in. (1,675 mm) high guardrail is intended to prevent personnel alongside the manlift from being able to lean over the guardrails and into the floor opening area. In addition, guardrails constructed of a top railing and toeboard shall incorporate an intermediate railing positioned within the middle third of the distance between the toeboard and top railing.

laws.title: Runway enclosure
laws.content:
A manlift runway shall be enclosed throughout its height and shall have a fire-resistance rating of not less than two hours. Any door to a manlift runway shall be located not less than 30 inches from the outside edge of the floor opening, shall open outward, shall be self-closing and shall have a fire-resistance rating of not less than one and one-half hours. Where, due to the structure of the building, the requirements for fire rating in this section do not prohibit the piercing of any floor, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may waive the provisions in this section for manlift runway construction.

(Code 1964, §§ 5.1, 5.2; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(5.1, 5.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Types
laws.content:
Machines shall be the direct-connected type. Cast-iron gears shall not be used. There shall be no 90 degree shoulders machined onto any shaft in manlift machines or pulleys. Machines shall be designed and constructed to catch and hold the driving pulley in the event of shaft failure.

**EXCEPTION:** Existing multiple V-belt drive systems are permissible. All new installations shall be the direct-connected type. When one V-belt is replaced, all belts shall be replaced.

laws.title: Size
laws.content:
The grab surface of the handhold shall be not less than nine inches (230 m) in width or less than three inches (75 mm) in depth, and shall provide two inches (50 mm) of clearance from the belt. Fastenings for handholds shall be located at least one inch (25 mm) from the edge of the belt.

§ 8-10-13

DETROIT CITY CODE

laws.title: Lower limit safety stops
laws.content:
Two separate automatic safety stops shall be provided to shut off the electric power and apply the brake when a loaded step passes the bottom landing (refer to paragraph 4.6.2). One of these devices shall activate while the step is still in the horizontal position. The automatic safety stop may consist of one of the following:

(a) A split-rail or equivalent safety stop located on the opposite guide rail.

(b) An electronic device.

(c) A treadle safety stop.

No lower limit safety stops are required for a permanently installed riser, provided that it is ten inches (254 mm) in height or less from the floor.

An automatic lower limit safety stop requiring manual resetting shall be installed to cut off the power and apply the brake when a loaded step passes the lower terminal landing and before the loaded step has reached a point 12 inches below the lower and terminal landing.

(Code 1964, §§ 5.3, 5.4, 5.5; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(5.3, 5.4, 5.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Inscription
laws.content:
Signs shall be provided on each landing, or stenciled on the belt approximately at eye level above each step, giving the following instructions:

FACE THE BELT

USE THE HANDHOLD

TO STOP, PULL ROPE IN DIRECTION OF TRAVEL

DO NOT CARRY TOOLS, PACKAGES, PIPES, OR LUMBER

laws.title: Visitor Warning Sign
laws.content: A conspicuous sign shall display the following wording at each landing:

laws.title: Authorized Personnel Only
laws.content:
The sign shall be of block letters not less than two inches (50 mm) in height and shall be a color offering high contrast with the background color.

Each manlift enclosure door shall have posted thereon a sign in letters not less than one inch high reading as follows:

laws.title: Establishment and approval of fees
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of appeals, permits, inspections, re-inspections, and other fees that are required by this article. The fees that are authorized by this subsection shall cover the costs that are incurred by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department when rendering such services in the administration and enforcement of this article.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(Code 1964, § 3.7; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

CD8:270

laws.title: Permit required; application; emergency alterations; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) A permit to construct, install or alter any manlift in the City of Detroit shall only be issued to an unlimited-elevator contractor licensed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code. Such a permit shall not be issued until after the unlimited-elevator contractor has filed with the Department an application on a form provided by the Department, which is accompanied by detailed plans and specifications showing the proposed installation or alteration.

(b) In case of emergency alterations, the permit shall be obtained within 72 hours from the time of alteration. Ordinary repairs and replacements may be made in accordance with the provisions of this article without filing such application.

(c) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that an unlimited-elevator contractor is not eligible to apply for a permit where the unlimited-elevator contractor, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

CD8:271
§ 8-10-22

DETROIT CITY CODE

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(d) An unlimited-elevator contractor against whom any fee is assessed is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until payment of the outstanding fee is made to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(e) An unlimited-elevator contractor against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the unlimited-elevator contractor can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

laws.title: Certificate of Registration required; annual renewal; posting
laws.content:
(a) A person shall not use, or cause to be used, any equipment covered under this article that requires a periodic inspection under Section 8-10-42 of this Code without first securing a Certificate of Registration for a Manlift from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(b) Where equipment is installed under current installation permit requirements and has not been subject to a periodic inspection by the Department, a Certificate of Registration for a Manlift will be issued by the Department without a fee after inspection and approval of the equipment. The Certificate of Registration shall be renewed in accordance with Subsection (c) of this section.

(c) The Certificate of Registration for a Manlift shall be renewed annually on or before May 31st upon payment of the non-refundable fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-10-21 of this Code.

(d) Upon issuance, the current, original Certificate of Registration for a Manlift shall be posted in a conspicuous place inside an office that is accessible during business hours for observation by an authorized representative of the Department.

(Code 1964, § 3.3; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Payment of fees for permits and inspections
laws.content:
Any fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-10-21 of this Code for the issuance of a permit, or for a required inspection, under this article shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at the time that the permit is issued or the inspection is made. Where the fee is paid by check or money order, it shall be made payable to the "Treasurer, City of Detroit."

(Code 1964, § 3.3; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Appeals from decisions, determinations, or orders; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) An interested person, or the person's authorized agent, aggrieved by a decision, determination, or order of the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code, which refuses to grant an application for a permit or makes any other decision pursuant or related to this code, may appeal in writing for a variance to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Board of Appeals for Construction. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the code or the rules governing construction have been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of the code do not apply, or an equal or better form of construction is proposed. As provided for in Section 8-1-15 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, the decision of the Board of Appeals is final and neither the City nor the applicant may appeal the decision.
