laws.title: Installation, alteration, and repair of manlifts
laws.content:
(a) No person, except an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, shall install, alter or repair any manlift, or arrange for the performance of such work on a contractual basis.

(b) No installation, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting or inspection shall be done on any device covered by this article, except by, or under the immediate supervision of, a person who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

(Code 1964, § 3.1; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Existing installations
laws.content:
Where in good repair, existing installations may be continued in their present form, provided, that such installations present no apparent hazard through methods of installation or operation or in their design. Where alterations or changes are proposed or made, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to prohibit such alteration or to require such other additions and alterations or changes as the Department deems necessary for the safe operation of such altered equipment. Where, in the opinion of the Department, such existing installation is found to be in a dangerous condition, or where the design or method of operation in combination with devices used is considered inherently dangerous or where there is an immediate hazard to those riding on or using such equipment, it shall be the duty of the Department to make or order such tests or inspections as are deemed necessary to determine the condition of the equipment and to order such alterations or additions as are deemed necessary to eliminate the existing dangerous condition.

(Code 1964, § 1.3; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(1.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Electrical requirements
laws.content:
All electrical equipment and wiring, including the main disconnect switch, for the manlift machine shall be installed in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. All other electrical equipment and wiring falling within the scope of this article shall be installed and serviced by persons licensed under, and in accordance with the requirements of, Chapter 8, Article IX, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Detroit Elevator Code*.

(Code 1964, § 5.7; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(5.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Inspection and approval required before putting into service
laws.content:
No person shall put into service any manlift that shall hereafter be constructed, installed, rebuilt, or altered until the manlift has been inspected and approved by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and a Certificate of Registration for a Manlift is issued by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 3.2; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Responsibility for equipment; notification of defects; servicing
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift shall be responsible for the care, operation, and maintenance of equipment covered by this article. Such registrant shall cause to be made periodic inspections and to maintain in proper working order all equipment covered by this article.

(b) It shall be the duty of any person employed as an unlimited elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, is an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, or is an inspector employed by an insurance company authorized to do business in this state to promptly notify the person in charge of any equipment covered by this article, and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, concerning any defects known to the individual that affect the safe operation of the equipment.

(c) No person shall knowingly use or permit or cause the use of any manlift having defects affecting the safe operation thereof. No person shall alter, repair, or make adjustments on any manlift or the machinery thereof while such manlift is available for use by persons other than the persons installing, altering, repairing, inspecting, or maintaining the manlift or the machinery thereof.

CD8:274

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-10-47

(d) All manlifts shall be inspected and serviced by an unlimited-elevator journey person who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code at such periods as may be necessary, but not less than once every 30 days, to maintain the equipment in a safe operating condition.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.4, 3.9; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.4, 3.9), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Frequency of inspections; payment required when service rendered
laws.content:
(a) The Building Official, as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code, and designated inspectors of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, are authorized:

(1) To make inspections and tests of all new installations of, or alterations to, manlifts;

(2) To inspect manlifts every six months;

(3) To make or cause to be made such other inspections and tests as are deemed necessary for the purpose of safety and the enforcement of this article; and

(4) To issue orders for alterations, repairs and the correction of unsafe conditions and violations of this article.

(b) Unless previously made, any payment for an inspection shall be made, as required by Section 8-10-24 of this Code, at the time that the service is rendered.

(Code 1964, § 4.1; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Right of entry for inspection
laws.content:
(a) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this article, the holder of a Certificate of Registration for a Manlift, the owner, or an authorized agent of the owner, of any building in the City where any equipment covered under this article is installed, or any building, premises, or structure that is owned, operated, or maintained by the City, shall permit and assist the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code, or any designated and authorized inspector, to enter the building to make inspections of any equipment during reasonable hours subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures.

(b) Where access to the location of equipment covered under this article is denied by the registrant or the owner of the equipment, or where access is otherwise not obtained, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may pursue recourse, as provided by law, to conduct an investigation pursuant to this article. Accordingly, the registrant, and the owner, shall be responsible for making arrangements for access to the site and equipment to facilitate the completion of any inspection.

(Code 1964, § 4.0; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Interference with Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department personnel prohibited
laws.content:
Any person who refuses to comply with this article, or assists in the violation of any provision of this article, or in any manner hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents or interferes with Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department inspectors in the performance of any duty imposed by this article, or refuses to permit such inspectors to perform their duty by barring entrance at reasonable hours to buildings or premises for the purpose of enforcement of this article, shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Section 8-10-3 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 6.1; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(6.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Approval of overtime inspection required
laws.content:
In order to obtain an inspection by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours, the responsible party shall provide a letter to the Department for its approval prior to the service being rendered.

(Code 1964, § 3.8; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.8), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Equipment found unsafe
laws.content:
Where, upon inspection of equipment covered by this article, such equipment should be found in an unsafe condition, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve a written notice of the findings upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift or the owner stating a time when the

CD8:275
§ 8-10-47

DETROIT CITY CODE

repairs must be completed, provided, that, where the required work is, or repairs are in the nature of an emergency and the neglect of which would endanger human life, the equipment shall be sealed out of service as provided for in Section 8-10-48 of this Code and such work or repairs ordered to be done at once. After the serving of such notice, it shall be the duty of the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift, or the owner, to proceed within the time allowed to make such repairs or changes as are necessary to place said equipment in a safe condition, and it shall be unlawful to operate such equipment after the date stated in such notice, except where an extension of time, in writing, has been secured from the Department, unless such repairs and changes have been made and the equipment approved by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.3; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Authority to seal equipment out of service
laws.content:
In addition to the penalties provided for in Section 8-10-3 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to close down any manlift for the following reasons:

(1) For failure to secure a Certificate of Registration for a Manlift or to renew such Certificate;

(2) When in case of emergency, in the opinion of a designated inspector of the Department, any device covered by this article is in such condition as to render the device unsafe for operation; or

(3) For willful failure to comply with the notice issued by the Department for the correction of a violation.

(Code 1964, § 4.4; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Notice of sealing out of service
laws.content:
(a) Except in the case of an emergency, before sealing out of service any manlift, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve written notice upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift or the owner of the equipment, which provides that the Department intends to seal the equipment out of service and the reason or reasons for such action.

(b) Where in the case of an emergency and the continued use of equipment creates the possibility of danger to the public, a written notice shall be served stating that the equipment has been taken out of service and the reason or reasons for such action.

(Code 1964, § 4.5; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Labeling device out of service; unlawful to deface of remove sign or tag or to remove seal
laws.content:
(a) Any device sealed out of service by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall be conspicuously labeled with a sign or tag indicating the reason for such closing down.

(b) It shall be a violation of this section:

(1) To deface a sign or tag posted under Subsection (a) of this section; or

(2) To remove a sign or tag posted under Subsection (a) of this section without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department; or

(3) To tamper with, or remove, a seal installed under Subsection (a) of this section without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.6; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(4.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Holder of Certificate of Registration or owner of equipment to notify City of accident
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift, or the owner of the equipment, shall notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department within one business day after receiving a report of an accident as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code.

(b) Upon reasonable notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift, or the owner of the equipment, shall provide the Department access to facilitate an investigation of any equipment that was involved in the accident as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 3.5; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance
laws.content:
§ 8-11-3

defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code, by the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Manlift, or by the owner of such equipment, an inspection shall be made of the equipment.

laws.title: Unlawful to use equipment following accident until approval
laws.content:
Where an accident, as defined in Section 8-10-11 of this Code, involves the failure, breakage, damage, or destruction of any part of the apparatus or mechanism of the device that affects the safe operation of the equipment, it shall be unlawful to repair or service, or use, the equipment until after an investigation, inspection and approval by a designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for continued use of such equipment.

(Code 1964, § 3.6; Ord. No. 308-H, § 1(3.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

Secs. 8-10-54—8-10-60. Reserved.

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
(a) Any person, or anyone acting in behalf of said person, who violates any provision of this article, shall be subject, upon conviction thereof, to a fine or not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

laws.title: Appeals from decisions, determinations, or orders; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) An interested person, or the person's authorized agent, aggrieved by a decision, determination, or order of the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code, which refuses to grant an application for a permit or makes any other decision pursuant or related to this code, may appeal in writing for a variance to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Board of Appeals for Construction*. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the code or the rules governing construction have been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of the code do not apply, or an equal or better form of construction is proposed. As provided for in Section 8-1-15 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, the decision of the Board of Appeals is final and neither the City nor the applicant may appeal the decision.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a variance where the person or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., *Government Organization and Employees*; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

laws.title: Construction, installation, alteration, repair, and dismantling
laws.content:
(a) All mechanical equipment covered by this article, with the exception of the foundations, tower sections and guide rails that are permanently attached to the tower sections, shall be constructed or installed by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, except when construction or installation is made by, or under the direct supervision of, the manufacturer of the material hoist. All alterations to material hoists shall be made only by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

(b) The actual work of construction, installation, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting, inspection, or dismantling of any material hoist covered by this article, shall be done by, or under the immediate supervision of, a person who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

laws.title: Existing installations
laws.content: Where in good repair, existing installations may be continued in their present form, provided, that such installations present no apparent hazard through methods of installation or operation or in their design. Where alterations or changes are proposed or made, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to prohibit such alteration or to require such other additions and alterations or changes as the Department deems necessary for the safe operation of such altered equipment. Where, in the opinion of the Department, such existing installation is found to be in a dangerous condition, or where the design or method of operation in combination with devices used is considered inherently dangerous or where there is an immediate hazard to those riding on or using such equipment, it shall be the duty of the Department to make or order such tests or inspections as are deemed necessary to determine the condition of the equipment and to order such alterations or additions as are deemed necessary to eliminate the existing dangerous condition.

laws.title: Electrical requirements
laws.content:
(a) The maximum system or circuit potential permitted on any equipment in the hoistway or on the hoist shall be not more than 600 volts. Where the potential exceeds 120 volts, either a grounding conductor shall be incorporated in the traveling cable or a separate grounding conductor shall be installed. A visual indicator shall be included in the grounding circuit, so arranged as to indicate continuously the continuity of the grounding conductor. The type and size of the grounding conductor and the grounding fastening means shall conform to the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. The grounding circuit shall include a device which will interrupt the electric circuit to the load in the event of a ground fault.

(b) All electrical equipment and wiring, including the main disconnect switch in or adjacent to the machinery and control space of the material hoist, shall be installed in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. All other electrical equipment and wiring that are within the scope of this article shall be installed and serviced by, or under the immediate supervision of, a person who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

laws.title: Inspection and approval required before putting into service
laws.content:
No person shall put into service any material hoist that shall hereafter be constructed, installed, rebuilt or altered until the material hoist shall have been inspected

CD8:282

laws.title: Responsibility for equipment; notification of defects; servicing
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist shall be responsible for the care, operation, and maintenance of the equipment covered by this article. Such registrant shall cause to be made periodic inspections and to maintain in proper working order the equipment covered by this article.

(b) It shall be the duty of any individual who is employed as an operator of the material hoist, an unlimited-elevator journeyperson licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, or an inspector from an insurance company authorized to do business in this state to promptly notify the person in charge of any equipment covered by this article, and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, any defects known to the individual that affect the safe operation of the equipment.

(c) No person shall knowingly use or permit or cause the use of any material hoist having defects affecting the safe operation thereof. No person shall alter, repair, or make adjustments on any material hoist or the machinery thereof while such hoist is available for use by persons other than the persons installing, altering, repairing, inspecting or maintaining the material hoist or the machinery thereof.

(d) All material hoists shall be inspected and serviced by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City, at such periods as may be necessary, but not less than once every 30 days, to maintain the equipment in a safe operating condition.

laws.title: Frequency of inspections; payment required when service rendered
Right of entry for inspection
laws.content:
(a) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this article, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist, or the owner or an authorized agent of the owner, of any building in the City where any equipment covered under this article is installed, or any building, premises, or structure that is owned, operated, or maintained by the City, shall permit and assist the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code, or any designated and authorized inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, to enter the building and to make inspections of any equipment during reasonable hours subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures.

(b) Where access to the location of equipment covered under this article is denied by the registrant or the owner of the equipment, or where access is otherwise not obtained, the Department may pursue recourse, as provided by law, to conduct an investigation pursuant to this article. Accordingly, the registrant and the owner shall be responsible for making arrangements for access to the site and equipment to facilitate the completion of any inspection.

DETROIT CITY CODE

**Sec. 8-11-44. Interference with Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department personnel prohibited.**

Any person who refuses to comply with this article, or assists in the violation of any provision of this article, or in any manner hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents or interferes with any designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in the performance of any duty imposed by this article, or refuses to permit such inspector to perform their duties by barring entrance at reasonable hours to buildings or premises for the purpose of enforcement of this article, shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Section 8-11-3 of this Code.

**Sec. 8-11-45. Approval of overtime inspection required.**

In order to obtain an inspection by Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours, the responsible party shall provide a letter to the Department for its approval prior to the service being rendered.

**Sec. 8-11-46. Reports of inspectors.**

A designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall make a written report of each inspection and file same in the records of the Department. When requested, a copy of such report shall be mailed to the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or to the owner of the equipment.

**Sec. 8-11-47. Equipment found unsafe.**

Where, upon inspection of a material hoist covered by this article, such equipment is found in an unsafe condition, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve a written notice of the findings upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or the owner stating a time when repairs must be completed, provided, that, where the required work is, or repairs are, in the nature of an emergency, the neglect of which would endanger human life, the material hoist shall be sealed out of service as provided for in Section 8-11-48 of this Code and such work or repairs ordered to be done at once. After the serving of such notice, it shall be the duty of the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or the owner to proceed within the time allowed to make such repairs or changes as are necessary to place said material hoist in a safe condition, and it shall be unlawful to operate such equipment after the date stated in such notice, except where an extension of time, in writing, has been secured from the Department, unless such repairs and changes have been made and the equipment approved by the Department.

**Sec. 8-11-48. Authority to seal material hoist out of service.**

In addition to the penalties provided for in Section 8-11-3 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to seal out any material hoist covered by this article for the following reasons:

(1) For failure to secure a Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or to renew such Certificate; or

(2) When in case of emergency, in the opinion of the designated inspector of the Department, any material hoist covered by this article is in such condition as to render the equipment unsafe for operation; or

(3) For willful failure to comply with the notice issued by the Department for the correction of a violation.

**Sec. 8-11-49. Notice of sealing out of service.**

(a) Except in the case of an emergency, before sealing out of service any material hoist, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve written notice upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or the owner of the equipment, which provides that the Department intends to seal the equipment out of service and the reason or reasons for such action.

(b) Where in the case of an emergency and the continued use of equipment creates the possibility of danger to the public, a written notice shall be served stating that the equipment has been taken out of service and the reason or reasons for such action.

**Sec. 8-11-50. Labeling material hoist out of service; unlawful to deface of remove sign or tag or to remove seal.**

(a) Any material hoist sealed out of service by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall be conspicuously labeled with a sign or tag indicating the reason for such shutdown.

laws.title: Holder of Certificate of Registration or owner of equipment to notify City of accident
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist, or the owner of the equipment, shall notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department within one business day after receiving a report of an accident as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code.

(b) Upon reasonable notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist, or the owner of the equipment, shall provide the Department access to facilitate an investigation of any equipment that was involved in the accident as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code.

laws.title: Accident inspection
laws.content: Upon notification of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department of an accident, as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code, by the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist, or by the owner of such equipment, an inspection shall be made of the equipment.

laws.title: Unlawful to use equipment following accident until approval
laws.content:
Where an accident, as defined in Section 8-11-11 of this Code, involves the failure, breakage, damage, or destruction of any part of the apparatus or mechanism of the device that affects the safe operation of the equipment, it shall be unlawful to repair or service, or use, the equipment until after an investigation, inspection and approval by a designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for the continued use of such equipment.

laws.title: Operator required
laws.content: Each material hoist shall be operated only by an operator who is assigned to this duty by the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or by a person having control or management of the material hoist.

laws.title: Qualifications of operators
laws.content:
An operator shall:

(1) Be 21 years of age or older;

(2) Be physically able to load and operate the equipment; and

(3) Be selected with consideration for his or her ability to perform their duties in a careful and competent manner.

laws.title: Instructions to operators
Procedure during repairs or alterations
laws.content: The operator shall place the material hoist out of service during the course of alterations, raising or lowering the height of the tower, adjustments, repairs, servicing or inspection. During the course of this work, the operator shall operate the hoist only in response to directions from the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. The operator shall not return the material hoist to service until this work has been completed and has been given permission to do so by the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City.

laws.title: Overloading prohibited
laws.content: An operator shall not permit the load on the material hoist to exceed the maximum rated load established by the manufacturer.

laws.title: Responsibility of holder of Certificate of Registration
laws.content: It shall be the responsibility of the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist to ensure that the operator is not under the influence of alcohol or drugs, operates the personnel hoist in a safe manner, and carries out the obligations assigned to him or her under the provisions of this article.

laws.title: Regulation of operators
laws.content:
(a) Where any operator is found making repairs, adjustments or otherwise tampering with controls or safety devices of a material hoist, is operating a material hoist in a manner dangerous to life, or is observed operating a material hoist while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, a designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to bar the operator from operating any material hoist in the City.

(b) It is a violation of this section for any person who is barred under Subsection (a) of this section to operate or to seek employment to operate a material hoist in the City unless reinstated by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(c) After written notice of the action taken under Subsection (a) of this section has been served by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Material Hoist or the owner of the equipment, it is a violation to permit any person who is barred from operating a material hoist under Subsection (a) of this section and has not been reinstated by the Department to operate a material hoist.

(d) An operator who is barred from operating a material hoist under Subsection (a) of this section may appeal such order to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Board of Appeals for Construction.

laws.title: Additions to Section 5 of ASSE Standard, Construction of Towers, Masts and Hoistway Enclosures
laws.content:
Section 5 of ASSE Standard, Construction of Towers, Masts and Hoistway Enclosures is amended to read as follows:

5.3.1. Hoists Located Outside of Structures. For hoists located outside of structures, the enclosures, except those at the lowest landing, may be omitted on the sides where there is no floor, ladders, stairways or scaffold adjacent to the hoistway. Enclosures on the building side of the hoistway shall be full height or a minimum of eight feet (2.44 m) high at each floor landing, and the enclosure shall extend not less than 30 inches (76.2 cm) on either side of the moving car or counterweight. Enclosures at the pit shall not be less than eight feet (2.44 m) high on all sides of the moving car or counterweight. Personnel hoists may share a multiple or common hoistway only with other personnel hoists.

5.4.8. Personnel hoistways shall have a minimum separation of ten feet (3.05 m) from any material hoistway, which is measured horizontally between adjacent vertical supports from the hoistway of any construction or material hoists.

(Code 1964, § 5.1; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(5.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Permit required; application; emergency alterations; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions

Such a permit shall not be issued until after the unlimited-elevator contractor has filed with the Department an application on a form provided by the Department, which is accompanied by detailed plans and specifications showing the proposed construction, installation, or alteration.

laws.title: Construction, installation, alteration, repair, and removal
laws.content:
(a) All mechanical equipment covered by this article, with the exception of the foundations, tower sections and guide rails that are permanently attached to the tower sections, shall be constructed or installed by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City, except when construction or installation is made by, or under the direct supervision of, the manufacturer of the personnel hoist. All alterations to personnel hoists shall be made only by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City.

(b) The actual work of construction, installation, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting, inspection or removal of any personnel hoist covered by this article, shall hereafter be done by, or under the immediate supervision of, a person who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson. (Code 1964, § 3.1; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Existing installations
laws.content: Where in good repair, existing installations may be continued in their present form, provided, that such installations present no apparent hazard through methods of installation or operation or in their design. Where alterations or changes are proposed or made, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to prohibit such alteration or to require such other additions and alterations or changes as the Department deems necessary for the safe operation of such altered equipment. Where, in the opinion of the Department, such existing installation is found to be in a dangerous condition, or where the design or method of operation in combination with devices used is considered inherently dangerous or where there is an immediate hazard to those riding on or using such equipment, it shall be the duty of the Department to make or order such tests or inspections as are deemed necessary to determine the condition of the equipment and to order such alterations or additions as are deemed necessary to eliminate the existing dangerous condition.

laws.title: Electrical requirements
laws.content:
(a) The maximum system or circuit potential permitted on any equipment in the hoistway or on the hoist shall be not more than 600 volts. Where the potential exceeds 120 volts, either a grounding conductor shall be incorporated in the traveling cable or a separate grounding conductor shall be installed. A visual indicator shall be included in the grounding circuit, so arranged as to indicate continuously the continuity of the grounding conductor. The type and size of the grounding conductor and the grounding fastening means shall conform to the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. The grounding circuit shall include a device which will interrupt the electric circuit to the load in the event of a ground fault.

(b) All electrical equipment and wiring, including the main disconnect switch in or adjacent to the machinery and control space of the personnel hoist, shall be installed in accordance with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Electrical Code*. All other electrical equipment and wiring that are within the scope of this article shall be installed and serviced by, or under the immediate supervision of, a person who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyman. (Code 1964, § 5.5; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(5.5), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 567-H, § 1(5.5), eff. 11-9-1983)

laws.content:

**Sec. 8-12-34. Inspection and approval required before putting into service.**

No person shall put into service any personnel hoist that shall hereafter be constructed, installed, rebuilt or altered until the personnel hoist shall have been inspected and approved by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and a Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist is issued by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 3.2; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Secs. 8-12-35—8-12-40. Reserved.**

laws.title: Maintenance, Inspection, and Enforcement
laws.content:
**Sec. 8-12-41. Responsibility for equipment; notification of defects; servicing.**

(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist shall be responsible for the care, operation, and maintenance of equipment covered by this article. Such registrant shall cause to be made periodic inspections and to maintain in proper working order all equipment covered by this article.

(b) It shall be the duty of any individual who is employed as an operator of the personnel hoist, an unlimited-elevator journeyperson licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, or an inspector from an insurance company authorized to do business in this state to promptly notify the individual in charge of any equipment covered by this article, and to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, any defects known to the individual that affect the safe operation of the equipment.

(c) No person shall knowingly use or permit or cause the use of any personnel hoist having defects affecting the safe operation thereof. No person shall alter, repair, or make adjustments on any personnel hoist, or its equipment, while such hoist is available for use by persons other than those installing, altering, repairing, inspecting or maintaining the personnel hoist or its equipment.

(d) All personnel hoists shall be inspected and maintained by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, at such periods as may be necessary, but not less than once every 30 days, to ensure that the equipment is performing in a safe operating condition.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.4, 3.5; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.4, 3.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-42. Frequency of inspections; payment required when service rendered.**

(a) The Building Official, as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code, and designated employees of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department are authorized:

(1) To make inspections and tests of any new construction or installation of, or any alteration to, personnel hoists;

(2) To inspect personnel hoists every three months;

(3) To make or cause to be made such other inspections and tests as are deemed necessary for the purpose of safety and the enforcement of this article; and

(4) To issue orders for alterations, repairs, and the correction of unsafe conditions and violations of this article.

(b) Unless previously made, any payment for an inspection shall be made, as required by Section 8-12-24 of this Code, at the time that the service is rendered.

(Code 1964, § 4.1; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.1), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 567-H, § 1(4.1), eff. 11-9-1983)

**Sec. 8-12-43. Right of entry for inspection.**

(a) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this article, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, the owner, or an authorized agent of the owner, of any building in the City where any equipment covered under this article is constructed, installed or removed, or any building, premises or structure that is owned, operated or maintained by the City, shall permit and assist the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code, or any designated and authorized inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, to enter the building to make inspections of any equipment during reasonable hours subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures.

(b) Where access to the location of equipment covered under this article is denied by the registrant or the owner of the equipment, or where access is otherwise not

obtained, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may pursue recourse, as provided by law, to conduct an investigation pursuant to this article. Accordingly, the registrant, and the owner, shall be responsible for making arrangements for access to the site and equipment to facilitate the completion of any inspection.

(Code 1964, § 4.0; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-44. Interference with Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department personnel prohibited.**

Any person who refuses to comply with this article, or assists in the violation of any provision of this article, or in any manner hinders, obstructs, delays, resists, prevents or interferes with any designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in the performance of any duty imposed by this article, or refuses to permit such inspector to perform their duties by barring entrance at reasonable hours to buildings or premises for the purpose of enforcement of this article, shall be subject to the penalties provided for in Section 8-12-3 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 7.1; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(7.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-45. Approval of overtime inspection required.**

In order to obtain an inspection by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department during periods other than regular working hours, the responsible party shall provide a letter to the Department for its approval prior to the service being rendered.

(Code 1964, § 3.9; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.9), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-46. Reports of inspectors.**

A designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall make a written report of each inspection and file same in the records of the Department. When requested, a copy of such report shall be mailed to the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, or to the owner.

(Code 1964, § 4.2; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-47. Equipment found unsafe.**

Where, upon inspection of equipment covered by this article, the equipment is found in an unsafe condition, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve a written notice of the findings upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist or the owner stating a time when repairs must be completed, provided, that, where the required work is, or repairs are, in the nature of an emergency and the neglect of which would endanger human life, the equipment shall be sealed out of service as provided for in Section 8-12-48 of this Code and such work or repairs ordered to be done at once. After the serving of such notice, it shall be the duty of the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, or the owner, to proceed within the time allowed to make such repairs or changes as are necessary to place said equipment in a safe condition, and it shall be unlawful to operate such equipment after the date stated in such notice, except where an extension of time, in writing, has been secured from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, unless such repairs and changes have been made and the equipment approved by the Department.

(Code 1964, § 4.3; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-48. Authority to seal personnel hoist out of service.**

In addition to the penalties provided for in Section 8-12-3 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to seal out of service any personnel hoist covered by this article for the following reasons:

(1) For failure to secure a Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist or to renew such Certificate; or

(2) When in case of emergency, in the opinion of the designated inspector of the Department, any personnel hoist covered by this article is in such condition as to render the equipment unsafe for operation; or

(3) For willful failure to comply with the notice issued by the Department for the correction of violations.

(Code 1964, § 4.4; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

**Sec. 8-12-49. Notice of sealing out of service.**

Except in the case of an emergency, before sealing out of service any personnel hoist covered by this article, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall serve written notice upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist or

laws.title: Labeling personnel hoist out of service; unlawful to deface or remove sign or tag or to remove seal
laws.content:
(a) Any personnel hoist sealed out of service by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall be conspicuously labeled with a sign or tag indicating the reason for such shutdown.

(b) It shall be a violation of this section:

(1) To deface a sign or tag posted under Subsection (a) of this section; or

(2) To remove a sign or tag posted under Subsection (a) of this section without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department; or

(3) To tamper with, or remove, a seal that is installed under Subsection (a) of this section without the approval of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.  
(Code 1964, § 4.6; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(4.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Holder of Certificate of Registration or owner of equipment to notify City of accident
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, or the owner of the equipment, shall notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department within one business day after receiving a report of an accident as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code.

(b) Upon reasonable notice from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, or the owner of the equipment, shall provide the Department access to facilitate an investigation of the equipment that was involved in the accident as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code.  
(Code 1964, § 3.6; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Accident inspection
laws.content: Upon notification of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department of an accident, as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code, by the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist, or by the owner of such equipment, an inspection shall be made of the equipment.

laws.title: Unlawful to use equipment following accident until approval
laws.content:
Where an accident, as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code, involves the failure, breakage, damage, or destruction of any part of the apparatus or mechanism that affects the safe operation of the equipment, it shall be unlawful to repair or service, or use the equipment until investigation, inspection and approval by a designated inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for continued use of such equipment.  
(Code 1964, § 3.7; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(3.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Operator required
laws.content:
Each personnel hoist shall have stationed within the car, and shall be operated only by, an operator, as defined in Section 8-12-11 of this Code.  
(Code 1964, § 6.0; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Qualifications of operators
laws.content:
An operator shall:

(1) Be 21 years of age or older;

(2) Be physically able to load and operate the equipment; and

(3) Be selected with consideration for their ability to perform his or her duties in a careful and competent manner.  
(Code 1964, § 6.2; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Responsibility of holder of Certificate of Registration
laws.content:
It shall be the responsibility of the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist to ensure that the operator is not under the influence of alcohol or drugs, operates the personnel hoist in a safe manner, and carries out the obligations assigned to him or her under the provisions of this article.  
(Code 1964, § 6.1; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Instructions to operators
Procedure during repairs or alterations
laws.content:
The operator shall place the personnel hoist out of service during the course of alterations, raising or lowering the height of the tower, adjustments, repairs, servicing or inspection. During the course of this work, the operator shall operate the hoist only in response to directions from the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City. The operator shall not return the personnel hoist to service until this work has been completed and has been given permission to do so by the unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City.

(Code 1964, § 6.4; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.4), eff. 3-2-1979)

CD8:296

laws.title: Operation and communication system
laws.content:
(a) A personnel hoist shall be operated by an operator stationed in the hoist using either a car switch or constant pressure-type switches located in the hoist, which must be held manually in the closed position by the operator in order to permit operation of the driving machine and which will open automatically when released by the operator.

(b) An approved intercom system shall be installed inside the personnel hoist and on each landing served by the hoist, provided, that such system shall not include cell phones, radios, or walkie-talkies.

(Code 1964, § 6.5; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Authorized passengers
laws.content:
The only persons permitted to ride on personnel hoists are workers or other authorized personnel associated with the work being done.

(Code 1964, § 6.6; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Use of personnel hoist for carrying materials
laws.content:
A personnel hoist may be used for carrying materials, provided, that:

(1) The hoist is designed, constructed, and installed for the type of loading to be used;

(2) During the time that materials are being carried, only workers necessary to handle the materials shall be carried; and

(3) The materials and any passengers do not exceed the maximum rated established by the manufacturer.

(Code 1964, § 6.7; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Overloading prohibited
laws.content:
An operator shall not permit the load on the personnel hoist to exceed the maximum rated load established by the manufacturer.

(Code 1964, § 6.8; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.8), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Regulation of operators
laws.content:
(a) Where any operator is found making repairs, adjustments or otherwise tampering with controls or safety devices of a personnel hoist, is operating a personnel hoist in a manner dangerous to life, or is observed operating a personnel hoist while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, a designated inspector of the Buildings,

Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to bar the operator from operating any personnel hoist in the City.

(b) It is a violation of this section for any person who is barred under Subsection (a) of this section to operate or to seek employment to operate a personnel hoist in the City unless reinstated by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(c) After written notice of the action taken under Subsection (a) of this section has been served by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department upon the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Personnel Hoist or the owner of the equipment, it is a violation to permit any person who is barred from operating a personnel hoist under Subsection (a) of this section and has not been reinstated by the Department to operate a personnel hoist.

(d) An operator who is barred from operating a personnel hoist under Subsection (a) of this section may appeal such order to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Board of Appeals for Construction.

(Code 1964, § 6.2; Ord. No. 309-H, § 1(6.2), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Purpose, scope, and applicability
laws.content:
(a) In order to provide for the safety of life and limb as well as of others who may be exposed, this article covers the design, construction, installation, registration, alteration, inspection, testing, maintenance, operation, and repairing of permanent installations of powered platforms in the City of Detroit. Where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of this article will result in unnecessary hardship or involve practical difficulties, the Board of Appeals shall have the authority, upon appeal in specific cases, to authorize a variance, or to modify the requirements of this article so that the results will not be contrary to the public interest and so that the intent of this article shall be observed, public safety secured, and substantial justice done.

(b) Powered platforms are permitted to be used in the City only for the purposes of window washing or maintenance to the exterior of buildings.

(Code 1964, §§ 1.0, 1.2, 1.6; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(1.0, 1.2, 1.6), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
(a) Any person, or anyone acting in behalf of said person, who violates any provision of this article, shall be subject, upon conviction thereof, to a fine or not more than $500.00 or to imprisonment for a period of not more than 90 days, or to both such fine and imprisonment in the discretion of the court.

(b) Each day that a violation of this article continues or is permitted to exist without compliance shall constitute a separate offense punishable upon conviction in the manner prescribed in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1964, § 6.0; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(6.0), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Additions to Section 3 of ASME Standard, Equipment Design and Construction Requirements
laws.content:
Section 3 of the ASME Standard, Equipment Design and Construction Requirements, is amended to read as follows: 3.1.4.1 Sign required on platform. The manufacturer shall permanently and conspicuously affix a metal sign with letters at least one-half inch in height on the platform, indicating the maximum loads, which shall read as follows: **MAXIMUM CAPACITY** **PERSONS: [MAXIMUM NUMBER]** Materials and equipment: Only those necessary for window washing, exterior building maintenance, or inspection and maintenance of the hoist. Max. Concentrated Load: ________ Max. Capacity Load: ________ 3.3.3 Operating Controls for Powered Roof Carriage. [Subsections (a) and (b)] (c) Powered platforms designed for use by two individuals shall be provided with two continuous pressure, weatherproof, electric type controls. The platform shall be provided with an approved means of preventing the platform from inclining more than eight degrees out of level and/or an approved alarm which will sound when the platform inclines eight degrees or more out of level. 3.10.9 Replacement of wire ropes. The wire ropes used in hoisting the powered platform shall be replaced whenever there are six or more broken wires in any one lay of the wire rope, or whenever the ropes are damaged or in a deteriorated condition, but in any case at intervals not in excess of the following:
Drum or Sheave Diameter/Rope Diameter Ratio Replacement-Maximum Interval
10 to less than 20 18 months
20 to less than 30 24 months
30 to less than 40 30 months
40 and over 36 months
3.10.10 Four-point suspension required. Powered platforms shall be suspended by at least four wire ropes attached at points not more than 25 percent of the length of the platform measured from each end of the platform, provided, that the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may accept two wire ropes used for actually hoisting the platform if a least two other wire ropes, serving as approved safety back-up suspension means in the judgment of the Department, are installed. (Code 1964, §§ 5.2, 5.3, 5.6, 5.7; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(5.2, 5.3, 5.6, 5.7), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Addition to Section 5 of ASME Standard, Inspections, Tests, Operation, and Maintenance
laws.content:
Section 5 of the ASME Standard, Inspections, Tests, Operation, and Maintenance, is amended to read as follows:

5.2.3 Riders, materials, and equipment. No more than two individuals shall ride on any powered platform, except where special permission has been obtained from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department in specific instances to allow for more than two individuals to ride. Materials and equipment that are carried on any powered platform shall include only those items necessary for window washing, maintenance to the exterior of a building, or inspection and maintenance of hoisting equipment.

(Code 1964, § 5.1; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(5.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Permit required; application; emergency alterations; persons ineligible to apply for permit; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) A permit to construct, install, or alter any powered platform in the City shall only be issued to an unlimited-elevator contractor licensed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code. Such a permit shall not be issued until after the unlimited-elevator contractor has filed with the Department an application on a form provided by the Department, which is accompanied by detailed plans and specifications showing the proposed installation or alteration.

(b) In case of emergency alterations, the permit shall be obtained within 72 hours from the time of alteration. Ordinary repairs and replacements may be made in accordance with the provisions of this article without filing such application.

(c) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that an unlimited-elevator contractor is not eligible to apply for a permit where the unlimited-elevator contractor, or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure, is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

(i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

(ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

(iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

(iv) Is a financial institution with power:

A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

(a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

(b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

(c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., Government Organization and Employees; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings and loan association, savings bank, or credit union whose deposits are insured by an agency of the United States government and that maintains a principal office or branch office in this state under the laws of this state or the United States;

c. A mortgage servicer, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651a, meaning a person that, directly or indirectly, services or offers to service mortgage loans and that is subject to the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, being MCL 445.1651 to 445.1684; or

d. A credit union service organization that is organized under the laws of this state or the United States.

(d) An unlimited-elevator contractor against whom any fee is assessed is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until payment of the outstanding fee is made to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(e) An unlimited-elevator contractor against whom any Notice of Violation is pending is not eligible to apply for an additional permit until there is compliance with the outstanding Notice of Violation unless the unlimited-elevator contractor can demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that the failure to comply was due to conditions or circumstances beyond his or her control.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.0, 602.7; Code 1984, § 9-2-5; Ord. No. 256-H, § 1(602.7), eff. 6-23-1978; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(3.0), eff. 3-2-1979; Ord. No. 24-16, § 1(9-2-5), eff. 8-1-2016)

laws.title: Certificate of Registration required; annual renewal; posting
laws.content:
(a) A person shall not use, or cause to be used, any equipment covered under this article that requires a periodic inspection under Section 8-13-42 of this Code without first securing a Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(b) Where equipment is installed under current installation permit requirements and has not been subject to a periodic inspection by the Department, a Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform will be issued by the Department without a fee after inspection and approval of the equipment. The Certificate of Registration shall be renewed in accordance with Subsection (c) of this section.

(c) The Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform shall be renewed annually on or before May 31st upon payment of the non-refundable fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-13-21 of this Code.

(d) Upon issuance, the current, original Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform shall be posted in a conspicuous place inside an office that is accessible during business hours for observation by an authorized representative of the Department.

(Code 1964, § 3.3; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(3.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Payment of fees for permits and inspections
laws.content:
Any fee that is established and approved in accordance with Section 8-13-21 of this Code for the issuance of a permit, or for a required inspection, under this

laws.title: Building Construction and Property Maintenance

article shall be paid to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at the time that the permit is issued or the inspection is made.

(Code 1964, § 3.3; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(3.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Appeals from decisions, determinations, or orders; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) An interested person, or the person’s authorized agent, aggrieved by a decision, determination, or order of the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-13-11 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, which refuses to grant an application for a permit or makes any other decision pursuant or related to this code, may appeal in writing for a variance to the Board of Appeals in accordance with Chapter 8, Article I, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, *Board of Appeals for Construction*. An application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the code or the rules governing construction have been incorrectly interpreted, the provisions of the code do not apply, or an equal or better form of construction is proposed. As provided for in Section 8-1-15 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, the decision of the Board of Appeals is final and neither the City nor the applicant may appeal the decision.

(b) As permitted under Section 9c of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act, being MCL 125.1509c, the City enacts, through this provision, that a person is not eligible to apply for a variance where the person or the owner of the affected or proposed building or structure is delinquent in paying a civil fine, costs, or a justice system assessment imposed by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau established under Section 3-2-51 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, provided, that:

(1) This prohibition does not apply to an application for a permit where the work authorized under the permit will correct, in whole or in part, the blight violation that was the subject of the delinquent payment; and

(2) This prohibition does not apply to an applicant where the applicant became the owner of the property by foreclosure or by taking a deed in lieu of foreclosure and is one of the following:

a. 1. A government-sponsored enterprise as likewise defined in 2 USC 622(8) meaning a corporate entity created by a law of the United States that:

    (i) Has a federal charter authorized by law;

    (ii) Is privately owned, as evidenced by capital stock owned by private entities or individuals;

    (iii) Is under the direction of a board of directors, a majority of which is elected by private owners;

    (iv) Is a financial institution with power:

        A. To make loans or loan guarantees for limited purposes such as to provide credit for specific borrowers or one sector; and

        B. To raise funds by borrowing, which does not carry the full faith and credit of the Federal Government, or to guarantee the debt of others in unlimited amounts; and:

            (a) Does not exercise powers that are reserved to the Government as sovereign, such as the power to tax or to regulate interstate commerce;

            (b) Does not have the power to commit the Government financially, but it may be a recipient of a loan guarantee commitment made by the Government; and

            (c) Has employees whose salaries and expenses are paid by the enterprise and are not federal employees subject to 5 USC 1 et seq., *Government Organization and Employees*; or

2. The Michigan State Housing Development Authority created under the State Housing Development Authority Act of 1966, being MCL 125.1401 to 125.1499c;

b. A financial institution, as likewise defined in Section 4(c) of the Michigan Strategic Fund Act, being MCL 125.2004(c), meaning a state or nationally chartered bank or a state or federally chartered savings

laws.title: Installation, alteration, and repair of powered platforms
laws.content:
(a) All mechanical equipment with the exception of the roof-car rails or tracks and guide rails, and all electrical work in the equipment up to the power outlet boxes on the roof, shall be installed by a an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code or by, or under, the direct supervision of the manufacturer of the powered platform. All alterations to a powered platform shall be made only by an unlimited-elevator contractor who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-55 of the 2019 Detroit City Code.

(b) Unless otherwise provided for in this article, electrical and mechanical equipment and work shall comply with the requirements of Chapter 8, Article IX, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Detroit Elevator Code.

(c) No installation, except as provided for in Subsection (a) of this section, alteration, repair, servicing, adjusting, or inspection shall be done on any device covered by this article, except by, or under, the immediate supervision of an individual who is licensed by the City as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, or by an employee of the manufacturer who has credentials to perform such work. (Code 1964, § 3.1; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(3.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Existing installations
laws.content: Where in good repair, existing installations may be continued in their present form, provided, that such installations present no apparent hazard through methods of installation or operation or in their design. Where alterations or changes are proposed or made, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to prohibit such alteration or to require such other additions and alterations or changes as the Department deems necessary for the safe operation of such altered equipment. Where, in the opinion of the Department, such existing installation is found to be in a dangerous condition, or where the design or method of operation in combination with devices used is considered inherently dangerous or where there is an immediate hazard to those riding on or using such equipment, it shall be the duty of the Department to make or order such tests or inspections as are deemed necessary to determine the condition of the equipment and to order such alterations or additions as are deemed necessary to eliminate the existing dangerous condition. (Code 1964, § 1.3; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(1.3), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Electrical requirements
laws.content: All electrical work, other than as specified in Section 8-13-25 of this Code, including the power outlet boxes on the roof, shall be done in accordance with Chapter 8, Article III, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Electrical Code. (Code 1964, § 5.8; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(5.8), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Structural requirements
laws.content: The load carrying capacity of the building roof shall meet the requirements of Chapter 8, Article II, of the 2019 Detroit City Code, Building Code. (Code 1964, § 5.9; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(5.9), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Inspection and approval required before putting into service
laws.content:
No person shall put into service any powered platform that shall hereafter be constructed, installed, rebuilt, or altered until the powered platform has been

CD8:304

laws.title: Responsibility for equipment; notification of defects; servicing
laws.content:
(a) The holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform shall be responsible for the care, operation, and maintenance of equipment covered by this article. Such registrant shall cause to be made periodic inspections and to maintain in proper working order all equipment covered by this article.

(b) It shall be the duty of any individual employed as an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, is an individual working under the direct supervision of an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, or is an inspector employed by an insurance company authorized to do business in this state to promptly notify the person in charge of any equipment covered by this article, and to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, any defects known to the individual that affect the safe operation of the equipment.

(c) No person shall knowingly use or permit or cause the use of any powered platform having defects affecting the safe operation thereof. No person shall alter, repair, or make adjustments on any powered platform or its equipment while such platform is available for use by persons other than those installing, altering, repairing, inspecting, or maintaining the powered platform or its equipment.

(d) All powered platforms shall be inspected and maintained by an unlimited-elevator journeyperson who is licensed by the City under Section 8-9-75 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, at periods as may be necessary, but not less than once every 90 days, to ensure that the equipment is performing in a safe operating condition.

(Code 1964, §§ 3.4, 3.5; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(3.4, 3.5), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Frequency of inspections; payment required when service rendered
laws.content:
(a) The Building Official, as defined in Section 8-13-11 of this Code, and designated employees of the Buildings, Safety Engineering and Environmental Department are authorized:

(1) To make inspections and tests of all new installations of, or alterations to, powered platforms;

(2) To inspect powered platforms every 12 months;

(3) To make or cause to be made such other inspections and tests as are deemed necessary for the purpose of safety and the enforcement of this article; and

(4) To issue orders for alterations, repairs, and the correction of unsafe conditions and violations of this article.

(b) Unless previously made, any payment for an inspection shall be made, as required by Section 8-13-24 of this Code, at the time that the service is rendered.

(Code 1964, § 4.1; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(4.1), eff. 3-2-1979)

laws.title: Right of entry for inspection
laws.content:
(a) For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this article, the holder of the Certificate of Registration for a Powered Platform, the owner, or an authorized agent of the owner, of any building in the City where any equipment covered under this article is installed, or any building, premises, or structure that is owned, operated, or maintained by the City, shall permit and assist the Building Official, as defined in Section 8-13-11 of this Code, or any designated and authorized inspector, to enter the building to make inspections of any equipment during reasonable hours subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures.

(b) Where access to the location of equipment covered under this article is denied by the registrant or the owner of the equipment, or where access is otherwise not obtained, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may pursue recourse, as provided by law, to conduct an investigation pursuant to this article. Accordingly, the registrant, and the owner, shall be responsible for making arrangements for access to the site and equipment to facilitate the completion of any inspection.

(Code 1964, § 4.0; Ord. No. 310-H, § 1(4.0), eff. 3-2-1979)
