§ 19-3-880

laws.title: Storage areas, redeeming machines, receptacles and waste handling units, location
laws.content:
(a) An area designated for refuse, recyclables, returnables, and, except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, a redeeming machine for recyclables or returnables shall be located so that it is separate from food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles and a public health hazard or nuisance is not created.

(b) A redeeming machine may be located in the packaged food storage area or consumer area of a food establishment if food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are not subject to contamination from the machines and a public health hazard or nuisance is not created.

(c) The location of receptacles and waste handling units for refuse, recyclables, and returnables may not create a public health hazard or nuisance or interfere with the cleaning of adjacent space.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.19)

laws.title: Storing refuse, recyclables, and returnables
laws.content:
Refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be stored in receptacles or waste handling units so that they are inaccessible to insects and rodents.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.110)

laws.title: Areas, enclosures, and receptacles, good repair
laws.content:
Storage areas, enclosures, and receptacles for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be maintained in good repair.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.111)

laws.title: Outside storage prohibitions
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, refuse receptacles not meeting the requirements specified under Section 19-3-854(a) of this Code such as receptacles that are not rodent-resistant, unprotected plastic bags and paper bags, or baled units that contain materials with food residue may not be stored outside.

(b) Cardboard or other packaging material that does not contain food residues and that is awaiting regularly scheduled delivery to a recycling or disposal site may be stored outside without being in a covered receptacle if it is stored so that it does not create a rodent harborage problem.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.112)

laws.title: Covering receptacles
laws.content:
Receptacles and waste handling units for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be kept covered:

(1) Inside the food establishment if the receptacles and units:

a. Contain food residue and are not in continuous use; or

b. After they are filled; and

(2) With tight-fitting lids or doors if kept outside the food establishment.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.113)

laws.title: Using drain plugs
laws.content:
Drains in receptacles and waste handling units for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall have drain plugs in place.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.114)

laws.title: Maintaining refuse areas and enclosures
laws.content:
A storage area and enclosure for refuse, recyclables, or returnables shall be maintained free of unnecessary items, as specified under Section 19-3-1084 of this Code, and clean.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.115)

laws.title: Cleaning receptacles
laws.content:
(a) Receptacles and waste handling units for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be thoroughly cleaned in a way that does not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single-service and single-use articles, and waste water shall be disposed of as specified under Section 19-3-834 of this Code.

(b) Soiled receptacles and waste handling units for refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent them from developing a buildup of soil or becoming attractants for insects and rodents.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-501.116)

Secs. 19-3-868—19-3-880. Reserved.

CD19:107
$\S 19-3-881$

DETROIT CITY CODE

laws.title: Frequency
laws.content:
Refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the premises at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-502.11)

laws.title: Receptacles or vehicles
laws.content:
Refuse, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the premises by way of:

(1) Portable receptacles that are constructed and maintained according to law; or

(2) A transport vehicle that is constructed, maintained, and operated according to law.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-502.12)

laws.title: Community or individual facility
laws.content:
Solid waste not disposed of through the sewage system such as through grinders and pulpers shall be recycled or disposed of in an approved public or private community recycling or refuse facility; or solid waste shall be disposed of in an individual refuse facility such as a landfill or incinerator which is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to law.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 5-503.11)

laws.title: Surface characteristics
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be:

(1) Smooth, durable, and easily cleanable for areas where food establishment operations are conducted;

(2) Closely woven and easily cleanable carpet for carpeted areas; and

(3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, warewashing areas, toilet rooms, mobile food establishment servicing areas, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

(b) In a temporary food establishment:

(1) If graded to drain, a floor may be concrete, machine-laid asphalt, or dirt or gravel if it is covered with mats, removable platforms, duckboards, or other approved materials that are effectively treated to control dust and mud; and

(2) Walls and ceilings may be constructed of a material that protects the interior from the weather and windblown dust and debris.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-101.11)

laws.title: Surface characteristics
laws.content:
(a) The outdoor walking and driving areas shall be surfaced with concrete, asphalt, or gravel or other materials that have been effectively treated to minimize dust, facilitate maintenance, and prevent muddy conditions.

(b) Exterior surfaces of buildings and mobile food establishments shall be of weather-resistant materials and shall comply with law.

(c) Outdoor storage areas for refuse, recyclables, or returnables shall be of materials specified under Sections 19-3-852 and 19-3-853 of this Code.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-102.11)

laws.title: Floors, walls, and ceilings
laws.content:
Except as specified under Section 19-3-924 of this Code and except for antislip floor coverings or applica-

CD19:108
FOOD

§ 19-3-941

tions that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.11)

laws.title: Floors, walls, and ceilings, utility lines
laws.content:
(a) Utility service lines and pipes may not be unnecessarily exposed.

(b) Exposed utility service lines and pipes shall be installed so they do not obstruct or prevent cleaning of the floors, walls, or ceilings.

(c) Exposed horizontal utility service lines and pipes may not be installed on the floor.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.12)

laws.title: Floor and wall junctures, coved, and enclosed or sealed
laws.content:
(a) In food establishments in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than one mm (one thirty-second inch).

(b) The floors in food establishments in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and sealed.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.13)

laws.title: Floor carpeting, restrictions and installation
laws.content:
(a) A floor covering such as carpeting or similar material may not be installed as a floor covering in food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, warewashing areas, toilet room areas where handwashing lavatories, toilets, and urinals are located, refuse storage rooms, or other areas where the floor is subject to moisture, flushing, or spray cleaning methods.

(b) If carpeting is installed as a floor covering in areas other than those specified under Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be:

(1) Securely attached to the floor with a durable mastic, by using a stretch and tack method, or by another method; and

(2) Installed tightly against the wall under the covering or installed away from the wall with a space between the carpet and the wall and with the edges of the carpet secured by metal stripping or some other means.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.14)

laws.title: Floor covering, mats and duckboards
laws.content:
Mats and duckboards shall be designed to be removable and easily cleanable.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.15)

laws.title: Wall and ceiling coverings and coatings
laws.content:
(a) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are easily cleanable.

(b) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and sealed to provide a smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable surface.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.15)

laws.title: Walls and ceilings, attachments
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, attachments to walls and ceilings such as light fixtures, mechanical room ventilation system components, vent covers, wall mounted fans, decorative items, and other attachments shall be easily cleanable.

(b) In a consumer area, wall and ceiling surfaces and decorative items and attachments that are provided for ambiance need not meet this requirement if they are kept clean.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.17)

laws.title: Walls and ceilings, studs, joists, and rafters
laws.content:
Except for temporary food establishments, studs, joists, and rafters may not be exposed in areas subject to moisture.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-201.18)

Secs. 19-3-929—19-3-940. Reserved.

Subdivision B. Functionality

laws.title: Light bulbs, protective shielding
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

CD19:109
§ 19-3-941

DETROIT CITY CODE

(b) Shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant bulbs need not be used in areas used only for storing food in unopened packages, if:

(1) The integrity of the packages cannot be affected by broken glass falling onto them; and

(2) The packages are capable of being cleaned of debris from broken bulbs before the packages are opened.

(c) An infrared or other heat lamp shall be protected against breakage by a shield surrounding and extending beyond the bulb so that only the face of the bulb is exposed.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.11)

laws.title: Heating, ventilating, air conditioning system vents
laws.content:
Heating, ventilating, and air conditioning systems shall be designed and installed so that make-up air intake and exhaust vents do not cause contamination of food, food-contact surfaces, equipment, or utensils.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.12)

laws.title: Insect control devices, design and installation
laws.content:
(a) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device.

(b) Insect control devices shall be installed so that:

(1) The devices are not located over a food preparation area; and

(2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.13)

laws.title: Toilet rooms, enclosed
laws.content:
Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the premises shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.14)

laws.title: Outer openings, protected
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsections (b), (c), and (e) of this section and under Subsection (d) of this section, outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by:

(1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings;

(2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and

(3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

(b) Subsection (a) of this section does not apply if a food establishment opens into a larger structure, such as a mall, airport, or office building, or into an attached structure, such as a porch, and the outer openings from the larger or attached structure are protected against the entry of insects and rodents.

(c) Exterior doors used as exits need not be self-closing if they are:

(1) Solid and tight-fitting;

(2) Designated for use only when an emergency exists, by the fire protection authority that has jurisdiction over the food establishment; and

(3) Limited-use so they are not used for entrance or exit from the building for purposes other than the designated emergency exit use.

(d) Except as specified in Subsections (b) and (e) of this section, if the windows or doors of a food establishment, or of a larger structure within which a food establishment is located, are kept open for ventilation or other purposes or a temporary food establishment is not provided with windows and doors as specified under Subsection (a) of this section, the openings shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by:

(1) 16 mesh to 25.4 mm (16 mesh to one inch) screens;

(2) Properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or

(3) Other effective means.

(e) Subsection (d) of this section does not apply if flying insects and other pests are absent due to the location of the establishment, the weather, or other limiting condition.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.15)

§ 19-3-964

laws.title: Exterior walls and roofs, protective barrier
laws.content: Perimeter walls and roofs of a food establishment shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.16)

laws.title: Outdoor food vending areas, overhead protection
laws.content: Except for machines that vend canned beverages, if located outside, a machine used to vend food shall be provided with overhead protection. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.17)

laws.title: Outdoor servicing areas, overhead protection
laws.content: Except for areas used only for the loading of water or the discharge of sewage and other liquid waste, through the use of a closed system of hoses, servicing areas shall be provided with overhead protection. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.18)

laws.title: Outdoor walking and driving surfaces, graded to drain
laws.content: Exterior walking and driving surfaces shall be graded to drain. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.19)

laws.title: Outdoor refuse areas, curbed and graded to drain
laws.content: Outdoor refuse areas shall be constructed in accordance with law and shall be curbed and graded to drain to collect and dispose of liquid waste that results from the refuse and from cleaning the area and waste receptacles. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.110)

laws.title: Private homes and living or sleeping quarters, use prohibition
laws.content: A private home, a room used as living or sleeping quarters, or an area directly opening into a room used as living or sleeping quarters may not be used for conducting food establishment operations. $^{P}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.111)

laws.title: Living or sleeping quarters, separation
laws.content:
Living or sleeping quarters located on the premises of a food establishment such as those provided for lodging registration clerks or resident managers shall be separated from rooms and areas used for food establishment operations by complete partitioning and solid self-closing doors. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-202.112)

Secs. 19-3-953—19-3-960. Reserved.

laws.title: Minimum number
laws.content: Handwashing sinks shall be provided as specified under Section 19-3-751 of this Code. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.10)

laws.title: Handwashing cleanser, availability
laws.content: Each handwashing sink or group of two adjacent handwashing sinks shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.$^{Pf}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.11)

laws.title: Hand drying provision
laws.content:
Each handwashing sink or group of adjacent handwashing sinks shall be provided with:

(1) Individual, disposable towels;$^{Pf}$

(2) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel;$^{Pf}$ or

(3) A heated-air hand drying device;$^{Pf}$ or

(4) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.$^{Pf}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.12)

laws.title: Handwashing aids and devices, use restrictions
laws.content:
A sink used for food preparation or utensil washing, or a service sink or curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water or similar wastes, may not be provided with the handwashing aids and devices required for a handwashing sink as specified under Sections 19-3-857(c), 19-3-962, and 19-3-963 of this Code. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.13)

CD19:111
§ 19-3-965

DETROIT CITY CODE

laws.title: Handwashing signage
laws.content:
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.14)

laws.title: Disposable towels, waste receptacle
laws.content:
A handwashing sink or group of adjacent handwashing sinks that is provided with disposable towels shall be provided with a waste receptacle as specified under Section 19-3-857(c) of this Code.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-301.20)]

Secs. 19-3-967—19-3-970. Reserved.

Subdivision B. Toilets and Urinals

laws.title: Minimum number
laws.content:
Toilets and urinals shall be provided as specified under Section 19-3-752 of this Code.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-302.10)

laws.title: Toilet tissue, availability
laws.content:
A supply of toilet tissue shall be available at each toilet.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-302.11)

Secs. 19-3-973—19-3-980. Reserved.

Subdivision C. Lighting

laws.title: Intensity
laws.content:
The light intensity shall be:

(1) At least 108 lux (ten footcandles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry food storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

(2) At least 215 lux (20 footcandles):

a. At a surface where food is provided for consumer self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or packaged foods are sold or offered for consumption;

b. Inside equipment such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and

c. At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, warewashing, and equipment and utensil storage, and in toilet rooms; and

(3) At least 540 lux (50 footcandles) at a surface where a food employee is working with food or working with utensils or equipment such as knives, slicers, grinders, or saws where employee safety is a factor.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-303.11)

Secs. 19-3-982—19-3-990. Reserved.

Subdivision D. Ventilation

laws.title: Mechanical
laws.content:
If necessary to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes, mechanical ventilation of sufficient capacity shall be provided.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-304.10)

Secs. 19-3-992—19-3-1000. Reserved.

Subdivision E. Dressing Areas and Lockers

laws.title: Designation
laws.content:
(a) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if employees routinely change their clothes in the establishment.

(b) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-305.11)

Secs. 19-3-1002—19-3-1010. Reserved.

Subdivision F. Service Sinks

laws.title: Availability
laws.content:
A service sink or curbed cleaning facility shall be provided as specified under Section 19-3-753(a) of this Code.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-306.10)

CD19:112
FOOD

§ 19-3-1073

Secs. 19-3-1012—19-3-1020. Reserved.

laws.title: Subdivision A. Handwashing Sinks
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1021. Conveniently located.**

Handwashing sinks shall be conveniently located as specified under Section 19-3-761 of this Code.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-401.10)

Secs. 19-3-1022—19-3-1030. Reserved.

laws.title: Subdivision B. Toilet Rooms
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1031. Convenience and accessibility.**

Toilet rooms shall be conveniently located and accessible to employees during all hours of operation.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-402.11)

Secs. 19-3-1032—19-3-1040. Reserved.

laws.title: Subdivision C. Employees Accommodations
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1041. Designated areas.**

(a) Areas designated for employees to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination.

(b) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles cannot occur.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-403.11)

Secs. 19-3-1042—19-3-1050. Reserved.

laws.title: Subdivision D. Distressed Merchandise
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1051. Segregation and location.**

Products that are held by the permit holder for credit, redemption, or return to the distributor, such as damaged, spoiled, or recalled products, shall be segregated and held in designated areas that are separated from food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles.$^{Pr}$  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-404.11)

Secs. 19-3-1052—19-3-1060. Reserved.

laws.title: Subdivision E. Refuse, Recyclables, and Returnables
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1061. Receptacles, waste handling units, and designated storage areas.**

Units, receptacles, and areas designated for storage of refuse and recyclable and returnable containers shall be located as specified under Section 19-3-860 of this Code.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-405.10)

Secs. 19-3-1062—19-3-1070. Reserved.

laws.title: Physical Facilities—maintenance and Operation
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1071. Repairing.**

Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.11)

**Sec. 19-3-1072. Cleaning, frequency and restrictions.**

(a) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

(b) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  
(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.12)

**Sec. 19-3-1073. Cleaning floors, dustless methods.**

(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, only dustless methods of cleaning shall be used, such as wet cleaning, vacuum cleaning, mopping with treated dust mops, or sweeping using a broom and dust-arresting compounds.

(b) Spills or drippage on floors that occur between normal floor cleaning times may be cleaned:

(1) Without the use of dust-arresting compounds; and

CD19:113
§ 19-3-1073

DETROIT CITY CODE

(2) In the case of liquid spills or drippage, with the use of a small amount of absorbent compound such as sawdust or diatomaceous earth applied immediately before spot cleaning.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.13)

laws.title: Cleaning ventilation systems, nuisance and discharge prohibition
laws.content:
(a) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials.

(b) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health hazard or nuisance or unlawful discharge.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.14)

laws.title: Cleaning maintenance tools, preventing contamination
laws.content:
Food preparation sinks, handwashing sinks, and warewashing equipment may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes. $^{Pf}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.15)

laws.title: Drying mops
laws.content:
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.16)

laws.title: Absorbent materials on floors, use limitation
laws.content:
Except as specified in Section 19-3-1073(b) of this Code, sawdust, wood shavings, granular salt, baked clay, diatomaceous earth, or similar materials may not be used on floors.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.17)

laws.title: Cleaning of plumbing fixtures
laws.content:
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.18)

laws.title: Closing toilet room doors
laws.content:
Except during cleaning and maintenance operations, toilet room doors as specified under Section 19-3-944 of this Code shall be kept closed.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.19)

laws.title: Using dressing rooms and lockers
laws.content:
(a) Dressing rooms shall be used by employees if the employees regularly change their clothes in the establishment.

(b) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.110)

laws.title: Controlling pests
Removing dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests
laws.content:
Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the premises at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.112)

laws.title: Storing maintenance tools
laws.content:
Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be:

(1) Stored so they do not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles; and

CD19:114
FOOD

§ 19-3-1110

(2) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.113)

laws.title: Maintaining premises, unnecessary items and litter
laws.content:
The premises shall be free of:

(1) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and

(2) Litter.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 6-501.114)

laws.title: Prohibiting animals
Identifying information, prominence
laws.content:
Containers of poisonous or toxic materials and personal care items shall bear a legible manufacturer’s label. $^{Pf}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-101.11)

Secs. 19-3-1092—19-3-1100. Reserved.

Subdivision B. Working Containers

laws.title: Common name
laws.content:
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. $^{Pf}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-102.11)

Secs. 19-3-1102—19-3-1110. Reserved.

CD19:115
$\S 19-3-1111$

DETROIT CITY CODE

laws.title: Subdivision A. Storage
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1111. Separation.**

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by:

(1) Separating the poisonous or toxic materials by spacing or partitioning; $^{\text{P}}$ and

(2) Locating the poisonous or toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service or single-use articles. This subsection does not apply to equipment and utensil cleaners and sanitizers that are stored in warewashing areas for availability and convenience if the materials are stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. $^{\text{P}}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-201.11)

**Secs. 19-3-1112—19-3-1120. Reserved.**

laws.title: Subdivision B. Presence and Use
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1121. Restriction.**

(a) Only those poisonous or toxic materials that are required for the operation and maintenance of a food establishment, such as for the cleaning and sanitizing of equipment and utensils and the control of insects and rodents, shall be allowed in a food establishment. $^{\text{Pf}}$

(b) Subsection (a) of this section does not apply to packaged poisonous or toxic materials that are for retail sale.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-202.11)

**Sec. 19-3-1122. Conditions of use.**

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be:

(1) Used according to:

a. Law and this Code;

b. Manufacturer’s use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer’s label instructions that state that use is allowed in a food establishment; $^{\text{P}}$

c. The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials; $^{\text{P}}$ and

d. Additional conditions that may be established by the regulatory authority; and

(2) Applied so that:

a. A hazard to employees or other persons is not constituted; $^{\text{P}}$ and

b. Contamination, including toxic residues due to drip, drain, fog, splash or spray on food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles is prevented, and for a restricted use pesticide, this is achieved by: $^{\text{P}}$

1. Removing the items; $^{\text{P}}$

2. Covering the items with impermeable covers; $^{\text{P}}$ or

3. Taking other appropriate preventive actions; $^{\text{P}}$ and

4. Cleaning and sanitizing equipment and utensils after the application. $^{\text{P}}$

(3) A restricted use pesticide shall be applied only by an applicator certified as defined in 7 USC 136 Definitions, (e) Certified Applicator, of the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act, or a person under the direct supervision of a certified applicator. $^{\text{Pf}}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-202.12)

**Secs. 19-3-1123—19-3-1130. Reserved.**

laws.title: Subdivision C. Container Prohibitions
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1131. Poisonous or toxic material containers.**

A container previously used to store poisonous or toxic materials may not be used to store, transport, or dispense food. $^{\text{P}}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-203.11)

**Secs. 19-3-1132—19-3-1140. Reserved.**

laws.title: Subdivision D. Chemicals
laws.content:
**Sec. 19-3-1141. Sanitizers, criteria.**

Chemical sanitizers and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food-contact surfaces shall meet the re-

CD19:116
FOOD

§ 19-3-1163

requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, Tolerance Exemptions for Active and Inert Ingredients for Use in Antimicrobial Formulations (food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-204.11)

laws.title: Chemicals for washing, treatment, storage and processing fruits and vegetables, criteria
laws.content:
(a) Chemicals used to wash or peel raw, whole fruits and vegetables shall meet the requirements specified in 21 CFR 173.315, Chemicals Used in Washing or to Assist in the Peeling of Fruits and Vegetables.$^{P}$

(b) Ozone as an antimicrobial agent used in the treatment, storage, and processing of fruits and vegetables in a food establishment shall meet the requirements specified in 21 CFR 173.368, Ozone.

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-204.12)

laws.title: Boiler water additives, criteria
laws.content:
Chemicals used as boiler water additives shall meet the requirements specified in 21 CFR 173.310, Boiler Water Additives.$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-204.13)

laws.title: Drying agents, criteria
laws.content:
Drying agents used in conjunction with sanitization shall:

(1) Contain only components that are listed as one of the following:

a. Generally recognized as safe for use in food as specified in 21 CFR 182, Substances Generally Recognized as Safe, or 21 CFR 184, Direct Food Substances Affirmed as Generally Recognized as Safe;$^{P}$

b. Generally recognized as safe for the intended use as specified in 21 CFR 186, Indirect Food Substances Affirmed as Generally Recognized as Safe;$^{P}$

c. Approved for use as a drying agent under a prior sanction specified in 21 CFR 181, Prior-Sanctioned Food Ingredients;$^{P}$

d. Specifically regulated as an indirect food additive for use as a drying agent as specified in 21 CFR Parts 175—178;$^{P}$ or

e. Approved for use as a drying agent under the threshold of regulation process established by 21 CFR 170.39, Threshold of Regulation for Substances Used in Food-Contact Articles;$^{P}$ and

(2) When sanitization is with chemicals, the approval required under Subsection (1)c or e of this section or the regulation as an indirect food additive required under Subsection (1)d of this section, shall be specifically for use with chemical sanitizing solutions.$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-204.14)

Secs. 19-3-1145—19-3-1150. Reserved.

Subdivision E. Lubricants

laws.title: Incidental food contact, criteria
laws.content:
Lubricants shall meet the requirements specified in 21 CFR 178.3570, Lubricants with Incidental Food Contact, if they are used on food-contact surfaces, on bearings and gears located on or within food-contact surfaces, or on bearings and gears that are located so that lubricants may leak, drip, or be forced into food or onto food-contact surfaces.$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-205.11)

Secs. 19-3-1152—19-3-1160. Reserved.

Subdivision F. Pesticides

laws.title: Restricted use pesticides, criteria
laws.content:
Restricted use pesticides specified under Section 19-3-1122(3) of this Code shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 152 Subpart I, Classification of Pesticides.$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-205.11)

laws.title: Rodent bait stations
laws.content:
Rodent bait shall be contained in a covered, tamper-resistant bait station.$^{P}$

(FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-206.12)

laws.title: Tracking powders, pest control and monitoring
laws.content:
(a) Except as specified in Subsection (b) of this section, a tracking powder pesticide may not be used in a food establishment.$^{P}$

(b) If used, a nontoxic tracking powder such as talcum or flour may not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-206.13)

Secs. 19-3-1164—19-3-1170. Reserved.

*Subdivision G. Medicines*

laws.title: Restriction and storage
laws.content:
(a) Except for medicines that are stored or displayed for retail sale, only those medicines that are necessary for the health of employees shall be allowed in a food establishment. $^{P}$

(b) Medicines that are in a food establishment for the employees’ use shall be labeled as specified under Section 19-3-1091 of this Code and located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles. $^{P}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-207.11)

laws.title: Refrigerated medicines, storage
laws.content:
Medicines belonging to employees or to children in a day care center that require refrigeration and are stored in a food refrigerator shall be:

(1) Stored in a package or container and kept inside a covered, leakproof container that is identified as a container for the storage of medicines; $^{P}$ and

(2) Located so they are inaccessible to children. $^{P}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-207.12)

Secs. 19-3-1173—19-3-1180. Reserved.

*Subdivision H. First Aid Supplies*

laws.title: Storage
laws.content:
First aid supplies that are in a food establishment for the employees’ use shall be:

(1) Labeled as specified under Section 19-3-1091 of this Code; $^{P}$ and

(2) Stored in a kit or a container that is located to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, and linens, and single-service and single-use articles. $^{P}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-208.11)

Secs. 19-3-1182—19-3-1190. Reserved.

*Subdivision I. Other Personal Care Items*

laws.title: Storage
laws.content:
Except as specified under Sections 19-3-1172 and 19-3-1181 of this Code, employees shall store their personal care items in facilities as specified under Section 19-3-1001(b) of this Code. (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-209.11)

Secs. 19-3-1192—19-3-1200. Reserved.

laws.title: Separation
laws.content:
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by:

(1) Separating the poisonous or toxic materials by spacing or partitioning; $^{P}$ and

(2) Locating the poisonous or toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service or single-use articles. $^{P}$ (FDA Food Code 2009, § 7-301.11)

Secs. 19-3-1202—19-3-1210. Reserved.

laws.title: Adoption of Michigan Public Health Code; continuing violation; civil violation and penalties; misdemeanor violation and penalties
laws.content:
(a) There is hereby adopted by reference the provisions of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 through 333.25211, as if fully set out in this chapter.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq.

(c) Any person who violates any provision of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq., may be issued a citation or a misdemeanor violation, as provided for in the Code, for each day that the violation continues.

(d) In accordance with Section 2461(1) of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.2461(1), any person who violates any provision of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq., which provides the issuance of a citation shall be subject to a civil penalty under the administrative process delineated in Section 2461(2) of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.2461(2), as follows:

(1) A warning for a first violation;

(2) A fine not exceeding $100.00 for a second violation within one year; and

(3) A fine not exceeding $500.00 for a subsequent violation within one year.

(e) In accordance with Section 1299 of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1299, any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq., which is designated as a misdemeanor or for which a penalty is not otherwise provided, shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each such violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each violation that is issued unless a specific penalty is provided for in the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq.

(Code 1984, § 24-11-14; Ord. No. 25-05, § 1(24-11-14), eff. 8-3-2005)

laws.title: Fee schedules for Health Department services; establishment, approval, publication, and availability; bi-annual review required
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Public Health Director is authorized to establish and collect necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of collection mechanisms for service requests, including laboratory tests, environmental inspections, registrations, permits, certifications, plan reviews, and other activities determined by the Public Health Director, and which are necessary to protect the public health and welfare of the People of the City.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Health Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Public Health Director at least once every two years.

(Code 1964, § 28-1-6; Code 1984, § 24-1-1; Ord. No. 23-92, § 1(24-1-1), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Payment of fees
laws.content:
Prior to approval of registration, certifications, permits and general license inspections, payment of all fees assessed by the Health Department is required. This requirement is in addition to any other specific health, sanitation, or safety conditions or requirements imposed by the Health Department.

(Code 1984, § 24-1-1.1; Ord. No. 23-92, § 1(24-1-1.1), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Enforcement authority
laws.content:
The Health Department, as an authorized agent of the City and as an authorized local public health department under the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.1101 et seq., is empowered to enforce this chapter and this Code, state statutes and regulations pertaining to public health and safety, and to establish rules and policies necessary for enforcement.

(Code 1984, § 24-1-1.2; Ord. No. 23-92, § 1(24-1-1.2), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each violation that is issued.

CD20:8

laws.title: Articles of bedding sold as new to be of all new material and labeled
laws.content:
No person shall sell as new any article of bedding or filling material unless it is made from all new material and a label, meeting all specifications of Division 2 of this article, is securely attached to the outside covering.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-4; Code 1984, § 24-7-4)

laws.title: Articles of bedding to have registration number
laws.content:
No person shall sell, offer for sale, exchange, lease, deliver or consign for like purpose, any article of bedding required to be labeled by this article unless the label contains a registration number as set forth in Division 3 of this article.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-5; Code 1984, § 24-7-5; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-5), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Labeling and sterilization of secondhand bedding
laws.content:
No person shall sell any secondhand bedding or bedding articles, or renovated or repaired bedding or bedding articles containing secondhand materials, unless they are labeled "Made of Secondhand Material," as specified in Division 2 of this article, and sterilized or fumigated as set forth in Division 4 of this article.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-6; Code 1984, § 24-7-6; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-6), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Sale of secondhand filling material for use in bedding
laws.content:
No person shall sell any secondhand filling material which is to be used for filling articles of bedding unless the packages or containers in which it is sold are marked or labeled as containing secondhand material and the same information is also indicated on the bill of sale or invoice for such material.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-7; Code 1984, § 24-7-7)

laws.title: Use of certain materials in bedding prohibited
False or misleading statements on labels; removal, defacement, or alteration of labels; false representations as to sterilization and fumigation
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to use any false or misleading statement, term or designation on any label required by this article or in any advertisement pertaining to any merchandise regulated by this article, or to remove, deface or alter any required label or the statement of filling materials made thereon, or to indicate in any way that bedding articles are "sterilized" or "fumigated" unless they have been so sterilized or fumigated by methods approved by the Public Health Director.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-11; Code 1984, § 24-7-11)

laws.title: Authority to inspect bedding and manufacturing stock; authority to take samples for testing; examination of records; seizure of articles
laws.content:
(a) The Public Health Director shall have the authority to inspect articles of bedding and manufacturing stock offered for sale or processed in the City. When necessary to verify the composition of the concealed contents of an article, the Public Health Director shall have the authority to open a seam of the article for visual examination or to remove a sample portion for laboratory examination.

(b) The Public Health Director shall have the authority to examine the records of the owner and manufacturer if the laboratory tests do not determine whether filling material is as stated on the label.

(c) In addition, the Public Health Director may seize and hold for evidence any article of bedding or manufacturing stock made, possessed, or offered for sale that does not conform to the requirements of this article.  
(Code 1964, § 28-9-12; Code 1984, § 24-7-12)

laws.title: Application, fee, and revocation of permits
laws.content:
(a) No person shall remake, renovate, or repair an article of bedding for another person, or deliver to another person an article of bedding which has been reno-

CD20:9
$\S 20-2-11$

DETROIT CITY CODE

vated or repaired, unless the person performing such processing shall file a written application for and receive a permit from the Public Health Director.

(b) Where the Public Health Director determines, upon investigation, that the place and equipment designated for the conduct of such business is in compliance with the law, the Public Health Director shall issue a renovation permit. Such permit shall be issued to the applicant upon the payment of the requisite fee.

(c) Such permit shall be valid until July 31st next following, and may be annually renewed on August 1st of each succeeding year upon making of application for such permit to the Public Health Director and upon the payment of the requisite fee.

(d) A fee shall be charged for the processing and issuance of a permit under this section. In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter and based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the permit, the Public Health Director shall establish and collect this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsections (b) and (c) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Public Health Director at least once every two years.

(e) A permit issued under this section may be revoked as provided in Section 20-2-12 of this Code upon proof by conviction of a violation of any provision of this article.

(Code 1984, § 24-7-16; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-16), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Hearing on revocation of permit; prosecution not prejudiced
laws.content:
Whenever found that any registration or permit has been obtained improperly, or has been used fraudulently or in any way in violation of this article, or whenever the required fees or charges shall be unpaid, the Public Health Director shall notify the person holding the permit to appear before a hearings officer at a stated time and to show cause why the permit should not be revoked.

After such hearing or upon failure of the permit holder to appear as specified, if the hearings officer determines that the permit should be revoked, the hearings officer shall issue a written decision and order providing the reasons why the permit is being revoked. Action under this section shall not prejudice the prosecution of any misdemeanor violation of this article.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-17; Code 1984, § 24-7-17)

Secs. 20-2-13—20-2-30. Reserved.

laws.title: Required; size; contents
laws.content:
No person shall sell any article of bedding or any filling materials for bedding unless there is attached thereto a label made of substantial cloth or other suitable material, which shall not flake when abraded. Such label shall be at least two inches by three inches in size. Upon each such label there shall be legibly and indelibly stamped or printed in ink in English all of the following information:

(1) The name of the material or materials used to fill such articles of bedding;

(2) The name and address of the manufacturer, jobber, distributor or vendor of the article of bedding, and the registration number of the manufacturer;

(3) In letters at least one-eighth of one inch high, in bold, black type, the words "All New Material" if such articles of bedding contain no second-hand materials; or in bold, black type, at least one-quarter of one inch high, the words, "Made of Secondhand Material" if such article of bedding contains any secondhand material; and in bold, black letters, at least one-eighth of one inch high, the word "Sterilized" or "Fumigated" if such article of bedding has been sterilized or fumigated, along with the permit number of the person who sterilized or fumigated the same and the date thereof;

(4) The body of labels bearing the descriptive words "All New Material" shall be white; the body of labels bearing the descriptive words "Made of Secondhand Material" shall be yellow; and

(5) All articles of bedding or filling materials for sale or use in the City shall have the date of delivery or the date of manufacture stamped on

CD20:10
HEALTH

§ 20-2-50

the label, either plainly or in a code registered with the Public Health Director. In the case of articles containing secondhand material or articles sterilized or fumigated, the date of affixing the required label or the date of sterilization shall be plainly stamped on all required labels.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-18; Code 1984, § 24-7-23)

laws.title: Bedding containing foam
laws.content:
The label on any article of bedding containing foam shall state whether it is rubber or synthetic foam and whether it is in the mold, sheet, flake, shredded, ground or crushed form. The label shall also state the thickness of rubber or synthetic foam pads or sheets. Where the bedding contains second grade rubber, it shall be stated on the label.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-19; Code 1984, § 24-7-24)

laws.title: Bedding containing artificially-colored filling materials to have same indicated on label
laws.content:
Where any article of bedding contains artificially-colored filling materials, the label on such article of bedding shall contain the word "colored" immediately preceding the description of such materials.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-21; Code 1984, § 24-7-26)

laws.title: Feather products and feather mixtures
laws.content:
(a) Feather mixtures shall be designated by the name, character and percentage of each material used, or the entire mixture shall be designated by the name of the lowest grade of material used. For example, if the filling is a mixture of goose and duck feathers, either this mixture shall be designated as goose and duck feathers and the percentage of each shall be stated on the label, or the entire mixture shall be designated as duck feathers.

(b) Crushed, curled, stripped, or chopped feathers shall be so designated on the label, along with the name of the fowl from which they came.

(c) Reasonable tolerances in connection with percentages of feathers and down may be allowed for the purpose of adjusting unintentional errors due to mechanical difficulties in arriving at exact percentages.

(d) Material labeled "Down" shall contain at least 90 percent pure down.

(e) Where the feathers of any fowl are named on the label, the material shall contain at least 90 percent of such feathers.

(f) Where, in connection with feathers or down, two or more ingredients in an article are named on the label, a tolerance of ten percent on the percentage of each ingredient may be allowed.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-22; Code 1984, § 24-7-27)

laws.title: Use of term "pure," "100%," or similar terms
laws.content:
The terms "pure," "100%," or terms of similar import shall be used only if the material is exactly as stated. No tolerance shall be allowed where such terms are used on the label.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-23; Code 1984, § 24-7-28)

laws.title: Improperly labeled articles may be ordered off sale
laws.content:
(a) The Public Health Director may order off sale and may so tag any article of bedding or material which is not labeled as required by this article or which has been labeled with a misleading term, description, designation or statement. Articles or materials ordered off sale or seized by the Public Health Director shall not be displayed or sold, or the contents thereof be altered, interfered with or removed, in whole or in part, or the articles or contents thereof be removed from the premises where ordered off sale or seized, until such articles or materials are released by the Public Health Director. All articles or materials ordered off sale or seized shall be subject to frequent examination by the Public Health Director and shall be so placed or stored as to be readily accessible at all times, and shall be produced for examination upon request of such officer until released.

(b) Nothing in this section shall prevent the removal of any article of bedding ordered off sale or seized from premises where on sale to a warehouse or other place of storage accessible to the enforcing officer, or return of such article to the manufacturer, provided, that the Public Health Director is notified in writing of intent to so remove or return and furnished any information, inventory or sample reasonably necessary to complete the Public Health Director's record as to the violation alleged.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-26; Code 1984, § 24-7-31)

Secs. 20-2-37—20-2-50. Reserved.

laws.title: Registration by manufacturers
laws.content:
(a) Each manufacturer of articles of bedding or filling material which are to be sold in the City and each person engaged in the sterilization of bedding or filling material, shall file an application with the Health Department for a registration number accompanied by an initial registration fee to be determined by the Health Department. This shall be in addition to all permits required by Division 4 or 5 of this article.

(b) The Public Health Director shall register each applicant upon approval and adopt the registrant’s current uniform registration number, or assign the registrant a registration number, if necessary, which thereafter shall constitute the registrant’s identification record, and such registration shall not be used by any other person. The registration shall expire on the first December 31st following the date of issuance. Within 30 days following expiration, a registrant may apply for renewal of registration by submitting an application together with payment of a fee in an amount to be determined by the Health Department and approved by resolution of the City Council. If the application and fee are not submitted within 30 days following expiration of the registration, the applicant shall also pay a late fee in an amount as determined by the Health Department.

(Code 1984, § 24-7-43; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-43), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Reporting requirements
laws.content:
(a) At least once every year, every registrant shall make a report to the Health Department as to the exact number of articles of bedding the permit holder sold or sterilized in the City during the reporting period, and, at the same time, shall pay to the Health Department the amount of the registration fee. The report and payment shall be transmitted to the Health Department not more than 30 days after the end of the reporting period. The report shall be made by the permit holder or by the permit holder’s authorized representative. The report shall be accompanied by a statement from a certified public accountant. Where the registrant fails to submit the report, the enforcing officer, or the Health Department or its designee, shall have the right to examine or have examined the books and records of the holder of the registration to verify the amount of payment due. The cost of making this examination shall be charged to holder of the registration. Any default in payment, the filing of a fraudulent or misleading report, or the failure to submit timely reports may be deemed sufficient cause for revocation of any registration as provided in Section 20-2-12 of this Code.

(b) In the event that a registrant cannot by business records determine the exact number of articles of bedding sold in the City as required by Subsection (a) of this section, such registrant may, in lieu thereof, report and pay at the same time and on the same basis set forth in Subsection (a) of this section an amount based on no less than the number of articles of bedding shipped by such registrant to all customers having retail outlets in the City.

(Code 1984, § 24-7-45; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-45), eff. 8-24-1992)

*Editor’s note—Ord. No. 24-92, § 1, adopted Aug. 7, 1992, amended 1984 Code, § 24-7-45 to read as herein set out. Formerly, said section pertained to stamp exemption permits and was derived from the 1964 Detroit City Code, § 28-9-29.*

Secs. 20-2-53—20-2-70. Reserved.

laws.title: Processes subject to approval of Public Health Director
laws.content:
All sterilization or fumigation processes used in the manufacture, renovation, or sterilization of articles of bedding or filling materials shall be subject to approval by the Public Health Director.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-30; Code 1984, § 24-7-57)

laws.title: Equipment and methods of sterilization
laws.content:
Sterilization shall be performed in equipment acceptable to the Public Health Director by the pressure steam method, the dry heat method, or other acceptable methods.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-31; Code 1984, § 24-7-48)

laws.title: Equipment and methods of fumigation
laws.content:
Fumigation shall be performed in equipment acceptable to the Public Health Director by using carbon dioxide and ethylene oxide, or formaldehyde and moisture, or other acceptable fumigants and methods.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-32; Code 1984, § 24-7-59)

CD20:12

laws.title: Permit required; application; records to be kept
laws.content:
(a) No person shall be considered to have qualified to apply an acceptable sterilizing or fumigating process, as required by this article, until such process has been registered with and approved by the Public Health Director, and until a numbered registration permit has been issued. Such permit shall be conspicuously posted on the premises near the sterilization or fumigation equipment. Holders of permits to apply sterilization or fumigation methods shall keep an accurate record of all articles or materials that may have been sterilized or fumigated, including the date of the same, and such records shall be available for inspection at any time by the Public Health Director.

(b) No application for a permit to perform sterilization or fumigation processes outside the City in order to comply with this article shall be approved except after personal inspection of such sterilizing or fumigating process and apparatus by the Public Health Director, unless the City or state where the equipment is located has an inspection service which is acceptable to the Public Health Director. The expenses for such inspection outside of the City, in addition to the permit fee, shall be paid by the applicant.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-33; Code 1984, § 24-7-60)

laws.title: Fees, term, renewal, and non-transferability of permits
laws.content:
(a) A fee shall be charged for the processing and issuance of a permit under this section. In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter and based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the permit, the Public Health Director shall establish and collect this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (c) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Public Health Director at least once every two years.

(c) Any person applying for a permit required under this division shall, on approval of such person's application, pay the requisite fee. Such permit shall be valid until July 31st next following. Subsequently, such permit may be renewed on August 1st of each succeeding year, upon the making of application therefor and payment of the requisite fee to the Health Department. Such permit shall not be transferable.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-34; Code 1984, § 24-7-61; Ord. No. 24-92, § 1(24-7-61), eff. 8-24-1992)

laws.title: Revocation of permits
laws.content:
A sterilization or fumigation permit may be revoked for cause, as provided in Section 20-2-12 of this Code. A reissue of such permit shall be subject to the same fees and provisions as the initial permit.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-35; Code 1984, § 24-7-62)

laws.title: Fumigation or sterilization may be done for manufacturer, renovator, or seller by person holding permit
laws.content:
Nothing in this article shall prevent any person engaged in the manufacture, renovation or sale of any article or material which requires sterilization or fumigation under the provisions of this article from having such sterilization or fumigation performed by any person who has a valid permit for such purposes, provided, that the number of such permit shall appear on the label hereafter described, attached to each article.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-36; Code 1984, § 24-7-63)

laws.title: Requirements not applicable to work done for owner of article
laws.content:
The provisions of this division relating to sterilizing or fumigating shall not apply to the repairing, renovating or remaking of any article by or for the owner thereof for the owner's own use only, provided, that there shall immediately be attached thereto, at the time received, a red tag on which is legibly written the date of receipt and the name and address of the owner.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-37; Code 1984, § 24-7-64)

laws.title: Application, fee, and revocation of permits
laws.content:
(a) No person shall remake, renovate, or repair an article of bedding for another person, or deliver to another person an article of bedding which has been renovated or repaired, unless the person performing such processing shall file a written application for and receive a permit from the Public Health Director.

(b) Where the Public Health Director determines, upon investigation, that the place and equipment designated for conducting such business is in compliance with this Code, the Public Health Director shall issue a renovation permit. Such permit shall be issued to the applicant upon the payment of the requisite fee.

(c) Such permit shall be valid until July 31st, and may be renewed on August 1st of each succeeding year upon the making of application for such permit to the Public Health Director and upon the payment of the requisite fee.

(d) A fee shall be charged for the processing and issuance of a permit under this section. In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter and based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the permit, the Public Health Director shall establish and collect this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsections (b) and (c) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Public Health Director at least once every two years.

(e) A permit issued under this section may be revoked as provided in Section 20-2-12 of this Code upon proof by conviction of a violation of any provision of this article.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-38; Code 1984, § 24-7-76)

laws.title: Use of secondhand materials
laws.content:
No person shall add any secondhand material in remaking, repairing or renovating any article of bedding for another person, nor shall any person deliver to another person any article of bedding to which has been added any secondhand material during the remaking, repairing or renovating thereof. Exception may be made to this prohibition, provided, that the purchase order or repair order signed by the ultimate owner includes written instructions to use secondhand material, and a label, as specified in Section 20-2-31(3) of this Code is attached to the article, indicating that secondhand material has been used, and that such material has been sterilized in accordance with Division 4 of this article.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-39; Code 1984, § 24-7-77)

laws.title: Applicability of division
laws.content:
The provisions of this division shall not be applicable to any manufacturer who shall repair an article of bedding which has previously been manufactured by such manufacturer and which is being repaired under guarantee for the original purchaser provided, that the manufacturer shall not add any secondhand materials to the article being repaired or renovated.

(Code 1964, § 28-9-40; Code 1984, § 24-7-78)

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each violation that is issued.

laws.title: Public Health Director authorized to promulgate administrative rules and regulations; periodic inspection
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the Public Health Director shall promulgate administrative rules and regulations covering body art facilities and shall periodically inspect the premises to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article and the promulgated rules and regulations.

(Code 1964, § 59-1-8; Code 1984, § 53-1-1)

laws.title: Owner of body art facility; duties
Tattoo, brand, or body-piercing on minor; consent of parent or guardian required; individual under influence of alcoholic beverage or controlled substance
laws.content:
(a) Subject to Section 20-3-21 of this Code, an individual shall not tattoo, brand, or perform body piercing on a minor unless the individual obtains the prior written informed consent of the minor’s parent or legal guardian. The minor’s parent or legal guardian shall execute the written, informed consent required under this subsection in the presence of the individual performing the tattooing, branding, or body piercing on the minor or in the presence of an employee or agent of that individual.

(b) An individual shall not tattoo, brand, or perform body piercing on another individual if the other individual is under the influence of an alcoholic beverage or a controlled substance.

(Code 1964, § 59-1-10; Code 1984, § 53-1-3)

Cross reference—Minors, generally, Ch. 29.

State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 333.13102.

laws.title: Giving or selling body piercing kit or device to minor prohibited
laws.content:
A person shall not give or sell to a minor a body piercing kit or other body piercing device.

State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 333.13110.

Secs. 20-3-7—20-3-20. Reserved.

CD20:16

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to conduct or to maintain any body art facility in the City without first having obtained a license from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to operate such business.

(Code 1964, § 59-1-1; Code 1984, § 53-2-1)

laws.title: Exemptions
laws.content:
The license that is required by this division shall not be required of a licensed physician, who, in such physician’s office or in a hospital, causes a person to be tattooed for medical identification.

(Code 1964, § 59-1-2; Code 1984, § 53-2-2)

laws.title: Application; information required
Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee
laws.content:
(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the Charter for the processing and issuance of a license under this division. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

*Cross reference—Licenses, generally, Ch. 28.
