laws.title: Penalties for violation; options to cure
laws.content:
(a) The Housing and Revitalization Department shall investigate compliance and enforce the provisions of this article for Type 1 through Type 5 qualifying transactions. To reduce duplication of enforcement efforts, for Type 6 qualifying transactions, the Housing and Revitalization Department shall investigate compliance and enforce the provisions of this article for tax abatements that do not receive federal funding. For penalty purposes, the Housing and Revitalization Department is responsible for the verification of compliance monitoring.

(b) Unless otherwise set forth in the transactional documents for Types 1 through 6 qualifying transactions, the contract or development agreement for any qualifying transaction shall contain provisions such that, where the requirements of this article are not met or maintained, the developer or owner shall be responsible for the payment to the City of the following penalties, provided, that when penalties apply whichever penalty is greater will be imposed:

(1) For Type 1 through 5 qualifying transactions as follows:

a. Upon the failure to maintain and provide the required number of dwelling units available for rent or lease at affordable rates, both of the following:

i. The excess of actual rent received over the affordable rate that would otherwise apply; and

ii. A penalty for each unit not in compliance in the amount not less than 25 percent of the affordable monthly rent for each month or part of a month of non-compliance;

b. The enforcement costs of the City; and

c. Any other sanction or penalty under applicable law, rules, or regulations.

(2) For Type 6 qualifying transactions as follows:

a. Upon the failure to maintain and provide the required number of dwelling units available for rent or lease at affordable rates, an amount equal to the difference for the year of non-compliance between the amount of *ad valorem* tax otherwise due on the property without the Tax Abatement Certificate and the amount of the specific tax due on the property with the Tax Abatement Certificate, multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is shortfall of the number of dwellings units available for rent or lease at affordable rates and the denominator of which is the total number of dwellings units required to be available for rent or lease at affordable rates;

b. The enforcement costs of the City; and

c. Any other sanction or penalty under applicable law, rules, or regulations.

(c) The penalties described in Subsection (b) of this section shall be assessed to the developer or owner subject to the following:

(1) Prior to the application of the penalty, the owner shall have 60 days from the due date of the annual report to the City of Detroit to cure the non-compliance;

Examples of good cause include, but are not limited to, situations where the current qualifying tenant’s income increases above the applicable Area Median Income thresholds and situations where affordable dwelling units are not currently occupied by qualifying tenants, but the owner is actively marketing the units to qualifying tenants.

laws.title: Detroit Affordable Housing Development and Preservation Fund
laws.content:
(a) The City shall create an appropriation within the Housing and Revitalization Department’s budget deemed the “Detroit Affordable Housing Development and Preservation Fund” for the deposit and expenditure of penalties collected pursuant to this article.

(b) The objective of the Fund is:

(1) To foster and promote the purpose and intent of this article;

(2) To prioritize the means by which funding for new residential housing projects addresses housing for those with the greatest economic need, being households earning up to 50 percent of the Area Median Income;

(3) To increase accessibility to safe, affordable housing for those facing high housing costs;

(4) To prioritize permanent housing affordability and sustainability within the City; and

(5) To prioritize the preservation of existing affordable housing units.

(c) In addition to the deposit of penalties for violations under Section 22-3-6 of this Code, the City’s annual budget or an amendment thereto shall contain an appropriation to the Fund. It is expected that the annual appropriation or budget amendment will be not less than 40 percent of the net receipts received by the City of Detroit of all commercial property sales during the previous fiscal year. At the close of the fiscal year on June 30th, the Housing and Revitalization Department shall calculate 40 percent of the actual land sales of the prior year and provide such information to the City Council by August 1st.

(d) Unless specifically stated otherwise in the budget closing resolution, funds not expended within such appropriation during a given fiscal year shall remain in such appropriation and carry forward into the subsequent fiscal year to fund future affordable residential housing projects and other eligible activities.

(e) Subject to approval of the City Council, the City may also accept and deposit into the Fund or subaccounts of the Fund donations and grants from private or public sources, subject to conditions of such grants, for use in accordance with the purpose of the Fund.

(f) Subject to approval of the City Council, the City may also accept and deposit into the Fund or subaccounts of the Fund negotiated settlement agreements as to penalties for use in accordance with the purpose of the Fund. The Housing and Revitalization Department shall negotiate the proposed settlements.

(g) Agreements or contracts for the expenditures from the Fund shall be authorized by the City Council.

(h) In addition to the affordability administrative procedures promulgated under Section 22-3-9 of this Code, the Director of the Housing and Revitalization Department shall promulgate and publish on the City’s website administrative procedures requiring Fund moneys to be used to support housing opportunities for Detroit residents with incomes up to 50 percent of the Area Median Income for activities consistent with this article.

(1) To the extent possible, not less than 70 percent of Fund moneys shall be allocated to directly benefit households earning up to 30 percent of the Area Median Income; the remaining 30 percent of moneys may be used to benefit households earning up to 50 percent of the Area Median Income. Fund moneys shall not be used to benefit households earning more than 50 percent of the Area Median Income.

(2) Not less than 70 percent of Fund moneys shall be allocated in areas of persistent poverty, as identified by the U.S. Census Bureau, and/or are

**Sec. 22-4-6. Validity of certificate and report; responsibility of City for defects.**

a. Uptake rate within established zones (ratio of current Neighborhood Enterprise Zones H Certificates and active Principal Residency Exemptions);

b. Financial impact of new zones on all *ad valorem* taxing authorities; and

c. Other pertinent information related to neighborhood stabilization, including, but not limited to:

    1. Current assessed value;

    2. Length of residency;

    3. Market sale comparables;

    4. Effective property tax rate (ratio of current property tax payment and assessed value); and

    5. Current Certificate expiration dates.

(2) City Council may opine, by adoption of a resolution outlining its findings on each of the criteria listed in Subsection (b)(i) of this section, whether the maps need to be modified or maintained in their current configuration.

(g) In addition to the above requirements, all repair-to-own contractors shall:

The price of properties offered for sale under this article shall be the lowest price as determined by the standard appraisal methods used by the City as applied by the Planning and Development Department, which shall include a method that values repair costs. The price shall be reduced by the costs to the repair-to-own contractor for clearing title problems not resolved by the City. The price shall be based on a full and fair exchange of value for value. In calculating the value received by the City from the repair-to-own contractor in the exchange, the Planning and Development Department shall include, but not limit itself to:

laws.title: Duties of landlord
laws.content:
(a) A landlord shall not enter into a rental agreement with the occupant if the landlord knows, or has reason to know, that the rental property is infested with bed bugs.

(b) A landlord shall be responsible for all of the following:

(1) Having a licensed pest management professional, as defined in Section 22-7-1 of this Code, inspect a rental property for bed bugs prior to leasing, or renting the property to others.

(2) Providing proof to the occupant, prior to or upon signing the rental agreement of the rental property, that the property was inspected by a licensed pest management professional and is bed bug free.

(3) Providing informational material to the occupant regarding bed bug prevention from the state or City’s website, or any other informational forum.

(4) Within seven days after receiving written or electronic notice from an occupant, or other reliable source of a suspected infestation in the occupant’s rental property, the landlord shall order an inspection of the rental property for bed bugs by a pest management professional. If an infestation of a rental property is confirmed, the landlord shall immediately order an inspection of any adjoining or adjacent rental units to the infested rental property;

(5) Within seven days after an infestation of a rental property is confirmed:

a. The landlord and occupant shall begin treatment by hiring a pest management professional chosen by the landlord to eradicate the bed bugs; or

b. For the purposes of single-family dwellings only, the use of suggested self-help treatment methods listed on the state’s website may be used to eradicate bed bugs, provided, that:

i. Following a self-help treatment method used for an infested rental unit, the landlord shall have an inspection of the unit conducted by a pest management professional within 14 days to confirm the unit is free from bed bugs;

ii. If a self-help treatment method is used on a rental unit and upon inspection by a pest management professional bed bugs are still present in the unit, the landlord shall hire a pest management professional to treat the rental unit; and

iii. Self-help treatment methods shall not be used in situations where the rental unit is overwhelmingly infested with bed bugs.

(6) Maintaining a record of the pest control measures performed by the pest management professional on the rental property and shall comply with the following:

a. The record shall include reports and receipts prepared by the pest management professional;

b. A log of all infestation reports made by occupants;

c. The record shall be maintained for three years; and

(8) With exception to Subsection (c) of this section, the landlord shall remove any items or materials the occupant has placed in a sealed plastic bag and properly labeled for disposal, immediately from the premises, in accordance with Section 22-7-7 of this Code.

(c) Occupants of a single-family dwelling shall be responsible for removing any infested items or materials and disposing of them in accordance with Section 22-7-7 of this Code.

laws.title: Prohibition on housing provider inquiring into criminal convictions of applicants and their household members until being interviewed or qualified; basis for adverse action
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided in Section 22-8-6 of this Code, housing providers shall not:

(1) Inquire about or require applicants to disclose conviction history as part of tenant screening process until the housing provider:

a. Has determined the applicant is qualified to rent the housing unit under all of the housing provider’s criteria not related to potential past criminal convictions or an unresolved arrest; and

b. Has provided to the applicant a conditional lease agreement that commits the unit to the applicant as long as the applicant passes the conviction history review.

(2) Base an adverse action in whole or in part:

a. On an unresolved arrest or an arrest not leading to a conviction;

b. On participation in or completion of a diversion or a deferral of judgment program;

c. On a conviction that has been judicially dismissed, expunged, voided, invalidated or otherwise rendered inoperative by a court of law or by executive pardon.

d. On a conviction or any other determination or adjudication in the juvenile justice system, or information regarding a matter considered in or processed through the juvenile justice system;

e. On a misdemeanor conviction that is more than five years old, calculated from the date of sentencing; or

f. On information pertaining to an offense or violation other than a felony or misdemeanor, such as a civil infraction.

(3) A housing provider shall not include questions regarding or require applicants to disclose on any housing application the facts or details of any conviction history or any matter identified in Subsection (2) of this section.

(b) It is the responsibility of a housing provider to ensure that its employees and agents comply with this article.

(Code 1984, § 26-5-5; Ord. No. 01-19, § 1(26-5-5), eff. 9-1-2019)

(b) Regarding applicants and their household members, a housing provider may base an adverse action in whole or in part on directly-related convictions that includes one or more of the following:

(1) Any conviction where state or federal law prohibits the applicant from being eligible for public housing; or

laws.title: Procedures for use of evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors in housing decisions; requirement for individualized assessment
laws.content:
(a) Consistent with the procedures in this section and subject to state and federal law, a housing provider shall offer the applicant a reasonable opportunity to present evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors related to convictions within the previous five years.

(b) In reviewing an applicant’s criminal history and making a decision related to eligible housing based on such history, a housing provider shall conduct an individualized assessment, considering only:

(1) Convictions that warrant denial based on local, state, or federal law; and

(2) Time that has elapsed since the conviction; and

(3) Whether it is a directly-related conviction, as defined in Section 22-8-3 of this Code, that has direct and specific negative bearing on the safety of persons or real property; and

(4) Any evidence of inaccuracy or evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors presented by the applicant.

(c) If a housing provider intends to base an adverse action related to eligible housing on an item or items in the applicant’s conviction history, prior to taking any adverse action the housing provider shall provide the applicant with a copy of the background check report, and shall notify the applicant of the prospective adverse action and the items forming the basis for the prospective adverse action.

(d) If, within 14 calendar days of the date that the notice described in Subsection (c) of this section is provided by the housing provider to the applicant, the applicant gives the housing provider notice in writing of evidence of the inaccuracy of the item or items of conviction history or evidence of rehabilitation or other mitigating factors set forth in this section, the housing provider shall delay any adverse action for a reasonable period of not less than five calendar days after receipt of the information. During that time the housing provider shall reconsider the prospective adverse action in light of the information provided by the applicant or potential applicant.

(e) The housing provider shall promptly notify the applicant of any final adverse action based upon their conviction history or contents of the criminal background check.

(f) It shall be unlawful for any housing provider to engage in any communication, including the production or dissemination of advertisements, related to eligible housing, which expresses, directly or indirectly, that any person with an arrest or conviction record will not be considered for the rental or lease of real property or that may not apply for the rental or lease of real property, except as required by local, state, or federal law. For purposes of this subsection, engaging in a communication includes, but is not limited to, making a verbal statement or producing or disseminating any solicitation, advertisement, or signage.

(Code 1984, § 26-5-7; Ord. No. 01-19, § 1(26-5-7), eff. 9-1-2019)

(a) The administering agency shall investigate complaints regarding a housing provider’s alleged violation of this article. The administrative agency may engage third-party assistance to conduct its investigation.

(1) Where the Director of the administering agency determines that a violation has not occurred, he or she shall issue a determination that a housing provider is not in violation of this article. This determination shall be provided to the housing provider and the complainant.

(2) Where the Director of the administering agency determines that a violation has occurred, he or she shall issue a determination that a housing provider is in violation of this article, provided, however, for a first violation, or for any violation during the first 12 months following the effective date of this article, which was September 1, 2019, the Director must issue warnings and notices to correct, and offer the housing provider technical assistance on how to comply with the requirements of this article. For a second violation, the administering agency shall refer its determination for each applicant to whom the violation occurred, or is continuing, to the enforcing agency for action, to the housing provider, and to the complainant.

(3) Where the Director of the administering agency determines that a violation has occurred, he or she shall forward a copy of the determination to the Michigan Department of Civil Rights for consideration.

(b) The administering agency is authorized, in consultation with the Mayor’s Office, to take appropriate steps to assist in the enforcement of this article, including the investigation of any possible violations of this article. The administering or enforcing agencies shall not find a violation based on a housing provider’s decision that an applicant’s conduct is a directly-related conviction, as defined in Section 22-8-3 of this Code, unless the housing provider failed to conduct the individualized assessment as required under Section 22-8-7 of this Code.

(c) If multiple applicants are impacted by the same violation at the same time, for example, all applicants for a certain housing unit are asked for their conviction history on the initial application, each violation shall be treated as a separate violation.

laws.title: Definitions
laws.content:
For the purpose of this article, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section:

*Assisted living* means a residential care facility designed primarily for older people who typically have no serious health problems but who may have chronic or debilitating conditions requiring assistance with daily activities. Permitted services include, but are not limited to, staff-supervised meals, housekeeping, personal care, medication supervision, and social activities. Both private and shared sleeping rooms may be provided. Facilities providing regular care under supervision of physicians are not considered assisted-living facilities.

*Congregate care* means a dependent elderly housing facility with cooking facilities within the unit, but with a central dining service option.

*Emergency generator* means, as likewise defined in 40 CFR 98.6, a stationary combustion device, such as a reciprocating internal combustion engine or turbine that serves solely as a secondary source of mechanical or electrical power whenever the primary energy supply is disrupted or discontinued during power outages or natural disasters that are beyond the control of the owner or operator of the facility.

*Fuel cell* means, as likewise defined in Section 2 of the Michigan Next Energy Authority Act, being MCL 207.822, an electrochemical device that uses an external fuel and continuously converts the energy released from the oxidation of fuel by oxygen directly into electricity without combustion and consists of an anode, a cathode, and an electrolyte.

*Fuel cell energy system* means, as likewise defined in Section 2 of the Michigan Next Energy Authority Act, being MCL 207.822, one or more fuel cells or fuel cell stacks and an inverter or other power conditioning unit, which may also include a fuel processor.

*Fuel cell stack* means, as likewise defined in Section 2 of the Michigan Next Energy Authority Act, being MCL 207.822, an assembly of fuel cells.

*Fuel processor* means, as likewise defined in Section 2 of the Michigan Next Energy Authority Act, being MCL 207.822, a device that converts a fuel, including, but not limited to, methanol, natural gas, or gasoline, into a hydrogen rich gas, without combustion for use in a fuel cell.

*Home for the aged* means a supervised personal care facility, other than a hotel, adult foster care facility, hospital, nursing home, or county medical care facility that provides room, board, and supervised personal care to 21 or more unrelated, non-transient, individuals 55 years of age or older and includes a supervised personal care facility for 20 or fewer individuals 55 years of age or older if the facility is operated in conjunction with and as a distinct part of a licensed nursing home as defined in Section 20109 of the Michigan Public Health Code, being MCL 333.20109.

*Independent living* means a multiple-family housing form with full facilities for self-sufficiency in each individual dwelling unit.

*Nursing home* means, as likewise defined in Section 36-2-1 of this Code, a facility that provides organized nursing care and medical treatment to seven or more unrelated individuals suffering or recovering from illness, injury or infirmity and that is not a unit in a correctional facility that is operated by the Michigan Department of Corrections.

*Senior citizen* means a resident that is 55 years of age or older.

*Senior housing facility* means an institution, other than a hospital or hotel, that provides housing or room and board to persons aged 55 years or older and that is

licensed by the State of Michigan or operates exclusively as assisted living as defined in this section, congregate care as defined in this section, home for the aged as defined in this section, independent living as defined in this section, or nursing home as defined in this section.

*Storage battery* means, as likewise defined in Section 17101 of the Michigan Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, being MCL 324.17101, a battery that is used to start an internal combustion engine or as the principal electrical power source for a vehicle, in which the electrodes are grids of lead containing lead oxides that change in composition during charging and discharging, and the electrolyte is dilute sulfuric acid.

*Uninterruptible power supply or uninterruptible power source* means an electrical apparatus that provides emergency power to a load when the input power source or main power fails.

(Ord. No. 15-19, § 1(26-9-2), eff. 3-1-2020)

**Sec. 22-9-3. Enforcement and penalties.**

(a) The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department has the authority to inspect a senior housing facility to ensure compliance with this article should a complaint be made regarding the alternative emergency energy sources.

(b) The Fire Marshal has the authority to inspect a senior housing facility to ensure compliance with this article during an annual inspection and any other inspection of the facility.

(c) In accordance with Section 41(4) of the Michigan Home Rule City Act, being MCL 117.41(4) and Sections 1-1-9(a)(3) and 3-2-1 of this Code, a violation of this article is deemed to be a blight violation.

(d) Owners of the senior housing facility who violate any section of this article may be issued a blight violation notice pursuant to Chapter 3 of this Code for each day that the violation continues.

(Ord. No. 15-19, § 1(26-9-5), eff. 3-1-2020)

**Sec. 22-9-4. Alternative emergency energy source required.**

All senior housing facilities, as defined in Section 22-9-2 of this Code, shall have an alternative emergency energy source as listed in Subsection 22-9-4(a) or (b) of this Code.

(Ord. No. 15-19, § 1(26-9-3), eff. 3-1-2020)

**Sec. 22-9-5. Alternative emergency energy source options.**

(a) All senior housing facilities, as defined in Section 22-9-2 of this Code, shall have an alternative emergency energy source under this subsection or under Subsection (b) of this section. In accordance with the National Electrical Code 70, Article 700.12(A)—(E), which is contained the Michigan Electrical Code and is enforced by the City as provided for in Section 8-3-2 of this Code, an alternative emergency energy source shall include at least one of the following:

(1) A storage battery shall be used as a source of power for emergency systems and shall be of suitable rating and capacity to supply and maintain the total load for a minimum period of one and a half hours:

a. The storage battery may be alkali or acid type and shall be designed and constructed to meet the requirements of emergency service and shall be compatible with the charger for that particular installation as in accordance with NEC 70, Article 700.12(A);

b. Automotive type batteries shall not be used; and

c. An automatic battery charging means shall be provided by the senior housing facility; or

(2) An uninterruptable power supply shall be used to provide power for emergency systems and shall comply with the applicable provisions of NEC 70, 700.12(A); or

(3) A separate service shall be a service conductor sufficiently remote electrically and physically from any other service conductors to minimize the possibility of simultaneous interruption of supply, and shall be in accordance with the standards set forth in the Article 230 of the NEC; or

(4) A fuel cell system used as a source of power for emergency systems shall be of suitable rating and capacity to supply and maintain the total load for not less than two hours of full demand operation:

a. Installation of a fuel cell system shall meet the requirements of Parts II through VIII of Article 692 of the NEC; and

laws.title: Additional Duties of Human Rights Department
laws.content:
In accordance with the general duties that are provided for under Section 7-704 of the Charter, subject to the policies established by the Human Rights Commission, the Human Rights Department possesses the following specific duties, which arise from the department’s general duties:

(1) To receive, investigate and pass upon complaints and to initiate its own investigation and complaints of racial and ethnic group tension, prejudice, intolerance, bigotry and disorder occasioned thereby, and to assist in the resolution of such tension;

*Cross references—Requirement for City residency for appointment and re-appointment to City board or commission, § 2-4-1; requirement for City Clerk to verify residency when taking and subscribing oath of office for members of City boards and commissions, § 2-4-2; ethics, § 2-5-1 et seq.

(2) To act in an advisory and enforcement capacity, when directed by the Mayor, Human Rights Commission, or other operations of any City department, or upon its own initiation where questions arise concerning race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, public benefit status, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression. All City departments, agencies, and commissions shall cooperate with the Human Rights Department when called upon to render such assistance as may be reasonably required in the implementation of this section; and

(3) To issue publications and reports of investigations and research designed to promote the mission of the Human Rights Department.

laws.title: Interference with enforcement
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, employer, labor organization, or employment agency, to willfully resist, prevent, impede or interfere with the Human Rights Department or any of its members or representatives in the performance of duty under this chapter, provided, that utilizing the procedure for a review of an order shall not be deemed to be such willful conduct.

(Code 1984, § 27-2-14; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-10.11), eff. 2-9-1979)

laws.title: Prohibited conduct
Exception for religious organizations
laws.content:
It shall not be considered a discriminatory practice for a religious organization or institution:

(1) To restrict any of its facilities or housing, education, or accommodations, which are operated primarily in connection with the promotion of the religious principles under which the religious organization or institution is established or maintained, to persons of the denomination involved; or

(2) To restrict employment opportunities as such to persons of that denomination, where a *bona fide* religious purpose exists for such restriction.

(Code 1984, § 27-2-12; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-10.8), eff. 2-9-1979)

laws.title: Respondent operating under government license
laws.content:
Where the Human Rights Department, upon notice and hearing, determines that a respondent operating by virtue of a license issued by the City or other political subdivision, or the state or federal government, or any agency of these, has violated this chapter and that the violation was authorized, requested, commanded, performed or knowingly permitted by the respondent, or by an officer or agent of the respondent acting within the scope of his or her employment or duty, and upon failure of such respondent to correct the unlawful practice and comply with Department orders, the Department shall so certify to the licensing agency. Until the Human Rights Department’s finding is reversed through judicial review,

laws.title: Other civil rights retained
laws.content:
Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as preventing the Human Rights Department, upon approval of the Human Rights Commission, from securing civil rights guaranteed by law other than the civil rights that are contained within this chapter.

laws.title: Complaint; contents thereof; limitation of action; running of limitations of action
laws.content:
(a) A complaint shall be submitted to the Human Rights Department specifying the alleged act or acts of discrimination, which violate this chapter, and shall be documented on a form provided by the Department.

(b) A complaint that is filed under this chapter shall be signed by the person who is making the complaint.

(c) Any complaint that is filed under this chapter shall be filed within one year after the alleged act or acts of discrimination. No action may be taken on any complaint, which is filed later than one year after the alleged act or acts of discrimination.

(Code 1984, § 27-2-7; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-10.3), eff. 2-9-1979; Ord. No. 2020-35, § 1, eff. 11-11-2020)

laws.title: Acceptance of complaints
laws.content:
(a) The Human Rights Department shall not accept a complaint from a complainant who has previously filed a complaint involving the same transaction or occurrence with any other city, state, or federal civil rights agency, department or commission, unless:

(1) The prior complaint was dismissed on grounds not dispositive of the merits; or

(2) Jurisdiction of the complaint is referred any another other city or from a state, or federal civil rights agency, department or commission.

(b) Subsection (a) of this section shall not be deemed to prohibit the Human Rights Department from referring a complaint to the appropriate state or federal civil rights agency.

(c) In accordance with administrative rules that are promulgated pursuant to Section 23-2-12 of this Code:

(1) The Human Rights Department shall acknowledge receipt to each complainant, and forward the complaint to the person who, or entity which, is complained against; and

(2) The person who, or entity which, is complained against shall have the opportunity to submit a written response to the complaint.

(Code 1984, § 27-2-16; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-10.13), eff. 2-9-1979; Ord. No. 330-H, § 1(2-7-10.13), eff. 7-16-1979; Ord. No. 09-08, § 1(27-2-16), eff. 5-22-2008)

laws.title: Review of decision
laws.content:
(a) Where a complainant or respondent is aggrieved by a decision of the Human Rights Department, including a cease and desist order, and a refusal to issue a complaint, except a decision of ineligibility to do business with the City, the complainant or respondent may pursue review of the decision, within 21 days of entry of the order, from a court of appropriate jurisdiction through any available equitable remedy. Where the complainant or respondent do not pursue review within 21 days after the service of the order, the Human Rights Department may seek a decree for the enforcement of the order from a court of appropriate jurisdiction.

(b) An appeal by a person who, or firm or corporation which, is aggrieved by a decision of ineligibility to do business with the City, may be heard by the City Council, or such other appellate body as may be provided by this Code under Section 9-302 of the Charter.

laws.title: Certification availability and duration
Notification concerning change of status
laws.content: A certified business is required to immediately notify in writing the Human Rights Department regarding any change in its circumstances, which affect any representation that the business made in its application or status concerning the business' certification.

laws.title: De-certification due to misconduct
laws.content:
(a) The Human Rights Department shall de-certify any business that obtains its certification through fraud, deceit or misrepresentation, or that fails to report any changes that materially affect its qualification for certification.

(b) Upon de-certification, the name of the business shall be removed for a period of three years from all vendor lists that are maintained by the Office of the Chief Financial Officer and by the Human Rights Department under Section 23-2-43 of this Code.

laws.title: Establishment of Certified Business Register
laws.content:
(a) The City of Detroit establishes a Certified Business Register, which shall be available during business hours for review by businesses, non-profit organizations, other governmental agencies, and members of the public to identify Detroit-Based Businesses, Detroit-Based Small Businesses, Detroit-Resident Businesses, Minority-Owned Business Enterprises, and Woman-Owned Businesses, with which they may wish to do business.

(b) Upon certification, the Human Rights Department shall list the Detroit-Based Business, the Detroit-Based Small Business, the Detroit-Headquartered Business, the Detroit-Resident Business, the Minority-Owned Business Enterprise, and Woman-Owned Business in the Certified Business Register.

(c) The Human Rights Department shall continually update the Certified Businesses Register as new businesses are certified and currently-listed businesses choose not to be re-certified or are de-certified by the Department.

laws.title: Promulgation of procedural rules
laws.content:
In accordance with Section 7-705 of the Charter, the Director of the Human Rights Department is authorized, with the consent of the Human Rights Commission, to promulgate procedural rules for the appeal process that is authorized by this division.

laws.title: Discrimination generally
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any educational institution, public or private, or any person acting as director or principal, or who is otherwise in charge or control of such institution, or any agent of such persons, or any person connected with teaching or rendering any other service in such institution, or any employee thereof, to discriminate in any manner against any student, parent of such student, school employee or applicant, or other individual because of race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, public benefit status, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression.

(Code 1984, § 27-5-1; Ord. No. 330-H, § 1(2-7-5), eff. 7-16-1979; Ord. No. 09-08, § 1(27-5-1), eff. 5-22-2008)

laws.title: Discriminatory practices
Designation of racial or ethnic classification in writing developed by educational institution; transmission of information to federal agency; the term "writing" defined
laws.content:
(a) An educational institution shall do both of the following if that educational institution lists racial or ethnic classifications in a writing, and if that educational institution requests that an individual select one of those classifications to designate such individual's race or ethnicity:

(1) Include in the writing the term "multiracial" as a classification, and a definition of that term that substantially provides that the term "multiracial" means having parents of different races.

(2) Exclude from the writing the term "other" as a classification.

(b) If a federal agency requires an educational institution to transmit information obtained from an individual pursuant to a writing described in Subsection (a) of this section, but rejects the classification "multiracial," the educational institution shall redesignate the individuals identified as multiracial by allocating those individuals to racial or ethnic classifications approved by the federal agency in the same ratio that those classifications occur within the general population of the group from which the information was solicited.

(c) As used in this section, the term "writing" means as defined in Section 2 of the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, being MCL 15.232.

laws.title: Exemptions
laws.content:
(a) Where the law of this state mandates, it is not an unlawful practice to deny admission to any institution or school.

(b) It is not an unlawful practice to deny admission to any religious institution or school where that denial is based on the existence of a *bona fide* religious purpose and where such denial is in furtherance of the principles and doctrines of such institution or school and not intended to abridge the civil rights, privileges and freedom of those individuals so excluded.

(c) This article does not prohibit the board of a school district or intermediate school district or the board of directors of a public school academy from establishing and maintaining a single-gender school, class, or program within a school as provided under Sections 475 and 1146 of the Michigan Revised School Code, being MCL

(Code 1984, § 27-5-3; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-5.2), eff. 2-9-1979; Ord. No. 330-H, § 1(2-7-5.2), eff. 7-16-1979)

laws.title: Employer; prohibited practices; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) An employer shall not do any of the following:

(1) Fail or refuse to hire or recruit, discharge, or otherwise discriminate against an individual with respect to employment, compensation, or a term, condition, or privilege of employment, because of race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, public benefit status, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression;

(2) Limit, segregate, or classify an employee or applicant for employment in a way that deprives or tends to deprive the employee or applicant of an employment opportunity, or otherwise adversely affects the status of an employee or applicant because of race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, public benefit status, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression;

(3) Segregate, classify, or otherwise discriminate against a person on the basis of sex or sexual orientation with respect to a term, condition, or privilege of employment, including, but not limited to, a benefit plan or system; or

(4) Treat an individual affected by pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition differently for any employment-related purpose from another individual who is not so affected but similar in ability or inability to work, without regard to the source of any condition affecting the other individual's ability or inability to work. For purposes of this subsection, the term "a medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth" does not include nontherapeutic abortion not intended to save the life of the mother.

(b) This section does not prohibit the establishment or implementation of a *bona fide* retirement policy or system that is not a subterfuge to evade the purposes of this section.

(c) This section does not apply to the employment of an individual by such individual's parent, spouse, or child.

(Code 1984, § 27-3-1; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-3), eff. 2-9-1979; Ord. No. 330-H, § 1(2-7-3), eff. 7-16-1979; Ord. No. 09-08, § 1(27-3-1), eff. 5-22-2008)

laws.title: Provisions required in City contracts
laws.content:
(a) All contracting City departments and agencies shall include in all contracts negotiated or renegotiated by them a covenant obligating the contractor not to discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment, training, education, or apprenticeship connected directly or indirectly with the performance of the contract, with respect to such employee’s hire, promotion, job assignment, tenure, terms, conditions or privileges of employment because of race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, public benefit status, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression. Breach of this covenant shall be deemed a material breach of the contract. This section shall not apply where it is determined by the Human Rights Department that such requirements are *bona fide* occupational qualifications reasonably necessary to performance of the duties required for employment. The burden of proof that the occupational qualifications is *bona fide* is upon the employer.

(b) All contracting City departments and agencies shall include in all contracts negotiated or renegotiated by them a covenant obligating the contractor to furnish information required by the agency or the Human Rights Department pursuant to Subsection (a) of this section. Breach of this covenant shall be deemed a material breach of the contract.

(c) All contracting City departments and agencies shall include in all contracts negotiated or renegotiated by them a liquidated damages clause to allow for recovery from the contractor, by set-off against the unpaid portion of the contract price, or otherwise pursuant to the contract, a specified dollar amount per day, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, for each day that the contractor fails to comply with this article as determined by the Human Rights Department, the said sum being fixed as negotiated and agreed upon by and between the contractor and the City because of the impracticability and extreme difficulty of fixing and ascertaining the actual damages, which the City would sustain in the event of such a breach of contract, and said amount is agreed to be the amount of damages which the City would sustain.

(d) Prior to the award and effective date of contract with the City, the Human Rights Department shall review and determine whether the prospective contractor is in compliance with Section 23-4-1 of this Code.

(e) In accordance with Section 7-704 of the Charter and Article II, Division 2, of this chapter, the Human Rights Department is authorized to investigate and make a determination regarding any employment complaint.

(f) In the event of the contractor’s failure to comply with the equal employment opportunity provisions of its contract with the City or orders as issued by the Human Rights Department, the City may, at its option:

(1) Cancel, terminate or suspend the contract in whole or in part;

(2) Recover liquidated damages pursuant to Subsection (c) of this section; or

(3) Utilize other legal or equitable remedies.

(g) In order to ensure compliance with this section, the Human Rights Department is authorized:

(1) To gather, at the direction of the Mayor, contractual information from all City contracting departments and agencies;

(2) To evaluating employment data submitted by contractors; and

(3) To engaging in contract compliance reviews and hearings to determine fair employment practices and enforcement of this section in determining eligibility status to do business with the City.

(h) Any appeal of a final determination by the Human Rights Department shall be in accordance with Section 7-706 of the Charter. (Code 1984, § 27-3-2; Ord. No. 303-H, § 1(2-7-3.1), eff. 2-9-1979; Ord. No. 09-08, § 1(27-3-2), eff. 5-22-2008)

laws.title: Applicability to private club
laws.content:
(a) This section applies to a private club that is defined as a place of public accommodation, resort or amusement in Section 23-1-2 of this Code.

(b) Where a private club allows use of its facilities by one or more adults per membership, the use must be equally available to all adults entitled to use the facilities under the membership. All classes of membership shall be available without regard to race, color, religious beliefs, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression. Memberships that permit use

during restricted times may be allowed only if the restricted times apply to all adults using that membership.

(c) A private club that has food or beverage facilities or services shall allow equal access to those facilities and services for all adults in all membership categories at all times. This subsection shall not require service, or access to facilities, to persons which would violate state or federal law or this Code regarding the sale, consumption, or regulation of alcoholic beverages.

(d) This section does not prohibit a private club from sponsoring or permitting sports schools or leagues for children less than 18 years of age that are limited by age or to members of one sex, if comparable and equally convenient access to the club’s facilities is made available to both sexes and if these activities are not used as a subterfuge to evade the purposes of this article.

(b) This article shall not apply to a private club, or other establishment not open to the public, except to the extent that the goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations of the private club or establishment are made available to the customers or patrons of another establishment that is a place of public accommodation or is licensed by the state under the Michigan Liquor Control Act of 1998, being MCL 436.1 et seq. laws.title: Employment
laws.content:
(a) Unlawful practices. It shall be an unlawful employment practice for any employer, employment agency, or labor organization, or any agent or employee thereof to do or attempt to do, in whole or in part, any of the following:

(1) Discharge, fail or refuse to hire, or otherwise discriminate against any person with respect to compensation, terms, conditions or privileges of employment on the basis of the fact that such person has AIDS or any condition related to AIDS;

(2) Limit, segregate, or classify employees or applicants for employment in any manner which would deprive or tend to deprive any person of employment opportunities, or adversely affect such person's status as an employee on the basis of the fact that such a person has AIDS or any condition related to AIDS;

(3) Fail or refuse to refer for employment or otherwise discriminate against any person on the basis of the fact that such person has AIDS or any condition related to AIDS;

(4) Fail or refuse to include in its membership or to otherwise discriminate against any person; to limit, segregate, or classify its membership; to classify or fail or refuse to refer for membership any person in any way which would deprive or tend to deprive such person of employment opportunities, or otherwise affect such person's status as an employee or as an applicant for employment; or

(5) Discriminate against any person in admission to, or employment in, any program established to provide apprenticeship or other training or retraining, including any on-the-job training program on the basis of the fact that such person has AIDS or any condition related to AIDS.

(b) Bona fide occupational qualification not prohibited; burden of proof. Nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to prohibit a medical procedure or testing based upon a bona fide occupational qualification. In any action brought under this article, if a party asserts that an otherwise discriminatory practice is justified as a bona fide occupational qualification, the party shall have the burden of proving that:

(1) The discrimination is in fact a necessary result of a bona fide occupational qualification; and

(2) There exists no less discriminatory means of satisfying the occupational qualification.

(c) Exceptions.

(1) It shall not be an unlawful discriminatory practice for an employer to observe the conditions of a bona fide employee benefit system, provided, that such systems or plans are not a subterfuge to evade the purposes of this article, provided further, that no such system shall provide an excuse for failure to hire any person.

(2) Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit any act specifically authorized by the laws of the state or any actions taken by or under the direction of the Health Department in order to protect the public health, based upon clear and convincing evidence of a compelling governmental interest in protecting the public health, where such actions are narrowly and specifically directed to that interest, and where

laws.title: Violations and penalties
laws.content:
(a) Where a public servant is alleged to have violated this article, a complaint may be filed with the Department of Human Rights in accordance with Section 23-2-11 of this Code, which shall cause an investigation to be completed regarding the allegations contained within the complaint.

(b) Where a public servant is alleged to have violated this article, and said public servant is under the investigative purview of the Board of Police Commissioners, any complaint filed with the Department of Human Rights shall be forwarded immediately to the Board of Police Commissioners for investigation and disposition in accordance with Section 7-803 of the Charter.

(c) Where a public servant is alleged to have violated this article, and the investigation conducted by the Human Rights Department so warrants, the matter shall be referred, as appropriate, for review, investigation, and disposition to the City Council in accordance with Section 2-107(B) of the Charter for forfeiture proceedings for an office held by an elective City officer, or to the appointing authority in accordance with Section 2-107(C) of the Charter for removal proceedings of a City appointee. Any disciplinary action shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Charter and other laws, City personnel rules, civil service rules, union contracts, or other departmental or agency rules and regulations.

(d) Where a complaint is referred to City Council in accordance with Section 2-107(C) of the Charter, City Council shall exercise its powers of investigation pursuant to Sections 4-109 and 4-110 of the Charter to hold hearing and investigate the matter.

(Code 1984, § 27-9-7; Ord. No. 10-07, § 1(27-9-7), eff. 7-16-2007; Ord. No. 2020-11, § 1, eff. 7-17-2020)

laws.title: Bias-based policing by public servants who are police officers, on the basis of appearance, English-language proficiency, ethnicity, immigration status, manner of dress, national origin, age, height, weight, familial status, marital status, disability, physical characteristics, race, color, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression, or such officer’s perception of same prohibited; exception
Solicitation of immigration status by public servants who are police officers prohibited; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) A public servant who is a police officer:

(1) Shall not solicit information concerning immigration status for the purpose of ascertaining a person’s compliance with federal immigration law; or

(2) Shall not solicit information concerning immigration status from a person who is seeking police services, or is a victim, or is a witness; or

(3) Shall not subject a person to a higher level of scrutiny or to different treatment should a person utilize a passport or municipal identification card as a form of identification.

(b) Notwithstanding the prohibitions set forth in Subsection (a) of this section, public servants who are police officers are expressly permitted to solicit information concerning immigration status from the subject of an investigation only when relevant to the investigation or prosecution of a violent criminal offense, or when processing an arrested person on suspicion of committing a violent felony as defined in Section 23-8-2 of this Code.

(Code 1984, § 27-9-4; Ord. No. 10-07, § 1(27-9-4), eff. 7-16-2007; Ord. No. 2020-11, § 1, eff. 7-17-2020)

laws.title: Solicitation of immigration status by public servants who are not police officers prohibited; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) A public servant who is not a police officer:

(1) Is prohibited from inquiring into the immigration status of any person, or engaging in activities designed to ascertain the immigration status of any person, while acting within the scope of such public servant’s authority, or employment, as a public servant.

(2) Shall not subject a person to a higher level of scrutiny or to different treatment should a person utilize a passport or municipal identification card as a form of identification.

(b) Notwithstanding the prohibitions set forth in Subsection (a) of this section, public servants who are not police officers are expressly permitted to engage in the following activities:

(1) Solicitation of information concerning immigration status where specifically required by any federal or state law, or this Code, or program, as a condition of eligibility for the service sought; or

(2) Solicitation of information concerning immigration status for the purpose of completing I-9 Forms, and, when relevant, in making hiring and payroll withholding decisions, including, but not limited to, completing I-9 Forms, questioning a person to complete the I-9 Form, obtaining documents that support the I-9 Form, and allowing federal authorities to audit an I-9 Form in accordance with law.

(Code 1984, § 27-9-5; Ord. No. 10-07, § 1(27-9-5), eff. 7-16-2007; Ord. No. 2020-11, § 1, eff. 7-17-2020)

laws.title: Reporting requirements

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It is unlawful for any person or entity to do any of the following acts:

(1) To knowingly present false information to the City in the course of applying for a municipal identification card;

(2) To alter, copy, or replicate a municipal identification card without the authority of the City;

(3) To use the municipal identification card issued to another person with the intent to cause a third person or entity to believe that the cardholder is the person to whom the card was issued; or

(4) To fail to surrender a municipal identification card when ordered to do so by the administering agency or by a City department or agency under Section 23-9-9(a) of this Code.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of Subsection (a) of this section shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

(Code 1984, § 27-10-11; Ord. No. 18-16, § 1(27-10-11), eff. 12-3-2016)

laws.title: Issuance, surrender, and replacement of municipal identification cards
laws.content:
(a) Upon request, the administering agency shall issue a municipal identification card to any resident who meets the application requirements set forth in Section 23-9-5 of this Code and pays the applicable fee.

(b) The card shall bear the Seal of the City. The administering agency shall cause the card to be produced in a form intended to thwart replication or counterfeiting.

(c) A card shall be valid for a maximum of two years and shall expire either two years from the date of issuance or when the cardholder is no longer a resident of the City of Detroit, whichever occurs first.

(d) Cardholders shall surrender their municipal identification card to the administering agency upon moving residence outside of the City.

(e) In the event a municipal identification card is stolen, lost or destroyed, the applicant shall re-apply and pay the application fee for a replacement card. An application for a replacement card shall be treated as a new application and the replacement card shall be valid for a maximum of two years from the date of issuance so long as residency in the City is maintained during that time.

(Code 1984, § 27-10-3; Ord. No. 18-16, § 1(27-10-3), eff. 12-3-2016)

laws.title: Application; eligibility and point system requirements
laws.content:
(a) To obtain a municipal identification card, a resident or their legal guardian shall complete and sign the application in the presence of a notary public, under penalty of perjury, requiring proof of identity and proof of residency within the City. Such forms of proof shall be:

(1) Issued by a governmental entity; or

(2) Issued by an entity that takes reasonable steps to verify the identity and/or residency of the individual to whom the card is issued; or

(3) Of a type that is normally accepted as proof of identity and/or residency in the ordinary course of business.

(b) The administering agency shall retain the original application and copies of an applicant’s supporting documentation, including all proof of identity and proof of residency credentials, pursuant to an approved records retention and disposal schedule. The administering agency shall develop and submit to the state for approval an agency-specific retention and disposal schedule setting forth a retention period of two years from the date of issuance.

(c) Documentation of an applicant’s proof of identity and proof of residency shall include:

(1) Any combination of items from Categories A or B, totaling at least 300 points; and

(2) A minimum of one identity credential from Category A containing a photograph and date of birth of the applicant; and

(3) One item from Category C showing proof of City residency within the previous 60 days; and

(4) Items presented by the applicant shall only be used to satisfy one credential and receive point value for that single credential in any category. Items cannot be used in more than one category or to satisfy more than one credential.

(d) Presentation of any one of the following documents shall fully satisfy the proof of residency and identity requirements delineated in Subsection (c) of this section:

(1) Unexpired U.S. passport; or

(2) Unexpired standard or enhanced Michigan operator or chauffeur’s license with a current Detroit address; or

(3) Expired standard or enhanced Michigan operator or chauffeur’s license with a current Detroit

laws.title: Promulgation of procedural rules; implementation of article; language assistance services
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the head of the administering agency is authorized to promulgate procedural rules necessary to effectuate the purpose of this article. The City shall require applicants to declare the information provided in their applications under penalty of perjury by signing the application in the presence of a notary public.

laws.title: Fees
laws.content:
(a) The City shall charge a fee not to exceed $25.00 for each application submitted. Such fees shall not exceed the costs reasonably associated with the production of municipal identification cards and administration of the Municipal Identification Card Program.

(b) The fee charged to minors who are at least 14 years of age but not yet 18 years of age or senior citizens who are 62 years of age or older shall not exceed $10.00.

(c) The fee for renewal or replacement of a municipal identification card shall not exceed $10.00.

laws.title: Acceptance by City departments
laws.content:
(a) When requiring members of the public to provide identification or proof of residency in the City, each City department or agency shall accept a municipal identification card issued pursuant to this article as valid identification and as valid proof of residency in the City, unless such City department or agency has reasonable grounds for determining that the card is counterfeit, altered, or improperly issued to the cardholder, or that the individual presenting the card is not the individual to whom the card was issued. In such cases, the card shall be confiscated and returned to the administering agency with a transmittal letter documenting the circumstances surrounding the confiscation. After review, the administering agency may revoke or return the card to the individual.

(b) Other than requiring the City to accept the municipal identification card as proof of identification and City residency, this section is not intended to replace, preempt, or supersede any other requirements for production of other forms of identification in connection with the administration of City benefits and services. The requirements of this section do not apply under circumstances where:

(1) A federal or state statute, administrative regulation, directive, or court decision requires the City to obtain different identification or proof of residency;

laws.title: Placement of required monuments and markers
laws.content:
(a) The Director of the Department of Public Works may waive, with the approval of the City Council, the placing of required monuments and lot markers for one year from date of plat when it is determined that proposed construction within the subdivision will endanger the monuments and markers. Where placement is waived, $40.00 per monument and a $15.00 per lot marker shall be deposited with the Department of Public Works.

(c) Upon receipt of a surveyor’s certificate that monuments and markers have been placed, the Director of the Department of Public Works shall check for accuracy of placement and approve the refund of any deposited moneys.

laws.title: Determination of minimum lot sizes; street location and width; utility easements
laws.content:
(a) The following requirements shall apply in the determination of minimum lot sizes:

(1) When the public sewer and public water are available in single-family residential zones, the width, depth, and area of lots shall generally conform to or exceed the width, depth and area of other residential parcels in the surrounding neighborhood, provided, that no lot shall be platted at a width or area that is less than the minimum lot size required for the zoning district as established by Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, at the time the preliminary plat is submitted. Where a proposed lot is located in more than one zoning district, the width, depth and area shall comply with the requirements of the more restrictive zone;

(2) Where public sewer and public water are available in two-family and multiple-family residential zones, the width, depth, and area of lots shall generally either conform to or exceed the width, depth and area of other residential parcels in the surrounding neighborhood but must be of a size sufficient for the types of structures which may be erected, to meet the requirements of Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, and Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, Building Code, at the time the preliminary plat is submitted. No lot shall be platted at a width or area that is less than the minimum lot size required for the zone in which such lot is located as established by Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning;

(3) Lot size requirements may be waived by the Director of the Planning and Development Department where the property is already developed and the proposed plat would create parcels conforming to existing individual building units; and

(4) In areas that are zoned for non-residential purposes, the minimum lot width shall be 20 feet and the minimum lot area shall be 2,000 square feet.

(b) The following requirements shall apply to street location and width:

(1) The proposed subdivision shall provide adequate street widths as determined by the objectives of the Master Plan of Policies at the date of submitting of the preliminary plat;

(2) Outlots, which would control access to streets, shall be prohibited;

(3) Any proposed subdivision that includes land located in a floodplain shall be subject to the floodplain control provisions in Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, and Section 138 of the Michigan Land Division Act, being MCL 560.138. Restrictive covenants shall be required to ensure conformance with the floodplain control provisions in Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning. Such restrictive covenants shall be reviewed and approved by the Corporation Counsel and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and shall be filed with the final plat; and

(4) The plat shall not be isolated from or isolate other land from existing public streets unless other suitable access is provided as determined by the Planning and Development Department.

(c) Adequate easements shall be provided for full service of public utilities to every lot within the subdivision. When determined necessary by the Planning and Development Department to comply with the development objectives in the area, certain easements may be limited to underground utilities only.

(Code 1964, § 58A-1-7; Code 1984, § 51-1-4)

State law references—Subdivision within or abutting floodplain, plat requirements, MCL 560.138; subdivision within floodplain, conditions for approval, MCL 560.194.

CD24:4

laws.title: Public improvements
laws.content:
(a) Generally. This section sets forth and defines the public improvements which may be required to be constructed by or at the expense of the proprietor as conditions for final plat approval. All construction shall conform to the applicable provisions in Chapter 43 of this Code, Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places, and Chapter 48 of this Code, Utilities, and to the current standards of the departments involved, and workmanship shall be inspected and approved by the City departments having jurisdiction over the installation. Standards shall be those in effect at the time the preliminary plat is submitted.

(b) Sanitary sewers and storm drainage. When a proposed subdivision is located adjacent to, or reasonably near a public sanitary or combined sewer, the sanitary sewers and other required appurtenances thereto shall be installed in such a manner and be connected to the existing system so that all lots, regardless of their size, will be adequately served. An adequate storm drainage system, including necessary storm or combined sewers, drain inlets, manholes, culverts, bridges, and other appurtenances will be required to remove stormwater from the area being subdivided.

(c) Water supply. An adequate water supply system, including necessary mains, water gates, manholes, fire hydrants, meters, and other required appurtenances shall be installed in such a manner as to adequately serve all lots shown on the plat for domestic, commercial or industrial use, as well as fire protection.

(d) Streets and alleys. All improvements within the jurisdiction of the Department of Public Works located within all streets and alleys, whether public or private, shall be constructed in accordance with Department standards in effect at the time the preliminary plat is submitted and, where required, shall include sidewalks and drainage structures.

(e) Street lighting. All streets and alleys, whether public or private, shall be adequately lighted to conform to standards of the Public Lighting Department in effect at the time the preliminary plat is submitted. Necessary lights, poles, wires, ducts, handholes, manholes, other appurtenances, and connections to existing systems shall be installed so that the subdivision is adequately served. (Code 1964, § 58A-1-8; Code 1984, § 51-1-5)

Cross reference—Improvements and special assessments, § 44-3-1 et seq.

laws.title: Documents providing for setting aside private areas for common use to be filed with final plat
laws.content:
Where the proposed plat includes provisions for setting aside areas for the private but common use of owners of property within the subdivision, deed covenants or other documents covering the use and maintenance of same shall be filed and recorded with the final plat and shall be subject to review and approval by the Corporation Counsel and appropriate City departments. (Code 1964, § 58A-1-9; Code 1984, § 51-1-6)

State law reference—Copies of documents for common use, MCL 560.258.

laws.title: Prepreliminary plat
laws.content:
(a) The proprietor or developer shall submit two copies of the prepreliminary plat to the Planning and Development Department for review of lot size, lot orientation, street layout, street width and overall compliance with Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, and the Master Plan of Policies. Review at this stage shall not constitute

any approval of the proposed preliminary plat but shall serve primarily as guidance to the prospective proprietor.

(b) The Planning and Development Department shall return, within 15 days, a copy of the prepreliminary plat to the proprietor or developer, together with a written response concerning the proposal.

(c) If the findings of the Planning and Development Department indicate that the preliminary plat conforms to the requirements of this section, the Planning and Development Department shall forward a copy of its response to the City Clerk.

(Code 1964, § 58A-1-3; Code 1984, § 51-2-1; Resolution, 1968 Journal of City Council, pp. 2975—2979)

laws.title: Final plat
laws.content:
(a) Where, before the date of expiration of the final approval of the preliminary plat, the proprietor submits a final plat for approval, the City Clerk shall accept same and record the date received. Whenever a final plat is submitted to the City Clerk, it must be accompanied by:

(1) Cash deposit, certified check, surety bond, or bank letter of credit in an amount approved, depending upon the departments involved, by the Water and Sewerage Department, the Department of Public Works, or the Public Lighting Department sufficient to ensure payment of cost to the City for installation of street improvements, pavements, street lighting, sewers and water facilities when required by this Code, provided, that, where a surety bond or bank letter of credit is filed, then such bond or bank letter of credit must be approved by the Corporation Counsel. Whenever cash or a certified check is submitted to the City Clerk, the Clerk shall promptly deposit these funds in a refundable deposit account with the City Treasurer:

a. Where the lots are less than 65 feet in width or have an area less than 12,000 square feet and sewer or water facilities are not existing within the platted area, it is mandatory that prior to certifying the plat, the City Clerk receive notification from the Water and Sewerage Department that a deposit sufficient to ensure installation of those required services has been secured as provided in Section 188(2) of the Act, being MCL 560.188(2).

b. Where sewer and water facilities are existing within the plat and street or other improvements exist or are not required, the departments involved shall certify thereto on the contract forms as delineated in Subsection (c) of this section.

(2) An affidavit from the proprietor or surveyor that monuments and lot markers are in place. Where the Director of the Department of Public Works has approved delaying the placing of monuments for one year, the City Clerk shall secure a deposit sufficient to ensure installation of same in accordance with requirements of this article; and

(3) Copy of the preliminary plat approved by the Health Department in conformance with Sec-

CD24:7
$\S 24-2-24$

DETROIT CITY CODE

tion 118 of the Act, being MCL 560.118, is not required if the area is served by sewer and water facilities and the Water and Sewerage Department has notified the City Clerk as required in Subsection (a)(1)a. of this section.

(b) All easements shall be dedicated to the public and shall be indicated as "public easements" on the final plat.

(c) There shall be a set of contract forms covering the installation of each of the following: water; sewer; street and alley improvements, including sidewalks; street lighting; and survey monuments. Each set is to consist of three copies and each set is to be approved by the Corporation Counsel. The contract forms shall be available in the Planning and Development Department, the Water and Sewerage Department, the Department of Public Works, the Public Lighting Department and the Office of the City Clerk. The enforcement of these contracts shall be the function of the department executing them.

(1) Water. Whenever a provision for the installation of water is necessary as outlined in Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be the duty of the Water and Sewerage Department, through its general manager or a delegated assistant, to complete the contract form and place therein the amount of deposit required to ensure installation of water facilities as provided for by this article. Where water facilities exist within the plat, it shall be so stated in the contract form. The amount of the deposit shall not be less than the amount covered by assessment roll, and, where there is no assessment roll, then such deposit shall be in an amount as determined by the Water and Sewerage Department in accordance with the law.

(2) Sewers. Whenever a provision for the installation of sewers is necessary as outlined in Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be the duty of the Water and Sewerage Department, through its general manager or a delegated assistant, to complete the contract form and place therein the amount of deposit required to ensure the installation of the sewers as provided by this article. Where sewer facilities exist within the plat, it shall be so stated in the contract form. The amount of the deposit shall be in an amount as determined by the Water and Sewerage Department in accordance with the law.

(3) Street and alley improvements. Whenever a provision for the installation of street and alley improvements including sidewalks is necessary as outlined in Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be the duty of the Department of Public Works to complete the contract form and place thereon the amount of deposit required to ensure the installation of the street and alley improvements, including sidewalks as provided by this article. Where improvements are existing within the plat, it shall be so stated in the contract form. The amount of deposit shall be in an amount as determined by the Department of Public Works in accordance with the law.

(4) Street lighting. Whenever a provision for street lighting is necessary as outlined in Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be the duty of the Public Lighting Department, through its Director, to complete the contract form and place therein the amount of deposit required to ensure the installation of these facilities as provided by this article. Where improvements are existing within the plat, it shall be so stated in the contract form. The amount of the deposit shall be in an amount as determined by the Public Lighting Department in accordance with this article.

(5) Survey monuments. Whenever an agreement to delay the placing of survey monuments and lot markers has been approved by the Department of Public Works as outlined in Subsection (a) of this section, it shall be the duty of the Department of Public Works to complete the contract form and place thereon the amount of deposit required to ensure the installation of the monuments and lot markers within the time allowed by this article. Where the monuments and lot markers have been properly placed within the subdivision, it shall be so stated in the contract form. The amount of deposit shall be in an amount as determined by the Department of Public Works in accordance with this article.

(Code 1964, § 58A-1-5; Code 1984, § 51-2-3; Resolution, 1968 Journal of City Council, pp. 2975—2979)

State law references—Survey monuments, MCL 560.125, 560.126; final plat, MCL 560.131—560.173.

laws.title: Division of platted lots
laws.content:
(a) In order to divide the platted lots, the Board of Assessors shall have received:

(1) Written request signed by all parties in interest showing the legal descriptions of the resultant parcels of the requested real property division;

(2) Two plot plans showing dimensions of such resultant parcels;

(3) A fee of $5.00 for each of such resultant parcels; and

(4) A tax memorandum from the City Treasurer showing tax status of all lots involved.

(b) After receipt of the items that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section, the Board of Assessors may divide the platted lots in accordance with the following:

(1) The Board of Assessors may permit division of lots into two, three, or four parts when the area and width of each of the resulting parcels equal or exceed the area and width of a lot as originally platted;

(2) The Board of Assessors may permit the division of lots into two, three, or four parts when the Planning and Development Department has certified that the resulting parcels satisfy the minimum lot size requirements of this article, and where a residential parcel has certified that the width, depth, and area of the resulting parcels either conform to or exceed the width, depth, and area of other residential parcels in the surrounding neighborhood; and

(3) Where there are unusual or unique circumstances, the City Council may approve, after report and recommendation from the Planning and Development Department, division of lots into two, three, or four parts when resulting parcels are less than the original size of lots and when resulting parcels do not satisfy minimum lot requirements of this article. The report of the Planning and Development Department must indicate that the proposed division of a platted lot would allow the development of the land in such a manner as to be compatible with the surrounding land use and development and not contrary to the spirit and purpose of this article and Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, or that the property is presently developed and the proposed division creates parcels conforming to existing individual building units.

(c) In no event shall a division of real property descriptions be made upon the rolls where there are any due and unpaid City taxes or special assessments.
