laws.title: Inspection and certification of approval; land use; construction requirements; maintenance, fire protection and safety, and health and sanitation requirements
Investigation of applicant; qualifications for applicants; findings by Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center
Investigation by Office of Chief Financial Officer required to confirm no City tax or assessment arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by this division shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax, or special assessments are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Liability and property damage insurance required
laws.content:
(a) Every applicant for a license under this division shall file with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center, a certificate of insurance, which has been approved by the Law Department, that states the applicant carries public liability and property damage insurance in the following minimum amounts: $25,000.00 single liability; $50,000.00 total liability; $10,000.00 property damage, and that names the City of Detroit as an additional insured party. Such insurance shall be carried by a firm or corporation duly licensed or permitted to do an insurance business in the state. Further, such insurance shall be kept and maintained in continuous force and effect so long as the applicant and owner of such facility shall be licensed under this division to operate the same within the City.

(b) No license shall be valid in the event of the cancellation of such insurance. Any insurance company issuing insurance as required by this section shall notify the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center of the cancellation of such insurance or any part thereof. The policy shall not expire, or the cancellation take effect, until after ten days’ notice, in writing, is given by the company to the City to run from the date notice is received at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

laws.title: Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to take action upon application
laws.content: Upon compliance with Sections 30-2-21 through 30-2-28 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall issue an annual license for a business in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

laws.title: Posting required; non-transferable
laws.content:
(a) Upon issuance by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center and after receipt by the applicant, a license that is issued under this division shall be posted at all times by the licensee inside the licensed premises in a conspicuous location near the entrance.

(b) All licenses issued under this division are not transferable to another individual, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity.

laws.title: Expiration date and renewal requirements
laws.content:
(a) A license that is issued under this division shall expire on December 31st of each year.

(b) A license that is issued under this division shall remain valid until the expiration date unless suspended or revoked in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

(c) A license that is issued under this division may be renewed only by submitting a completed application and paying the required fee as provided for in this division.

(d) An application for renewal of a license that is issued under this division shall be filed before January 1st of each year.

(Code 1964, § 48-3-7; Code 1984, § 35-4-18.5; Ord. No. 01-85, § 1(48-3-7), eff. 2-4-1985)

laws.title: Suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal
laws.content: A license that is issued under this division may be suspended, revoked, or denied renewal in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

No. 500-H, § 1(62-3-4), effective May 21, 1982 and Ord. No. 01-85, § 1(62-3-6), effective February 4, 1985.

*Cross reference*—Transportation for hire, Ch. 47.

laws.title: Name, address, and license number of trailer owner to be displayed on trailers
laws.content:
Every person operating or causing to be operated upon any of the streets, alleys, avenues, or other public places in the City any trailer, as defined in this article, and prior to the holding out for hire as a trailer owner, shall display on both sides of every trailer, the name, address and license number of the person operating or causing such trailer to be operated. Letters and figures making up the name, address, and license number to be at least three inches in height and not less than one inch in width. The trailer owner shall also keep attached to such trailer at all times a license plate to be furnished by the City, and shall provide a receptacle on the right side of the trailer where a copy of the statement provided for in Section 30-3-5 of this Code can be inserted so that all documents contained therein will be visible at all times.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-8; Code 1984, § 34-4-2)

laws.title: Current state and City trailer license plates required
laws.content:
No trailer owner shall rent a trailer for a local purpose when such trailer does not have thereon current Michigan trailer license plates and current City trailer license plates.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-11; Code 1984, § 34-4-3)

laws.title: Statement from persons renting trailers—Required; copy of same to be placed on trailer
laws.content:
(a) Before any person or entity licensed under this article as a trailer owner shall furnish or rent a trailer to another, such person shall obtain from the person renting such trailer a signed statement, which shall state the name and address of the person owning the articles or goods to be moved in such trailer, the date of the removal, and the address of the place from which and to which the removal is to be made. It shall be the duty of the person licensed under this article to ensure that all of the above required information is placed on such statement, and that the signature and address of the person making such statement is placed on such statement before the trailer is given to the person renting same. It shall be the further duty of the person licensed under this article to place upon such statement the City license number of the trailer that is rented, the name and address of the owner of the propelling vehicle as it appears on the certificate of registration, the name and address

of the operator as it appears on the operator's license, and the Michigan license plate number of the vehicle to which such trailer its attached.

(b) No trailer shall be allowed to leave the premises or lot of the trailer owner until the trailer owner has obtained a fully completed statement, as provided for in Subsection (a) of this section, and a copy thereof has been placed in the receptacle on the trailer, as provided for in Section 30-3-7 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-12; Code 1984, § 34-4-4)

laws.title: Same—Blank forms
laws.content:
The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall furnish to the trailer owner licensed under this article, without cost, printed blanks in book form, entitled, "Statements to be Completed Before Trailers Are Rented." Such books of blank statements shall be prepared so statements can be filled out in triplicate.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-13; Code 1984, § 34-4-5)

laws.title: Same—Statements to be in triplicate; disposition of copies of same
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of all persons licensed under this article to obtain the statement referred to in Section 30-3-5 of this Code, in triplicate, the original copy of which shall be forwarded to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center within ten days from the time it is obtained. Such statements shall be deemed public documents, shall be open to public inspection and shall be kept on file by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center. The second copy of such statement shall be placed on the trailer, as provided in Section 30-3-5 of this Code, and shall remain there in full view during the particular move for which it is issued. The third copy shall be retained by the person licensed to rent trailers, and shall be on hand at all times at the premises of the licensee and subject to police inspection. Such statement shall be completed each time the trailer is taken from the licensee's lot or premises and, if any trailer is not returned to the licensee's lot or premises within 24 hours from the time it is rented or taken away, it shall be the duty of the person licensed under this article to make a notation upon the statement sent into the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center, which indicates when such trailer was rented and when such trailer was returned.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-14; Code 1984, § 34-4-6)

laws.title: False statements
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person securing or renting a trailer, or a trailer owner, or other person to make or sign any false statements, to give any fictitious name or address, or to aid or abet the making or signing of a false statement or the giving of any fictitious name or address.

(Code 1964, § 62-3-15; Code 1984, § 34-4-7)

laws.title: Impersonation of City employees
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to falsely assume or pretend to be a police officer, a firefighter, an inspector of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, a health officer, health inspector or public health nurse of the Health Department, an assessor or such assessor’s agent or employee, an inspector or meter reader for the Water and Sewerage Department, or any other person employed by the City or by any other governmental agency for the protection of the peace, health, and safety of the City, or to take upon such person to act as such or to require any person to aid and assist such person in any manner pertaining to the duties of persons employed by the City for the protection of the peace, health, and safety of the People of the City of Detroit.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-25; Code 1984, § 38-2-1)

*Cross reference—Wearing of uniforms simulating police uniforms, § 26-2-2.*

*State law reference—False personation of officers, MCL 750.215.*

*Cross reference—Administration generally, Ch. 2.*

laws.title: Interference with public servants in the performance of their duties unlawful
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly or intentionally:

(1) Fail to comply with the lawful command of a police officer;

(2) Interfere with or obstruct any public servant in the performance of their duties as a public servant; or

(3) Engage in any threatening or intimidating conduct toward any public servant in the performance of their duties as a public servant that places the public servant in reasonable apprehension of physical harm in the furtherance of such duties.

(b) For purposes of this section, the following words and phrases shall have the meaning respectively ascribed to them by this subsection:

*Police officer* means any person sworn as a member of the Police Department authorized to enforce this Code, state law, and, where applicable, federal law.

*Public servant* means the Mayor, members of the City Council, the City Clerk, appointive officers, any member of a board, commission, or other voting body that is established by either branch of City government by the Charter or by this Code, and any appointee, any employee, or any individual who provides services to the City within or outside of its offices or facilities pursuant to a personal services contract.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-26.1; Code 1984, § 38-2-2; Ord. No. 2021-39, § 1, eff. 11-19-2021)

*State law reference—Obstruction of police officer, MCL 750.479.*

laws.title: Interference with firefighters or members of Emergency Medical Service; obedience to orders of firefighters
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly obstruct or interfere with any member of the Fire Department in the performance of such member’s duties or to willfully disobey any reasonable order, rule, or regulation of the officer commanding any Fire Department while in the vicinity of any fire or alarm of fire.

laws.title: False reports to police
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to report or cause to be reported any felony or misdemeanor, or give any information relating to any such felony or misdemeanor, to the Police Department or to any member of the Police Department by telephone, in writing or by any other means of communication, knowing that no such felony or misdemeanor has in fact been committed.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to give any information or report to any member of the Police Department relating to any felony or misdemeanor, when the information or report is false and such person knows the information or report to be false.

(Code 1964, $\S 39-1-14$ ; Code 1984, $\S 38-2-4$ )

State law references—False reporting of crime, MCL 750.411a; false reports to police radio broadcasting stations, MCL 750.509.

(Code 1964, $\S 19-1-2$ ; Code 1984, $\S 38-13-3$ ; Ord. No. 2021-29, $\S 1$ , eff. 10-19-2021)

(h) A public accommodation shall not do either of the following:

(1) Require documentation when making an inquiry under Subsection (g) of this section; or

(2) Make an inquiry under Subsection (g) of this section where it is readily apparent that the service animal is trained to do work or perform tasks for an individual with a disability.

(i) A person with a disability shall be permitted to be accompanied by his or her service animal in all areas of a place of public accommodation where members of the public, program participants, clients, customers, patrons, or invitees are permitted to go, including public areas of establishments that sell or prepare food, even where state or local health codes prohibit animals on the premises. A public accommodation may exclude a service animal from a facility where the service animal’s presence interferes with legitimate safety requirements of the facility such as a surgery or burn unit in a hospital in which a sterile field is required.

(j) A public accommodation shall not isolate a person with a disability accompanied by his or her service animal, treat a person with a disability accompanied by his or her service animal less favorably than other patrons, or charge a fee to a person with a disability accompanied by his or her service animal that is not charged to other patrons without service animals. A public accommodation shall not ask or require a person with a disability to pay a surcharge, regardless of whether people accompanied by pets are required to pay a surcharge, or to comply with other requirements that are not applicable to people without pets. Where a public accommodation normally charges people for damage caused, the public accommodation may charge a person with a disability for damage caused by his or her service animal.

(k) A public accommodation that violates Subsections (b), (d), (g), (h), (i), or (j) of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-62; Code 1984, § 38-1-8)

laws.title: Protection of blind pedestrian carry cane, or using guide dog or walker; definitions; misdemeanor; penalties
laws.content:
(a) Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following words, terms, and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this subsection:

*Blind* means, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Michigan Use of Travel Aids by Blind Persons Act, being MCL 752.51a, a person who has a visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the better eye with correction, or has limitation of his or her field of vision such that the widest diameter of the visual field subtends an angular distance not greater than 20 degrees.

*Cane* means, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Michigan Use of Travel Aids by Blind Persons Act, being MCL 752.51a, an aid used by a blind pedestrian for travel and identification purposes that is white in color and with or without a red tip.

*Crosswalk* means, as likewise defined in Section 10 of the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.10:

(1) That part of a roadway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks on opposite sides of the highway measured from the curbs, or in the absence of curbs from the edges of the traversable highway; and

(2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface.

*Dog guide* means, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Michigan Use of Travel Aids by Blind Persons Act, being MCL 752.51a, a dog, in harness, that has been formally trained and that is used by a blind person as a travel aid.

*Walker* means, as likewise defined in Section 1a of the Michigan Use of Travel Aids by Blind Persons Act, being MCL 752.51a, an aid used by a blind pedestrian for travel and identification purposes that is white in color or has white legs with or without a red tip.

(b) White cane, with or without red tip, to be carried or used by blind persons only. It shall be unlawful for any person, except persons wholly or partially blind, to carry or use upon the public streets and highways of the City any cane, as defined in Subsection (a) of this section, provided, that such a cane may be used upon the streets, highways and other public places of the City by persons wholly or partially blind as a means of protecting them and for the purpose of identifying them to operators of motor vehicles and other pedestrians with whom they come in contact on such streets, highways, and public places.

(c) Duty of driver to take necessary precautions to blind pedestrian carrying cane or using dog guide or walker. A driver of a vehicle shall not approach a cross-

walk or any other pedestrian crossing without taking all necessary precautions to avoid accident or injury to a blind pedestrian carrying a cane, or using a dog guide or walker.

(d) Duty of driver to yield right-of-way to persons in crosswalks carrying white canes, or using dog guide or walker. Any driver of a vehicle approaching a crosswalk where a person blind or partially blind is holding a cane, as defined in Subsection (a) of this section, waist high over the street, or using a dog guide or walker, shall come to a full stop back of the crosswalk and remain stopped, taking such precautions as are necessary to avoid accident or injury to such blind person.

(e) Duty of driver to yield right-of-way to persons within intersections carrying white canes, or using dog guide or walker. Any driver of a vehicle who approaches a person lawfully within the intersection who is blind or partially blind, carrying a cane, as defined in Subsection (a) of this section, or being led by a guide dog wearing a harness and walking on either side of and slightly in front of such blind person shall immediately come to a full stop ten feet from the blind person and take such precautions before proceeding as may be necessary to avoid accident or injury.

(f) Penalties. A person who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or by a fine of not more than $100.00, or both in the discretion of the court.

(Code 1964, §§ 38-12-5, 38-12-6, 38-12-7, 38-12-8; Code 1984, §§ 55-12-25, 55-12-26, 55-12-27, 55-12-28)

State law reference—Protection of blind persons, MCL 752.51a et seq.

laws.title: Trespassing in vacant buildings, occupied dwellings, and active commercial establishments
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, except an officer, employee, or contractual agent of a governmental agency in the performance of a public duty to enter a vacant building, or the property on which the vacant building is located, without the express written authorization of the property owner, lessee, agent, or trustee thereof.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to enter, without permission, the occupied dwelling of another, or the property on which the occupied dwelling of another is located, after having been forbidden to do so by the owner or occupant, or the agent of the owner or occupant.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to remain on an active commercial establishment, or the property on which an active commercial establishment is located, after being requested to leave by the owner or occupant, or the agent of the owner or occupant.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-92; Code 1984, § 38-4-1; Ord. No. 19-12, § 1(38-4-1), eff. 9-28-2012)

Cross references—Unauthorized entry upon garden plots, § 33-3-4; trespassing by solicitors of fire repair contract, § 34-5-8.

laws.title: Signs on vacant buildings
laws.content:
(a) It shall be the duty of the Police Department, when requested by an owner or agent, to cause every vacant house, store, shop or other buildings, whatsoever, in the City to be placarded with a suitable sign, the same to be designed and procured in sufficient numbers by the Chief of Police or some other person designated by the Chief, such sign to read as follows: "THIS PROPERTY UNDER POLICE PROTECTION. ANY PERSON DEFACING, DESTROYING OR DAMAGING SAME OR ANY PART THEREOF WILL BE PROSECUTED."

(b) No person shall destroy, damage, deface, or molest any sign placed upon any vacant property as provided for in Subsection (a) of this section. Such signs shall be removed from such house, store, shop, or other building only upon authority of the Police Department. (Code 1964, § 39-1-47; Code 1984, § 38-4-8)

laws.title: Removal of bricks, piping, plumbing, lighting and heating fixtures, appliances, metal materials or appurtenances from vacant building or structure without written authorization
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for any person, except an officer, employee, or contractual agent of a governmental agency in the performance of a public duty to remove bricks, piping, plumbing, lighting or heating fixtures, appliances, iron, brass, copper, tin, zinc, aluminum or other scrap metal materials, or other appurtenances from any vacant building or structure in the City without the written authorization of the property owner, lessee, agent, or trustee thereof. (Code 1964, § 39-1-93; Code 1984, § 38-4-7)

laws.title: Possession of burglar's tools
laws.content:
(a) Any person who shall knowingly have in such person's possession or control any nitroglycerine, or other explosive, thermite, engine, machine, tool or implement, device, chemical or substance, adapted and designed for cutting or burning through, forcing or breaking open any building, room, vault, safe, motor vehicle, motor vehicle trunk or glove compartment, or other depository, or for starting the engine of a motor vehicle or driving away a motor vehicle without the regular key, in order to steal any money or other property, knowing the same to be adapted and designed for one or more of the purposes aforesaid, with intent to use or employ the same for one or more of the purposes aforesaid, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(b) For the purposes of this section, where it is established that any person had in such person's possession or control a vehicle repair tool commonly referred to as a knocker set, a slammer, or a puller, consisting of a shaft with a screw attached thereto and a weighted sleeve that slides on such shaft, outside the curtilage of such person's own domicile and outside the curtilage of a garage or repair shop where such person was employed, it shall be presumed that such person intended to use such vehicle repair tool for the purpose of driving away a motor vehicle. Such presumption may be rebutted by proof that such vehicle repair tool was in transit from one place to another and was essential for the possessor's employment, or that the possession was intended for a lawful purpose. (Code 1964, § 39-1-10; Code 1984, § 38-4-10)

State law reference—Possession of burglar's tools, MCL 750.116.

laws.title: Unauthorized ascending, scaling, climbing on, rappelling down, or descending of building or structure without written authorization
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully ascend, scale, climb on, rappel down, or descend any private, or public, building or structure without the written authorization of the property owner, lessee, agent or trustee thereof, or for any person ascending, scaling, climbing on, rappelling down, or descending any private, or public, building or structure, upon being notified to discontinue such activity by the owner, lessee, agent or trustee thereof, to neglect or refuse to do so. (Code 1984, § 38-4-1; Ord. No. 573-H, § 1(39-1-98), eff. 1-8-1984)

laws.title: Unauthorized entry into hospitals
laws.content: It shall be unlawful for any person to enter into any patient area or working area of any hospital unless such person has been properly authorized to enter into such areas by the hospital administrators. (Code 1964, § 39-1-23.1; Code 1984, § 38-4-2)

laws.title: Unauthorized entry into private residential swimming pools
laws.content:
No private residential swimming pool shall be entered except by the owner and the owner's invited guests. (Code 1964, § 39-1-87; Code 1984, § 38-4-3)

**Sec. 31-4-8. Malicious destruction of property; penalties.**

(a) No person shall willfully and maliciously destroy, damage, mutilate, or in any manner deface, including, but not limited to, placing graffiti upon any real or personal property of another person, whether public or private, where the resulting damage is less than $200.00.

(b) Because a violation of this section substantially corresponds to a violation of Sections 377a(1)(d), 380(1), and 380(5) of the Michigan Penal Code, being MCL 750.377a(1)(d), MCL 750.380(1) and MCL 750.380(5), the penalty for violation shall be imprisonment for not more than 93 days or a fine of not more than $ 500.00, or both, for each such offense, in accordance with Section 3(k) and Section 4i(k) of the Michigan Home Rule City Act, being MCL 117.3(k) and MCL 117.4i(k), and Section 1-1-9(a)(1) of this Code.

(Code 1964, §§ 39-1-30, 39-1-46, 39-1-48, 39-1-55; Code 1984, § 38-4-4; Ord. No. 02-15, § 1(38-4-4), eff. 3-3-2015)

*State law reference—Willful and malicious destruction of property, MCL 750.377a et seq.*

**Sec. 31-4-9. Destruction, damage, defacement or pollution of drinking fountains.**

No person shall destroy, damage or in any manner deface any of the drinking fountains located in the City, throw or deposit any substance therein or in any manner pollute the water in the basins of such fountains or detach the cups therefrom.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-12; Code 1984, § 38-4-5)

**Sec. 31-4-10. Damaging, polluting, drawing water, etc., from reservoirs.**

(a) No person shall damage any public reservoir, break or enter the same, or throw or deposit any substance therein.

(b) No person shall draw off any water therefrom, except in case of fire or for the use of the Fire Department, without authority from the City Council, the Board of Water Commissioners, or the Fire Department.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-60; Code 1984, § 38-4-6)

*Cross reference—Water generally, § 48-1-1 et seq.*

*State law reference—Maliciously destroying dams, canals, etc., MCL 750.378.*

**Sec. 31-4-11. Serial numbers of appliances, watches, outboard motors, and other items.**

(a) Removal, concealing, defacement, alteration, and the like prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to conceal or misrepresent the identity, by removing, concealing, defacing, adding to, substituting, or altering the serial number or manufacturer’s number, of any motor, appliance, mechanical device, watch, clock, camera, precision instrument, outboard motor, radio, shotgun or any other article or thing whereon the manufacturer has placed numbers for the purpose of identification of such motor, appliance, mechanical device, watch, clock, camera, precision instrument, outboard motor, radio, shotgun, article or thing, or to alter or replace any part of such motor, appliance, mechanical device, watch, clock, camera, precision instrument, outboard motor, radio, shotgun, article or thing bearing the serial or manufacturer’s number with a new or replaced part upon which the proper serial or manufacturer’s number has not been stamped or placed.

(b) Dealing in or possession of articles where serial number defaced or altered. It shall be unlawful to deal in or possess any motor, appliance, mechanical device, watch, clock, camera, precision instrument, outboard motor, radio, shotgun or other article or thing from which the serial numbers have been removed, concealed, defaced, added to, substituted or altered, when such article or thing has had serial or other numbers placed thereon by the manufacturer for identification.

(c) Possession of articles with numbers removed, concealed, defaced, altered, and the like prima facie evidence of violations. In all prosecutions under this section, possession by any dealer, distributor, wholesaler, or other person in the business of buying and selling any motor, appliance, mechanical device, watch, clock, camera, precision instrument, outboard motor, radio, shotgun or other article or thing with the manufacturer’s number or identification number removed, concealed, defaced, added to, substituted or altered shall be prima facie evidence of a violation of this section.

(Code 1964, §§ 39-1-63—39-1-65; Code 1984, § 38-4-9)

**Sec. 31-4-12. Sales at price greater than printed on ticket prohibited.**

Unless authorized by state law or by this Code, no person shall sell, or offer for sale, any ticket of admission to any athletic event, concert, public entertainment, show, or theater at a price greater than the price that is printed on the ticket.

(Code 1984, § 5-1-2; Ord. No. 11-04, § 1(5-1-2), eff. 4-7-2004)

*State law reference—Sale of tickets, MCL 750.465.*

laws.title: Engaging in business of parking of vehicles on public property
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, either by such person or through another, to engage in the business of parking of vehicles or reserving space for the parking of vehicles upon any public highway or public place in the City for remuneration, by tips or otherwise, or to solicit the business of parking vehicles or reserving space for the parking of vehicles upon any highway or public space in the City.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-43; Code 1984, § 38-1-6)

*Cross reference—Traffic and vehicles, Ch. 46.*

laws.title: Bringing alcoholic liquor onto licensed premises
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to bring any alcoholic liquor upon the premises of a licensee, or upon the designated location of a special licensee, who is licensed to sell alcoholic liquor under the Michigan Liquor Control Code of 1998, being MCL 436.1101 *et seq.*

(Code 1964, § 39-1-94; Code 1984, § 38-1-14)

laws.title: Spitting in public
laws.content:
Spitting upon floors of public buildings or buildings used for public assemblages upon the floors or platforms or any part of any railway, boat or other public conveyance or upon any public sidewalk is prohibited. Expectoration may be made into gutters or receptacles provided for same.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-72; Code 1984, § 38-1-9)

*Cross reference—Health generally, Ch. 20.*

laws.title: Use of steam-producing equipment restricted
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful in the City for any person or anyone acting in behalf of any other person to use any equipment for cleaning purposes, other than the cleaning of buildings or other fixed structures, that emits steam, water vapor, or high velocity water within 200 feet of any dwelling or other residential occupancy, except in a building that shall have no openings that permit any such high velocity water, water vapor, or steam resulting from the operation of such equipment so as to not create a nuisance to the neighboring property.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-77; Code 1984, § 38-1-10)

laws.title: Disorderly conduct
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to make or assist in making any noise, disturbance, or improper diversion, or any rout or riot, by which the peace and good order of the neighborhood is disturbed.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-7; Code 1984, § 38-5-1; Ord. No. 29-10, § 1(38-5-1), eff. 12-10-2010; Ord. No. 42-16, § 1(38-5-1), eff. 12-22-2016)

laws.title: Loitering in public buildings for purpose of soliciting legal services or services of sureties
laws.content:

(Code 1964, § 39-1-31; Code 1984, § 38-1-4)

laws.title: Same—Throwing of bottles, cans, receptacles or objects prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to cast, throw, hurl or fling any bottle, can, receptacle, or any other object which could cause injury or damage in the spectator area where any athletic contest or exhibition is conducted, or into or upon the area used to conduct such contest or exhibition, while the same is in progress and during intermissions and delays of such contest or exhibition.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-2; Code 1984, § 38-5-4)

*Cross reference—Amusements and entertainments generally, Ch. 5.*

laws.title: Keeping of house of assignation or prostitution, gaming house, or disorderly business or house prohibited
laws.content:
No person shall keep, within the City, any house of assignation, or place of prostitution for the resort of prostitutes, or a disorderly saloon, barroom, tavern, beer hall, grocery, theater, room, ordinary house or building of any kind, or any house, room or building for gaming with cards, dice, billiards, nine- or ten-pin alleys, wheels of fortune, boxes, machines or other instruments or devices whatever, or shall in any manner contribute to the support, carrying on or keeping of any such house or place.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-8; Code 1984, § 38-5-5)

*State law references—House of ill fame, MCL 750.452; gaming room, MCL 750.303.*

laws.title: Leasing building for prohibited purposes
laws.content:
No person shall knowingly let or lease any house, saloon, barroom, tavern, theater, store, room or building of any kind to be used as a house of assignation, place of prostitution for the resort of prostitutes or disorderly persons, or for the purpose of gambling for money or other property, or as a disorderly house, saloon, barroom, tavern, theater or room, or knowing such person’s house, building or place to be so used, willingly permit its further use for any such purpose.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-9; Code 1984, § 38-5-6)

**Sec. 31-5-15. Prohibiting unauthorized entry upon and use of designated race course.**

(a) Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following words and phrases shall have the meaning respectively ascribed to them by this subsection:

*Designated race course* means any track which has been formed by the temporary closing of public streets or public rights-of-way for the purpose of conducting a motorized race which may include, but is not limited to, vehicles referred to as "Formula One Cars" or "Indy Cars" or "CART Racing Cars."

*Officially closed to the public* means when construction of the designated race course is completed for racing:

(1) By the erection of necessary barricades to prevent the ingress and egress of persons who are not participants or officials; and

(2) By the posting of signs along the track to give notice that unauthorized entry upon and use of the designated race course by persons who are not participants or officials is prohibited.

*Officials* means persons who, as employees or agents of the City or the organization sponsoring the racing events, are allowed ingress and egress upon the designated race course to protect the peace, health, safety, and welfare of the public, participants, or other officials and/or to maintain the designated race course.

*Participants* means persons who are allowed ingress and egress upon the designated race course to operate and maintain their respective racing vehicles and/or to assist in conducting the racing events.

(b) Designated race course, unauthorized entry prohibited, exceptions.

(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to be, enter, walk, jog, roller skate, skateboard, bicycle or drive any motorized vehicle upon a designated race course at any time after the track has been officially closed to the public.

(2) This section shall not apply to participants or officials.

(Code 1984, § 38-5-7; Ord. No. 11-89, § 1(38-5-7), eff. 6-15-1989)

**Sec. 31-5-16. Firing of cannon.**

No person shall fire a cannon in any public street, avenue, alley, park or other public place without first having obtained a written permit from the Mayor, which permit shall only be granted when it appears to the Mayor that such firing is to be done under the supervision of experienced gunners. No such permit from the Mayor shall be construed to incur on the part of the City any liability for damage by reason of any accident caused by such firing.

(Code 1964, § 66-1-9; Code 1984, § 38-10-10)

**Sec. 31-5-17. Spectating, organizing, and participating in the preparations for a dangerous driving exhibition; presence; definitions.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly:

(1) Be present as an exhibition spectator at a dangerous driving exhibition conducted on a public street, a highway, or private property open to the general public without the consent of the owner, operator, or agent thereof;

(2) Be present as a exhibition spectator where preparations for a dangerous driving exhibition are being made;

(3) Act as an exhibition organizer of a dangerous driving exhibition; or

(4) Participate in the preparations for a dangerous driving exhibition.

(b) A person is considered to be present at a dangerous driving exhibition when within 200 feet of any portion of the location of the event, or within 200 feet of any portion of the location where preparations for a dangerous driving exhibition are being made.

(c) For purposes of this section, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this subsection:

*Dangerous driving exhibition* means an event where a motor vehicle is involved in drag racing or another form of driving prowess, including, but is not limited to, donuts, drifting, and sliding, which is recklessly dangerous and threatens the health and safety of the public, interferes with pedestrian and vehicular traffic, creates a public nuisance, or interferes with the right of private businesses or residents to enjoy the use of their property.

*Donuts* means a driving technique where a driver maneuvers a vehicle to create circles or figure eights by intentionally and unnecessarily causing the vehicle to move in a zigzag or circular course, or to gyrate or spin around.

laws.title: Prohibition on direct fueling of an unregistered ATV or ORV at gas stations
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for an owner, operator, or employee of any gas station or other retail dealer of gasoline to sell, offer for sale, or attempt to sell gasoline for use in any unregistered ATV or ORV, or permit any such vehicle’s tank to be filled.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to purchase or attempt to purchase gasoline from a gas station for use in an unregistered ATV or ORV.

(c) Signs with the words "FUELING OF AN UNREGISTERED ATV OR ORV PROHIBITED" shall be posted at all dispensing locations.

(d) Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this subsection:

*ATV* means a vehicle, also referred to as an "all-terrain vehicle," with three or more wheels that is designed for off-road use, has low-pressure tires, has a seat designed to be straddled by the rider, and is powered by a 50cc to 1,000cc gasoline engine or an engine of comparable size using other fuels.

*ORV* means a motor-driven off-road recreation vehicle, also referred to as an "off-road vehicle," capable of cross-country travel without benefit of a road or trail, on or immediately over land, snow, ice, marsh, swampland, or other natural terrain. A multitrack or multiwheel drive vehicle, a motorcycle or related 2-wheel vehicle, a vehicle with three or more wheels, an amphibious machine, a ground effect air cushion vehicle, or other means of transportation may be an ORV. An ATV is an ORV. An ORV does not include a registered snowmobile, a farm vehicle being used for farming, a vehicle used for military, fire, emergency, or law enforcement purposes, a vehicle owned and operated by a utility company or an oil or gas company when performing maintenance on its facilities or on property over which it has an easement, a construction or logging vehicle used in performance of its common function, or a registered aircraft.

(Ord. No. 2023-28, § 1, eff. 8-24-2023)

laws.title: Abandonment of iceboxes, refrigerators, freezers and other airtight containers
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful, in the City, for any person to leave outside of any building, structure or dwelling, in a place accessible to children, any abandoned, unattended or discarded icebox, refrigerator, freezer or any other container of any kind which has an airtight snaplock or other locking device thereon without first removing the doors or covers from such icebox, refrigerator, freezer or container.

(b) Any owner of any vacant building shall remove the doors or covers from all iceboxes, refrigerators, freezers or containers within the vacant building. The owner of any garage accessible to children shall remove the doors or covers from all iceboxes, refrigerators, freezers or containers within the garage.

laws.title: Unsolicited delivery of dangerous substances
laws.content:
No person shall deliver, leave or place upon the steps, porch, doorway or premises of any dwelling within the City any goods, wares, merchandise, liquids, mixtures or any product whatsoever, which contain substances or ingredients that are or may become inherently or potentially dangerous, deleterious, poisonous or noxious to human beings or animals, or that may be inflammable or dangerously volatile, unless or until the owner, lessee, tenant or person residing within such dwelling or such person’s agent shall have authorized such delivery or personally accepts the same.

laws.title: Duty of riparian owners to erect and maintain barriers, dikes, and embankments as protection from floodwaters
laws.content:
Whenever the Director of the Department of Public Works finds that, because of the rising of the level of the waters in canals, rivers, navigable streams or similar places in the City, the safety, health, property and general welfare of the public is endangered by floodwaters and that immediate action is necessary to protect such public interests, the Director shall notify the riparian owners thereon, at the address given in the last assessment roll, and shall also post a notice on every lot, building or structure thereon to immediately provide adequate barriers, dikes or other embankments to protect against the overflow of floodwaters. Should any such owner fail to so provide, the Director shall proceed, with the sanction of the City Council, to provide such barriers, dikes or embankments. No barrier, dike or embankment, once so constructed, shall be altered or removed without the consent, in writing, of the Director. Each riparian owner shall maintain such structures at such owner’s own expense. From time to time, the Director may examine such structures, and shall give notice to any owner as aforesaid of failure to maintain. If, after notice, such owner fails to maintain as required, the Director shall enter upon such premises and reinforce or replace such defective barriers, dikes, or embankments. Such reinforcement or replacement shall be at the expense of such riparian owner, and the City shall bring an action against the owner for the full cost of the reinforcement or replacement.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-6; Code 1984, § 38-6-4)

laws.title: Filling or draining of excavations on private property; barricades
laws.content:
Every person having control or management of land on which there is an excavation, other than for construction purposes under a building permit, shall cause the same to be filled with earth, clay, sand or other solid filler, even with the grade of the land before any excavation was made, or shall cause any water therein to be drained therefrom and shall thereafter prevent water from accumulating or standing therein. Substantial barricades, at least four feet in height, shall also be provided and maintained around all such excavations.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-13; Code 1984, § 38-6-5)

**Sec. 31-7-2. Disturbing schools.**

No person shall willfully or maliciously make or assist in making any noise, disturbance, or improper diversion by which the peace, quietude, or good order of any public, private, or parochial school is disturbed.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-57; Code 1984, § 38-7-2)

*Case law annotation—Section upheld against attack as being overboard. McAlpine v Reese, 309 F Supp 136 (ED Mich SD, 1970).*

**Sec. 31-7-3. Indecent or obscene conduct.**

No person shall engage in indecent or obscene conduct in any building or on any property adjacent to any building in the City occupied as a public, private, or parochial school.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-58; Code 1984, § 38-7-3)

**Sec. 31-7-4. Unauthorized persons not to enter or remain in school buildings.**

(a) No person shall create a disturbance in any private, public or parochial school, or on the surrounding school grounds, or on fields or recreational areas or other grounds lawfully used for school activities while such activities are in progress.

(b) No person, who is not a regularly enrolled student, or a teacher or other employee, at such school, shall enter and remain in any public, private or parochial school building between 7:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on days when school is in session, unless such person has first proceeded to the administrative offices and identified themselves to the principal or the principal’s designee.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to enter and remain in any public, private or parochial school, or on surrounding school grounds within 250 feet of the school building, between 7:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on days when school is in session, except for regularly enrolled students, or teachers or other employees, who have not been excluded from the school on the applicable date, unless the person has first proceeded to the administrative offices and identified themselves to the principal or the principal’s designee.

(Code 1964, §§ 39-1-59, 39-1-59.1; Code 1984, § 38-7-4; Ord. No. 29-08, § 1(38-7-4), eff. 12-19-2008)

**Sec. 31-7-5. Presence on school grounds after sunset.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to be on any school grounds after sunset unless such person is actively engaged in a school-sponsored function or a supervised recreational activity, or is participating in an athletic event or is a spectator at such event.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-59.4; Code 1984, § 38-7-5)

**Sec. 31-7-6. Unauthorized borrowing of money or thing of value from students in school or traveling to or from school.**

It shall be unlawful for any person to borrow or attempt to borrow any money or thing of value from any student in any public, private or parochial school or on any public, private or parochial school property in the City or during any time when any such student is going to or returning from any regularly scheduled session of any such school without first obtaining the written approval of the principal of such school or other person designated by the principal to issue written approval.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-59.2; Code 1984, § 38-7-6)

laws.title: False alarms; repeat offenders; exemptions
laws.content:

**Sec. 31-9-26. Selling, furnishing, supplying, or giving away of hypodermic syringes or needles prohibited.**

It shall be unlawful to sell, furnish, supply, or give away to any person any hypodermic syringe or needle, or other instrument or implement which may be adapted for the dispensing or use of any controlled substance by subcutaneous injection or intracutaneous injection, or any other manner or method of introduction into the human body, unless:

(1) The person who is selling, furnishing, supplying, or giving away said hypodermic syringe or needle, or other instrument or implement is licensed by the state;

(2) The person who is buying or receiving said hypodermic syringe or needle, or other instrument or implement, is in possession of a prescription form for such item; and

(3) The prescription referred to in Subsection (2) of this section is issued by a licensed medical doctor or osteopathic physician within the period of one year prior to the purchase or receipt of said hypodermic syringe or needle, or other instrument or implement.

(Code 1984, § 38-11-26; Ord. No. 15-96, § 1(38-11-26), eff. 8-16-1996)

**Sec. 31-9-27. Fraud and deceit in obtaining hypodermic syringes or needles by, and unauthorized use of, a prescription form prohibited.**

(a) Any fraud, deceit, misrepresentation, subterfuge, or concealment of a material fact, including providing a false name or a false address for the purpose of obtaining any hypodermic syringe or needle or other instrument or implement or providing a false statement upon any prescription form, shall be deemed a violation of this division.

(b) A person who has obtained the possession of any hypodermic syringe, needle, or other instrument shall not use or alter the same, or permit or authorize its use or alteration, for any purpose other than that specifically provided for by the prescription form.

(Code 1984, § 38-11-27; Ord. No. 15-96, § 1(38-11-27), eff. 8-16-1996)

**Sec. 31-9-28. Presence in places where hypodermic syringes or needles are illegally stored or kept prohibited.**

A person shall not knowingly remain in any building, dwelling, store, vehicle, boat, boathouse, airplane or any other place where any hypodermic syringe, needle, or other instrument or implement adapted for the use of any controlled substance by subcutaneous injection or intracutaneous injection, or any other manner or method of introduction into the human body, is illegally sold, dispensed, furnished, given away, stored, or kept with the intent to unlawfully use or possess such hypodermic syringe, needle, implement or instrument.

(Code 1984, § 38-11-28; Ord. No. 15-96, § 1(38-11-28), eff. 8-16-1996)

**Sec. 31-9-29. Exceptions for possession of drug paraphernalia, including hypodermic syringes and needles.**

The provisions of this division that restrict the possession of any drug paraphernalia, including any hypodermic syringe, needle, or other implement or instrument adapted for the use of subcutaneous injection or intracutaneous injection, or any other manner or method of introduction into the human body, shall not apply:

(1) To an object sold, or offered for sale, to a person licensed under the Michigan Occupational Code, being MCL 339.101 through 339.2677, for use in said profession, or to any intern, trainee, apprentice or assistant in a profession that is licensed under the Michigan Occupational Code, being MCL 339.101 through 339.2677, for use in said profession;

(2) To an object sold, or offered for sale, to any hospital, sanitarium, clinical laboratory, or other health care institution, including a penal, correctional, or juvenile detention facility for use in said institution;

(3) To an object sold, or offered for sale, to a dealer in medical, dental, surgical, or pharmaceutical supplies;

(4) To equipment, a product, or material which may be used in the preparation or smoking of tobacco or smoking herbs other than a controlled substance;

(5) To a blender, bowl, container, spoon, or mixing device not specifically designed for a use defined in Section 31-9-21 of this Code;

laws.title: Self-executing, severability, and conflicting provisions
laws.content: This division shall be liberally construed so as to effectuate the purposes hereof. If any term, clause, provision, or part of this division or its application is held invalid or unenforceable, such invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect other terms, clauses, provisions, parts or applications of this division that can be given effect without the invalid terms, clauses, provisions, parts, or applications. All terms, clauses, provisions, parts or applications of this division are self-executing except as specified herein, are severable, and except where otherwise indicated in the text shall supersede conflicting provisions or amendments of this Code and any regulations promulgated thereto. (Ord. No. 2021-62, § 1, eff. 11-12-2021)

laws.title: Prohibition generally; exception
laws.content:
(a) A person shall not engage in a game of chance that is prohibited by state law.

(b) A person shall not have in such person's possession any evidence of illegal gambling that is in the nature of policy or pool tickets, slips or checks, or memoranda of any combination or bet, or any policy, wheel, dice, implement, apparatus or material of any form of illegal gambling or lottery.

(c) A person who is the owner or is in control of a premises shall not knowingly permit the use or occupancy thereof for gambling, or the use, possession, or presence of gambling apparatus or paraphernalia therein, unless the person in control of the premises is licensed to operate a casino by the Michigan Gaming Control Board in accordance with the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, being MCL 432.201 et seq.

(Code 1984, § 38-8-1; Ord. No. 15-99, § 1(38-8-1), eff. 7-23-1999)

laws.title: Lotteries, pools, bucket shops, and any like scheme
laws.content:
No person shall keep, carry on, maintain or aid in keeping, carrying on or maintaining any lottery, policy, pool, bucket shop, board, exchange or any like scheme or policy for drawing or disposing of money or any other property within the City. The term "lottery," as used in this section, shall be construed to include any scheme for the selling, giving, presenting or distributing of any stamp, trading stamp, coupon or other device which shall entitle the purchaser of property, goods, wares, or merchandise to demand or receive from any person, other than the vendor of any article, property, goods, wares, merchandise, or money other than that actually sold to the purchaser; or the delivery to any person by any person other than the vendor of any article, property, goods, wares, merchandise or money other than that actually sold, upon presentation of any such stamp, trading stamp, coupon or other device; or the issuing, selling, giving or distributing by any person of any stamp, trading stamp, coupon or other device to any person engaged in any trade, business or profession, with the promise, expressed or implied, that such person will give to the person presenting such trading stamp, coupon or other device to such person any money or anything of value without receiving from such person the value thereof, or make to any person any concession or preference in any way on account of the presentation of such stamp, trading stamp, coupon or other device or the distributing or presenting by any person engaged in any trade, business or profession to any person dealing with such person any such stamp, trading stamp, coupon or other device in consideration of any article or thing, purchased or any service performed by such person; or the selling or offering for sale of any real estate or article of merchandise of any description whatever or any ticket of admission to any exhibition or performance or other place of amusement, with a promise expressed or implied to give or bestow or in any manner hold out the promise of the gift or bestowal of any article or thing for and in consideration of a purchase by any person of any other article or thing, whether the object shall be for individual gain or for any other purpose.

(Code 1964, § 39-1-33; Code 1984, § 38-8-2)

*Case law annotations—Pari-mutuel betting on horse races is not a lottery. Rohan v Detroit Racing Ass'n, 314 Mich 326; 22 NW2d 433 (1946). See also, People v Reilly, 50 Mich 384; 15 NW 520 (1883).*

laws.title: Impoundment of abandoned carts; redemption of same by owner; establishment, approval, publication, and payment of fee

Based upon the required metallic tag, the Police Department shall notify the owner, who may reclaim the same by the payment of the fee established under Subsections (b) and (c) of this section. laws.title: Minors purchasing firearms; sales to minors
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person under 18 years of age to purchase a firearm. It shall be unlawful for any person to sell a firearm to any person under 18 years of age.

(Code 1964, § 66-4-4; Code 1984, § 38-10-60; Ord. No. 25-86, § 1(38-10-60), eff. 1-10-1987)

laws.title: License required to purchase pistol; fee
laws.content:
(a) Except as otherwise provided in the Michigan Concealed Weapons Act, being MCL 28.421 et seq., a person shall not purchase a pistol in the City without first having obtained a license for the pistol.

(b) The Chief of Police shall issue, with due speed and diligence, licenses to purchase, carry, possess, or transport pistols to qualified applicants residing within the City, as applicable unless the Chief of Police has probable cause to believe that the applicant would be a threat to themselves or to other individuals, or would commit an offense with the pistol that would violate a law of this or another state or of the United States.

(c) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Chief of Police is authorized to establish and collect necessary fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of processing applications for licenses to purchase pistols, which are determined to be necessary for the public health, safety, and welfare of the City under this division. The fees authorized by this section shall cover the costs of rendering such services and shall be reviewed, revised, and approved as necessary in accordance with this section. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Police Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Chief of Police at least once every two years.

(Code 1964, § 66-1-2; Code 1984, § 38-10-2; Ord. No. 12-89, § 1(38-10-2), eff. 1-23-1990)

laws.title: Carrying pistol in public; transportation of firearm or certain pneumatic guns in vehicles; penalties
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to carry a pistol concealed on or about his or her person, or whether concealed or otherwise, in a vehicle operated or occupied by him or her, contrary to the Chapter XXXVII of the Michigan Penal Code, Firearms, being MCL 750.222 et seq.

Supp. No. 4

laws.title: Offenses

§ 31-13-25

(b) Except for a pistol carried or transported lawfully under the Chapter XXXVII of the Michigan Penal Code, Firearms, being MCL 750.222 et seq., it shall be unlawful for any person to transport or possess in or upon a motor vehicle or any self-propelled vehicle designed for land travel, a firearm, or a pneumatic gun that expels a metallic BB or metallic pellet greater than .177 caliber, unless the firearm or pneumatic gun is unloaded and is one or more of the following:

(1) Taken down.

(2) Enclosed in a case.

(3) Carried in the trunk of the vehicle.

(4) Inaccessible from the interior of the vehicle.

(c) A person who violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not more than 90 days, or a fine of not more than $100.00, or both in the discretion of the court.

(d) Subsections (a) and (b) of this section do not apply to any of the following:

(1) A peace officer of an authorized police agency of the United States, of the state, or of a political subdivision of the state, who is regularly employed and paid by the United States, the state, or a political subdivision of the state.

(2) A person who is regularly employed by the Michigan Department of Corrections and who is authorized in writing by the Director of the Michigan Department of Corrections to carry a concealed weapon while in the official performance of such person’s duties or while going to or returning from those duties.

(3) A person employed by a private vendor that operates a youth correctional facility authorized under Section 20g of the Michigan Corrections Code of 1953, being MCL 791.220g, who meets the same criteria established by the Director of the Michigan Department of Corrections for departmental employees described in Subsection (d)(2) of this section and who is authorized in writing by the Director to carry a concealed weapon while in the official performance of such person’s duties or while going to or returning from those duties.

(4) A member of the United States Army, Air Force, Navy, or Marine Corps or the United States Coast Guard while carrying weapons in the line of or incidental to duty.

(5) An organization authorized by law to purchase or receive weapons from the United States or from the state.

(6) A member of the National Guard, Armed Forces Reserve, the United States Coast Guard Reserve, or any other authorized military organization while on duty or drill, or in going to or returning from a place of assembly or practice, while carrying weapons used for a purpose of the National Guard, Armed Forces Reserve, United States Coast Guard Reserve, or other duly authorized military organization.

(7) A security employee employed by the state and granted limited arrest powers under MCL 28.6c.

(8) A motor carrier officer appointed under MCL 28.6d.

laws.title: Brandishing firearm in public
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided in Subsection (b) of this section, a person shall not willfully and knowingly brandish a firearm in public.

(b) Subsection (a) of this section does not apply to any of the following:

(1) A peace officer lawfully performing such officer’s duties as a peace officer; or

(2) A person lawfully acting in self-defense or defense of another under the Michigan Self-Defense Act, being MCL 780.971 through 780.974.

laws.title: Prohibitions against possession or receipt of firearms or ammunition; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to possess or receive any firearms or ammunition when that person is subject to a court order that:

(1) Was issued after a hearing of which such person received actual notice and at which such person had an opportunity to participate;

(2) Restrains such person from harassing, stalking, or threatening an intimate partner of such person or child of such intimate partner or person, or engaging in other conduct that would place an intimate partner in reasonable fear of bodily injury to the partner or child; and

(3) Either:

a. Includes a finding that such person represents a credible threat to the physical safety of such intimate partner or child; or

b. By its terms explicitly prohibits the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against such intimate partner or child that would reasonably be expected to cause bodily injury.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person who has received a conviction for the crime of domestic violence, as defined in Section 31-13-1 of this Code, to possess or receive any firearm or ammunition, provided, that a person shall not be considered to have received a conviction for the crime of domestic violence, as defined in Section 31-13-1 of this Code, unless:

(1) The person was represented by counsel in the case, or knowingly and intelligently waived their right to counsel in the case; and

(2) In the event the person was entitled to a jury trial, the case was either tried by a jury, or the person knowingly and intelligently waived the right to have the case tried by a jury, by guilty plea or otherwise.

(c) Subsection (b) of this section shall not apply with respect to the sale or disposition of a firearm or ammunition to a licensed importer, licensed manufacturer, licensed dealer, or licensed collector who, pursuant to federal law, is either not precluded from dealing in firearms or ammunition, or has been granted relief from disabilities therein.

(d) Any conviction for the crime of domestic violence, as defined in Section 31-13-1 of this Code, which has been expunged or set aside or for which a person has been pardoned or has had their civil rights restored, shall not be considered a conviction for purposes of this section unless such pardon, expungement, or restoration of civil rights expressly provides that the person may not ship, transport, possess, or receive firearms.

(Ord. No. 2021-37, $\S 1$ , eff. 11-4-2021; Ord. No. 2023-39, $\S 1$ , eff. 11-22-2023)

laws.title: Possession; sale; advertising; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) It is unlawful for any person to possess or transfer replica or facsimile firearms within the corporate limits of the City.

(b) It is unlawful for any person to display, market for sale, or sell replica or facsimile firearms within the corporate limits of the City.

(c) It is unlawful for any person to place an advertisement in any newspaper, magazine, handbill, sign, poster, other publications, or other advertising media with knowledge that the purpose of the advertisement, in whole or in part, is to promote within the corporate limits of the City the possession, transfer, or sale of objects designed and manufactured as replica or facsimile firearms.

(d) The provisions of this section shall not apply to replica or facsimile firearms which, because of their distinct color, exaggerated size or permanently affixed international blaze orange markings on the receiver portions of the product and blaze orange plug recessed no more than six millimeters from the muzzle end of the barrel, cannot reasonably be perceived to be real firearms.

(e) The possession, manufacture, marketing, distribution, and sale of replica or facsimile firearms are permitted if such devices are possessed, manufactured, marketed, distributed, or sold:

(1) Solely for subsequent transportation in intrastate, interstate, or foreign commerce; or

(2) Solely for lawful use in theatrical productions, including motion picture, television, and stage productions.

Such devices shall not be displayed to the general public or sold for other uses within the corporate limits of the City regardless of where manufactured or purchased.

(Code 1984, § 38-16-2; Ord. No. 10-88, § 1(38-16-2), eff. 6-2-1988)

laws.title: Brandishing

(b) It is unlawful for any person, with knowledge that a peace officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, or paramedic is engaged in the performance of such peace officer’s, firefighter’s, emergency medical technician’s or paramedic’s duties, to draw, exhibit, or brandish replica or facsimile firearms in their presence.

(Code 1984, § 38-16-3; Ord. No. 10-88, § 1(38-16-3), eff. 6-2-1988)

laws.title: Civil forfeiture

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article, except for Section 32-1-20 of this Code, shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

(d) A person who is found guilty for violating Section 32-1-20 of this Code, or for violating Section 32-1-43 of this Code on three or more occasions within a one-year period, shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and fined a minimum of $400.00 and, in the discretion of the court, sentenced up to 90 days in jail for each misdemeanor that is issued.

(Code 1964, §§ 41-2-35, 41-2-27(d); Code 1984, §§ 39-2-18, 39-2-49(e))

laws.title: Liability for damage to vehicles; licensees not liable for loss of, or damage to, personal property when liability disclaimed, limited, or regulated on parking ticket
laws.content:
(a) Each licensee under this article shall be liable for any damage to any motor vehicle stored or parked in such licensee’s commercial parking lot, by or through his own negligence or that of his employees. This section shall have no application to loss of or damage to personal property left or contained in motor vehicles, the liability for which may be disclaimed, limited or regulated by appropriate contractual provisions contained in the parking ticket, provided, that a sign, approved by the Chief of Police, giving notice to that effect, is posted on the commercial parking lot. Failure to pay any final judgment for damage to or loss of a car within 60 days after its final rendition shall automatically revoke the license of such licensee, and such licensee shall not be entitled to any renewal of any license until the satisfaction of any such outstanding judgment, and satisfaction as to such licensee’s financial responsibility. In the event of revocation of the license of any commercial parking lot, any subsequent applicant for a license for such lot shall give satisfactory evidence of financial responsibility.

(b) No contract, agreement, lease, receipt, rule or regulation shall exempt any person operating a commercial parking lot from damage or loss caused by the negligence of such person or any employee of such person or while in the employ of such person.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-11; Code 1984, § 39-2-2)

*State law reference—Liability of garage keeper, MCL 256.541 et seq.*

**Sec. 32-1-4. Attendant required.**

(a) Each licensee operating a commercial parking lot shall provide an attendant during all posted hours of operation.

(b) Each licensee operating a commercial parking lot shall provide an attendant at the lot beyond the posted operating hours for as long as is necessary to ensure that all spaces at such lot are unobstructed, thus allowing the vehicle owner to unpark and exit freely.

(c) This section shall not apply to a commercial parking lot advertised as "park and lock," where the vehicle owner deposits a parking fee into the lot's collection box prior to leaving his vehicle unattended at such lot, provided, that all parking spaces at such lot remain unobstructed, thereby permitting the vehicle owner free egress at all times.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-11.1; Code 1984, § 39-2-3; Ord. No. 600-H, § 1(41-2-11.1), eff. 12-11-1984)

**Sec. 32-1-5. Duties of licensee as bailee; quality of attendants.**

Each licensee under this article shall faithfully perform such licensee's duties as bailee and shall use such licensee's best endeavors to employ honest and competent attendants and help on such licensee's commercial parking lot. Failure to comply with this section shall be cause for revocation of the license of such licensee.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-12; Code 1984, § 39-2-4)

**Sec. 32-1-6. Fire extinguishing apparatus required; manner of storing vehicles.**

Commercial parking lots shall be equipped with proper fire extinguishing apparatus, subject to the approval of the Fire Department. All motor vehicles shall be so stored that they may be reached easily in case of fire or other emergency.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-13; Code 1984, § 39-2-5)

*Cross reference—Fire prevention and protection generally, Ch. 18.*

**Sec. 32-1-7. Loitering.**

It shall be unlawful for any licensee under this article to permit any person not employed by such licensee to loiter in or about the commercial parking lot of such licensee.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-14; Code 1984, § 39-2-6)

*Cross reference—Loitering generally, § 31-5-7.*

**Sec. 32-1-8. Duty to keep lot and surrounding sidewalks free from dirt, ice, litter, sleet and snow.**

Each licensee under this article shall keep the commercial parking lot and the sidewalks surrounding the commercial parking lot free from dirt, ice, litter, sleet and snow and shall keep the sidewalks in safe condition for the travel of pedestrians, provided, that the licensee may use a portion of the commercial parking lot to pile ice and snow.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-15; Code 1984, § 39-2-7)

*Cross reference—Snow removal generally, § 43-13-1 et seq.*

**Sec. 32-1-9. Barriers.**

(a) Commercial parking lots shall be enclosed with a continuous barrier along all portions contiguous to street or alley frontage, except at points of ingress and egress. Barriers shall be at least three feet in height and shall consist of one of the following types of construction:

(1) Steel posts connected with one-quarter-inch rod chains or one-half-inch steel cable;

(2) Woven wire fence construction of not less than No. 9 gauge galvanized wire;

(3) Angle iron posts and bumpers;

(4) Structural steel channeling or rail; or

(5) Wood posts not less than six inches by six inches with rails not less than six inches by six inches.

(b) Barriers shall be properly maintained in a neat, orderly manner and kept free from signs, advertising and other displays. The requirement for a continuous barrier to enclose commercial parking lots shall apply to all parking lots in the area within which surfacing is required under this article and also to all other lots located outside these areas wherein the parked cars are not locked and keys removed while stored on the parking lots.

(Code 1964, § 41-2-16; Code 1984, § 39-2-8)

**Sec. 32-1-10. Surfacing of parking areas.**

(a) Parking areas of commercial parking lots shall have a smooth and durable surface that will not retain water and that will remain free of dust or loose particles. They shall be constructed of crushed stone, slag, gravel or cinders, bound together by a surface treatment of bituminous material or a surfacing equivalent thereto. This section shall apply only to lots lying within or having a frontage of the perimeter streets of the areas bounded by Fisher Freeway on the north, Brush on the

laws.title: Use of streets, sidewalks, or alleys for standing or parking of vehicles prohibited

laws.title: Maximum capacity
laws.content:
(a) When a commercial parking lot is filled to maximum capacity, the licensee or such licensee’s employee shall place a conspicuous sign at each entrance thereof, reading, in letters not less than six inches in height, "FILLED TO CAPACITY," and such sign shall be displayed continuously as long as such condition exists.

(b) The maximum capacity shall be clearly indicated on the license certificate issued for a commercial parking lot, and such certificate shall be conspicuously displayed on the premises thereof by the licensee.

(c) The maximum capacity shall be the number of cars that can be handled on the lot without resorting to streets for maneuvering of such cars as determined by the licensee and approval by the Department of Public Works. (Code 1964, § 41-2-19; Code 1984, § 39-2-14)

laws.title: Right of operator to refuse to park large trucks, trailers, or other vehicles
laws.content: Any operator of a commercial parking lot shall have the right to refuse parking for any truck, trailer or other vehicle which, because of its size, shape or movability or its operating condition, in the opinion of the operator, or such operator’s employees or attendants, could be a hazard, nuisance or danger to other vehicles or to persons or property upon the lot. (Code 1964, § 41-2-20; Code 1984, § 39-2-15)

laws.title: Driveway and barrier openings
laws.content:
(a) All driveways to commercial parking lots shall be constructed in accordance with Section 43-6-27 of this Code.

(b) The width of barrier openings at points of ingress and egress to commercial parking lots shall not exceed 40 feet if entrance and exit are combined, or 20 feet if entrance and exit are separate. The number of barrier openings shall not exceed one entrance and one exit on any one street, provided, that where, because of the size or shape of the lot, this limitation would make the operation of the lot extremely difficult or where, because
