laws.content:
(a) The contributions for a member to the Benefit Plan to provide for the payment of death benefits delineated in Section 35-3-171 of this Code shall be adopted and amended from time to time by City Council resolution.

(b) The Board shall certify the rates and submit them to the City Council for approval. The City shall make the proper deduction from the salary or compensation of each member from the date of the member’s enrollment in the Benefit Plan to the date his name last appeared on a City payroll. Every member shall be deemed to consent and agree to the deduction made and provided for in this section and receipt for the member’s full salary or compensation and payment of his salary or compensation, less such deduction, shall be a full and complete discharge of all claims and demands, whatsoever, for the services rendered by such person during the period covered by such payment, except as to the benefits provided for by the Benefit Plan. The proper authority or officer responsible for making up the payroll shall certify to the City Treasurer the amounts to be deducted from the pay of each member, and each of such amounts shall be deducted by the City Treasurer, and, when deducted, shall be paid into the funds of the Benefit Plan.

(Charter 1918, T-IX, C-VIII, § 12; Code 1964, § 16-9-7; Code 1984, § 13-8-10(1) and (3))

laws.title: Contribution by members on leave of absence
laws.content:
A member who is granted a leave of absence, as defined in Section 35-3-102 of this Code, shall continue as a member of the Benefit Plan for a period of 30 days following the date the member’s name last appeared on a City payroll, with pay, for the exclusive purpose of receiving a death benefit that is provided for in this division. Upon the expiration of the 30-day period, the individual may continue as a member of the Benefit Plan for the remaining period of the member’s leave of absence, not to exceed four years following the date the member’s name last appeared on a City payroll, with pay, for the exclusive purpose of receiving a death benefit provided for in this division, provided, that within 30 days following the date the member’s name last appeared on a City payroll, with pay, the member contributes to the Benefit Plan an amount equal to $0.20 for each week, or fraction thereof, of the member’s leave of absence, from and after the first 30 days and not to extend beyond the expiration of the leave of absence which may not exceed four years, provided further, that should such a member fail to pay the member’s contribution, through check or money order, as required by this section, the member shall cease to be a member and shall not be entitled to the death benefit provided for in this division.

(Charter 1918, T-IX, C-VIII, § 12; Code 1964, § 16-9-7; Code 1984, § 13-8-10(4))

laws.title: Deficiency appropriations
laws.content:
Where the amounts credited to the Benefit Plan on account of the death benefit portion of the Benefit Plan, together with the City’s contributions for the fiscal year are insufficient to meet all demands made upon the Benefit Plan on account of death benefits, the amount of such insufficiency shall be provided by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(Code 1964, § 16-9-9; Code 1984, § 13-8-12)

Secs. 35-3-177—35-3-190. Reserved.

CD35:54

laws.title: (a) Members generally
laws.content:
Except as herein provided, membership in the Benefit Plan shall include any of the following persons:

1. Any active City elective officer, City appointee, or City employee who qualifies as a member under Section 35-3-194 of this Code and has selected coverage within the Benefit Plan on or after the effective date of coverage.

2. Any active City elective officer, City appointee, or City employee who is a member of the Benefit Plan and who becomes a disability retiree under the provisions of Chapter 39, Article I, of this Code, General Retirement System, and has selected the protection plan, provided, that the officer, appointee, or employee’s membership shall terminate upon the officer, appointee, or employee’s conversion date.

3. Any active City appointee or City employee who is a member of the Benefit Plan, becomes a disability retiree under the provisions of Chapter 39, Article II, of this Code, Police and Fire Retirement System, and has selected the protection plan, provided, that the appointee or employee’s membership shall terminate upon the appointee or employee’s conversion date.

laws.title: (b) Active employees of boards, commissions, or courts
laws.content: Active employees, of boards, commissions, or courts serving the City may be included as a member for the purpose of coming under the provisions of this division where, at such time as they are eligible, their inclusion as a member is mutually agreeable between the City Council and governing board or commission, or court.

laws.title: (c) Employees not included in membership
laws.content:
The following employees shall not be included as members of the Benefit Plan:

1. Individuals whose City services are compensated pursuant to a personal service contract or on a contractual or fee basis irrespective of their status as a common law employee;

CD35:55
§ 35-3-193

DETROIT CITY CODE

(2) City employees who work less than 1,440 hours of straight time in a fiscal year without a break in service of more than six weeks; and

(3) Officers and employees of the Detroit Board of Education.

(d) Termination of membership. Except as provided for in Subsection (e) of this section, the membership of an individual shall terminate as of the date the individual ceases to qualify as a member. Furthermore, except as provided in Subsection (f) of this section, membership shall be terminated where a City employee loses the employee’s active employee status.

(e) Extension of membership. An individual who is a member shall continue to be a member:

(1) During the period of the individual’s absence from City service, not to exceed four months, provided the individual receives a leave of absence approved by the Civil Service Commission.

(2) During the period of the individual’s absence from City service, not to exceed four years, provided the individual requires a leave of absence, for health purposes only, approval by the Civil Service Commission.

(3) During the period the individual receives benefits under the income protection plan.

(f) Board may decide who is member. In all cases of doubt, the Board shall decide who is a member within the meaning of this division.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-2; Code 1984, § 13-9-3)

laws.title: Preparation of specifications
laws.content:
The Board is authorized to prepare specifications for the creation of a life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment insurance protection plan and for the securing of proposals thereon, subject to the approval of the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-4; Code 1984, § 13-9-5)

laws.title: Agreement with life insurance company
laws.content:
Upon approval of the City Council of the matters in Section 35-3-195 of this Code, the City is authorized to enter into an agreement, subject to the approval of the City Council, with a life insurance company to provide life insurance, dependent life insurance, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance protection, as provided for in Section 35-3-197 of this Code for the members of the protection plan. All other matters regarding life insurance, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance protection, shall be governed by the agreement between the Board and the life insurance company.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-5; Code 1984, § 13-9-6)

Such child is not covered until the child becomes 14 days of age, but where the member has the coverage, the child is automatically covered upon reaching 14 days of age. (2) Where a husband and wife are both City employees and both carry employee life insurance, then only the husband or the wife is eligible to enroll for dependent life insurance which would cover their children. Both husband and wife may enroll each other for dependent life insurance coverage. (e) The insurance provided under this section shall be subject to all the qualifications specified in Subsection (d) of this section. (Code 1964, § 16-12-3; Code 1984, § 13-9-7)

laws.title: Payment of benefits upon death of member
laws.content:
Upon due proof of the death of a member prior to the member's retirement from City service, the amount of term life insurance benefit elected by the member and the amount of accidental death coverage, if applicable, to which the member was eligible shall be paid by the insurance carrier to such person as the member shall have nominated by written designation duly executed and filed with the Board or with the insurance carrier. If there is no such designated person, such amount shall be paid to the member's estate.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-7; Code 1984, § 13-9-8)

laws.title: Contributions to group insurance protection plan—By members
laws.content:
The contributions of any member to the group insurance protection plan shall be as follows:

(1) The contributions of a member to the protection plan to provide for the payment of life, accidental death and dismemberment insurance and dependent life insurance elected by the member shall be the amount provided for by City Council resolution as amended from time to time.

(2) The Board shall certify the proper authority or officer responsible for making up the payroll, the amount of deduction to be made from the pay of each member, and the proper authority or officer responsible for making up the payroll shall cause to be deducted from the salary or compensation of each member, from the date of the member's commencement in the protection

plan to the date his or her name last appeared on a City payroll with pay, the amount of contributions so determined. Appropriate payroll deductions shall be made from members' compensation in accordance with applicable law. In order for a member to be eligible for benefits under this division, the member must provide the appropriate written authorization for payroll deductions. All contributions deducted shall be paid to the applicable fund, which ensures the benefits of the protection plan.

(3) Where a member is absent for a period not to exceed four months with leave of absence approved by the Civil Service Commission or the member's department director or agency head, whichever is applicable under the law, or during a period of the member's absence from City service not to exceed four years with a leave of absence for health purposes only, approved by the Civil Service Commission or during the member's absence from City service when the member receives benefits under the income protection plan, the member shall pay the full amount of the group insurance premium during such period.

Any member who ceases to be a member for any reason shall have the right to convert the group life insurance coverage, without a physical examination, to an individual life insurance policy prior to expiration of the applicable election period, and shall be responsible for payment of the entire premium.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-8; Code 1984, § 13-9-9)

laws.title: Same—By City
laws.content:
The contributions by the City and any of its eligible subdivisions shall be the difference between the total insurance premium, less the amount of the member's contribution and less the amount of any rebate or dividend paid by the insurance carrier to the City.

(Code 1964, § 16-12-10; Code 1984, § 13-9-10)

laws.title: Contribution to group life insurance plan by City when a member incurs total and permanent disability
laws.content:
(a) Where a member, while insured under the group insurance protection plan incurs total and permanent disability, provided, that the total and permanent disability continues, the member may, at any time within one year after the date of discontinuance of the member's

premium payments for said term life insurance, submit written proof of the member's total and permanent disability to the City and make application to have the City pay the member's contributions towards the cost of the life insurance on the member only.

(b) Where the written proof of total disability is satisfactory to the City, the City will pay said member's insurance contribution beginning with the date of discontinuance of the member's premium contribution, during the continuation of the member's disability, for a period not to exceed one year from the date the member's premium contributions were discontinued.

(c) The payment of the members contribution will be extended by the City during the continuance of the members total and permanent disability for successive periods of one year each, provided, that the member submits written proof of the continuance of such permanent and total disability within the respective three-month period immediately preceding the end of the year.

(d) The group insurer shall have the right and opportunity to have such employee examined by physicians designated by the carrier when and so often as the carrier may reasonably require during disability, but not more frequently than annually after the premium contribution has been continued for two full years by the City paying the member's contribution.

(e) Where the member has furnished due proof that the member is totally and permanently disabled but nevertheless again becomes able to perform some work or engage in some business or occupation for compensation or profit, or where the member remains totally and permanently disabled, but refuses to be examined as above or fails to furnish within the time allowed satisfactory proof of continuance of total and permanent disability, payment of the member's premium as specified under this section shall immediately terminate. The member shall thereupon be entitled to rights and benefits under the conversion privilege of the group term life insurance policy, together with insurance protection during the 31-day period allowed for conversion, as if employment had then terminated, unless the employee returns to work with the City during such period and is again eligible to become insured under the policy.

(f) This section shall apply only to those members whose total disability occurs on or after December 1, 1975, and the amount of increased insurance for those members whose total disability commenced prior to December 1, 1975, and who became eligible for increases in the amounts of insurance subsequent to December 1,

laws.title: Offered by City
laws.content:
The Benefit Plan is hereby offered to duty-disability retirees subject to the provisions of this division.

(Code 1964, § 16-14-2; Code 1984, § 13-10-2)

laws.title: Enrollment
laws.content:
Duty-disability retirees may enroll in the Benefit Plan on forms to be furnished by the Office of Chief Financial Officer. Any duty-disability retiree who fails to enroll for such hospitalization, medical, dental, and optical care benefits may enroll in the Benefit Plan, without medical examination, during any future open enrollment period.

(Code 1964, § 16-14-3; Code 1984, § 13-10-3)

laws.title: Inclusion of husband, wife, and children of husband, or wife in Benefit Plan
City to enter into agreements with health care providers
laws.content:
The City shall enter into agreements with health care providers for hospitalization, medical, dental, and optical care benefits for duty-disability retirees, subject to the approval of the City Council to service the members of the Benefit Plan.

(Code 1964, § 16-14-5; Code 1984, § 13-10-5)

laws.title: Contributions by duty-disability retirees
laws.content:
The contribution of a duty-disability retiree to the Benefit Plan to provide for the payment of hospitalization and medical service that are provided for in Sections 35-3-223 and 35-3-224 of this Code shall be the excess of the City’s contribution for the cost of hospitalization on a monthly basis.

(Code 1964, § 16-14-6; Code 1984, § 13-10-6)

laws.title: Deductions from payrolls
laws.content:
(a) Deductions shall be calculated by the appropriate division of the Human Resources Department and shall be presented to the Board. The Board shall certify to the City Council the amount of the deduction to be made from the retirement allowance of each member, and the Human Resources Department shall deduct from the salary or compensation of each duty-disability retiree, from the date of his or her enrollment in the Benefit Plan, the amount of contributions so determined. Every duty-disability retiree shall be deemed to consent and agree to the deduction made and provided for in this section and the receipt of his or her full retirement allowance, less such deduction, shall be a full and complete discharge of all claims and demand, whatsoever, during the period covered by such payment except as to the benefits provided by the Benefit Plan. The proper authority or officer responsible for making up the pension payroll shall certify to the City Treasurer the amounts to be deducted from the retirement allowance of each member and each of such amounts shall be deducted by the City Treasurer, and, when deducted, shall be paid into the funds of the Benefit Plan.

(b) Each member authorizes the City to report to applicable tax authorities the value of coverage offered under the Benefit Plan for any other non-dependent, which is includable as income under the United States Internal Revenue Code, being 26 USC 1 et seq., under this Code, or under other applicable tax law. In addition, each member authorizes the City to make appropriate tax withholding from the member’s salary or compensa-

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Sign displayed
laws.content:
All licensees under this article shall display a sign that designates the type of dwelling in letters not less than two inches high in a conspicuous place at the entrance thereof and on the outside of the building.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-11; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-11), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Register required; use of fictitious names prohibited
laws.content:
(a) Every licensee or such licensee’s agent or employee, under this article shall provide, and maintain a register in which shall be inscribed, in ink or electronically, at the time of arrival, the correct name of every guest renting or occupying a room, together with the home street and city address of such guest, and the number of the space assigned, together with the date and time when such space was rented. When any guest shall terminate such guest’s stay, it shall be the duty of the licensee, or the licensee’s agent or employee, to ensure that the time thereof is entered in the register. Such register shall be open to inspection to police and fire officers on official business.

(b) Whenever a licensee or the licensee’s agent or employee knows or has reasonable cause for believing that any person has inscribed a false name or given false information in such register, it shall be the licensee’s duty to forthwith notify the Police Department of the same.

(c) It shall be unlawful for any person to write or cause or permit to be written in any register any other or different name or designation than the legal name of the person so registered.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-12; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-12), eff. 4-7-2004)

State law reference—Registration of persons in accommodations for transients, MCL 125.781 et seq.

laws.title: Responsible party to notify Fire Department
laws.content:
In each establishment licensed under this article, except a rooming house, the licensee shall at all times, at the place of registration, have a person, whether the licensee or another, who shall be charged with the duty of immediately notifying the Fire Department when a fire occurs therein. Any person therein who discovers such a fire shall immediately notify the person on duty at the place of registration.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-13; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-13), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Ignition of fire prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, in smoking or attempting to light or to smoke a cigarette, cigar, pipe or tobacco in any form for which lighters or matches are used, or in the use of flammable liquids, to set fire to any bedding, curtain, drapery, furniture, or household furnishings in any establishment licensed under this article.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-14; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-14), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Liability for loss
laws.content:
Each licensee under this article, except the licensee of a rooming house, who provides a safe or suitable vault for the custody of money, bank notes, jewelry, articles of gold and silver manufacture, precious stones, personal ornaments, railroad mileage books or tickets, negotiable or valuable papers, shall keep the same in good order and shall not be liable for the loss of or injury of any such property belonging to any guest unless such guest has

laws.title: Posting of notification of fire; liability for loss; ignition of fire prohibited
laws.content: In a conspicuous place in the lobby and in each sleeping room of every establishment licensed under this article, the licensee shall cause to be posted a plainly printed notice advising as to the provisions of Sections 36-1-5 through 36-1-7 of this Code. (Code 1984, § 44-2-16; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-16), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Locks and bolts required on doors, windows, and transoms
laws.content: Each licensee under this article shall keep on the doors of the sleeping rooms used by the guests suitable locks and bolts and on the transoms and windows of rooms suitable fastenings, where applicable. (Code 1984, § 44-2-17; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-17), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Occupancy of rooms by minors
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any licensee under this article, or such licensee’s agent or employee, to permit any minor under 18 years of age to be housed in any establishment licensed under this article, unless such presence is with the consent or knowledge of the parent, guardian or adult lawfully in charge of such minor. Where the minor has not obtained the consent or knowledge of the parent, guardian or adult lawfully in charge of the minor, such licensee, or such licensee’s agent or employee shall forthwith notify the Police Department of the presence of such minor. (Code 1984, § 44-2-18; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-18), eff. 4-7-2004)

*State law reference—Renting rooms to minors, MCL 427.301 et seq.*

laws.title: Defrauding innkeeper prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to act with intent to defraud an innkeeper by staying at a bed and breakfast inn, hotel, or motel as a guest and obtaining any food, entertainment, or accommodation without payment, except when credit is given by express agreement.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to obtain credit at any bed and breakfast inn, hotel, or motel for food, entertainment, or accommodation by means of giving false information on a lodging registration form or the presenting of false or fictitious credentials.

(c) A person in violation of Subsection (a) or Subsection (b) of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor, except no conviction shall be had unless the complaint is made within 60 days of the time of the violation. (Ord. No. 2021-31, § 1, eff. 10-19-2021)

*Editor’s note—Ord. No. 2021-31, § 1, effective October 19, 2021, renumbered §§ 36-1-11 and 36-1-12 as §§ 36-1-12 and 36-1-13.*

laws.title: Compliance with state housing law and this Code
laws.content:
Every establishment licensed under this article, and every part thereof, shall comply with the Housing Law of Michigan, being MCL 125.401 et seq., and this Code. (Code 1984, § 44-2-19; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-19), eff. 4-7-2004; Ord. No. 2021-31, § 1, eff. 10-19-2021)

*Editor’s note—See editor’s note, § 36-1-11.*

laws.title: Rules and regulations generally
Interior stairway required; same to comply with requirements of Building Code
laws.content:
In addition to the other provisions of Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, *Building Code*, every public lodging house shall have at least one interior enclosed stair, extending from the ground floor of the building through the upper habitable floor. Such enclosure shall be constructed in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, *Building Code*.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-32; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-32), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Requirements for new establishments
Requirements specific to hostels
Required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to conduct or to maintain any bed and breakfast inn, hotel, motel, non-profit single-room occupancy housing, public lodging house, rooming house, or hostel in the City without first having obtained a license from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to operate such business.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-41; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-41), eff. 4-7-2004; Ord. No. 2019-48, § 1, eff. 1-13-2020)

laws.title: Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee
laws.content:
(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the Charter for the processing and issuance of a license under this division. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) A fee shall be charged each new licensee, any current licensee who applies to renew an existing license, or a current licensee applying for a license at another location.

(d) Prior to the expiration of a current license, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay an annual fee for the renewal of a license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation of the business for the location until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-42; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-42), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Inspection and certification of approval; land use; construction requirements; maintenance, fire protection and safety, and health and sanitation requirements
Investigation required by Police Department to confirm non-conviction of certain crimes
laws.content:
(a) The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall refer all applications for licenses under this article to the Chief of Police, or the agent of the Chief of Police, who shall cause each such application to be investigated to determine whether the applicant has been convicted of violating any of the laws of the United States or the state, or any provisions of this article or this Code, and to determine if there are any other facts which would tend to show whether or not the applicant is a suitable person to conduct such activity. Any person who has been convicted of any crime involving a morals charge within the last ten years shall be ineligible for licensing under this article. In the case of a rooming house, an applicant who, within the past ten years, has received a license by the state to operate an adult foster care facility pursuant to the Michigan Adult Foster Care Facility Licensing Act, being MCL 400.701 et seq., and such license was revoked, suspended, or otherwise terminated shall be ineligible for licensing under this article.

(b) The Chief of Police, or the designee of the Chief of Police, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the Fire Department, and the Health Department shall submit to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center, in writing, a summary of the information obtained, accompanied by a recommendation as to whether the license should be granted, refused, revoked or renewed, as the case may be.

(c) The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center may conduct any investigation that it deems advisable for the purpose of determining whether or not the applicant is a suitable person to conduct the business.

(Code 1984, § 44-2-44; Ord. No. 10-04, § 1(44-2-44), eff. 4-7-2004)

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:

laws.title: Access
Staffing and training
laws.content:
(a) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall maintain a minimum staffing ratio of one staff member for every 20 residents, or fraction thereof, during waking hours, and one staff member for every 30 residents, or fraction thereof, during sleeping hours.

(b) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall ensure that all staff members are trained in the following areas:

(1) First-aid;

(2) Fire and emergency procedures, including the proper use of fire extinguishers;

(3) Resident complaint and grievance procedures;

(4) Special needs of the homeless;

(5) Resident confidentiality requirements; and

(6) The appropriate chains of authority or command within the shelter.

(c) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall not staff, with or without remuneration:

(1) In any position that entails direct contact with residents, any person convicted of arson, murder or attempted murder, or any degree of criminal sexual conduct; or

(2) In any position that entails direct contact with residents, any person convicted of any other crime involving assaultive or violent behavior for a period of ten years from the date of conviction; or

(3) In any position that entails contact with minor residents, any person convicted in any state or other country of any crimes against children as described in Sections 135 through 145d of the Michigan Penal Code, being MCL 750.135 through 750.145d.

To ensure compliance with these provisions, the owner and/or operator of a shelter shall require all such staff members to obtain a police clearance and to execute a sworn statement affirming that they do not have a criminal record involving the aforementioned offenses. Unless they receive actual knowledge which contradicts a

CD36:11
§ 36-2-4

DETROIT CITY CODE

clearance and/or sworn statement and fail to act upon the information, owners and/or operators of a shelter who are in possession of such clearance and sworn statement are deemed to be in compliance with this section. (Code 1984, § 44-5-3; Ord. No. 23-94, § 1(44-5-3), eff. 5-1-1995; Ord. No. 07-95, § 1(44-5-3), eff. 5-2-1995)

laws.title: Space and security
laws.content:
(a) The absolute maximum occupancy for each shelter shall be established by the building official.

(b) Unless an exemption has been granted by the appropriate department, the owner and/or operator of a shelter shall provide sleeping accommodations for each resident which shall consist either of a bed or of a crib with a mattress.

(c) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall provide adequate sleeping space, 45 square feet of floor area per bed or crib, and such space shall be limited to not more than eight beds or cribs in any one room.

(d) When the National Weather Service reports either that the temperature or wind chill is below 32 degrees Fahrenheit or that a weather advisory is in effect, the owner and/or operator of a shelter shall be excused from the sleeping space requirements which are contained in Subsection (c) of this section. (Code 1984, § 44-5-4; Ord. No. 23-94, § 1(44-5-4), eff. 5-1-1995; Ord. No. 07-95, § 1(44-5-4), eff. 5-2-1995)

laws.title: Minor residents
laws.content:
(a) At all times, minor residents, who are under the age of 17, shall be attended to or supervised by a parent, a guardian, or a qualified staff member.

(b) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall not allow minor residents who are under the age of 17 years, to sleep in areas which accommodate adult residents outside of each minor resident’s immediate family without assigning at least one staff member to monitor such minor resident. In order to facilitate monitoring by the assigned staff member, each minor resident should be placed in close proximity to such minor resident’s respective family and to other minor residents or families with minor residents.

(c) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall:

(1) Ensure that all school-age minor residents are enrolled in, and have the opportunity to attend school as required under Section 1561 of the Michigan Revised School Code, being MCL 380.1561;

(2) Provide space and time to enable school-age minor residents to complete homework assignments; and

(3) Cooperate with parents, guardians, and appropriate school personnel to promote the educational needs of school-age minor residents.

(d) The owner and/or operator of a shelter shall make every effort to provide minor residents with recreational activities and facilities which are separate from those for adult residents. (Code 1984, § 44-5-5; Ord. No. 23-94, § 1(44-5-5), eff. 5-1-1995; Ord. No. 07-95, § 1(44-5-5), eff. 5-2-1995)

laws.title: Additional fire safety requirements
Additional health, hygiene, and sanitation requirements
laws.content:
In addition to the requirements contained in Chapter 19, Article III, of this Code, Food Sanitation Standards, and the Michigan Public Health Code, which is adopted by reference into this Code through Section 20-1-1, in-

CD36:12
PUBLIC LODGING

§ 36-2-22

cluding, but not limited to, communicable diseases and medical waste, and applicable administrative rules of the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, being the 1979 Administrative Code and Annual Administrative Code Supplements, the owner and/or operator of a shelter shall:

(1) Provide clean towels, soap, toilet tissue, and bed linens to all residents for use at the facility;

(2) a. Wash all clothing, towels, and bed linens of residents with communicable diseases or conditions separately from other laundry with detergent and bleach or an equivalent disinfecting agent in water which is at least 130 degrees Fahrenheit; or

b. Have such items laundered by a commercial service; and

(3) a. Keep all medication, except refrigerated and time-sensitive emergency medication such as nitroglycerin and inhalers, in a locked storage area;

b. Ensure that a staff member with access to the locked area be on-site and available at all times;

c. Provide refrigeration space, through staff members, for medication requiring refrigeration; and

d. Maintain a log for all prescription medication which indicates the name of the resident, the name of the medication, the prescribed dosage, the time to be taken, and time taken.

(Code 1984, § 44-5-7; Ord. No. 23-94, § 1(44-5-7), eff. 5-1-1995; Ord. No. 07-95, § 1(44-5-7), eff. 5-2-1995)

laws.title: Temporary emergency shelters
laws.content:
(a) The owner and/or operator of a temporary emergency shelter shall:

(1) Maintain and post in a conspicuous place a valid occupancy permit for the usual purpose of the structure; and

(2) Maintain a minimum staffing ratio of one staff member for every 20 residents, or portion thereof, during waking hours and one staff member for every 30 residents, or portion thereof, during sleeping hours.

(b) Each time operation commences, the owner and/or operator of a temporary emergency shelter shall file a letter of notification with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center within 48 hours thereof, excluding holidays and weekends. The letter of notification shall include a statement indicating compliance with this section. In lieu of this procedure, the coordinating entity for rotating temporary emergency shelters may file with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center a quarterly letter of notification which lists participating temporary emergency shelter facilities and the prospective dates of their operation.

(Code 1984, § 44-5-8; Ord. No. 23-94, § 1(44-5-8), eff. 5-1-1995; Ord. No. 07-95, § 1(44-5-8), eff. 5-2-1995)

Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

laws.content:
(a) Based upon administrative rules promulgated by the Health Department pursuant to Section 2-111 of the Charter, the owner and/or operator of a shelter shall submit, along with their application for license, appropriate written house rules which shall be reviewed and approved by the Health Department prior to issuance of a license by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

laws.title: Food menu required prior to licensure
laws.content:
(a) Based upon administrative rules promulgated by the Health Department pursuant to Section 2-111 of the Charter, the owner and/or operator of a shelter which provides food shall submit, along with their application for license, an appropriate menu which has been approved by a dietitian registered with the American Dietetic Association (ADA) as verified by such dietitian’s name, signature and current ADA registration number, and such approval reviewed by the Health Department prior to issuance of a license by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(b) In preparing such menu based upon rules promulgated by the Health Department, the owners and/or operators of a shelter shall:

(1) Provide meals that, as recommended by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, are nutritious and adequate in quantity to meet the basic dietary needs of their residents; and

(2) Make every attempt to meet the special dietary needs of their residents including, but not limited to, dietary restrictions based upon known medical conditions.

(c) In addition, the owners and/or operators of a shelter who provide food shall make a reasonable effort to make meals available for residents who indicate that, due to personal business reasons, they are unable to return to the shelter at mealtime.

laws.title: Warming centers
laws.content:
(a) The City shall make available a building or buildings by renting or leasing a privately- or publicly-owned building, or provide a City-owned building or buildings, for use as warming centers.

(b) A warming center shall operate from November 15th through April 15th between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

(a) The City shall make available an air-conditioned building or buildings by renting or leasing a privately- or publicly-owned building, or provide a City-owned building or buildings, for use as cooling centers.

(b) A cooling center shall operate from June 15th through September 15th between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m.

(a) The Director of the Recreation Department is hereby authorized to prescribe, in the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code, the days and hours when public markets shall be open for business.

No person shall refuse to comply with the directions of, or interfere with, the authorized employees or the police in carrying out the provisions of this chapter or the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code.

laws.title: Minors on public market property
laws.content:
No children under 18 years of age shall be allowed on public market property during the hours that buying and selling operations are being conducted, unless accompanied by a parent, guardian or employer, or unless they can furnish proof that they have been sent to the public market by a parent, guardian or employer for the purpose of buying farm products, provided, that this section shall not apply to workers on public markets who are approved and registered under Section 37-2-10 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-26; Code 1984, § 31-1-25)

Cross reference—Minors generally, Ch. 29.

laws.title: Posting of advertisements, notices, posters, and signs without permission prohibited; selling of goods and distribution of handbills for commercial purposes without permission prohibited; blocking or impeding pedestrian or vehicular traffic prohibited
laws.content:
(a) Unless authorized by the Market Manager in the public market, no person shall:

(1) Post on any public building or structure at a public market any advertisement, notice, poster, or sign;

(2) Sell or attempt to sell, display or demonstrate any goods, merchandise, real estate, animals, vehicles or other materials; or

(3) Distribute advertising or other printed material, cards, handbills or pamphlets for commercial purposes.

(b) No person shall block or impede pedestrian or vehicular traffic in the public market, provided, that such person shall first be given the opportunity to comply by a police officer or by the Market Manager or designee.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-24; Code 1984, § 31-1-23)

Cross reference—Advertising generally, Ch. 4.

laws.title: Solid waste
laws.content:
(a) The storage, preparation, collection, transport, disposal and placement at any public market of solid waste, as defined in Section 42-1-1 of this Code, are governed by Chapter 42 of this Code, Solid Waste and Illegal Dumping.

(b) The Department of Public Works and the Police Department are responsible for enforcement of Chapter 42 of this Code at any public market.

(c) Any person who violates Chapter 42 of this Code, including illegal dumping, at any public market is subject under Chapter 42:

(1) To issuance of a blight violation notice, to a civil fine, and paying the cost of removal by the City of Detroit.

(2) To the institution of an appropriate action or proceeding in equity to prevent, restrain, correct, or abate any blight violation; and

(3) To legal action to abate a public or private nuisance.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-16; Code 1984, § 31-1-15)

Cross reference—Solid waste and illegal dumping, Ch. 42.

laws.title: Parking of vehicles
laws.content:
(a) Administrative actions.

(1) The Market Manager is authorized to lay out and mark off on public market pavement such driveways as the Market Manager considers necessary to properly serve the public market selling and parking areas, and the Market Manager may determine which public market roadways, if any, should be temporarily or permanently

CD37:4
PUBLIC MARKETS

restricted to one-way traffic. Such roadways shall be properly equipped with traffic signs covering such regulations.

(2) From 12:00 noon until 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, when the public market is not in business session, spaces for parking or storage of vehicles may be rented on the Eastern Market from the Market Manager in such designated parking areas of the public market as the Market Manager deems practical, considering the demands of public market operations, maintenance, and cleaning. Any such spaces shall be marked on the pavement, numbered, and leased at rates to be set as are other public market fees and rentals. Appropriate evidence of the payment of such fees shall be issued to the renters.

Under this subsection, the time when such parking or storage of vehicles is permitted may be extended by the Market Manager into the forenoon hours in such parking areas as the Market Manager can determine from experience will not be needed in the operation of the public market at any particular time of year. Under such circumstances, an amended schedule of rental charges shall be applied by the Market Manager.

(3) The registration plate displayed on a motor vehicle whose driver acts contrary to this section, constitutes *prima facie* evidence that the owner of such motor vehicle was the person who parked, or placed, the motor vehicle at the improper location.

(4) The parking of any vehicle on any public market contrary to Subsections (a)(1) through (3) of this section is declared a nuisance and, in addition to the penalties provided for under Sections 46-1-32 and 46-1-33 of this Code, such vehicle may also be removed and conveyed by, or under the direction of the Police Department, by towing the same, or otherwise, to a vehicle pound.

(b) Violations.

(1) Any violation concerning illegal parking at any public market is governed by Section 46-4-17 of this Code.

(2) The Police and Municipal Parking Departments are responsible for the enforcement of Section 46-4-17 of this Code at any public market.

(3) Any person who violates Section 46-4-17 of this Code at any public market is subject under Chapter 46 to issuance of a civil infraction notice or citation, to a civil fine, and to the payment of costs.

(Code 1964, §§ 33-1-5, 33-1-18; Code 1984, §§ 31-1-5, 31-1-17; Ord. No. 337-H, § 1(33-1-18), eff. 7-31-1979)

laws.title: Restrictions on sales
laws.content:
(a) Stall renters shall be allowed to sell on a public market those products which have been approved by the Market Manager including, but not limited to, wholesome fresh, canned, dried or prepared food products and certain other products of the farm, garden, greenhouse, apiary or of the forest, such as poultry, domesticated rabbits, flowers, plants, nuts, herbs, hay, straw, Christmas trees and greens, provided, that, in so doing, they shall comply with this Code and administrative rules relating thereto, authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code and, provided further, that all live poultry, rabbits and other animals authorized for sale on the public market shall be confined in approved crates.

(b) Merchandise or goods of other nature, including, but not limited to, clothing, jewelry, small electronics, books, and crafts, which shall be approved by the Market Manager, may be sold by producers, street vendors, merchants or other persons in designated areas of the public market. The sellers of such merchandise or goods shall comply with this Code and administrative rules relating thereto, authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code.

(c) Except as permitted by Subsections (a) and (b) of this section, no farm products or merchandise of any other nature shall be sold by producers, street vendors, merchants or other persons on the areas provided for vehicular parking on public market property, or on City streets, alleys or sidewalks within a radius of 500 feet from the boundary of any public market, provided, that this section shall not be construed to prevent wholesale farm product merchants with established business from displaying their farm products on the sidewalk in front

(Code 1964, §§ 33-1-7, 33-1-20; Code 1984, §§ 31-1-7, 31-1-20; Ord. No. 07-07, § 1(31-1-7, 31-1-20), eff. 4-6-2007)

**Sec. 37-2-2. Charges for rental of public market spaces; failure to pay rent.**

(a) Stall spaces on a public market shall be rented either by the day or by the year for occupancy during specific public market sessions, as agreed, but with the understanding that the rights of the renter may be cancelled for failure to pay rent or to comply with the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code. The rentals charged shall be at rates approved by the City Council. The annual rental period on all stalls shall begin on April 1st and expire on March 31st. Stalls rented on or after October 1st shall be charged at one-half the annual rate, but no reduction in annual fees shall be made previous to October 1st. All public market fees and stall rentals shall be paid in advance. In giving refunds to annual stall renters who are permitted to vacate their stalls or whose stall privileges are cancelled, the use of the stall during any month or fraction thereof from May 1st to November 1st shall be charged at double the *pro rata* monthly rate, while for other months the single *pro rata* monthly rate shall apply.

(b) All assignments of stall space made on an annual basis and all annual rental fees accepted under the provisions of this chapter shall be so made and accepted with the express reservation of the right to cancel, any time for cause, any assignment or stall space and refund to the renter the amount of the annual rental covering the unexpired portion of any rental year. In the discretion of the Market Manager, that part of this section requiring all stall rentals shall be paid in advance may be modified in any year to the extent that all renters who pay annual stall rentals may pay such rental in two approximately equal parts, the second part to be paid not later than July 31st of each year.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-8; Code 1984, § 31-1-8)

**Sec. 37-2-3. Information required of renters.**

Before allowing a renter of stall space to sell on a public market, the Market Manager shall require, on a form that is provided by the Recreation Department and signed in the presence of a notary public, such information with reference to the person’s address, character, the nature and extent and location of such person’s business,

the names and amounts of the products such person produces, or which such person sells on the public market, the period when such person comes to the public market, and such other data as may be deemed necessary for the protection of the public and the proper administration of the public market.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-9; Code 1984, § 31-1-9)

**Sec. 37-2-4. Subletting and assignment of stall spaces.**

No person renting a stall space on a public market shall sublet or assign such space, or any privileges pertaining thereto, except with the prior written approval of the Market Manager in accordance with the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-10; Code 1984, § 31-1-10)

**Sec. 37-2-5. Authority of Director of Recreation Department to require sales slips, receipts, and signs.**

In order that business conducted on a public market may be facilitated, and disputes, mistakes, dishonesty and fraud eliminated so far as possible, the Director of the Recreation Department is authorized to require, through the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code, that sellers deliver to buyers approved sales slips, receipts, contracts covering any business transactions involving goods displayed for sale, offered for sale or sold on a public market, or covering goods offered by sellers on a public market for future delivery. The Director of the Recreation Department may also require, through the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code, that every person who sells on a public market display an approved sign in an approved space in connection with such person’s stall space or on such person’s vehicle, giving the name and address and other identification of the producer or dealer operating in the stall space.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-11; Code 1984, § 31-1-11)

**Sec. 37-2-6. Grade names, descriptions, and prices of products.**

The Director of the Recreation Department is authorized to fix, in the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code, the public market grades and descriptions under which various products shall be displayed and sold on a public market, and to require the proper display of grade names, descriptions and prices.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-12; Code 1984, § 31-1-12)

laws.title: Inspection of farm products by health officers; offering for sale, displaying, or selling unwholesome food prohibited
laws.content:
All products sold or bought on a public market shall be open to inspection by the Director of the Health Department in accordance with Chapter 19 of this Code, *Food*, or by state health officials. No food product shall be offered for sale, displayed, or sold on a public market, which is unwholesome or unfit for human consumption.  
(Code 1964, § 33-1-19; Code 1984, § 31-1-18)

laws.title: Sales to be made by stall renters only
laws.content:
No person, except stall renters who are authorized to operate during public market hours, shall sell, transfer or handle farm products or any other goods on any part of public market property, either during or outside of public market hours, provided, that this section shall not be construed to prevent wholesale farm product merchants with established places of business in the immediate area from delivering their farm products on public market property in hand-propelled trucks, provided further, that the Market Manager may issue special permits, upon payment of approved fees, whenever in the Market Manager’s opinion such action is desirable.  
(Code 1964, § 33-1-17; Code 1984, § 31-1-16)

laws.title: Payment for purchases
laws.content:
No person shall remove any products, containers, or any other property from the vehicle of or the display space allotted to any person who sells on a public market without previously having purchased and paid for, or without previously having made arrangements satisfactory to the seller for the purchase or transfer of, such products, containers, or other property.  
(Code 1964, § 33-1-14; Code 1984, § 31-1-14)

laws.title: Registration and approval of workers; badge; establishment and approval of fee
laws.content:
(a) No person shall work or offer such person’s service on a public market as a salesperson, delivery person, private security guard, or in a similar capacity unless such person is approved and registered by the Market Manager, provided, that this section shall not apply to persons who are assigned public market stall space or their regular employees when carrying on their own business on the public market. Applications for such registration shall be made to the Market Manager on a form that is provided by the Recreation Department. The application shall be considered complete when the person has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

(2) The applicant’s current mailing and e-mail addresses; and

(3) The name of the entity, if any, for which the applicant is providing services.

Any information provided in the application in accordance with this subsection shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Market Manager within ten business days of a change of circumstances that would render false or incomplete the information that was previously submitted.

(b) All applicants who are approved and registered shall be issued a badge by the Market Manager, which shall remain the property of the City, and such badge shall be worn by the person registered in a visible way during the time such person is present on the public market. The privileges of any person so registered may be suspended or revoked for good cause shown and after a hearing by the Director of the Recreation Department and the badge recalled.

(c) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Recreation Department is authorized to establish and collect a necessary fee with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of the registration and badge. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fee shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Office of the Market Manager, at the Recreation Department, and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Recreation Department at least once every two years.  
(Code 1964, § 33-1-23; Code 1984, § 31-1-22)

laws.title: Food concessions
laws.content:
The Market Manager is authorized to conduct, on a public market, food service establishments, which will provide the buyers and sellers on the public market with

When such action becomes effective, no person shall display or offer for sale on the public market any prepared foods or beverages designed for the immediate consumption by the buyers and sellers on the public market for the reason that such operation by the Market Manager or by a private party establish their exclusive right to sell such foods and beverages on the public market.

(Code 1964, § 33-1-13; Code 1984, § 31-1-13)

laws.title: Authority to bar from public market privileges and grounds for certain violations
laws.content:
(a) Violation of this chapter, or of the administrative rules authorized by Section 37-1-3 of this Code; conviction on the charge of having violated any other provisions of this Code or of having committed a crime; attempts to establish or the establishment of abnormal or artificial prices for food products sold on a public market by agreement between sellers or between buyers or any other unfair and irregular means; repeated verified complaints against any person who buys or sells on a public market giving reasonably conclusive evidence that such person has practiced deception in such person's dealings on a public market by displaying or selling farm products so packed and faced as to misrepresent the average quality or condition of the farm products in the package, or by knowingly giving false information regarding the origin, variety, quality, condition or value of the farm products which such person sells, or by similar practice, shall, in addition to any other penalties which may be inflicted, be cause for the Market Manager to bar such person from the privileges and grounds of public markets for such period of time as may be deemed advisable.

(b) Any person barred for a specific period of time from public market grounds shall not, during such time, sell or buy, through themselves or any other person, on public markets or drive their vehicle upon the public market property during public market hours. laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this chapter.

(b) Any person who violates this chapter may be issued a violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating this chapter shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued, and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each violation that is issued.

laws.title: Licensed premises to be open for inspection by Police Department and other City departments
laws.content:
For the purpose of ensuring compliance with this chapter, members of the Police Department, or any employee or agent of a City department that is authorized by this Code, may enter any area within the premises used in the operation of a rental hall or a banquet facility at reasonable times to inspect, subject to constitutional restrictions on unreasonable searches and seizures. Where entry is refused, or not obtained, the City is authorized to pursue recourse as provided by law.

(Code 1964, § 53-1-12; Code 1984, § 46-1-2)

Cross reference—Inspection of premises generally, § 28-1-6.

laws.title: Licenses and permits for dances, entertainment or other activity or event required
laws.content:
(a) A rental hall licensee shall not knowingly permit or allow dance or entertainment at the rental hall unless, where required by state law or this Code, applicable licenses and permits have been obtained by the person or entity sponsoring or conducting the activity or event.

(b) A banquet facility licensee shall obtain or maintain in conjunction with its Class C License issued under the Michigan Liquor Control Code of 1998, being MCL 436.1101 et seq., all state and City permits required for dance, entertainment, or other activities or events on the premises.

(Code 1964, § 53-1-14; Code 1984, § 46-1-4)

Cross reference—Public dance halls generally, § 5-10-1 et seq.

laws.title: Hours of operation
laws.content:
(a) A rental hall that is licensed under this chapter shall not operate between the hours of 4:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., except that, where a special licensee using a rental hall possesses a special license for the location that has been issued by the Michigan Liquor Control Commission in accordance with the Michigan Administrative Code, the rental hall shall not operate between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m.

(b) A banquet facility that is licensed under this chapter and, therefore, is licensed by the Michigan Liquor Control Commission in accordance with the Michigan Liquor Control Code of 1998, being MCL 436.1101 et seq., shall not operate between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m.

laws.title: Investigation required by Police Department
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by this article shall be issued or renewed, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall refer the application to the Chief of Police, or the Chief of Police’s designee, who shall cause an investigation whether, within the past three years, the applicant, or any of the applicant’s officers, has been convicted of fraud, embezzlement, arson, murder or attempted murder, or any degree of criminal sexual conduct as described in Sections 135 through 145d of the Michigan Penal Code, being MCL 750.135 through 750.145d.

laws.title: Investigation required by Office of Chief Financial Officer to confirm no City tax or assessment arrearage
laws.content:

laws.title: Retirement System Intended to be Tax-Qualified
laws.content: The Retirement System is a governmental plan under Section 414(d) of the Internal Revenue Code which is intended to be a qualified plan and trust pursuant to applicable provisions of the Internal Revenue Code. The Board shall construe and administer the provisions of the Retirement System in a manner that gives effect to the tax-qualified status of the Retirement System.

laws.title: Board of Trustees - Membership; Appointment
Board of Trustees; Oath; Term; Vacancies
laws.content:
Within ten days after appointment or election, each Trustee shall take an oath of office to be administered by the Detroit City Clerk.

The regular term of office for the elected Member Trustees and the Trustee appointed by the Mayor under Section 1.5(5) shall be for a period of six years, one such Trustee to be elected or appointed, as the case may be, each year. The term of office for the Retiree Trustee shall be two years.

DETROIT CITY CODE

If an active employee Trustee leaves the employ of the City, or if an elected or appointed Trustee fails to attend four consecutive scheduled Board meetings without being excused for cause by the Trustees attending such meetings, the Trustee shall be considered to have resigned from the Board. By resolution, the Board shall declare the office vacated as of the date of adoption of such resolution. If a vacancy occurs in the office of Trustee, the vacancy shall be filled at the next regular election held by the Board, or at any special election ordered by resolution adopted by the Board.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Officers and Employees
laws.content: The Board shall elect a chair and vice-chair from its members. The executive director of the Retirement System or its designee shall serve as secretary of the Board. The Board may employ such actuarial, medical and other contractors and employees as shall be required, subject to the powers and authority reserved to the Investment Committee and subject to the Public Employee Retirement System Investment Act, as amended, MCL 38.1132 et seq.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Meetings; Rules of Procedure; Votes; Quorum
laws.content:
(1) The Board shall hold regular meetings, at least one in each month, and shall hold special meetings as necessary. The Board shall designate the time and place thereof in advance. The Board shall adopt its own rules of procedure, including provisions for special meetings and notice thereof, and shall keep a record of proceedings. All meetings of the Board shall be public and are subject to the Michigan Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.261 et seq. All Board meetings shall be held within the City of Detroit.

(2) Each Trustee shall be entitled to one vote on each question before the Board. A majority vote of the Trustees present shall be necessary for a decision by the Trustees at any meeting of the Board.

(3) Five Trustees shall constitute a quorum.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Compensation; Expenses
laws.content:
Members of the Board of Trustees shall serve without additional compensation from the Employer, but they shall be compensated by the Retirement System as follows:

(1) Stipend. Trustees are eligible for a meeting stipend, provided the Trustee attends one or more regular or special Board meetings during a month. The stipend amount shall be a minimum of sixty-seven dollars ($67.00) per week multiplied by the Trustee’s years of service. Eligibility rules and the amount of the stipend shall be set by Board resolution. However, the amount of the weekly meeting stipend shall not exceed two hundred dollars ($200.00).

(2) Ex Officio Trustees. Ex Officio Trustees are not eligible for a stipend payment.

(3) Attendance. For purposes of this Section 1.10, attendance at a Board meeting shall include actual attendance at a meeting or being otherwise available to attend a Board meeting canceled for lack of a quorum.

Trustees shall be reimbursed from the Expense Fund for all actual, reasonable and necessary expenses incurred in the performance of their duties as Trustees.

laws.title: Rules for Administration of Funds
laws.content: Subject to the limitations contained in this Combined Plan Document, the Board of Trustees shall, from time to time, establish rules and regulations for the administration of the funds created by this Plan document and for the transaction of its business.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Certain Data to be Kept
laws.content: The Board shall keep, or cause to be kept, in convenient form, such data as shall be necessary for an actuarial valuation of the Retirement System and for checking and compiling the experience of the Retirement System. The ordinary actuarial, accounting and clerical services for the operation of the Retirement System shall be performed by the employees of the Retirement System.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Annual Audit Report
laws.content: The Board shall render a report to the Mayor, the City Council and the Investment Committee on or before the fifteenth day of January, showing the fiscal transactions of the Retirement System for the year ending on the preceding thirtieth day of June, the amounts of accumulated cash and securities in the various funds of the System, and the last balance sheet showing the financial condition of the Retirement System by means of an actuarial valuation of the assets and liabilities of the Retirement System.

laws.title: Retirement Systems
laws.content:

Trustees. Any legal advisor to the Board of Trustees shall be an attorney licensed to practice law in the State of Michigan and shall be experienced in matters relating to pension systems. The qualifications of legal counsel shall be approved by the Board of Trustees.

(2) Legal advisors to the Board of Trustees shall have such duties relative to pension matters as shall be assigned by the Board of Trustees.

(3) Costs and expenses relative to the position of legal advisors to the Board shall be payable out of the assets of the Retirement System, subject to the provisions of the *Public Employee Retirement System Investment Act, as amended, MCL 38.1132 et seq.*

laws.title: Designation of Actuary; Authority to Engage Additional Actuaries
laws.content:
The Retirement System actuary as of July 1, 2014 shall continue to serve as such until resignation or removal by the Board. In the event the Board desires to retain a new actuary, the Board and the Investment Committee shall collectively participate in the evaluation and selection of a qualified actuary. The Retirement System actuary shall be responsible for assisting the Board and the Investment Committee in performing their actuarial duties and shall comply with all requests for information or modeling requested by the Board or the Investment Committee, and shall attend meetings of the Board and Investment Committee as requested, so as to allow the Board and Investment Committee to perform satisfactorily the rights and duties set forth in the Combined Plan, the term sheet regarding Investment Committee Governance for General Retirement System, attached to that certain agreement by and between the Michigan Settlement Administration Authority, a Michigan body public corporation (the "Authority"), the Retirement System, the Police and Fire Retirement System for the City of Detroit, Michigan ("PFRS") and the City (the "State Contribution Agreement") as Exhibit A (the "Governance Term Sheet") and the Plan of Adjustment. Furthermore, the Board shall not act on any recommendation made by the Retirement System's actuary based on any calculation, assumption or assessment rejected by the Investment Committee.

Nothing herein shall be interpreted as limiting the Investment Committee's authority to engage an actuarial consulting firm other than the Retirement System's actuary to perform actuarial services deemed necessary to fulfill its fiduciary and other duties to the Retirement System as set forth in the Governance Term Sheet and the Plan of Adjustment.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Adoption of Mortality and Other Tables of Experience and Rates of Interest; Limitations on Payments by the Retirement System
laws.content:
(1) Subject to Section 15.1, the Board shall adopt such mortality and other tables of experience, and a rate or rates of interest, as shall be necessary for the operation of the System on an actuarial basis, provided, that the authority granted by this section shall not permit or be used to provide for an interest rate which would violate the prohibitions of subsection (2) or (3) of this section.

(2) The Retirement System and the Trustees charged with management of the System shall not make any payment to active or retired Members other than payments that are required by the governing documents of the Retirement System. This prohibition applies to all payments that are not authorized by this Combined Plan, whether such payments are those commonly referred to as a "thirteenth check" or by any other name.

(3) Anything in this Combined Plan Document or any other document to the contrary notwithstanding, the annual actuarial interest rate assumption for the period commencing July 1, 2014 and ending June 30, 2023 shall be six and three-quarters percent (6.75%).

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Annual Actuarial Valuation of Assets and Liabilities
laws.content: Subject to Section 15.1, each year, on the basis of such mortality and other tables of experience, and such rate or rates of regular interest as the Board shall adopt pursuant to Section 1.16, the Board shall cause to be made an actuarial valuation of the assets and liabilities of the Retirement System.

laws.title: Board of Trustees; Powers and Duties; Fiduciary Status; Fiduciary Duties
laws.content:
The Board of Trustees shall have such powers and duties as are necessary for the proper administration of the Retirement System and the custody and investment of Retirement System assets, other than those powers and duties reserved to the Investment Committee. To the extent the Board exercises discretion with respect to investment of Retirement System assets, each member of the Board of Trustees shall be an investment fiduciary as defined in the *Public Employee Retirement System Investment Act, as amended, MCL 38.1132 et seq.*, and shall discharge his or her duties with respect to the Retirement System in compliance with the provisions of the *Public Employee Retirement System Investment Act, as amended, MCL 38.1132 et seq.* A member of the Board of Trustees

DETROIT CITY CODE

shall discharge his or her duties with the care, skill and caution under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person, acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters, would use in the conduct of an activity of like character and purpose. Board members shall comply with all Board governance policies and procedures, including the Ethics and Code of Conduct Policies, unless such compliance would violate the member’s fiduciary duties or conflicts with the provisions set forth in this Combined Plan Document.

laws.title: Investment Committee; Term; Resignation and Removal; Vacancies
laws.content:
The term of office for the independent members of the Investment Committee shall be six years; provided,
