**Sec. 41-3-6. Retaining precious item for nine calendar days; alteration.**

A precious item that is received by a dealer shall be retained by the dealer for nine calendar days after receipt without any form of alteration other than that required to make an accurate appraisal of its value.

(Code 1964, $\S$ 30-2-7; Code 1984, $\S$ 49-3-4; Ord. No. 427-H, $\S$ 1(30-2-7), eff. 2-27-1981; Ord. No. 485-H, $\S$ 1(30-2-7), eff. 2-26-1982)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 445.485.*

**Sec. 41-3-7. Prohibited conduct.**

A dealer, or an agent or employee of a dealer, shall not:

(1) Knowingly receive or purchase a precious item from any person who is less than 18 years of age, or from any person known by the dealer or agent or employee of the dealer to have been convicted of theft or receipt of stolen property within the preceding five years, whether the person is acting in such person’s own behalf or as the agent of another.

(2) Knowingly receive or purchase a precious item from a person unless that person presents a valid driver’s license or a valid state personal identification card.

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 445.486.*

**Sec. 41-3-8. Exemptions from article.**

Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to apply on exchanges of, returns of, or credits on merchandise previously purchased from the dealer, where such merchandise is exchanged, returned or credited or accepted in full or part payment for new merchandise, or to the first purchase or sale in this country of any article imported from any other country.

(Code 1964, $\S$ 30-2-9; Code 1984, $\S$ 49-3-5)

**Sec. 41-3-9. Copy of article to be posted.**

Every dealer licensed under this article shall post in a conspicuous place in such dealer’s place of business a copy of this article, which shall be furnished by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(Code 1964, $\S$ 30-2-10; Code 1984, $\S$ 49-3-6)

Secs. 41-3-10—41-3-20. Reserved.

**DIVISION 2. LICENSE***

**Sec. 41-3-21. Required for primary and incidental businesses.**

It shall be unlawful for a person or dealer to conduct or to maintain any primary business, or any activity or dealing incidental to a regular jewelry business or any other business, of buying or selling any secondhand jewelry, used silverware, or other secondhand manufactured article, composed wholly or in part of gold, silver, platinum or other metal, or to engage in the business of buying and selling old gold, silver, platinum or other metal in the City without first having obtained a license from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to operate such business.

(Code 1984, $\S$ 49-3-18)

**Sec. 41-3-22. Application; information required.**

(a) An application for a license under this division shall be made on a form that is provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center. The application shall be considered completed when the appropriate person has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required license fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) Where the applicant is an individual:

a. The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

b. The applicant’s current mailing address and e-mail address; and

c. Written proof of age in the form of a driver’s license, or a picture identification document containing the applicant’s date of birth issued by a governmental agency,

(d) A scrap metal dealer shall maintain the conditions of its premises so as to avoid the imposition of artificial illumination, dirt, dust, litter, mud, noise, odors, vermin, vibration, water runoff, and other nuisances upon adjacent properties or rights-of-way.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-3; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-3), eff. 1-31-2007; Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Reporting violations; primary enforcement; examination of articles and materials by Police Department
laws.content:
(a) City of Detroit inspectors shall have the duty to report all alleged violations of this article to the Police Department, which shall have primary enforcement responsibility.

(b) Every scrap metal dealer shall provide, upon request, for examination by the Police Department or a designated enforcement officer any articles or materials that have been brought or received on the premises of the scrap metal dealer.

(Code 1984, §§ 49-8-5(b), 49-8-7; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-5(b), 49-8-7), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Loitering by minors prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for minors to loiter about the premises of any scrap metal dealer.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-9; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-9), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Pledges, pawns, and loans prohibited
laws.content:
A scrap metal dealer shall not receive, in the course of business, any article by way of a pledge or pawn, or shall loan or advance any sum of money on the security of any scrap metal.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-4; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-4), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Business transactions prohibited during certain hours
laws.content:
(a) A scrap metal dealer shall not purchase or receive any scrap metal by sale, barter, exchange or otherwise from any person between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

(b) This section shall not apply to the receipt of industrial scrap by a scrap metal dealer.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-8; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-8), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: (a) Scrap metal dealer
laws.content:
(1) Unless Section 41-4-10 of this Code applies, and except as provided for in Subsection (a)(2) of this section for an industrial or commercial customer, a scrap metal dealer shall only pay a seller using one of the following methods of payment in a purchase transaction and shall not pay the seller in cash or using any other method of payment:

a. A check or money order. A scrap metal dealer shall make and retain a photograph or digital or electronic image of the delivery of the check or money order to the seller, or individual acting on behalf of the seller, in the purchase transaction that includes the face of that seller or individual; or.

b. An electronic payment card or encrypted receipt that may only be converted to cash in an automated teller machine that is located on the scrap metal dealer’s premises, is used for the sole purpose of dispensing cash in connection with purchase transactions, and provides a digital or electronic image of the dispensing of the cash to the seller or individual acting on behalf of the seller in the purchase transaction that includes the face of that seller or individual. For purposes of this section and Section 41-4-10 of this Code, payment using an electronic payment card or encrypted receipt as described in this subsection is not considered a payment in cash.

(2) In a purchase transaction with an industrial or commercial customer:

a. The scrap metal dealer may pay using any of the following methods of payment, as agreed to by the scrap metal dealer and the industrial or commercial customer and, except as provided for in Subsection (a)(3)

Supp. No. 4

$\S 41-4-9$

DETROIT CODE

of this section, shall not pay the seller in cash or using any other method of payment:

1. By check, money order, or payment card, or receipt described in Subsection (a)(1)b of this section. Where a payment described in this subsection is mailed to the industrial or commercial customer, the scrap metal dealer may mail that payment to the street address or post office box of the industrial or commercial customer or to another person or post office box as directed by the industrial or commercial customer; or

2. By bank wire transfer or other electronic delivery to an account of the industrial or commercial customer.

b. The payment requirements described in Section 41-4-10(a) of this Code do not apply to the purchase of any of the items described in Section 41-4-10(a)(3)a through c of this Code by an industrial or commercial customer.

(3) A scrap metal dealer may accept barter or a trade or exchange of scrap metal or other property in a purchase transaction as all or part of the consideration for that transaction.

(4) A scrap metal dealer in a purchase transaction shall examine the identification presented under Subsection (b)(1) of this section by the seller or individual acting on behalf of the seller and, where the identification presented displays the date of birth of the individual, confirm that the individual is at least 16 years old based on that date of birth.

(5) A scrap metal dealer shall ensure that each scale operator, purchaser, and supervisor employed by the scrap metal dealer is trained concerning the legal requirements of this division and the responsibilities of the scrap metal dealer under this division.

(b) Seller shall, whether an individual, or an individual acting as an agent or representative of a seller.

(1) He or she shall present his or her operator’s or chauffeur’s license, military identification card, Michigan identification card, passport, or other government-issued identification containing his or her photograph to the scrap metal dealer and allow the scrap metal dealer to make a photocopy or electronic copy of the identification;

(2) He or she shall allow the scrap metal dealer to take his or her thumbprint, which is to be used only for identification purposes by the scrap metal dealer and for investigation purposes by a law enforcement agency;

(3) He or she shall provide the scrap metal dealer with a signed statement that certifies that he or she is the owner of, or is otherwise authorized to sell, the scrap metal to the scrap metal dealer and is at least 16 years old; and

(4) He or she shall certify that he or she has not been convicted of a crime involving the theft, conversion, or sale of scrap metal for the reason that conviction of such crime or crimes precludes entry into the purchase transaction.

laws.title: Payment methods for certain purchase transactions; electronic database; duties of scrap metal dealer upon implementation and operation of database; payment
laws.content:
(a) In a purchase transaction of any of the following items, the only methods of payment a scrap metal dealer may use to pay a seller are:

(1) A direct deposit or electronic transfer to the seller’s account at a financial institution;

(2) Subject to Subsection (c) of this section, payment with a check or money order described in Section 41-4-9(a)(1)a of this Code; or

(3) Subject to Subsection (5) of this section, payment with an electronic payment card or encrypted receipt described in Section 41-4-9(a)(1)b of this Code:

a. Catalytic converters, unless the seller is an automotive recycler as defined in Section of this Code, a manufacturer or wholesaler of catalytic converters, or a muffler shop, tire store or other retail business that sells converters separately or as part of an exhaust system;

b. Air conditioners, air conditioner evaporator coils or condensers, or parts of air conditioner evaporator coils and condensers; or

Supp. No. 4

CD41:42

laws.title: Secondhand Goods
laws.content:
§ 41-4-11

c. Copper wire, including copper wire that is burned in whole or in part to remove the insulation, copper pipe, or copper fittings.

(b) Where, under Section 6 of the Michigan Scrap Metal Regulatory Act, being MCL 445.426, the Department of State Police implements a single-shared electronic database and publishes notice that the database is implemented and in operation, a scrap metal dealer shall:

(1) Register or subscribe to the database and pay a reasonable fee for that registration or subscription; and

(2) By 12 noon of the next business day after a purchase transaction of one or more items described in Subsection (a)(3)a. through c. occurs, electronically report the purchase of the item or items to the database by providing the following information, provided, that a scrap metal dealer is not required to report the consideration paid for the item or items or other pricing information for inclusion in the database:

a. Name and address of the scrap metal dealer and seller;

b. Date and time of the purchase transaction;

c. A description of the item or items purchased; and

d. The weight or volume of the item or items purchased.

(c) Where the purchase price in a purchase transaction described in Subsection (a) of this section is $25.00 or more, or where the purchase price for all of a seller’s purchase transactions described in Subsection (a) of this section in a business day is $25.00 or more, the scrap metal dealer must pay the seller, for those items described in Subsection (a) only, by mailing one of the following items to the seller at the address shown on the identification card presented under Section 41-4-9(b)(1) of this Code, and shall not deliver that payment in person or using any other form of delivery:

(1) A check or money order described in Section 41-4-9(a)(1)a of this Code.

(2) An electronic payment card or encrypted receipt described in Section 41-4-9(a)(1)b of this Code.

(3) A non-transferable receipt that the seller may redeem at the scrap dealer’s premises for one of the items described in Subsection (c)(1) or (c)(2) of this section.

laws.title: Record of purchase transaction; preparation and maintenance; duration; location; availability for inspection; contents; exception; use of electronic record-keeping system
laws.content:
(a) Subject to Subsection (d) of this section, and except as otherwise provided in this section, a scrap metal dealer shall prepare and maintain a separate, accurate, and legible record of each purchase transaction. The scrap metal dealer shall:

(1) Maintain the records described in this section for at least one year;

(2) Keep the records in a location that is readily accessible to a local, state, or federal law enforcement agency, or to railroad police in investigation of stolen railroad property, for inspection during normal business hours; and

(3) Make the records, or copies of those records, available on request to any local, state, or federal law enforcement agency.

(b) The record of a purchase transaction described in Subsection (a) of this section shall include all of the following:

(1) The name and address of the seller and the name and address of the individual who is delivering the scrap metal where he or she is not the seller. Where an individual is a seller or representative of a seller in more than one purchase transaction, the scrap metal dealer may retain a copy of the individual’s information or document described in this subsection in a separate file and use that information in future purchase transactions.

(2) The name, address, and identifying number from the identification presented under Section 41-4-9(b)(1) of this Code. A legible scan or photocopy of the identification meets the requirement of this subsection. Where an individual is a seller or representative of a seller in more than one purchase transaction, the scrap metal dealer may retain a copy of the information or docu-

Supp. No. 4

CD41:43
$\S 41-4-11$

DETROIT CODE

ment described in this subsection in a separate file and use that information in future purchase transactions.

(3) Where the scrap metal is delivered by licensed vehicle, the license plate number of the vehicle.

(4) The date and time of the purchase transaction.

(5) A description of the predominant types of scrap metal purchased in accordance with the custom of the trade.

(6) The weight, quantity, or volume of the scrap metal purchased, described and calculated in accordance with the custom of the trade; the name of the scale operator who weighs and inspects that property; and the name of the employee of the scrap metal dealer who purchased or authorized the purchase of the scrap metal on the scrap metal dealer’s behalf where the purchaser was not the scale operator.

(7) A photograph or digital, electronic, or video image of the scrap metal purchased. A photograph or digital, electronic, or video image that meets one of the following is sufficient for purposes of this subsection even where each item of scrap metal is not shown in the image:

a. Where the scrap metal and the vehicle in which it is delivered are weighed, an overhead photograph or image of the vehicle and the scrap metal in the vehicle on the scale; or

b. Where only the scrap metal is weighed, a photograph or image of the scrap metal on the scale.

(8) The consideration paid and the method of payment.

(9) The signed statement described in Section 41-4-9(b)(3) of this Code.

(10) A legible thumbprint described in Section 41-4-9(b)(2) of this Code.

(11) A digital photograph of the seller, or the individual who is delivering the scrap metal where he or she is not the seller, that includes his or her face and is taken at the time the scrap metal is delivered to the scrap metal dealer.

(c) A scrap metal dealer is not required to obtain the information described in Subsection (b) of this section for a purchase transaction with an industrial or commercial customer that meets all of the following:

(1) Payment is made directly to the industrial or commercial customer;

(2) The personal and business identifying information of the industrial or commercial customer is on file with the scrap metal dealer and conforms to a written description of the type of scrap metal customarily purchased by the scrap metal dealer from that customer; and

(3) The information on file with the scrap metal dealer under Subsection (c)(2) of this section is periodically reviewed at least every two years and validated as current or updated by the scrap metal dealer.

(d) A scrap metal dealer may utilize an electronic record-keeping system for purposes of Subsection (a) of this section where that system allows for immediate access to each seller’s purchase transaction activities, documents and images, including, but not limited to, electronic copies of the records described in Subsection (b) or (c) of this section, the payment information contained in the card or receipt, and the image described in Section 41-4-9(a)(1)a of this Code or Section 41-4-9(a)(1)b of this Code.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-5; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-5), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Article containing nonferrous metal; tagging and holding by scrap metal dealer required; circumstances; creation and maintenance of records; certain sales prohibited
laws.content:
(a) A scrap metal dealer shall tag and hold, for seven calendar days, any article containing nonferrous metal purchased from a seller and that is offered for purchase under any of the following circumstances:

(1) The article has altered or obliterated serial numbers, and the person delivering the article does not have a written receipt or documentation;

(2) Where, due to the identification on the article or due to the type of article, the scrap metal dealer would reasonably be considered to have knowledge that the article is, or was, the property of a

Supp. No. 4

CD41:44

laws.title: Secondhand Goods
laws.content:
§ 41-4-13

governmental entity, and the person delivering the article does not have a written receipt or documentation;

(3) Where, due to the identification on the article, the scrap metal dealer would reasonably be considered to have knowledge that the article is, or was, the property of a business, and the person delivering the article does not have a written receipt or documentation;

(4) The article is a commemorative, decorative, or other cemetery-related or apparently ceremonial article, and the person delivering the article does not have a written receipt or documentation;

(5) The article is subject to a notification or bulletin from any law enforcement agency that is received by the scrap metal dealer prior to the purchase of the article; or

(6) Where the article is copper wiring, whether burned or with sheathing, and the person delivering the article does not have a written receipt or documentation.

(b) The tag and hold requirements of this section require the scrap metal dealer to also create and maintain the records required under Section 41-4-11 of this Code regarding those articles.

(c) The tag and hold requirements of Subsection (a) of this section do not apply:

(1) To any article containing nonferrous metal that does not conform to the circumstances described in Subsection (a) of this section; or

(2) To any article that has been the subject of tag and hold by one scrap metal dealer in compliance with this section where that article is resold directly to another scrap metal dealer. In addition, any article that was not initially subject to the tag and hold provisions of this section is not thereafter subject to the tag and hold provisions where that article is resold to another scrap metal dealer.

(d) Except in the case where the seller has specific written documentation that the seller is the owner, agent, or person with authority to possess and sell certain articles, a seller shall not sell or offer for sale, and a scrap metal dealer shall not purchase, any article containing nonferrous metal that is marked with any form of the name, initials, markings, or logo of a governmental entity, utility, cemetery or railroad, any beer kegs, or any public fixtures. Any sale is subject to the provisions of this division.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-6; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-6), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Sale or purchase of certain property prohibited; posting of warning notice required
laws.content:
(a) A person shall not knowingly sell or attempt to sell to a scrap metal dealer, and a scrap metal dealer shall not knowingly purchase or offer to purchase, any of the following types of property:

(1) Public fixtures, provided, that this subsection does not apply where the seller is a governmental unit or the seller has written authorization from the governmental unit that owned the property to sell the property;

(2) Metal articles or materials that are clearly marked as property belonging to a person other than the seller, provided, that this subsection does not apply where the seller has authorization from that person to sell the property;

(3) A commemorative, decorative, or other cemetery-related or apparently ceremonial article, provided, that this subsection does not apply where the seller is the owner of the article, where the seller is authorized by the owner of the article to sell the article, or where the seller of a cemetery-related article is the cemetery in which the article was located;

(4) Metal articles or materials removed from property owned by a railroad company or from a railroad right-of-way, provided, that this subsection does not apply where the seller is the owner of the metal articles or materials, is the manufacturer of the metal articles or materials, is a contractor engaged in the business of repairing railroad equipment, or is a person that has written authorization from that owner, manufacturer or contractor to sell those metal articles or materials; or

(5) A silver alloy telecommunication battery with a threaded insert terminal connection, provided, that this subsection does not apply to a battery used in auto or mobile equipment, or where the seller is a provider of telecommunication service

or the seller has written authorization from the provider of telecommunication service that owned the property to sell the property.

(b) In the event a scrap metal dealer has knowledge that, due to the identification or the type of article or material, or the fact that the article or material is the subject of a theft-alert report received by the scrap metal dealer, a person is attempting to sell or exchange an article or material that is stolen, the scrap metal dealer shall advise the Police Department, where possible, of the person’s identity, vehicle information, and a description of the article or material the person presented to the scrap metal dealer for sale or exchange.

(c) Every scrap metal dealer shall post a notice where articles or materials are received that is visible to its employees and to the public, which states in Roman letters not less than four inches in height;

> "In accordance with Section 41-4-13 of the 2019 Detroit City Code, it is a criminal offense for a scrap metal dealer to purchase or receive any article or material: 1) from any person under the age of 16 years, or 2) from any person without identification or a license, or 3) that is the property of the government, a business, or a cemetery and the person does not have a written receipt or other documentation which indicates where the person obtained the article or material, or 4) that is the subject of a theft-alert report from any law enforcement agency or a member of the public."

(Code 1984, § 49-8-10; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-10), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Registration with or subscription to, and use by employees of, database required
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 11(1) and (2) of the Michigan Scrap Metal Regulatory Act, being MCL 445.431(1) and (2), a scrap metal dealer shall register with or subscribe to, maintain that registration or subscription with, and use in the conduct of its business, an internet-based database available to scrap metal dealers, law enforcement agencies, and the general public that lists and tracks, at a minimum, thefts of scrap metal.

(b) A scrap metal dealer shall ensure that it makes available to each of its employees engaged in purchasing or weighing scrap metal sold or offered for sale to the scrap metal dealer each theft alert, or similar notice that a scrap metal theft has occurred, that the scrap metal dealer receives from the database service described in this section, and that those employees review any recent alerts or similar notices that they have not previously reviewed on a daily basis.

laws.title: Recording surveillance system required
laws.content:
(a) Every scrap metal dealer, as a condition of being licensed under this article to operate its business, shall have a video surveillance system installed on its premises where scrap metal, industrial scrap, and salvage vehicles are received. Such scrap metal dealer shall:

(1) Maintain the video surveillance system in good working condition and ensure that such system records persons bringing such items to the scrap metal dealer for sale or delivery;

(2) Make available, upon request, digital or video recordings from the surveillance system to the Police Department for review during regular business hours; and

(3) Retain surveillance recordings for at least 90 days.

(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

Secs. 41-4-16—41-4-20. Reserved.

laws.title: Required; surety bond prerequisite
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct or to maintain any business as a scrap metal dealer in the City without having first obtained a license from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to operate such business.

(b) A surety bond in the amount of $5,000.00 shall be required for any person desiring to engage in the business of scrap metal dealer in the City.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-21; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-22), eff. 1-31-2007; Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Application; information required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a license under this division shall be made on a form that is provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center. The application shall be considered completed when the appropriate person has signed and

Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee
laws.content:
(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the Charter for the processing and issuance of a license under this division. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) A fee shall be charged each new licensee, any current licensee who applies to renew an existing license, or a current licensee applying for a license at another location.

(d) Prior to the expiration of a current license, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay an annual fee for the renewal of a license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation of the business for the location until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-26; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-26), eff. 1-31-2007)

laws.title: Inspection and certification of approval; land use; construction requirements; maintenance, fire protection and safety, and health and sanitation requirements
Investigation by Police Department required to confirm non-conviction of certain crimes
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license required by this division shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to refer such application to the Chief of Police or the designee of the Chief of Police, who shall cause an investigation to be completed to determine whether the applicant, or any of the applicant’s officers, have been convicted of any offense during the past five years involving the theft of property, or of any felony during the past five years concerning fraud, embezzlement, dishonesty or assault.

(b) A scrap metal dealer license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center until the Chief of Police has given written confirmation that the applicant does not have any convictions for offenses which are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-24; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-24), eff. 1-31-2007)

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-24; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-24), eff. 1-31-2007)

**Sec. 41-4-27. Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to take action upon application.**

Upon compliance with Sections 41-4-21 through 41-4-26 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall issue an annual license for a business in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, *Licenses*.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-22(b); Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-22(b)), eff. 1-31-2007)

**Sec. 41-4-28. Posting required; non-transferable.**

(a) Upon issuance by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center and after receipt by the applicant, a scrap metal dealer license shall be posted at all times by the licensee inside the licensed premises in a conspicuous location near the entrance.

(b) All scrap metal dealer licenses that are issued under this article shall not be transferable.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-25; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-25), eff. 1-31-2007)

**Sec. 41-4-29. Expiration date and renewal requirements.**

(a) A license that is issued under this division shall expire on March 31st of each year.

(b) A license that is issued under this division shall remain valid until the expiration date unless suspended or revoked in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, *Licenses*.

(c) A license that is issued under this division may be renewed only by submitting a completed application and paying the required fee as provided for in this division.

(d) All applications for renewal of a license that is issued under this division shall be filed before April 1st of each year.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-26; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-26), eff. 1-31-2007)

**Sec. 41-4-30. Suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal.**

A license that is issued under this division may be suspended, revoked, or denied renewal in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, *Licenses*.

(Code 1984, § 49-8-27; Ord. No. 38-06, § 1(49-8-27), eff. 1-31-2007)

**Secs. 41-4-31—41-4-40. Reserved.**

laws.title: Generally
laws.content:
**Sec. 41-5-1. Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof.**

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

**Sec. 41-5-2. Permit required for removal of household appliances and appurtenances; tags or stickers to be issued to applicants.**

(a) No person shall remove any chandeliers, fixtures, plumbing articles, or similar appliances or appurtenances from any structure in the City without first securing a permit from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. Such permit shall be issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department upon proper application, giving the name and address of the applicant, the owner’s name, the address of the structure from which such chandeliers, fixtures, plumbing articles, or similar appliances or ap-

laws.title: Tags or stickers to be attached to household appliances and appurtenances prior to sale
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to sell or purchase any household appliances or appurtenances, such as chandeliers, secondhand plumbing articles or materials, and similar fixtures, unless the identification tag or sticker issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is affixed to each of such articles.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-5; Code 1984, § 49-2-2)

laws.title: Records to be kept by dealers
laws.content:
Every person licensed under this article shall keep a book in which shall be written in ink, at the time of the purchase of any housewrecking material, used building material, or used household appliances and appurtenances, a complete description of the person from whom such purchase was made, which description shall contain the name, street address, color, age, height and weight of such person, the date and hour of such purchase, the delivery vehicle license number and the number of the removal permit issued by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department. Such book shall at all times be open to the inspection of any member of the

Police Department. No entry in such book shall be erased, obliterated, altered or defaced.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-6; Code 1984, § 49-2-3)

laws.title: Tags to be attached to articles by dealers at time of purchase
laws.content:
Every licensed dealer under this article, at the time of making any purchase, shall attach a tag with a designating number thereon, legibly written, to each article purchased, and shall make entry of such number in the book required by Section 41-5-4 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-7; Code 1984, § 49-2-4)

laws.title: Dealer to report to police
laws.content:
Every licensed dealer under this article shall make out, every week day before the hour of 10:00 a.m., on blank forms to be furnished by the Police Department for that purpose, a legible and correct copy of the record required by Section 41-5-4 of this Code to be kept, containing the particulars of all purchases of such articles on the preceding business day, and shall deliver such copy of such record to the Chief of Police or the authorized representative of the Chief of Police.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-8; Code 1984, § 49-2-5)

Cross reference—Law enforcement, Ch. 26.

laws.title: Hours of operation
laws.content:
No licensed dealer in housewrecking material, used building material, and used household appliances and appurtenances shall permit such dealer’s store or place for buying and selling housewrecking material, used building material, and used household appliances and appurtenances to be open except between sunrise and 9:00 p.m. on any day except Saturday, on which day such store or place of business may be kept open for the transaction of business until 11:00 p.m.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-9; Code 1984, § 49-2-6)

laws.title: Articles to be held 15 days after purchase before sale
laws.content:
No person licensed under the provisions of this article shall sell or remove from such person’s place of business any housewrecking material, used building material, or

laws.title: Exemptions for article
laws.content:
The provisions of this article shall not apply to persons who are engaged in the business of razing whole structures and disposing of the materials secured through the razing of such whole structures and who are licensed as demolition contractors.  
(Code 1964, § 12-1-12; Code 1984, § 49-2-8)

laws.title: Posting of article
laws.content:

(Code 1964, § 12-1-13; Code 1984, § 49-2-9)

(Code 1964, § 12-1-1; Code 1984, § 49-2-21)

laws.title: Licenses limited to one place of business
laws.content:
No person who is licensed under this article shall keep more than one house, shop or place for buying, receiving, taking in or selling housewrecking material, used building material, or used household appliances and appurtenances of any description at any place other than such person's place of business.  
(Code 1964, § 12-1-3; Code 1984, § 49-2-22)

laws.content:
(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the Charter for the processing and issuance of a license under this division. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(c) A fee shall be charged each new licensee, any current licensee who applies to renew an existing license, or a current licensee applying for a license at another location.

Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation of the business for the location until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-2; Code 1984, § 49-2-23; Ord. No. 500-H, § 1(12-1-2), eff. 5-21-1982)

laws.title: Fee; bond
laws.content:
The Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center is hereby authorized to grant a license to any person to engage in the business of buying, selling and dealing in housewrecking material, used building material, or used household appliances and appurtenances, on the execution of a bond to the City in the penal sum of $1,000.00 with one or more sufficient sureties, conditioned that such person will faithfully observe the provisions of the Charter, this Code, and state law relative to the conduct of such business.

(Code 1964, § 12-1-2; Code 1984, § 49-2-23; Ord. No. 500-H, § 1(12-1-2), eff. 5-21-1982)

laws.title: Inspection and certification of approval; land use; construction requirements; maintenance, fire protection and safety, and health and sanitation requirements
laws.content:

(b) After completion of respective inspections, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the Fire Department, and the Health Department shall certify, in writing, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center that the applicant is in full compliance with all pertinent state codes and regulations, and this Code, including, but not limited to, the following requirements:

(1) Land use. The business meets the requirements of Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, including

laws.content:

(b) A used building materials dealer license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center until the Chief of Police has given written confirmation that the applicant does not have any convictions for offenses, which are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Investigation by Office of Chief Financial Officer required to confirm no City tax or assessment arrearage
laws.content:
(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by this division shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessments are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

laws.title: Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to take action upon application
laws.content:

laws.title: Posting required; non-transferable
laws.content:
(a) Upon issuance by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center and after receipt by the applicant, a license that is issued under this division shall be posted at all times by the licensee inside the licensed premises in a conspicuous location near the entrance.

(b) All licenses issued under this division are not transferable to another individual, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity.

laws.title: Expiration date and renewal requirements
laws.content:
(a) A license that is issued under this division shall expire on October 31st of each year.

(b) A license that is issued under this division shall remain valid until the expiration date unless suspended or revoked in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

(c) A license that is issued under this division may be renewed only by submitting a completed application and paying the required fee as provided for in this division.

(d) All applications for renewal of a license that is issued under this division shall be filed before November 1st of each year.

laws.title: Suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal
laws.content:

Secs. 41-5-33—41-5-40. Reserved.

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Copy of article to be posted in licensed place of business
laws.content:
Every licensee under this article shall post, in a conspicuous place in such person’s place of business, a copy of this article, which shall be furnished by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-5; Code 1984, § 49-6-2)

laws.title: Minimum size of premises; curb cuts and surfacing; permanent building required; separation from adjoining property
laws.content:
(a) No license shall be issued to operate as a used motor vehicle dealer unless the premises to be used shall have a minimum of 30 feet frontage on a street and contain a minimum of at least 2,400 square feet of space so as to properly display at least 12 vehicles. The premises must have proper curb cuts for entrance and exits and shall be surfaced with concrete, asphalt, crushed stone or other approved hard topping surface. A suitable building of a permanent nature shall be erected on the premises before a license is issued. The property shall be separated from all adjoining property by a masonry wall that is not less than five feet and more than eight feet in height.

(b) For the purpose of this section, the term "a building of a permanent nature" means a building of at least 200 square feet, constructed of wood, masonry or other approved building material and set on proper foundation, provided, that frame and all metal buildings less than 200 square feet may be erected as provided for in the Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, *Building Code*.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-10; Code 1984, § 49-6-14; Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Records and titles to be kept
laws.content:
(a) Every person licensed as a used motor vehicle dealer shall keep, at the place of business named in such license, a book, substantially bound and in a size not less than 14 inches in length and eight inches in breadth, in which shall be written in ink, in the English language, at the time of purchase, the complete description of the used vehicle purchased or taken in trade, including the title number, serial number, motor or vehicle number, year, make, body style and color; also, the name, address, age and description of the seller. At the time of sale of a motor vehicle, a corresponding entry shall be made in this book as to the date and the name and address of the purchaser.

(b) When vehicles are purchased or taken in trade, in addition to the keeping of the above-described book, the titles for these motor vehicles, properly assigned to the licensee, must be obtained at the time of purchase and shall be kept at the licensed place of business until such time as these vehicles have been sold or some other disposition made of them.

(c) Such books and titles at all times shall be open for the inspection of any member of the Police Department or the Director or investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(d) All entries in this book shall be made consecutively each business day. No entry in such book shall be erased, obliterated, destroyed or defaced, or any pages of the book removed.

(e) No licensed used motor vehicle dealer shall store, display or allow to be stored or displayed any vehicle upon the premises of such licensee unless such licensee has obtained proper title for such vehicle and proper entry is made in such licensee’s record book.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-11; Code 1984, § 49-6-15)

**Sec. 41-6-23. Exhibition of vehicles to police.**

Every licensed used motor vehicle dealer shall exhibit, on demand, all vehicles bought or received in such dealer’s possession for proper inspection to any officers of the Police Department, or the Director or any investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-12; Code 1984, § 49-6-16)

**Sec. 41-6-24. Use of streets, sidewalks, other parts of public highways, and non-designated property prohibited.**

No licensed used motor vehicle dealer shall make use of any street, sidewalk, or other parts of a public highway, or any other property not designated in such dealer’s license for the storing or displaying of vehicles.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-13; Code 1984, § 49-6-17)

**Sec. 41-6-25. Recording surveillance system required.**

(a) Every used motor vehicle dealer, as a condition of being licensed under this article to operate its business, shall have a video surveillance system installed on its premises where any used vehicle is purchased or taken in trade. Such used motor vehicle dealer shall:

(1) Maintain the video surveillance system in good working condition and ensure that such system records persons purchasing or trading used motor vehicles;

(2) Make available, upon request, digital or video recordings from the surveillance system to the Police Department for review during regular business hours; and

laws.content:
(a) A used vehicle parts business shall be carried on, maintained or conducted entirely inside an enclosed building or on premises entirely enclosed, except gates or doors for ingress or egress, by a masonry wall or a wooden fence, or a metal faced fence or a woven wire fence, at least eight feet in height, and constructed according to the requirements of Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, Building Code, Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, and other applicable provisions of this Code, provided, that on any part of any such premises along a public highway or street, any fence facing such highway or street shall only be constructed of solid masonry, solid wood or faced with solid metal.

(b) Where, owing to special conditions, the requirements for solid fences along highways and streets will result in unnecessary hardship or involve practical difficulties, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department or the Board of Zoning Appeals may vary or modify, in specific cases, the application thereof, imposing such conditions or limitations, which

the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department or Board of Zoning Appeals finds necessary to promote the public health, safety, and general welfare.

laws.title: Conditions of premises generally
laws.content:
(a) All walls or fences of a used vehicle parts business shall be maintained in accordance with Chapter 8, Article XV, of this Code, Property Maintenance Code, in a neat, substantial condition and the exterior thereof, except those of woven wire, shall be painted, provided, that as to such fences along public highways or streets, the exterior thereof shall be painted at least once every two years. The supporting uprights of all fences shall be placed on the inside thereof.

(b) No vehicle parts or other material of a used vehicle parts business shall be permitted to lean on or touch any such wall or fence, to be in front of or attached to or suspended on any such wall or fence or on the building thereof, to be piled, along any street or highway, within two feet from the base of the wall or fence nor in excess of the enclosing wall or fence within ten feet thereof, and in no case to be piled in a manner likely to endanger a person using any highway or street, provided, that this subsection shall not prohibit the erection or maintenance of bins or shelving not to exceed the height of the fence or wall, which are not attached to or affixed to such fence or wall, and at least five feet clearance is maintained in front of such bin or shelving.

(c) The material located in or on the premises of a used vehicle parts business shall be so arranged that reasonable inspection or access to all parts of the premises can be made by law enforcement officers.

laws.title: Suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal

laws.title: Enclosed building or masonry wall required
laws.content:

(1) Entirely inside an enclosed building; or

(2) On premises entirely enclosed, except gates or doors for ingress or egress, by a masonry wall constructed according to the requirements of Chapter 8, Article II, of this Code, Building Code, Chapter 50 of this Code, Zoning, and other applicable provisions of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-24; Code 1984, § 49-6-76; Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Condition of premises generally
laws.content:
(a) All masonry walls of an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall be maintained in accordance with Chapter 8, Article XV, of this Code, Property Maintenance Code, and the exterior thereof shall be painted, provided, that, as to such fences along public highways or streets, the exterior thereof shall be painted at least once every two years. The supporting uprights of all fences shall be placed on the inside thereof.

(b) No motor vehicle parts or other material of an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall be permitted to lean on or touch any such wall, to be in front of or attached to or suspended on any such wall or on the building thereof, or to be piled along any street or highway within two feet from the base of the wall or higher than the top of the enclosing wall and in no case to be piled in a manner likely to endanger a person using any such highway or street, provided, that this subsection shall not prohibit the erection or maintenance of bins or shelving not to exceed the height of the wall, which are not attached to or affixed to such wall and at least five feet clearance is maintained in front of such bin or shelving.

*Cross reference—Traffic and vehicles, Ch. 46.

(c) The material located in or on the premises of an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall be so arranged that reasonable inspection or access to all portions of the premises can be made by law enforcement officers.

(d) An automobile dismantling or wrecking business shall maintain the conditions of its premises so as to avoid the imposition of artificial illumination, dirt, dust, litter, mud, noise, odors, vermin, vibration, water runoff, and other nuisances upon adjacent properties or rights-of-way.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-24; Code 1984, § 49-6-77; Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Records to be kept
laws.content:
(a) Every person licensed as an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall keep, at the place of business named in such license, a book, substantially bound and in size not less than 14 inches in length and eight inches in breadth, in which shall be written in ink, in the English language, at the time of purchase, the complete description of the used vehicle purchased, including the title number, serial number, motor or vehicle number, year, make, body style and color, and the name, address, age and description of the seller. A corresponding entry shall be made in this book of dates when each vehicle was dismantled or wrecked.

(b) Licensees having a used car business included in combination with such license shall enter in this book, at time of sale, the date, name and address of the purchaser, as well as entering all used vehicles taken in trade on these transactions. Each licensee shall also keep a substantially bound book, in which shall be written, in ink, in the English language, at the time of purchase, the complete description of the used vehicle parts purchased, including any identifying marks or numbers contained thereon, and the date, name, address, age and personal description of the person from whom such purchases were made. At the time of sale, a corresponding entry shall be made containing like information as to the purchaser of such used vehicle parts, including those sold from dismantled or wrecked vehicles.

(c) When vehicles are purchased or taken in trade, in addition to the keeping of the above-described books, the titles for these vehicles properly assigned to the license must be obtained at the time of purchase and shall be kept at the licensed place of business until such time as these vehicles have been dismantled or wrecked; at which time the Michigan Secretary of State will pick up and cancel such titles; provided, that if the licensee is licensed in combination to do used vehicle business, then the titles will be kept until such vehicles are sold or some other disposition is made of them.

(d) Such books and titles at all times shall be open for the inspection of any member of the Police Department, or the Director or any investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(e) All entries in these books shall be made consecutively each business day. No entry in such books shall be erased, obliterated, destroyed or defaced, or any pages of the book removed.

(f) No person shall store, display or allow to be stored or displayed any motor vehicles or used vehicle parts upon the premises, unless such person has obtained proper title and ownership for such motor vehicles or used vehicle parts, and proper entry is made in such person’s record books.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-25; Code 1984, § 49-6-78)

laws.title: Exhibition of vehicles and parts to police
laws.content:
Every licensee as an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall exhibit, on demand, all motor vehicles and used vehicle parts bought or received in such licensee’s possession for proper inspection to any officers of the Police Department, or the Director or any investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(Code 1964, § 55-3-26; Code 1984, § 49-6-79)

laws.title: Use of streets, sidewalks, other parts of public highways, and non-designated property prohibited
laws.content:
No licensee as an automobile dismantling and wrecking yard shall make use of any street, sidewalk, or other parts of a public highway, or any other property not designated in such license for the storing or displaying of vehicles, used vehicle parts, or any other commodities.

laws.title: Loitering by minors prohibited

laws.title: Application; information required
laws.content:
(a) An application for a license under this subdivision shall be made on a form that is provided by the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center. The application shall be considered completed when the appropriate person has signed and dated the application in the presence of a notary public, has paid the required license fee, and has provided the information that is required on the form, including:

(1) Where the applicant is an individual:

a. The applicant’s full legal name and any other name used by the applicant during the preceding five years;

b. The applicant’s current mailing address and e-mail address; and

c. Written proof of age in the form of a driver’s license, or a picture identification document containing the applicant’s date of birth issued by a governmental agency, or a copy of a birth certificate accompanied by a picture identification document issued by a governmental agency;

(2) Where the applicant is a partnership:

a. The legal name and any other name used by the partners during the preceding five years; and

b. The current mailing address and e-mail address for the business;

(3) Where the applicant conducts business under a trade or assumed name:

a. The complete and full trade or assumed name;

b. The county where and date that the trade or assumed name was filed;

c. The name of the person doing business under such trade or assumed name, the manager, and other person in charge; and

d. The current mailing address and e-mail address for the business;

(4) Where the applicant is a corporation:

a. The full and accurate corporate name;

b. The state and date of incorporation;

c. The full names and addresses of officers, directors, managers, and other persons with authority to bind the corporation; and

d. The current mailing address and e-mail address for the business;

(5) The name, business address, and telephone number of the business;

(6) The name and business address of the statutory agent, or other agent, who is authorized to receive service of process; and

(7) Information on any convictions of a crime by any of the persons having an interest in the business.

(b) Any information provided in accordance with Subsection (a) of this section shall be supplemented in writing and sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center within

**Sec. 41-6-123. Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee.**

Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

laws.title: Fingerprinting of customers
laws.content:
(a) At the time any used goods dealer shall receive any article of personal property, or other valuable thing, or shall acquire or purchase any article of personal property, or other valuable thing, except new articles, wares, or merchandise purchased at wholesale from manufacturers, wholesale distributors or jobbers for retail sales to customers, except also motor vehicles, old rags, waste paper, books, magazines, tapestries, antiques and household furniture, the dealer shall take in duplicate the legible imprint of the right thumb of the person from whom such property was received, or if that is not possible, of the left thumb or some other finger of such person. Such fingerprint shall be taken under such rules and regulations as prescribed by the Commissioner of the State Police. One copy shall be forwarded within 48 hours to the Chief of Police, together with a statement of the nature of the property received. The second copy shall be forwarded within 48 hours, together with a statement of the nature of the property received, to the Commissioner of the State Police in East Lansing.

(b) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to apply to any used goods dealer purchasing scrap iron and metal, except scrapped motor vehicles not purchased from a licensed secondhand or junk dealer.

**Sec. 41-7-10. Purchase, receipt, or holding of iron, brass, and other metals.**

No used goods dealer shall purchase, receive or hold for scrap metal value any iron, brass, copper, tin, zinc, aluminum or other metal products or any article composed wholly or in part of any metal without obtaining a written statement, in the English language, containing a correct description thereof, signed by the party from whom the same is purchased or received, with their state driver’s license number or state police identification card number, and setting forth the time when such articles were received by such persons and from whom, and declaring that they were not obtained unlawfully or by theft. The burden of proving ownership and the right of transfer of any such articles mentioned in this section shall be assumed and maintained by the licensee under this article.

No used goods dealer shall sell or remove from his place of business any used goods sold to the dealer as provided in this article until the same shall have been in his possession at least 15 days.

(Code 1964, § 55-1-10; Code 1984, § 49-4-7)

Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to apply on exchanges of merchandise where such merchandise is accepted in full or part payment for new merchandise and is not resold from the premises to the general public.

(Code 1964, § 55-1-12; Code 1984, § 49-4-10)

Every used goods dealer shall post, in a conspicuous place in his place of business, a copy of this article, which shall be furnished by the Police Department.

laws.title: Conditions of premises generally
laws.content:
(a) All walls or fences of a used tire sales and service business, scrap tire storage business, or a scrap tire processing and recycling business shall be maintained in accordance with Chapter 8, Article XV, of this Code, Property Maintenance Code, and the exterior thereof, shall be painted, provided, that, as to such fences along public highways or streets, the exterior thereof shall be painted at least once every two years. The supporting uprights of all fences shall be placed on the inside thereof.

(b) No used tires or other material of a used tire sales and service business shall be permitted to lean on or touch any such wall or fence, to be in front of or attached to or suspended on any such wall or fence or on the building thereof, to be piled along any street or highway within two feet from the base of the wall or fence or in excess of the enclosing wall or fence within ten feet thereof, and in no case to be piled in a manner likely to endanger a person using any highway or street, provided, that this subsection shall not prohibit the erection or maintenance of bins or shelving not to exceed the height

(c) The material located in or on the premises of a used tire sales and service business shall be so arranged that reasonable inspection or access to all portions of the premises can be made by law enforcement officers.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Pledges, pawns, and loans prohibited
laws.content:
A used tire sales and service dealer, scrap tire storage dealer, or scrap tire processing and recycling dealer shall not receive, in the course of business, any used or scrap tires by way of a pledge or pawn, or shall loan or advance any sum of money on the security of such tires.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Records to be kept
laws.content:
(a) Every person operating a used tire sales and service business shall keep, at the place of business named in such license, a substantially bound book in which shall be written in ink, in the English language, at the time of purchase, the complete description of the used tire sales and service purchased, including any identifying marks or numbers contained thereon, and the date, name, address, age and personal description of the person from whom such purchases were made. At the time of sale, a corresponding entry shall be made containing like information as to the purchaser of such used tire sales and service.

(b) Such books at all times shall be open to the inspection of any member of the Police Department, or the Director or any investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(c) All entries in this book shall be made consecutively each business day. No entry in such book shall be erased, obliterated, destroyed or defaced, or any pages of the book removed.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Exhibition of parts to police
laws.content:
Every used tire sales and service business shall, on demand, exhibit all used tire sales and service bought or received in the possession of the business for proper inspection to any officer of the Police Department, or

the Director or any investigators of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Use of streets, sidewalks, other parts of public highways, and non-designated property prohibited
laws.content:

(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Business transactions prohibited during certain hours
laws.content:
A used tire sales and service dealer, a scrap tire storage dealer, and a scrap tire processing and recycling dealer shall not purchase or receive items by sale, barter, exchange, or otherwise from any person between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Loitering by minors prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any minor to loiter about the premises of any used tires sales and service dealer, scrap tire storage dealer, or scrap tire processing and recycling business.  
(Ord. No. 2023-8, § 1, eff. 3-3-2023)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Chapter 3 of this Code, Administrative Hearings and Enforcement, and Administrative Appeals, any person, or anyone acting on behalf of said person, who admits responsibility, or is found to be responsible, through a blight violation determination, for violation of any provision of this chapter shall be subject to a civil fine as provided for in Division 2 of this article, and to removal costs as provided for in Division 3 of this article.

(b) In the case of a firm or a partnership, the civil fine may be imposed upon the partners or members thereof, and in the case of a corporation, the civil fine may be imposed upon the officers thereof.

(c) Where the blight violation is issued and an admission of responsibility is made for the violation at the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau:

(1) A civil fine that is paid before the administrative hearing date shall be reduced by ten percent;

(2) A civil fine that is paid after the administrative hearing date shall be increased by ten percent;

(3) A civil fine that is paid on the administrative hearing date shall be neither reduced nor increased.

(d) Each day that a violation continues shall constitute a separate violation. The imposition of a fine under this chapter shall not be construed to excuse or to permit the continuation of any violation and, upon a blight violation determination, the violator may be subject to a civil fine for each day the violation continues. The determination as to whether an act or a failure to act is a continuing violation is within the discretion of the hearings officer.

(Code 1984, § 22-1-4; Ord. No. 15-02, § 1(22-1-4), eff. 9-27-2002; Ord. No. 35-04, § 1(22-1-4), eff. 12-1-2004)

laws.title: Civil fines for violation of Sections 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 42-2-50, 42-2-97(a) and 42-2-105 of this Code; cost of removal incurred by City
laws.content:
(a) A person who violates Section 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 23-2-50, 42-2-97(a) or 42-2-105 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $100.00 for the first offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(b) A person who violates Section 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 42-2-50, 42-2-97(a) or 42-2-105 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $300.00 for the second offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(c) A person who violates Section 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 42-2-50, 42-2-97(a) or 42-2-105 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $500.00 for the third offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(d) A person who violates Section 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 42-2-50, 42-2-97(a) or 42-2-105 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $1,000.00 for the fourth or subsequent offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(e) Each day on which any violation of Section 42-2-27, 42-2-46, 42-2-48, 42-2-49, 42-2-50, 42-2-97(a) or 42-2-105 of this Code continues shall constitute a separate violation. The imposition of a fine under this chapter shall not be construed to excuse or to permit the continuation of any violation and, upon a blight violation determination, the violator may be subject to a civil fine for each day the violation continues. The determination as to whether an act or a failure to act is a continuing violation is within the discretion of the hearings officer.

(a) A person who violates Section 42-2-21, 42-2-22, 42-2-23, 42-2-26(b), 42-2-47, 42-2-53, 42-2-54, 42-2-80, or 42-2-101 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $200.00 for the first offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(b) A person who violates Section 42-2-21, 42-2-22, 42-2-23, 42-2-26(b), 42-2-47, 42-2-53, 42-2-54, 42-2-80, or 42-2-101 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $ 300.00 for the second offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(c) A person who violates Section 42-2-21, 42-2-22, 42-2-23, 42-2-26(b), 42-2-47, 42-2-53, 42-2-54, 42-2-80, or 42-2-101 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $500.00 for the third offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(d) A person who violates Section 42-2-21, 42-2-22, 42-2-23, 42-2-26(b), 42-2-47, 42-2-53, 42-2-54, 42-2-80, or 42-2-101 of this Code is responsible for a blight violation and is subject to a civil fine of $ 1,000.00 for the fourth or subsequent offense and, in accordance with Section 42-1-41 of this Code, is responsible for the cost of removal by the City.

(e) Each day on which any violation of Section 42-2-21, 42-2-22, 42-2-23, 42-2-26(b), 42-2-47, 42-2-53, 42-2-54, 42-2-80, or 42-2-101 of this Code continues shall constitute a separate violation. The imposition of a fine under this section shall not be construed to excuse or to permit the continuation of any violation and, upon a blight violation determination, the violator may be subject to a civil fine for each day the violation continues. The determination as to whether an act or a failure to act is a continuing violation is within the discretion of the hearings officer.

Costs and fees for removing solid, medical or hazardous waste
laws.content:
In addition to any other penalty or sanction provided for in this chapter, or by any other applicable state or federal law, a violator shall pay the following, as applicable:

(1) The cost of removing all solid waste, medical waste, or hazardous waste which is the subject of the violation and the cost of damage to any land, water, wildlife, vegetation, or other natural resource, or to any facility which is damaged by the violation of this chapter. The United States Environmental Protection Agency’s Illegal Dumping Economic Assessment—Cost Estimating Model or the actual costs incurred by the Department of Public Works, or other City department, shall be considered sufficient proof of the cost to the City. Costs collected under this section shall be used to reimburse the Department of Public Works or other appropriate department for the cost of removing said solid waste, medical waste, or hazardous waste; and

(2) The reasonable fees that result from impoundment and storage under Section 42-1-42 of this Code, which are calculated as beginning on the date of impoundment. Fees collected under this section shall be disbursed to the Police Department, or to other appropriate departments that impounded the vehicle involved in the violation of this chapter.

(Code 1984, § 22-1-31; Ord. No. 15-02, § 1(22-1-31), eff. 9-27-2002; Ord. No. 06-03, § 1(22-1-31), eff. 4-9-2003; Ord. No. 35-04, § 1(22-1-31), eff. 12-1-2004)

laws.title: Impoundment and procedure for release of a vehicle; forfeiture of bond
laws.content:
(a) Impoundment and procedure for release of a vehicle. A police officer may impound a vehicle that is operated in the commission of a violation of this chapter. Upon impoundment, the vehicle is subject to a lien, subordinate to a prior lien of record, in the amount of any fine, costs, and damages that the violator may be ordered to pay under this chapter. The person who is issued the blight violation, or a person with an ownership interest in the vehicle, may obtain release of the vehicle by taking one of the following actions:

(1) Appearing at the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau, admitting responsibility, and pay all fines, costs and fees; or

(2) Admitting responsibility with explanation, or denying responsibility for the violation at the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau, and providing a copy of a certified bond in the amount of $1,500.00; or

(3) Where there is a blight violation determination by the Blight Administrative Hearings Bureau that the alleged violator is not responsible for the violation, the vehicle shall be released, and the administrative hearings officer shall assess, against the City, costs payable to the person who sustained any damage to the vehicle directly resulting from its impoundment.

(b) Forfeiture of bond. Where a blight violation determination regarding this chapter is made and the violator fails to pay any fine, costs or damages, or any installment

laws.content:
