(b) A maximum of one secondary street sign shall be placed at only one identified intersection in the area significant to the honoree’s historical residence or the location of the honoree’s historical contribution. If a secondary street sign is assigned to the same intersection as another secondary street sign, the secondary street sign that was assigned earlier may be subject to removal for the purpose of installing the secondary street sign that was assigned more recently pursuant to Section 43-3-44(d) of this Code.

(Ord. No. 2019-44, § 1, eff. 12-23-2019)

laws.title: Maintenance of secondary street signs

A missing or damaged secondary street sign shall be replaced by the Department of Public Works within 45 days from receipt of payment for the cost of replacement from the petitioner or City Council member who requested the secondary street sign.

laws.title: Limit on quantity of secondary street signs assigned per year

No more than five secondary street signs may be assigned by the City Council, whether through petition or City Council initiative, pursuant to this division, each calendar year.

laws.title: Official petition form required

(c) No form other than that referenced in Subsection (a) of this section shall be accepted as a valid petition for the assignment of a secondary street sign.

laws.title: Duties of the Legislative Policy Division to prepare report regarding assignment of secondary street sign through City Council initiative
laws.content:
(a) Between the dates of January 1st and April 30th of the calendar year immediately following the calendar year in which the request for a secondary street sign was forwarded to the Legislative Policy Division, but after submission of the report referenced in Section 43-3-62(c) of this Code, the Legislative Policy Division shall review all documentation submitted by the City Council member requesting the secondary street sign, and prepare and submit a report of its findings as to whether the proposed secondary street sign does or does not meet the following criteria:

(1) The proposed honoree positively reflects or exemplifies the cultural, social, economic, or political history of the City, state, nation, or world;

(2) The proposed honoree was a resident of the City for a cumulative time of not less than ten years;

(3) The proposed honoree either has been deceased for a period of not less than five years, or is otherwise eligible for an exception to such requirement pursuant to Section 43-3-41(c)(3) of this Code; and

(4) The proposed location of the secondary street sign bears a clear association with a site, building, structure, or event directly related to the proposed honoree.

(b) Upon finding that all of the criteria listed in Subsection (a) of this section are met, the Legislative Policy Division shall issue to the City Council a recommendation in favor of the proposed secondary street sign, and submit a resolution for consideration by the City Council that includes:

(2) The appropriateness of the location where the secondary street sign is proposed to be installed; and

(3) The requirement that the cost of designing, producing, and erecting the sign shall be paid, in advance, to the street fund by the City Council member requesting the secondary street sign.

(c) If the Legislative Policy Division determines that any of the criteria listed in Subsection (a) of this section are not met, its report to the City Council shall so indicate.

laws.title: Duties of the Department of Public Works regarding assignment of secondary street sign through City Council initiative

(2) The payment shall be deposited into the street fund.

(b) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Department of Public Works shall establish, subject to the approval of the City Council through adoption of a resolution, the amount of the installation fee described in Subsection (a)(1) of this section.

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Control of use of City streets, alleys, parks, and public and private rights-of-way for stringing and removal of wires, setting of poles, and location of underground conduits and cables; permit from Public Lighting Department for
laws.content:
(a) The Public Lighting Department shall control the use of the City’s streets, alleys, parks, and public and private rights-of-way for the stringing and removal of overhead wires, setting of poles, the location of underground conduits and cables to avoid conflict with street lighting, traffic signals, police, and fire and other wire communications installations in accordance with this article.

(b) Before any wires, cables or support wires shall be strung from any pole, tower or other structure, and before any pole is removed or installed in any street, alley, easement or private or public place in the City, and before the building destruction or removal of under-

ground conduits and/or cables may be effectuated, a permit authorizing such work shall first be obtained from the Public Lighting Department. A quarterly fee will be charged, based on actual time, material, transportation and applicable overhead charges for inspections and consultations required to carry out provisions of this article for such a permit. The Police Department is directed to promptly issue a misdemeanor violation against any person found stringing wires without a permit.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-1; Code 1984, § 42-1-1)

laws.title: Permit from Department of Public Works to erect poles and string wires—Required
laws.content:
No person shall erect any pole or train any wire for telephone, telegraph, electric lighting or other service lines above or below ground, or build any conduits in any street, alley, highway, or in any private right-of-way unless the same is authorized by a permit from the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-2; Code 1984, § 42-1-2)

laws.title: Same—Application; authority of Department of Public Works to grant permits
laws.content:
Any person may apply to and receive a permit from the Department of Public Works to lay conduits, erect poles, and place thereon or therein wires or other conductors for the purpose of furnishing telephone, telegraph and electric lighting, or other service wires to any person desiring the same within the district to be designated in the application to be made for such permit. The Department of Public Works is hereby authorized to issue such permits for the laying of conduits, erection of poles, and placing of wires therein or thereon in the streets, alleys or other public or private places in the City, subject to the conditions and restrictions imposed by this Code.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-3; Code 1984, § 42-1-3)

laws.title: Same—Rights to cease on order of Council
laws.content:
All rights acquired under any permit issued pursuant to Sections 43-4-3 and 43-4-4 of this Code shall cease whenever the City Council shall so direct. All poles, conduits, and wires shall thereupon be removed at the expense of the person erecting, building, or controlling the same.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-4; Code 1984, § 42-1-4)

laws.title: Manner of setting poles
laws.content:
All poles erected under the permit required by Section 43-4-3 of this Code shall be firmly set in the ground and in streets next to and within the curbline so as to cause the least obstruction, in such manner and of such uniform height, size, color, and material as shall be approved by the Public Lighting Department and the Department of Public Works. The number of cross-arms, minimum distance of the same from the surface of the street, the proximity of different wires to each other, their arrangement, including guy wires, and the like, shall be approved by the Public Lighting Department and the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-5; Code 1984, § 42-1-5)

laws.title: Public Lighting Department may require wires to be insulated; method of laying conduits generally
laws.content:
All operating and conducting mains and wires in the City shall be thoroughly and securely insulated with a material of sufficient thickness and durability to be not easily abraded or injured mechanically and impervious to water where deemed necessary by the Public Lighting Department. All conduits laid in streets, avenues, and other highways shall be in a line parallel with the curbline thereof at such distance from the curbline, or where the curbline should be, as designated by the Department of Public Works and to a depth as designated by the Department of Public Works. All conduits laid in private rights-of-way shall be located and placed at depths to be designated by the Department of Public Works. All service wires shall be connected only with a main laid in a conduit in the alley or at the side of the street nearest to the building into which it is desired to conduct such service wires.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-6; Code 1984, § 42-1-6)

laws.title: Supervision over construction of wires
laws.content:
The Public Lighting Department shall have the supervision of the construction of all lines of wire erected pursuant to this article. In the stringing of lines or wire or the laying of any conduits, as provided in this article, the Public Lighting Department shall prescribe and determine the public and/or private rights-of-way where it shall be lawful to erect or construct lines of wires above the ground or lay conduits in the ground.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-7; Code 1984, § 42-1-7)

**Sec. 43-4-9. Public Lighting Department may require wires to be put in conduits.**

Whenever the Public Lighting Department deems it to be in the public interest, the Department may require, as a condition to the issuing of any permit under this article, that the wires shall be laid in conduits and, if any wires shall be strung on poles along any highway and conduits shall afterwards be laid therein, the Department may require the wires so strung upon poles to be taken down and in their stead suitable wires put in the conduits, and, upon any refusal to do so, may remove the same. The Public Lighting Department may prescribe the terms and conditions upon which conduits shall be used for such purpose.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-8; Code 1984, § 42-1-8)

**Sec. 43-4-10. Removal of interfering wires.**

When any wires erected under any permit issued pursuant to Sections 43-4-3 and 43-4-4 of this Code shall interfere with any wires of the Public Lighting Department or other public service wires, the Public Lighting Department may direct the removal of the same or such alterations in relation thereto as will obviate or prevent such interference.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-9; Code 1984, § 42-1-9)

**Sec. 43-4-11. Poles to be used to maximum capacity.**

(a) The Public Lighting Department may require that all poles shall be used to their maximum capacity and the lines thereon so distributed as to obtain such results. The Public Lighting Department may require any person occupying a certain right-of-way with lines of insufficient capacity to accommodate the requirements of that locality to replace such poles with such other poles as may be approved by the Public Lighting Department.

(b) When any person has erected a pole on any portion of any street or alley, the pole shall be subject to the condition that the Public Lighting Department may authorize other persons to whom permits may be granted to use such pole upon such terms and conditions as the Public Lighting Department may direct.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-10; Code 1984, § 42-1-10)

**Sec. 43-4-12. Permittees not to damage streets, alleys, park or public squares, or shade trees, or to disturb or interfere with gas or water pipes, sewers, or wires or conduits; duty to indemnify City for damages.**

The person to whom the permit required by Section 43-4-3 of this Code is issued shall not damage any street, alley, park or public square, or any shade trees, or disturb or interfere with any water or gas pipes or with any public or private sewer laid or constructed by any authorized person or the wires and conduits of any telephone, telecommunications, telegraph, electric lighting, gas supply or of the Police Department or the Fire Department or Public Lighting Department and shall fully indemnify, and hold harmless, the City from all claims or damages for which the City might be made or become liable to pay by reason of the construction, maintaining, repairing, or operating of such poles, conduits, wires or other conductors or any apparatus connected therewith or otherwise arising from the use or the possession of the rights and privileges granted or from any neglect on the part of such person or such person’s employees to comply with any of the provisions of this Code and shall especially indemnify the City against and assume all liabilities and damages which may arise, come or occur to the City from any injury to persons or property from the doing of any work mentioned in this section, or the neglect of any person or such person’s employees to comply with any provisions of this Code relative to the use of streets or other public places, especially as to the putting up of lights or barriers at or around excavations. The acceptance by the person of such permit shall be an agreement to pay to the City any sum of money for which the City may become liable from or by reason of such injury.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-11; Code 1984, § 42-1-11)

**Sec. 43-4-13. Openings and excavations in streets.**

(a) At least 24 hours before opening or excavating in any street, alley or any public space for any purpose, the permittee under Section 43-4-3 of this Code shall notify, in writing, the Department of Public Works of such desire, stating the place where and the reason such opening is to be made, and obtain a permit for such opening or excavation from the Department of Public Works. In the opening and refilling of all openings and excavations, the relaying of the pavement and other work necessary to the complete restoration of the street, pavement, sidewalks, or grounds to equally good condition as when disturbed, the permittee or such permittee’s servants or employees shall be under the supervision of the Department of Public Works, or its agents, and shall promptly comply with any order of the Department of Public Works, or its agents, or the City Council in reference thereto, nor shall any street, avenue, or public place be allowed to remain open or encumbered for a longer period than shall be necessary to execute the work for

(b) The soil removed during such excavation shall be restored and the pavement relaid by the person making such excavation in as good a condition as before the making of such excavation, and shall be maintained in as good a condition as the surrounding pavement until the street or alley in each case is repaved. No excavation in any street, alley or public place shall be allowed to remain open, or such street, alley or public place to be encumbered, for a longer period than it shall be necessary to execute the work for which the same is made.

(c) The cost of restoring the soil or other cost arising from such excavations and the relaying of the pavement and the repairs thereto caused by the opening of any such street, alley, or public place shall be at the expense of the person making such excavation, and such work shall be done under the supervision of the Department of Public Works. The expense of such supervision shall be paid by the person making such excavation on presentation of bills certified by the Department of Public Works, and any expense to which the City shall be put from the neglect of such person or such person’s employees in the doing of any work, or the doing of the same in any unworkmanlike manner, or the digging of ditches or holes and erection of poles, or restoring the soil or any excavation, or relaying or replacing of any pavement shall be paid in like manner by such person on presentation of the bill of costs certified by the Department of Public Works. It shall be the duty of the person making such excavations or doing such other work in each instance to promptly pay all bills for labor and material, supervision, and the like, incurred by the Department of Public Works in relaying and restoring any pavement or surface disturbed by such person, and where such bills properly certified by the Department of Public Works remain unpaid for 30 days after the presentation to such person, it shall be the duty of the Department of Public Works to pay over to the credit of the proper fund the amount of any bills so remaining unpaid from the guarantee money deposited by such person with the Department of Public Works, and on refusal, neglect, or failure by such person to make such guarantee money good to its full extent, the Department of Public Works shall process any unpaid bill as an account receivable in accordance with Chapter 17, Article VI, of this Code, Uniform Procedure for Accounts Receivable.

laws.title: Bond required of persons constructing lines of wires, or laying of conduits
laws.content:
No permit authorized by this article shall become operative and authorize the construction of any line of wires above ground or the laying of any conduits until the person to whom the same may be granted shall have filed with the Office of Chief Financial Officer a satisfactory bond, to be approved by the Corporation Counsel, in the sum of $25,000.00, conditioned that the person to whom such permit is granted will faithfully comply with and perform the terms and conditions of this article and other provisions of this Code relating to the construction of such wires, and such person shall also have deposited and shall keep on deposit with the City Treasurer the sum of $200.00 to cover the expense of replacing of the soil in making the repairs to pavements required to be relaid by such person under the provisions of this article and as a guarantee for the prompt payment of any bills for such work presented by the Department of Public Works. Such deposit shall be maintained in the minimum amount of $200.00, and on failure to keep the same in such minimum amount, the permit shall become void.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-13; Code 1984, § 42-1-13)

laws.title: Opening and tampering with manholes, vaults, and junction boxes of public lighting system, and placing of wires in conduits or on poles of public lighting system prohibited
laws.content:
No person shall open or tamper with any manhole or any vault or junction box connected with the conduits of the public lighting system, or shall attempt to place or place any wires in such conduits or upon the poles of such system without permission in writing from the Public Lighting Department.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-15; Code 1984, § 42-1-14)

State law reference—Malicious mischief generally, MCL 750.377a et seq.

laws.title: Posting, painting, impressing or affixing placards, signs, banners, or notices to poles, boxes, lampposts, towers, wires, and appliances connected with public lighting system; kites and other obstructions; banners; presumption concerning identity of violator; enforcement
laws.content:
(a) Except as provided for in Subsection (b) of this section, no person shall post, paint, impress or in any way affix to any pole connected with the public lighting

CD43:23
§ 43-4-16

DETROIT CITY CODE

system of the City or any box, lamppost, tower, wire, or other appliance connected therewith, any placard, sign, banner, notice or announcement of any kind, or cause or allow any kite or other obstruction to become entangled with the wires or apparatus of the system.

(b) Banners may be affixed to Public Lighting Department poles in accordance with Division 4 of this article.

(c) With respect to any placard, sign, banner, notice, or announcement of any kind that violates any provision of this section, a rebuttable presumption exists that the placard, sign, banner, notice, or announcement was erected, affixed, placed or displayed at its location by, or with the consent of, the promoter of the event, offer, or service that is the subject of the placard, sign, banner, notice, or announcement.

(d) This section shall be enforced by the Police Department.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-16; Code 1984, § 42-1-15; Ord. No. 26-01, § 1(42-1-15), eff. 12-17-2001; Ord. No. 12-07, § 1(42-1-15), eff. 5-18-2007)

laws.title: Removal of poles not in use
laws.content:
All poles in the City on which no wires are strung or from which dead or unused wires are suspended shall be taken down and removed by the owners thereof on receipt of a proper notice from the Public Lighting Department. In case such notice is not complied with within 30 days from the date of its service, the Public Lighting Department shall cause such poles to be taken down and removed.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-17; Code 1984, § 42-1-16)

laws.title: Name of owner to be placed on poles
laws.content:
All persons owning or leasing poles of any kind in the City shall place upon each wood pole owned or leased by them the name of the person owning or leasing such wood pole. Such name shall be placed on each wood pole owned or leased by them at a height not lower than four feet or higher than eight feet from the ground.

(Code 1964, § 45-1-18; Code 1984, § 42-1-17)

Secs. 43-4-19—43-4-30. Reserved.

laws.title: Placing of uninsulated wires on same poles with high potential wires
laws.content:
No person shall string or place any bare grounded wire, telephone or telegraph cable, or, telephone or other signal lines on the same pole, stanchion or upright with high potential wire without separating such wires carrying high potential currents from such bare grounded wires, telegraph or telephone cables, or telephone or other signal wires by the distance prescribed by the National Electrical Safety Code issued by the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Any such person shall remove such bare wires, telephone, telegraph or other signal wires to conform to this section within 90 days from the date of serving of notice to separate such wires, given by the Public Lighting Department or its duly appointed agent. High potential wires mentioned in this section are defined as wires carrying voltages of 300 volts or over.

(Code 1964, § 45-2-1; Code 1984, § 42-2-1)

laws.title: Wires in iron pipes, or other metallic material; exposure of electrical wires without insulation
laws.content:
(a) No person shall encase, cover, or introduce any wire carrying electrical current into any iron pipe or any metallic electric conducting material affixed to any wooden pole, stanchion, or upright, which shall extend nearer than eight feet from the lowest cross-arm on such wooden pole, stanchion, or upright.

(b) It shall be unlawful to expose any electrical wire without such insulation in any manner, which shall form a connection or circuit with the earth in such manner as to be dangerous or injurious to life or health. This section shall not apply to, or prevent, the encasement of such wires in any nonconducting substance or material, such as wood, and the like.

(Code 1964, § 45-2-2; Code 1984, § 42-2-2)

laws.title: Examination of dangerous wires; notice to correct same
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of the Public Lighting Department, upon complaint of any member of the public, to examine or cause to be examined any dangerously exposed electrical wires, to notify the person owning or controlling the exposed wire of its dangerous condition, and to have the same remedied at once and made safe.

CD43:24

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-4-52

Upon the failure of such person to remedy and make safe such dangerously exposed wire, it is the duty of the Public Lighting Department to cause a complaint to be made for a breach of this section and to prosecute such person for such breach. Any refusal or neglect to remedy such dangerously exposed wire, after due and proper notice from the Public Lighting Department, shall constitute a violation of this section.

(Code 1964, § 45-2-4; Code 1984, § 42-2-3)

laws.title: Day circuits of high potential currents to be designated as such
laws.content:
All day circuits of high potential currents shall be designated by some mark or distinctive insulator upon each wire at each insulator to designate the same as such.

(Code 1964, § 45-2-5; Code 1984, § 42-2-4)

laws.title: Removal of dead wires
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of any person owning or in control of the same to remove from any building, structure, or pole all dead wires that are not in use within 30 days from notice given by the Public Lighting Department.

(Code 1964, § 45-2-6; Code 1984, § 42-2-5)

laws.title: Prohibited—Within one-half mile circle; exceptions
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to erect, maintain, or use overhead electrical supply or electrical signal wires or cables, except for street railway trolley or train, guard or span wires, and wires or cables for public lighting purposes by the Public Lighting Department or a municipal lighting authority established in accordance with the Michigan Municipal Lighting Authority Act, being MCL 123.1261 *et seq.*, in or over any street in that portion of the City within the one-half mile circle, which is defined as the land within one-half mile of the site of the Old City Hall, that is, the intersection of Woodward Avenue and Michigan Avenue.

(Code 1964, § 45-3-1; Code 1984, § 42-3-1; Ord. No. 01-14, § 1(42-3-1), eff. 4-3-2014)

laws.title: Same—On certain streets
Same—In certain alleys
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to erect, maintain, continue, or use overhead electrical supply or overhead electrical signal wires or cables, except for street railway trolley or train, guard or span wires, and wires or cables for public lighting purposes by the Public Lighting Department or a municipal lighting authority established in accordance with the Michigan Municipal Lighting Authority Act, being MCL 123.1261 et seq., in or over the alleys in that portion of the City bounded by the Detroit River, First Street to Howard Street, Howard Street to Cass Avenue, Cass Avenue to Michigan Avenue, Michigan Avenue to Park Place, Park Place to Grand River Avenue, Grand River Avenue to Bagley Avenue, Bagley Avenue to Park Boulevard, Park Boulevard to Elizabeth Street, Elizabeth Street to Woodward Avenue, Woodward Avenue to Adams Avenue, Adams Avenue to Witherell Street, Witherell Street to Madison Avenue, Madison Avenue to Randolph Street, Randolph Street to Gratiot Avenue, Gratiot Avenue to Brush Street, Brush Street to Lafayette Avenue, Lafayette Avenue to Randolph Street, Randolph Street to Congress Street, Congress Street to Randolph Street, and Randolph Street to the Detroit River.

(Code 1964, § 45-3-3; Code 1984, § 42-3-3; Ord. No. 01-14, § 1(42-3-3), eff. 4-3-2014)

laws.title: Overhead traffic signals and public lighting system wires and cable permitted
laws.content:
(a) Notwithstanding any of the provisions of this article to the contrary, it shall be lawful to erect, maintain, or use overhead electrical traffic signals, span wires, and cables in the streets of the City upon the recommendation of the Department of Public Works, and only after final approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) Notwithstanding any of the provisions of this article to the contrary, it shall be lawful for the Public Lighting Department or a municipal lighting authority established in accordance with the Michigan Municipal Lighting Authority Act, being MCL 123.1261 et seq., to erect, maintain, and use overhead electrical wires and cables for the public lighting system.

(Code 1964, § 45-3-5; Code 1984, § 42-3-4; Ord. No. 01-14, § 1(42-3-4), eff. 4-3-2014)

Secs. 43-4-55—43-4-80. Reserved.

laws.title: Policy
laws.content:
The City of Detroit will permit on its light poles only banners that promote or celebrate the City, its civic institutions, or public activities and events in the City.

CD43:26

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-4-84

The City's public lighting poles shall not be used for commercial advertising or for promoting any political or social advocacy organization or political message.  
(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
No person or entity shall install, place affix or attach a banner on any property within the City without first obtaining a permit. Public lighting poles and the public rights-of-way are owned and controlled by the City only. Permission to hang banners granted by banner permittees or entities other than City-authorized agencies will not be honored by the City.  
(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3401—3404))

laws.title: Application fee and refundable deposit
laws.content:
(a) All fees shall be used to fund the activities of the Department of Public Works and the Public Lighting Department directly related to the administration and enforcement of this article governing the placement of street banners within the City of Detroit. The application fee shall be paid at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(b) A $100.00 non-refundable application fee for all banner permit requests shall be required with the submission of the application. The non-refundable application fee shall not be waived or refunded under any circumstances.

(c) A refundable deposit for all banner permit requests shall be required upon approval of banner design and installation permit and shall be held in escrow for the duration of the application process and, where issued, the permit. A $500.00 refundable deposit shall be required for applications requesting to hang up to five banners. A $1,000.00 refundable deposit shall be required for applications requesting to hang six or more banners. The refundable deposit shall cover costs incurred by the City to remove banners that remain 72 hours after the approved display period expires, to inspect banners whenever appropriate, and to repair City light poles should damage occur. Where the expense of removal or repair exceeds the amount of deposit, the excess amount shall be collected from the person who, or entity which, the permit was issued.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3401—3404))

laws.title: Permit approval
laws.content:
(a) The number of banners to be installed and the location of each banner shall be approved by the Department of Public Works Traffic Engineering Division, the Public Lighting Department, and the City Council through adoption of a resolution. Banner permits are approved on a first-come, first-serve basis.

(b) Where an application for a permit to install banners meets the eligibility requirements of this policy and is approved by the City Council, a permit authorizing the installation of the requested banner or banners shall be issued as long as the required insurances policy, fees, and deposits have been submitted to, and accepted by, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3401—3404))

CD43:28

laws.title: Permit duration
laws.content:
(a) Business district banners to promote civic pride in a business district located in the greater downtown area and not a purely commercial enterprise may be displayed for 90 days. At the discretion of the City, the permit may be renewed or extended for an additional 180 days to a maximum of 270 days in a 12-month period, provided, that, in accordance with Section 43-4-86(a) of this Code, no other requests have been received for the light poles and subject to payment of fees for each renewal period.

(b) City banners sponsored by a City department, agency, board, commission, or authority for a City-administered program or event may be displayed for a period as determined by the Inter-departmental Banner Permit Application Review Board.

(c) Community banners to promote community identification and pride sponsored by a non-profit community based organization may be displayed for 90 days. At the discretion of the City, the permit may be renewed or extended for an additional 180 days to a maximum of 270 days in a 12-month period, provided, that, in accordance with Section 43-4-86(a) of this Code, no other requests have been received for the light poles and subject to payment of fees for each renewal period.

(d) Non-profit banners may be displayed for up to 90 days within a 12-month period with the possibility of permit renewal. At the discretion of the City, the permit may be renewed or extended for an additional 90 days to a maximum of 180 days in a 12-month period provided, that, in accordance with Section 43-4-86(a) of this Code, no other requests have been received for the light poles and subject to payment of fees for each renewal period.

(e) Permits for special event banners shall be based on the duration of the special event. Special event banners may be displayed a maximum of 30 days prior to the starting date of the event and shall be removed within 72 hours of the closing date of the event.

(f) Permits for holiday banners shall begin no earlier than November 1st and end no later than January 2nd of any given season.

(g) After expiration of a permit, or should the banner change in any way, an organization shall submit a new banner application to the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department.

(h) For all types of banners, permit duration must comply with state and county guidelines.  
(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Renewal process and fees
laws.content:
A renewal application shall be submitted a minimum of 20 calendar days prior to the expiration date of the banner permit. The renewal application form shall be submitted along with a $25.00 renewal request fee that shall be assessed for each renewal request. Renewals shall be considered on a first-come, first-serve basis, provided, that, in accordance with Section 43-4-86(a) of this Code, no other requests have been received or approved for the light poles.  
(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Banner design
laws.content:
(a) Street banners shall not exceed 30 inches in width by 94 inches in height and should be acrylic or vinyl with standard slitting, also known as "happy faces."

(b) Hardware shall be designed as not to cause damage to the light pole. The hardware shall be attached with stainless steel bands and fasteners. The banner shall be affixed to allow a minimum of 15 vertical feet clearance from the walkway surface.

(c) Commercial advertising is strictly prohibited on all banners, including telephone numbers, mailing addresses, and website addresses. Where a business sponsors the cost of the banner, or banners, for a non-profit organization and wishes to be identified, the designation of the sponsor, including all graphics and text, shall be placed at the bottom of the banner in a space no more than ten inches in height and 30 inches in width with letter size limited to four inch maximum and placed within this space. Banners with business sponsorship must include the words "sponsored by" preceding the sponsor information within the 30-inch by ten-inch space.

(d) Two banners shall be allowed on a single pole only where a double-banner design is being proposed or where both banners have the same design. Two banners unrelated in design or content shall not be allowed under any conditions.

(e) Banners may not include messages pertaining to the following:

(1) Advertising a product;

CD43:29
§ 43-4-89

DETROIT CITY CODE

(2) Adult entertainment and sexually-explicit products;

(3) Alcoholic beverages;

(4) Firearms;

(5) Political campaigns or related agendas; or

(6) Tobacco and related products.

(f) Horizontal banners, including banners that are hung across a street, are not permitted.

(g) Once the banner has been approved, no changes shall be made, including, but not limited to, text, graphics, size and the like, without the City’s written approval. Where changes are made without the City’s written approval, the City reserves the right to withdraw the approval to hang banners and recover the cost of removal from the sponsor.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Installation, maintenance, and removal
laws.content:
(a) Installation.

(1) Banner placement shall be a minimum of 120 feet or every other pole apart, whichever is greater, including banners that may exist at the time of installation. Banner installation shall be limited within the poles that may have banners to a 2,000-foot radius area of event location or within the stated organization boundaries. A permittee shall not remove existing banners of other groups under any circumstances.

(2) Every street banner must be installed and maintained so as to be safe at all times. Banners shall be displayed on the designated and approved Public Lighting Department light poles only. Banners shall not be attached to any traffic control device, on historically designated light poles, or as to obstruct the visibility of signs and signals that may be attached to other light poles or supports. Banner permits shall not be issued for poles that are not owned by the City.

(3) The permittee may hire a professional company to install and remove the banners and hardware, being the arms only and not the casting that is affixed to the pole, in accordance with the conditions of the approved permit and at no cost to the City.

(b) Maintenance. During the initial permit period and subsequent renewal period, permittees shall be responsible for inspecting banners and poles, and replacing or removing banners that are torn, defaced, or in general disrepair, including rigging.

(c) Removal.

(1) Upon expiration of a permit, all street banners covered under the permit shall be removed by the permittee within 72 hours of expiration unless a renewal is granted. Where the permittee fails to comply, the City may remove the banner or banners without notice to the permittee. In addition, where any street banner presents an immediate threat of harm to the public health, welfare or safety, the City shall summarily cause its removal. Where it is determined that a banner or banners are obstructing traffic controls, the City reserves the right to have such banner or banners removed by the permittee at no cost to the City.

(2) Where the City removes banners either because they present an immediate threat, are in disrepair or are obstructing traffic controls, or because the permit has expired, the permittee shall forfeit a portion or all of the $1,000.00 refundable deposit in order to cover the City’s costs for the removal. The remaining balance, if any, will be refunded to the permittee.

(3) Where the City removes any banner, there is no guarantee that the banners may be reclaimed by the sponsoring organization.

(4) Where the expense of removal exceeds the $1,000.00 deposit, the excess amount shall be collected from the person to whom, or entity to which, the permit was issued.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Indemnification
laws.content:
No permit shall be issued under this article unless the applicant or entity installing the street banners has on file with the City a satisfactory policy of insurance so conditioned as to insure the City, and its officers and employees, against any loss, cost, expense, injury, damage or liability incurred by reason of any personal injury or property damage sustained by any person, caused by or resulting from or which may be claimed to have been caused by or to have resulted from the installation or

CD43:30

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-5-2

maintenance of any street banner or appurtenance installed under the permit, or from any failure to install or maintain any such street banner or appurtenance in the manner required by this policy or from any dangerous or defective condition or nuisance created thereby or resulting therefrom. The City shall be named as an additional insured on the policy against any property damage or personal injury resulting from any such cause. The limit of liability upon any policy posted or maintained under this section shall not be less than $1,000,000.00.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Banner permits and other signage programs
laws.content:
Where a signage program, that is, directional, interpretive, or the like, is requested within a specific geographic area where a banner program exists, the City reserves the right to review and place limitations on either or both programs in order to reduce any potential overall negative impacts that both programs may have on the area.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Compliance
laws.content:
It is expected that permittees will make a good faith effort to comply with the requirements of this division concerning banners in the public right-of-way. Non-compliance with any provision in this division may affect the evaluation and approval of the permittee’s future banner permit applications or renewals.

(Res. of 11-30-2001 (2001 Journal of City Council, pp. 3501—3504))

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Construction and paving near and between tracks to be done in accordance with specifications; permittees responsible for maintenance of roadway and sidewalk between and near tracks; switches and other operating devices prohibited within street lines; change of street grade; permittee to save City harmless from damages, costs, and expenses
laws.content:
(a) All construction of spur tracks or side tracks, including paving, planking or placing of paving and sidewalks between the rails and 18 inches outside thereof or farther, if necessary to cover the approaches, shall be done by or in accordance with the directions of the Director of the Department of Public Works, when the permittee under this article has deposited a sufficient sum to cover the cost of the same and of installing the necessary drainage. Permittees authorized to install and maintain spur tracks shall at all times during the life of the permit pay the expense of repairing or repaving the roadway and sidewalk between the rails of the spur track or side track and for a distance of 18 inches or farther outside of the same, and for installing drainage whenever such repairs, repaving, or drainage is deemed necessary by the Director of the Department of Public Works. The Director may repair or rebuild, at the Director’s option, any spur track or side track at any time, with or without notice to the permittee, when, in the Director’s judgment, the same shall become dangerous to street traffic.

(b) No switches, frogs, or other operating devices will be permitted within the street lines, and tracks must be laid across streets at right angles or with the least possible curvature. No railroad corporation or other agency shall, by the installing of any spur track or side track, cause a change in the grade of any street where curb or pavement has been laid or the grade otherwise established by the Director of the Department of Public Works, except by permission of the City Council through adoption of a resolution. Any change of grade of a street contrary to this provision, which shall affect the relative physical condition of the street as established, shall au-

CD43:31
$\S 43-5-2$

DETROIT CITY CODE

automatically terminate all rights and privileges which the permittee may have acquired under the permit authorized by this article.

(c) Upon failure of the permittee to comply with the requirements of this article, such spur tracks or side tracks may be summarily removed and the street restored to a condition satisfactory to the Director of the Department of Public Works at the expense of the permittee.

(d) Such permittee shall indemnify and hold harmless the City from any damages, costs, and expenses arising from all or any one of the requirements in Subsections (a), (b), and (c) of this section. The failure of the Director of the Department of Public Works to give the permittee notice of such defective condition of that part of the roadway as such permittee is obligated hereunder to maintain shall not operate to defeat the right of the City to be indemnified and held harmless from any such damages, costs, and expenses.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-9; Code 1984, § 45-2-1)

laws.title: Removal of installations upon revocation or discontinuance of use of tracks
laws.content:
(a) Any person and successor permittees occupying any street, alley, or other public place in the City under the permit provided for in this article for the installation and maintenance of spur tracks or side tracks, shall remove, upon the revocation thereof, or upon the discontinuance of the use thereof, all installations of every kind, nature and description, at their own expense, under the direction of the Department of Public Works, and in accordance with the provisions of Sections 43-5-2 and 43-5-26 of this Code.

(b) Any person and successor permittees occupying any street, alley, or other public place for the purposes provided in this article, by the acceptance of such permit, expressly agrees to hold the City harmless from all damages, costs and expenses aforesaid, including the replacing of pavements, maintaining proper drainage, or any other expense which may be incurred by the City incidental to the maintenance of such spur track or side track.

(c) In the event of the repeal of this article or the rescission of any of the rights and privileges granted by this article or by any resolution of the City Council, such rights and privileges shall cease, and the grantee shall remove from the street, at such grantee’s own expense, the track laid under the authority of this article or any resolution of the City Council, and restore the roadbed equal to its condition at the time such tracks are removed.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-10; Code 1984, § 45-2-2)

laws.title: Map and survey of proposed tracks
laws.content:
(a) Any person desiring to construct side tracks or spur tracks shall cause a map and survey of the particular location of such proposed side tracks or spur tracks to be made, designating thereon the line of such side tracks or spur tracks and the lines upon which it is proposed to enter such private property, and connect with any railway. Such map and survey shall furnish complete means of identifying and ascertaining the precise position of every part of such side track or spur track, with courses and distances throughout, so that it may be determined with certainty where any portion of the same is to be located. Such map and survey shall be filed in the office of the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(b) The Director of the Department of Public Works shall examine the same, as well as the proposed location of the side track or spur track delineated thereon, and the Director of the Department of Public Works may make such alterations or changes therein as in the Director’s judgment the public interest may require, and report the same to the City Council, together with the Director’s approval or disapproval thereof. Where such map and survey is approved by resolution of the City Council, the work of constructing such spur track or side track shall be performed under the supervision and inspection of the Department of Public Works, at the cost of the permittee and in accordance with the plans submitted to and approved by the Department of Public Works. All paving or replacing of paving and sidewalks between the rails and 18 inches or farther outside thereof, where necessary to cover approaches, shall be done by the Department of Public Works when the permittee has deposited a sufficient sum to cover the cost of same and installing the necessary drainage, provided, that the kind of pavement shall be determined by the Director of the Department of Public Works. In the construction of the spur track or side track by the permittee, only "T" rails, not less than five inches in height, and sawed ties are to be used and, at all times during the life of the permit, the expense of repairing the roadways and sidewalks between the rails of such side track or spur track and for a distance of 18 inches or farther outside of same, where necessary, whenever such repairing or repaving is directed by the Director of the Department of Public

CD43:32

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-5-22

Works, shall be done by the Director of the Department of Public Works, at the expense of the permittee and after notice to the permittee from the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-11; Code 1984, § 45-2-3)

laws.title: Manner of laying rails in streets
laws.content:
The rails of side tracks and spur tracks shall be laid four feet 8½ inches apart with the upper surface of the rail flush with the surface of the street and in such manner as not to interfere with ordinary travel, and shall conform to the grade of the street as existing or as hereafter altered.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-12; Code 1984, § 45-2-4)

laws.title: Rails to be relayed at expense of permittee
laws.content:
Where it shall become necessary to relay the rails of any spur track or side track, the same shall be done at the expense of the permittee under this article.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-13; Code 1984, § 45-2-5)

laws.title: Right of City to occupy streets for building public works
laws.content:
The privileges granted by this article shall not restrict or alter the right of the City or any of its authorized departments and agencies to enter upon any street where side tracks or spur tracks are located and occupy the same in building public works for general public purposes of any kind whatsoever.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-14; Code 1984, § 45-2-6)

laws.title: Obstruction of streets
laws.content:
No person authorized to construct side tracks or spur tracks under this article shall permit any vehicle to stop or remain on the streets so as to obstruct the free and ordinary use thereon at any time.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-15; Code 1984, § 45-2-7)

laws.title: Reservation of right to amend or repeal article and rescind rights granted thereunder
laws.content:
The right to amend or repeal this article is hereby reserved, and the City Council may rescind, by resolution, the rights and privileges granted by this article or by any resolution of the City Council, and may adopt any resolution in relation to the maintenance and operation of side tracks or spur tracks as the City Council may deem necessary to protect the interest, safety, and welfare of the City and the public in relation thereto.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-16; Code 1984, § 45-2-8)

Secs. 43-5-10—43-5-20. Reserved.

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
No person shall occupy any part of any street, alley, or public place in the City for the installation, operation, or maintenance of any spur track or side track, or for the shipping or receiving freight cars over any railroad siding or spur track which crosses a public street or alley within the City without first having obtained a permit and having filed a bond and agreement as provided in this division.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-1; Code 1984, § 45-2-20)

laws.title: Issuance; fee; term; transferability
laws.content:
(a) Persons and their successors or assigns may be permitted, in the discretion of the City Council, upon application therefor, to install and maintain spur tracks or side tracks in the streets, alleys, and other public places in the City and to ship, receive, or transfer their freight cars upon such spur tracks or side tracks after having obtained a permit from the Director of the Department of Public Works for such purpose.

(b) As a condition precedent to the issuance of such permit, the permittee shall agree:

(1) To abide by and perform all of the conditions and other requirements imposed by this article or by resolution of the City Council, until such permit shall be revoked, transferred, or the spur track or side track shall be removed and the street restored to a condition satisfactory to the Director of the Department of Public Works by the permittee;

(2) To pay a fee of $25.00 in advance per year, covering the period from June 1 of one year to May 31 of the succeeding year or for any fractional part thereof for each spur track or side track crossing any street, alley or other public place, such fee to be collected by the City for each spur track or side track at each street, alley or other public place; and

(3) To file the bond and agreement required by this article, and to pay the premium thereon as long as spur tracks shall cross over public streets, alleys, or other public places.

CD43:33
§ 43-5-22

DETROIT CITY CODE

(c) Such permit shall be non-transferable, except with the express consent of the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-2; Code 1984, § 45-2-21)

laws.title: Permits for existing tracks
laws.content:
(a) Persons and their successors or assigns may be permitted, in the discretion of the City Council, to ship or receive freight cars over any existing railroad siding or spur track in the City which crosses a public street, alley or other public place, either within or without the lines of the right-of-way of any railroad, and which is not a public team track, in the judgment of the Director of the Department of Public Works, whether such spur track or side track is extended by or owned, controlled, or operated by a railroad company or other person, upon application therefor to the City Council for a permit to transfer freight cars across such street or alley or other public place. The Department of Public Works is hereby authorized, unless otherwise directed by the City Council, to issue a permit upon such application, conditioned upon the payment of an annual fee of $25.00 for each spur track or side track included in such permit, which amount shall be paid to the Department of Public Works in advance, on or before May 31st of each year, unless the permit is revoked by the Department of Public Works or the City Council for failure of the permittee to comply with the provisions of this article or other good and sufficient reason.

(b) The permittee shall also file with the Office of the Chief Financial Officer a good and sufficient surety in the amount of $5,000.00 or more that is approved by the Corporation Counsel as to form and execution. The bond shall name the City as obligee therein, be properly executed by the permittee and surety company, be conditioned on the payment by the permittee of the annual fee required, and agree to indemnify and hold the City harmless from any loss or damage, including personal injury and property damage, costs, and expense it may suffer or may be recovered against it, through accidents or otherwise from the use of such street, alley, or other public place by the permittee for the purpose provided for in Subsection (a) of this section. The permittee shall pay the premium on the bond, and liability thereunder shall continue as long as freight cars are transferred over public streets, alleys, or public places indicated on the permit, and for the period stated in this article.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-3; Code 1984, § 45-2-22)

laws.title: Revocable at will of City Council
laws.content:
Any person occupying or using any street, alley, or other public place in the City by reason of any permit issued under this article, by acceptance of such permit, expressly agrees that such permit shall be revocable, for good cause, at the will of the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-4; Code 1984, § 45-2-23)

laws.title: Disposition of receipts; record of issuance
laws.content:
Payments for permits issued under this article shall be deposited in the general fund, and a record of their issuance shall be kept by the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-5; Code 1984, § 45-2-24)

laws.title: Rights in streets, alleys, and other public places not waived by City by granting of permit; surety bond
Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
Cancellation of prior permits
laws.content:
All permits of every nature and description heretofore granted by the City or the Michigan Department of Transportation for the protection of the spur track or side track, or for the shipping or receiving freight cars upon and over any street, alley, or public place within the City inconsistent with or contrary to any of the provisions of this article are hereby revoked, cancelled and held for naught. The Director of the Department of Public Works shall notify every person holding or using any such spur track or side track, or shipping or receiving freight cars over and upon any street, alley, or public place within the City inconsistent with or contrary to the provisions of this article of the revocation and cancellation hereby provided.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-7; Code 1984, § 45-2-26)

laws.title: Release of bonds and agreements
laws.content:
(a) Bonds and agreements or bonds filed in the Office of Chief Financial Officer pursuant to the provisions of Sections 43-5-23 and 43-5-26 of this Code shall be and hereby are released from future coverage and from future premium payments thereon, whenever:

(1) The streets or alleys which are crossed by spur tracks or have side tracks thereon, for which permits were issued, are vacated either by resolution of the City Council or by court order;

(2) New bonds are filed in the Office of the Chief Financial Officer to replace existing bonds in the Chief Financial Officer’s custody, which assume future liability coverage; or

CD43:35
§ 43-5-28

DETROIT CITY CODE

(3) Permits issued under this article are revoked by the City Council.

(b) The Corporation Counsel is authorized to grant full releases on any of the aforesaid bonds, subject to the approval of the City Council, only after the full period of the statute of limitations of actions against such bonds shall have expired, provided, that no such releases shall be granted by the Corporation Counsel in any case until all fees, claims, and judgments are paid or settled by the permittee or the permittee’s surety.

(1) A permittee is indebted to the City arising out of any obligation assumed by the permittee under the permittee’s bond;

(2) That damage claims are pending against the City or the permittee arising out of the use and operation of such spur tracks or side tracks;

(3) That suits based upon such claims are pending in court;

(4) That judgments have been entered thereon against the City or the City and the permittee jointly. Where a permit issued under the provisions of Section 43-5-26 of this Code is revoked by the City Council, no full release shall be granted by the Corporation Counsel until the spur tracks or side tracks covered by the permit are removed in full compliance with the provisions of this article.

(c) Upon request, the Director of the Department of Public Works shall inform the Chief Financial Officer whether or not the City has a claim against a permittee arising out of the permittee’s bond or the provisions of this article and, upon request, the Corporation Counsel shall inform the Chief Financial Officer whether or not any claims are pending against the City or a permittee and whether or not any suits are pending in court, or whether or not any judgments have been entered thereon against the City or a permittee arising out of the permittee’s bond or the provisions of this article before granting final releases.

(Code 1964, § 49-2-8; Code 1984, § 45-2-27)

Secs. 43-5-29—43-5-50. Reserved.

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Permits for awnings over sidewalks
laws.content:
The Department of Public Works is hereby authorized to issue permits for the maintenance of awnings to be erected during inclement weather from the lot line to within two feet back of the face of any curbstone. Awnings must be erected on iron posts and shall be eight feet six inches above the sidewalk. No rails or strip of boards shall be used between the uprights, provided, that the erection and maintenance of such awnings neither shall obstruct public travel in any manner nor shall any such permit be granted for a longer period than 48 hours.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-3; Code 1984, § 50-4-1)

laws.title: Dust, dirt, and other refuse on sidewalks
laws.content:
No person shall permit any dust, dirt, or other refuse to remain for longer than 24 hours on the sidewalk in front of or adjacent to the side of any house, premises, building or lot owned, occupied or controlled by such person.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-4; Code 1984, § 50-4-2)

Secs. 43-6-4—43-6-20. Reserved.

CD43:36

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
(a) No sidewalk or driveway shall be hereafter laid in any street, alley, or other public place within the City without a permit from the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(b) The Department of Public Works is authorized to grant a permit to any owner of real estate in the City to construct a sidewalk or driveway in front of or adjacent to the real estate owned by such owner, conditioned that such owner personally is skilled and competent to construct such sidewalk or driveway and maintain the same hereafter and will observe the specifications of the Department of Public Works and build the sidewalk or driveway to the satisfaction of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, §§ 58-3-8, 58-3-11; Code 1984, § 50-4-16)

laws.title: Bond for contractors required
laws.content:
(a) In order to ensure the quality and guarantee the maintenance of sidewalks or driveways laid within the City, every person engaged in the business of laying and constructing sidewalks or driveways in the City shall be required to execute a good and sufficient surety bond to the City in the penal sum of $2,500.00.

(b) The bond required by Subsection (a) of this section shall be conditioned upon the faithful observance of the terms and conditions of the provisions of this Code with reference to the construction of sidewalks or driveways within the City and shall be further conditioned that the person executing such bond shall keep and maintain the sidewalk or driveway which such person constructs in good condition or repair and fit for public travel for a period of five years from and after the date of completion of construction of such sidewalk or driveway. Such bonds shall be approved by the Corporation Counsel.

(c) The bond required by Subsection (a) of this section may be prosecuted and recovery had by any person who shall have suffered any injury or damage by reason of inferior quality of material having been used in the construction of such sidewalk or driveway, or for any injury or damage suffered by such person on account of such sidewalk or driveway having become out of repair within five years from the date of completion of the construction of such sidewalk or driveway, in the name of the City for the use or benefit of such person.

(Code 1964, §§ 58-3-5—58-3-7; Code 1984, § 50-4-17)

laws.title: Standards and specifications
laws.content:
All sidewalks constructed in any street, alley, or other public place within the City shall be built in strict conformity with the specifications that are contained in the standards established by the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-12; Code 1984, § 50-4-18)

laws.title: Minimum width; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) All sidewalks constructed within the City shall be six feet in width, except as may be otherwise provided for or specified.

(b) The Director of the Department of Public Works may authorize the construction of walks of less than six feet in width where the existing walks on the street or adjacent streets are less than six feet in width and on streets where no walk exists in the block in which the new walk is to be constructed, when, in such Director’s opinion, a walk less than six feet in width is ample to accommodate the pedestrian traffic.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-9; Code 1984, § 50-4-19)

laws.title: Full-width sidewalks required along certain streets
laws.content:
(a) Sidewalks, to be known as full-width sidewalks, shall be constructed from the street curb to the lot line or building on the following streets or parts of streets:

All streets or parts thereof that are situated in the area bounded on the north by Columbia Avenue, on the south by the Detroit River, on the west by First Street and on the east by St. Antoine Street, and on the following streets: Adams, from Chrysler Freeway to Grand River; Brush, from Atwater to Vernor Highway; Cass, from John C. Lodge Freeway to West Grand Boulevard; Clifford, from Woodward to Sproat; Congress, from Third to Brush; Elizabeth, from Chrysler Freeway to Grand River; Fort Street West, from Woodward to Woodmere; Grand River West, from Woodward to the City limits; Gratiot, from Woodward to the City limits; Hastings, from Gratiot to Forest; Jefferson East, from Woodward to Baldwin; Jefferson East, from Montclair to the City limits; Jefferson West, from Woodward to Washington Boulevard; Jefferson West, from Clark to River Rouge; Lafayette West, from Griswold to West Grand Boule-

vard; Lafayette East from Randolph to Elmwood; Michigan, from Woodward to the City limits; Park, from Woodward to Peterboro; Third, from the Detroit River to the north side of Hancock; Third, from the north side of Hudson to the West Grand Boulevard; Woodward, from Jefferson to Clairmount; Fenkell, from Twelfth to west City limits; Livernois, from West Jefferson to Eight Mile Road; McNichols Road, from Gratiot to west City limits; Puritan, from Highland Park City limits west to Greenfield; Wyoming, from Plymouth to Seven Mile Road; and all other such streets, not herein specifically provided for, which may be designated hereafter by the Director of the Department of Public Works and approved by the City Council.

(b) The Director of the Department of Public Works may waive, subject to the approval of the City Council, the requirements of Subsection (a) of this section as to any portions of the delineated streets not requiring full-width sidewalks.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-10; Code 1984, § 50-4-20)

laws.title: Lines and stakes
laws.content:
Wherever sidewalks are ordered on any streets where none have existed, it shall be the duty of the Director of the Department of Public Works to establish a sidewalk line on such street for at least a distance that the sidewalks have been or are about to be ordered by setting stakes approximately 100 feet apart. Such stakes shall designate the outer edge of the sidewalk from the lot line, and the record of the same shall be entered into a book to be kept for such purposes in the Office of the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-13; Code 1984, § 50-4-21)

laws.title: Construction of driveways generally
laws.content:
All driveways crossing sidewalk space shall be constructed of concrete from the curbline to the lot line and placed, at a grade to be fixed by the Director of the Department of Public Works, according to specifications furnished by the Director, provided, that driveways constructed on unpaved streets may be constructed of crushed stone, slag, crushed brick, or bituminous material from the outer line of the gutter to the sidewalk.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-14; Code 1984, § 50-4-22)

laws.title: Use of mosaic, art marble, tile, coloring, and advertising in sidewalks prohibited; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) No person shall construct or maintain any mosaic, art marble, tiling or any colored material, name, numbers or advertising in any sidewalk space, which is the space between the lot line of the property and the street curbline, except a stamp or plate containing the name of the contractor or person laying such sidewalk, and the year in which the same was laid, in legible and indelible characters.

(b) No such mosaic, art marble, tiling or colored material, or open iron gratings over areaways now existing in any sidewalk space shall be repaired, but shall be entirely removed or closed in within five days, upon notice from the Department of Public Works and, where such notice is not complied with within the time specified therein, the Department of Public Works is authorized to proceed to remove and fill in the same and assess the cost against the abutting property.

(c) A concrete sidewalk may be constructed, in an approved color, at the discretion of the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-15; Code 1984, § 50-4-23)

laws.title: Covered areas or vaults in sidewalks
laws.content:
(a) In case of covered areaways or vaults in sidewalk space, the illuminated pavement shall have in the top coat of the concrete not less than two pounds of No. 10 Carborundum floated into every 15 square feet of surface between the prism or glass sidewalk lights.

(b) In the case of covered areaways or vaults, the live load of any sidewalk covering any areaway or basement in that space between the street curbline and the lot line shall be not less than 200 pounds per square foot. The live load per square foot for driveways over coal vaults or other vaults or covered areaways, where driving is permitted, shall not be less than 600 pounds per square foot.

(Code 1964, § 58-3-16; Code 1984, § 50-4-24)

Secs. 43-6-30—43-6-50. Reserved.

laws.title: Petition by two-thirds of abutting property owners required; investigation and report by Planning and Development Department
laws.content:
A petition for the vacating of any dedicated alley or portion thereof in a residential area in the City shall be presented to the City Council by not less than two-thirds of the owners of the property abutting on such alley or portion thereof sought to be vacated who shall signify, in

CD43:38

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-7-4

writing, their consent to the granting of such petition. Where property owners elect to keep the alley open either due to the need to gain access to their garages or for reasons verified and approved by the Director of the Department of Public Works, they shall be responsible for the cleanliness and maintenance of the alley. Where found in a littered condition, as defined under Sections 42-2-93 and 42-2-94 of this Code, the Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to barricade said alley as the Director deems necessary. No action shall be taken by the City Council regarding petitions for alley conversion until a complete investigation and report thereon shall have been made by the Planning and Development Department.

(Code 1964, § 58-5-1; Code 1984, § 50-6-1; Ord. No. 267-H, § 1(58-5-1), eff. 7-14-1978; Ord. No. 31-93, § 1(50-6-1), eff. 12-10-1993)

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Prohibited generally; presumptions concerning identity of violator; enforcement; exceptions
laws.content:
(a) No person shall obstruct or encumber any public wharf, street, alley, or any public place with animals, boxes, signs, barrels, posts, fences, buildings, dirt, stones, bricks, rubbish or any other material or thing whatsoever, except as otherwise provided for in this Code, or encroach upon or permit to remain or maintain in any such street, alley or public space, any building, structure or thing owned, occupied or used by such person, pro-

Supp. No. 2

CD43:40

laws.title: Streets, Sidewalks, and Other Public Places
laws.content:
§ 43-8-4

vided, that the Department of Public Works City Engineering Division may grant permission for a temporary obstruction of a sidewalk in front of business buildings for the purpose of elevating and receiving heavy merchandise, provided further, that the same shall not be piled over six feet high and the owner shall be responsible for any damage from such use of the walk. The authority to revoke such permission at any time is expressly reserved to the Department of Public Works.

(b) With respect to any advertisement, sign, or other obstruction or encumbrance that violates any provision of this section, a rebuttable presumption exists that the advertisement, sign, or other obstruction or encumbrance was erected, placed, or displayed at its location by, or with the consent of, the promoter of the event, offer, or service that is the subject of the advertisement, sign, or other obstruction or encumbrance.

(c) This section shall be enforced by the Police Department.

(d) This section shall not be construed to prohibit merchants and other business persons from using and occupying, for a width of three feet, the inside of the sidewalk space next to the building or lot line immediately in front of their place of business in all streets where the sidewalk space is ten or more feet in width, or receiving a permit for a temporary encroachment from the Department of Public Works for a designated sales area adjacent to the business, for the purpose of displaying, selling, or receiving and shipping their goods, wares, and merchandise between sunrise and sunset, when such use and occupation will not obstruct public travel.

(e) Where use and occupation will not obstruct public travel, the Department of Public Works City Engineering Division may permit merchants or other occupants of the buildings located on the south side of the Fisher Freeway Service Drive, between Russell Street and Riopelle Street; on the west side of Russell Street from the Fisher Freeway Service Drive to the alley north of and parallel with Adelaide Street; and on the east side of Market Street from the Fisher Freeway Service Drive to Winder Street, to use and occupy all of the space of eight feet in width, outside of a line three feet distant from the lot line, for the purpose of receiving and shipping their goods, wares, products and merchandise, or for displaying their goods, wares, products and merchandise used for exhibiting and advertising their business between sunrise and 11:00 a.m.

(f) This section shall not be construed to prevent the moving of goods, wares, and merchandise across any sidewalk in the way of trade or for the use of pedestrians.

(g) This section shall not be construed as giving authority to any owner or occupant of any premises to let, sublet, rent, lease, or grant free use to any person whatsoever any of the sidewalk space, which is the space between the lot line of the properly and the curbstone or any space outside of the lot line, on, above or below ground, for business stands of any kind or for any purpose whatsoever. Any person found doing business in such space may be summarily removed by the Police Department and shall be deemed in violation of this section.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-1; Code 1984, § 50-2-1; Ord. No. 13-07, § 1(50-2-1), eff. 5-18-2007; Ord. No. 2021-8, § 1, eff. 3-23-2021)

laws.title: Projecting structures or framework prohibited
laws.content:
No covered or uncovered structure or framework of even a quasi-permanent character, which is attached to the front or in front of any building, shall be permitted to be constructed or maintained so as to extend into the street beyond any lot line. Any such item constructed shall be removed within 24 hours after notice from the Department of Public Works to the owner or occupant of the building to remove the same. Where there is a failure to comply with such notice, the Department of Public Works may summarily remove the same and may issue a misdemeanor violation under this section against both owner and the occupant.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-2; Code 1984, § 50-2-2)

laws.title: Sidewalk telephone booths
laws.content:
(a) The City Council may authorize, by resolution, the Department of Public Works to issue a permit for the installation of an outdoor commercial telephone booth on that portion of the highway located between the property lot lines and the curb, subject to findings:

(1) By the Planning and Development Department that such use will not be injurious to the adjacent or contiguous properties; and

(2) By the Department of Transportation that the location thereof will not imperil public safety.

(b) Before such permit is issued, the petitioner shall file a surety bond in the penal sum of not less than $5,000.00, which saves and holds the City harmless from

Supp. No. 2
