any claims, damages, or expenses that may arise by reason of the issuance of such permit and the occupancy of the City property thereunder, and is approved by the Corporation Counsel.

(c) Any permit issued under this section is revocable at the will, whim, and caprice of the City Council and, as a condition of the permit, the permittee shall waive any right to claim damages against the City for the removal of such installation. The City Council may include additional conditions and limitations the Body finds necessary to protect the interests of the City.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-3; Code 1984, § 50-2-3)

laws.title: Flag poles
laws.content:
(a) The City Council may authorize, by resolution, the Department of Public Works to issue a permit for the temporary installation and maintenance of flag staffs or flag poles for the display of the American Flag only on the marginal area of the street, upon petition of the owner or lessee of the abutting property.

(b) Such request shall be made by petition to the City Council, and such petition shall have attached to it a survey or plan drawn to scale showing the proposed installation. The petition shall be referred to the Department of Public Works and the Building, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department for report and recommendation as to whether such use of the street will create a material hazard to the public, and whether the provision for closing the hole or openings for the flag staffs or flag poles is sufficient to protect the public from injury.

(c) Upon receipt of the aforesaid reports, the City Council may authorize, by resolution, the Department of Public Works to issue permits for the installation and maintenance of the flag staffs or flag poles for displaying the American Flag only, on condition that the petitioner file a corporate surety bond in the amount of not less than $2,000.00, to be approved by the Corporation Counsel, conditioned on such petitioner’s faithful performance of the terms of this article, and that the permittee will indemnify the City against all actions or claims of any kind whatsoever made by any person for injury to person or property by reason of the issuance of the permit for the installation or maintenance of the flag staffs or flag poles, that the permittee will assume full liability, and that such permittee will pay for the removal

and restoration of the marginal area when ordered to do so. Such permission is given at the will and caprice of the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-4; Code 1984, § 50-2-4)

laws.title: Fences, signs, and other approved obstructions
laws.content:
(a) The City Council may authorize, by resolution, the Department of Public Works to issue a permit for the installation of fences, signs, or any other approved obstruction by the owner of private property on City property between the established line of the sidewalk and the property line adjacent thereto.

(b) The owner of such private property shall attach to such owner’s petition to the City Council a plan or survey, explaining in detail such owner’s proposed use of the City property, and an agreement that the petitioner:

(1) Will keep the City property in a neat and orderly condition at all times;

(2) Agrees to make and execute an agreement saving and protecting the City from any claims, damages, or expenses that may arise by reason of the issuance of a permit and the permitted occupancy of the property thereunder;

(3) Confesses judgment on any claims, damages, or expenses thereunder; and

(4) Agrees to remove, at such owner’s own expense, any fences, signs, or other approved obstruction erected under this section when so notified to do so.

Where such obstruction is not removed when the permittee is notified for its removal, the Department of Public Works is hereby authorized and directed to remove such obstruction and to assess the cost of such removal against the adjoining property of the permittee.

(c) Any permit issued under this section is revocable at the will, whim, and caprice of the City Council. The permittee under this section shall waive, as a condition of the permit, any right to claim damages against the City for the removal of such installation. The City Council may include additional conditions and limitations necessary to protect the interests of the City.

(d) The City Council shall take no action relative to issuing a permit under this section until an investigation and report is received from the Department of Public Works and a report from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department that such installa-

Supp. No. 2

CD43:42

laws.title: Notice to remove obstructions; Department of Public Works authorized to remove obstructions
laws.content:
(a) In all cases of violation of the provisions of this division, the owner or occupant of the building or premises shall remove such obstructions within 24 hours after notice to do so from the Department of Public Works. Where the owner fails to remove the same, such removal shall be effected by the Department of Public Works.

(b) The notices to be given by the Department of Public Works, as provided by this section, shall be served upon the owner or occupant of such obstruction or the adjoining premises. Where the owner or occupant cannot be found, it shall be securely posted in some conspicuous place on such premises or abutting building. A compliance with such notice or the removal of the obstruction by the Department of Public Works shall not operate as a suspension of the penalties provided in Section 43-8-1 of this Code.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-6; Code 1984, § 50-2-6)

laws.title: Disposition of removed property; removal, inventory, and storage charges
laws.content:
(a) All obstructions or encumbrances that are enumerated in Sections 43-8-2, 43-8-3, 43-8-4, 43-8-5, and 43-8-6 of this Code, which have been removed by the Department of Public Works, as provided in Section 43-8-7 of this Code shall be considered abandoned 30 days after such removal or posting of the notice provided for in Section 43-8-7 of this Code. Upon the removal of such goods, material, or property by the Department of Public Works from the street, sidewalk or other public property, an inventory of such goods shall be made and signed by a representative of the Department of Public Works and a representative of the Police Department from the precinct wherein the property is located. A copy of such inventory shall be held both by the Department of Public Works and by the Police Department for a period of six years from the date of such removal.

(b) Where an owner appears to claim such goods, such owner shall pay the cost of removal, inventory, and storage. Such charges shall be paid within ten days after such claim is filed with the Department of Public Works. Where no person appears to reclaim such property or material, the Department of Public Works shall endeavor to secure bids for the sale of such property and, in the failure thereof, shall be empowered to sell or dispose of such goods.

(c) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to establish fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of removal, inventory, and storage under Subsection (a) of this section. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Posted at the Department of Public Works and made available at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Department of Public Works at least once every two years.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-7; Code 1984, § 50-2-7)

Secs. 43-8-9—43-8-20. Reserved.

laws.title: Encroachments prohibited; exceptions
laws.content:
No building or structure of any description shall extend beyond the lot line into any street, alley or public place, except as provided in this division.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-8; Code 1984, § 50-2-19)

laws.title: Surety bond or insurance required
laws.content:
(a) A party who owns any building or structure that is authorized by the City through a resolution adopted by the City Council prior to January 1, 1965, to encroach upon City-owned property shall file with the Debt Management Section of the Office of Chief Financial Officer either:

(1) A surety bond in the amount of $1,000,000; or

(2) A general liability insurance policy in the amount of $1,000,000, which names the City as an additional insured.

(b) In accordance with the terms of the surety bond or the general liability insurance policy, where a third-party claim is made against the City, a party who owns any building or structure that is authorized by the City

*Cross reference—Building construction and property maintenance, Ch. 8.

through a resolution adopted by the City Council prior to January 1, 1965, to encroach upon City-owned property:

(1) Shall resist and defend said claim against the City; and

(2) Shall assume all liability for the occurrence giving rise to the claim against the City.

(Code 1984, § 50-2-38; Ord. No. 23-96, § 1(50-2-38), eff. 10-14-1996)

laws.title: Temporary encroachments
laws.content:
The Director of the Department of Public Works may issue a permit for temporary encroachment in a street, alley, or public easement after receiving the approval of the City Council through adoption of a resolution. The City Council shall only approve an encroachment after receiving a report from the Department of Public Works and the Planning and Development Department. The City Council may attach conditions to its approval that will protect the health, welfare, and safety of the community. Any permit issued under this section shall be revocable at the will, whim, and caprice of the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-8.1; Code 1984, § 50-2-20)

laws.title: Plan of buildings to be filed
laws.content:
Before proceeding with the erection, enlargement, alteration or repair of any building in the City, which contemplates or requires the use or obstruction of any street, alley or public place, the owner of the building, or such owner’s agent, shall file with the Department of Public Works for approval a ground plan of the same, showing the line of the basement wall thereof and that the proposed structure does not by its walls, chimneys, bases, columns, entrances, ornamentations, or otherwise project within the lines of any street, alley or public place, except as permitted by this Code, together with the location of any areas or excavations beyond the lot lines, permission for the excavation of which may have been granted by the City Council through adoption of a resolution, together with a certified copy of the action of the City Council granting the same and the conditions of the grant.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-9; Code 1984, § 50-2-21)

laws.title: Street lines
laws.content:
Where a building is to be set at, near, or across the line of any street, alley or public place, the building owner, or the owner’s agent, shall apply, in writing, to the Director of the Department of Public Works for a written description of such line, which, upon receipt of a completed application, must not be unreasonably withheld by the Department. Failure to obtain a written description of such line does not absolve any person from any penalty for the violation of this section.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-10; Code 1984, § 50-2-22)

laws.title: Permit to store building materials in public places—Required; removal of materials when permit not obtained; removal, inventory, and storage charges
laws.content:
(a) No person, or such person’s agent, shall place any stone, timber, lumber, planks, boards, bricks or other materials, in or upon any street, alley or other public space, except for the purpose of erecting, enlarging, altering, or repairing any building or structure, where permission has been obtained from the Department of Public Works, within 48 hours after starting building operations. Where a permit is not obtained within the time specified, the Department of Public Works shall remove all such materials placed in any street, alley, or public space. Removal, inventory, and storage charges shall be made by the Department of Public Works. After 60 days from the time of removal, the Department of Public Works shall cause such material to be sold for removal, inventory, and storage charges.

(b) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to establish fees with the approval of the City Council, through adoption of a resolution, for the cost of removal, inventory, and storage under Subsection (a) of this section. After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Posted at the Department of Public Works and made available at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Department of Public Works at least once every two years.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-11; Code 1984, § 50-2-23)

laws.title: Same—Plans to be approved
laws.content:
Before granting a permit for the obstruction of any street, alley, or public place with material for use in the

CD43:44

laws.title: Same—When approval of plans not required
laws.content:
In case of the erection, enlargement, alteration, or repair of any dwelling or other building or structure and the walls, ornamentation, bay windows, verandas, porches, areas or entrance steps are at least 12 inches within the line of the lot on which constructed, the Department of Public Works may issue permits for use of the street, alley, or public place for the handling of material in connection with such work without requiring the submission of plans, provided, that:

(1) A certificate of the architect, building contractor, or owner of the building or structure shall be furnished to the Department of Public Works, showing that the location of the same as required by this section; and

(2) No encroachment shall be made upon any street, alley, or public place in the erection, enlargement, alteration, or repair of the same.  
(Code 1964, § 58-2-13; Code 1984, § 50-2-25)

laws.title: Same—Term; amount of space permitted to be occupied; construction of temporary sidewalks
laws.content:
A permit to store building materials in public places shall be good for 90 days, provided, that all the provisions relative to issuance are complied with, and that at the end of the 90-day period such permit may be renewed at the direction of the Director of the Department of Public Works. Materials for which such a permit is issued shall not be allowed to occupy or obstruct more than four feet of any street, alley or public space, or any portion thereof, other than that abutting the lot and premises on which such material is to be used. Where it is necessary to remove the sidewalk in front of such premises when building operations are contemplated or in progress, or where it is necessary to entirely obstruct the sidewalk, a temporary sidewalk shall be provided and maintained in a safe and sightly condition not less than three feet in width between the lot line or premises and the street, provided, that under no circumstances shall authority be granted to any person to obstruct or in any manner prevent the free passage of surface water through the gutter of any street, alley, or other public space. Such building materials shall not be allowed to remain in any street, alley, or other public space after the completion of building operations. Where surplus materials are not removed upon completion of the work from any street, alley or other public space, the same shall be removed by the Department of Public Works and inspection, removal and storage charges shall be made in accordance with Section 43-8-26 of this Code.  
(Code 1964, § 58-2-14; Code 1984, § 50-2-26)

laws.title: Same—Purpose of permit; occupation of sidewalk after expiration prohibited
laws.content:
(a) Permits under this division to occupy streets and sidewalks for purposes of building are intended only for use in connection with the actual erection, enlargement, alteration, or repair of buildings, and shall terminate with the completion of such operation.

(b) It shall be unlawful to occupy any sidewalk or street after the completion of the operation on account of which a permit has been issued by the Department of Public Works.

(c) It shall be unlawful to occupy a sidewalk or street, under authority of such permit, for the storage of articles not intended for immediate use in connection with the operations on account of which such permit has been issued, or for a longer period than stated in the permit.  
(Code 1964, § 58-2-15; Code 1984, § 50-2-27)

laws.title: Same—Revocation; reinstatement
laws.content:
Where work upon any building shall be conducted in violation of any of the provisions of this division, the Department of Public Works shall revoke the permit. It shall be unlawful, after the revocation of such permit, to proceed with such work unless such permit shall first have been reinstated or reissued by the Department of Public Works. The Department of Public Works shall not reinstate or reissue any revoked permit until the permittee comes into full compliance with this division.  
(Code 1964, § 58-2-16; Code 1984, § 50-2-28)

laws.title: Limitation on occupation of streets
laws.content:
The occupation of streets for the storage of building material in front of any one building, shall not exceed one-fourth of the width of the roadway of the same. In streets containing railroad tracks, such occupation shall not exceed one-half the distance from the curbstone to such railroad tracks.  
(Code 1964, § 58-2-17; Code 1984, § 50-2-29)

CD43:45
§ 43-8-33

DETROIT CITY CODE

laws.title: Sidewalks may be occupied only in front of premises for which permit issued; exception
laws.content:
(a) Permits issued under this division shall not authorize the occupation of any sidewalk or street, or part thereof, other than immediately in front of the premises of the building upon which such permit is issued.

(b) Where the written consent and a waiver of claims for damages against the City of the owners of properties adjoining the site of any proposed building is first obtained and filed with the Department of Public Works, the permission to occupy the roadway and the sidewalk may be extended beyond the limits of the frontage of such building upon the same terms and conditions as those fixed by this division for the occupation of sidewalk and street in front of the building site.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-18; Code 1984, § 50-2-30)

laws.title: Passageway required on sidewalk; elevation of sidewalk; protection of pedestrians
laws.content:
(a) While building operations are in progress, at least one-half of the sidewalk space in front of the premises of the building for which a permit is granted pursuant to this division shall be kept, at all times, free and unobstructed for the purpose of passage, and clear of solid waste, dirt, snow, and ice. Where there are excavations on either side of the same, such sidewalk shall be protected by substantial railings which shall be built and maintained thereon so long as such excavations continue. This section does not prohibit the maintenance of a driveway for the delivery of material across such sidewalk from the curbline to the building site.

(b) It shall be permitted, for the purpose of delivering material to the basement of the building, to elevate temporary sidewalks to a height not exceeding four feet above the curb level of the street. Where a sidewalk is so elevated, it shall be provided with good and substantial steps at both ends and shall have railings as required in Subsection (a) of this section on both sides.

(c) Where the building to be erected is more than four stories in height and is set at or near the street line, there shall be built over such sidewalk a roof having a framework and covering composed of support and stringers of three-inch by 12-inch timbers, not more than eight feet from centers, covered by two layers of two-inch plank. Such roof shall be maintained as long as material is being used or handled on such street from and above the level of such sidewalk.

(d) In all cases, such temporary sidewalks, their railings and approaches, and the roofs over the same shall be constructed with regard to ease of approach, strength, and safety to the satisfaction of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-19; Code 1984, § 50-2-31)

laws.title: Warning lights required
laws.content:
Red lights or lanterns shall be displayed and maintained during every night at each pile of material in any street, alley, or public place and at each end of every excavation.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-20; Code 1984, § 50-2-32)

laws.title: Removal of soil and solid waste; stone cutting and dressing prohibited on streets
laws.content:
Soil taken from excavations and solid waste taken from buildings shall not be stored either upon sidewalks or roadways of streets, and shall be removed from day to day as rapidly as produced. Where dry solid waste, apt to produce dust, is being handled, it shall be kept wetted down, so as to prevent being blown about by the wind. Stone cutting or stone dressing shall not be permitted on the street.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-21; Code 1984, § 50-2-33)

laws.title: Use of derricks
laws.content:
For all buildings more than four stories in height, the use of derricks upon sidewalks is prohibited.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-22; Code 1984, § 50-2-34)

laws.title: Scaffolds
laws.content:
All scaffolds erected within the lines of any street, alley, or public place for use in the erection, enlargement, alterations, or repair of any building shall be well and safely supported and of sufficient width and properly secured, so as to ensure the safety of persons walking thereon or of persons passing along the sidewalks or public places thereunder, to prevent the falling thereof or of any materials that may be used, placed, or deposited thereon.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-23; Code 1984, § 50-2-35)

laws.title: Enforcement of division
laws.content:
The Police Department, through its officers, and the Department of Public Works, through its employees who are inspectors, shall enforce the provisions of this article.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-24; Code 1984, § 50-2-36)

CD43:46

laws.title: Liability of contractors and architects for violations
laws.content:
Any contractor who shall construct any building or structure in violation of any of the provisions of this division, or any architect designing or having charge of such building or structure who shall allow the building or structure to be constructed, shall be liable to the penalties provided and imposed for such violation.

(Code 1964, § 58-2-25; Code 1984, § 50-2-37)

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
No person shall dig or tear up any pavement, sidewalk or crosswalk or dig any hole, ditch, drain or sewer in any street, alley or any public square without first obtaining a permit from the Director of the Department of Public Works.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-4; Code 1984, § 50-3-1)

laws.title: Cash deposit
laws.content:
A permit under this article shall only be granted in cases where the applicant has deposited with the Director of the Department of Public Works a sum sufficient to cover the estimated expense of refilling the soil removed and relaying the pavement.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-4; Code 1984, § 50-3-2)

laws.title: Barricades and lights—Public property
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of all persons to suitably barricade and light any excavated area on public property.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-7; Code 1984, § 50-3-3)

laws.title: Same—Private property adjacent to streets or alleys
laws.content:
Owners or occupants, or their agents, of any lots or grounds in the City, which are adjacent to any street or alley, are prohibited from excavating, or causing or permitting excavation of, such lots or grounds unless they are guarded by a good and sufficient fence or other barrier, at least four feet high, so as to prevent accidents to persons straying from the street or alley.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-8; Code 1984, § 50-3-4)

laws.title: Notice when excavations ready for backfilling and repaving
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of any person digging through or breaking any pavement, or digging any hole, ditch, drain, or sewer in any paved street, paved alley or other paved public space, to notify the Department of Public Works upon completion of such person’s work that the cut or job is ready for backfilling and repairing.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-5; Code 1984, § 50-3-5)

laws.title: Backfilling
laws.content:
Any cut into an unpaved street, or back of the curb upon a paved street, shall be refilled by the parties obtaining the permit. It shall be their duty to pound the soil so that the cut or trench is left in as good a condition as before.

(Code 1964, § 58-1-6; Code 1984, § 50-3-6)

laws.title: Grant of natural gas franchise; nonexclusive
laws.content:
(a) Subject to this division, applicable provisions of this Code, the Charter, the Michigan Constitution of 1963, applicable state statutes, rules and regulations, and applicable federal statutes, rules and regulations, the City hereby grants a non-exclusive franchise to MichCon, and its successors and assigns.

(b) This franchise grants to MichCon the right and privilege:

(1) To transact local business within the City;

(2) To lay, maintain, operate and use natural gas transmission or distribution facilities and other necessary equipment on, along, across, and under the highways, streets, alleys, bridges, and other public places within the City; and

(3) To convey, supply and sell natural gas within the City, and all other incidental matters thereto.

(Code 1984, § 50-10-2; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-2), eff. 9-17-1995)

laws.title: Term
laws.content:
Subject to revocation by the City at any time, the franchise granted under this division shall continue in effect for a period of 20 years from the effective date of this division, which was September 17, 1995.

(Code 1984, § 50-10-3; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-3), eff. 9-17-1995)

*Cross references—Telecommunication franchises, generally, Ch. 45, Art. III, Div. 1; uniform video service local franchise agreements, Ch. 45, Art. III, Div. 2.

laws.title: Natural gas service and extension of system
laws.content:
In accordance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, MichCon, and its successors and assigns, shall furnish natural gas to its customers residing or doing business within the City and, provided, that installations and any extensions shall be subject to the provisions of MichCon’s main extension program, area expansion program, or other applicable programs which are administered by the Michigan Public Service Commission, or successor agency having similar jurisdiction.

(Code 1984, § 50-10-4; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-4), eff. 9-17-1995)

laws.title: Use of streets and other public places
laws.content:
(a) MichCon, and its successors and assigns, shall not unnecessarily obstruct the passage of any of the highways, streets, alleys, or other public places within the City. In addition, within a reasonable time after making an opening or excavation, and at its sole cost and expense, MichCon shall restore to City specifications any property damaged, destroyed, or in any way altered as a result of the opening or excavation.

(b) Unless an emergency exists where MichCon determines that there is an immediate and serious threat to the health, safety or welfare of a customer, or the general public, and which requires immediate action, MichCon shall not open or excavate any road, street, alley, or highway in the City for the purpose of laying or maintaining natural gas transmission or distribution facilities and other necessary equipment, except upon application to the Michigan Department of Transportation, the Wayne County Department of Public Services Roads Division, the City, or other public authority having jurisdiction over the public way, stating the nature of the proposed work and the route. MichCon shall obtain a permit from the public authority having jurisdiction over the highway, street, alley, bridge, and other public place for all proposed work within the City. Prior to any application to construct underground natural gas transmission or distribution facilities and other necessary equipment within the City, the City may require a written notice from MichCon within a reasonable time. This notice shall be for the purpose of locating other utilities within the underground trench or excavation where MichCon’s natural gas transmission or distribution equipment is being installed or constructed.

(Code 1984, § 50-10-5; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-5), eff. 9-17-1995)

CD43:48

laws.title: Indemnification
laws.content: MichCon, and its successors and assigns, shall use due care in exercising the privileges in this division and, at its sole cost and expense, shall indemnify and hold harmless the City, and its employees and agents, from any liability which may be imposed upon or incurred by the indemnitees, for all damages and costs which may be recovered against the City arising from the default, carelessness, or negligence of MichCon or any of its officers, agents, and servants that may arise out of, or be in any way connected with, the operation and maintenance or condition of MichCon’s natural gas transmission or distribution system and other necessary equipment, or MichCon’s failure to comply with any federal or state statute, regulation or rule, or any provision of this Code. (Code 1984, § 50-10-6; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-6), eff. 9-17-1995)

laws.title: Standards and conditions of service; rules, regulations, and rates
laws.content: Under this division, the rates to be charged for natural gas within the City, and the standards and conditions of service and operation within the City, shall be the same as set forth in MichCon’s schedule of rules, regulations, and rates as applicable in the cities, villages, and townships where MichCon is now supplying natural gas service, or as shall hereafter be validly prescribed for the City under the orders, rules, and regulations of the Michigan Public Service Commission, or other authority having jurisdiction over the provision of such service within the City. (Code 1984, § 50-10-7; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-7), eff. 9-17-1995)

laws.title: Successors and assigns
laws.content: Whether so expressed or not, the words "Michigan Consolidated Gas Company" and "MichCon" are intended and shall be held and construed to mean and to include both Michigan Consolidated Gas Company and its successors and assigns. MichCon agrees not to assign or sell the franchise granted in this division without approval from the City. The City agrees not to unreasonably withhold its permission for an assignment or sale of the franchise granted in this division. (Code 1984, § 50-10-8; Ord. No. 22-95, § 1(50-10-8), eff. 9-17-1995)

laws.title: Grant of electric franchise; nonexclusive
laws.content:
The City of Detroit grants an electric franchise through:

(1) Chapter CLVIII, Brush Electric Light Company, and Chapter CLIX, Excelsior Electric Light Company, of the 1895 Detroit City Code, which in accordance with Chapter 282 of the 1936 Detroit City Code were saved from repeal in the 1895 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1936 Detroit City Code, which in accordance with Chapter 337 of the 1945 Detroit City Code were saved from repeal in the 1936 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1945 Detroit City Code, which in accordance with Chapter 470 of the 1954 Detroit City Code were saved from repeal in the 1945 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1954 Detroit City Code, which in accordance with Ordinance 1-G were saved from repeal in the 1954 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1964 Detroit City Code, and which in accordance with Section 1-1-7(4) of the 1984 Detroit City Code were saved from repeal in the 1964 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1984 Detroit City Code; and

(2) Chapter 401, Edison Electric Light Company, Chapter 402, Edison Illuminating Company, and Edison Illuminating Company-Supplementary Ordinance, and Chapter 403, Detroit Electric Light and Power Company, of the 1954 Detroit City Code, which in accordance with Ordinance 1-G were saved from repeal in the 1954 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1964 Detroit City Code, and which in accordance with Section 1-1-7(4) of the 1984 Detroit City Code were saved from repeal in the 1964 Detroit City Code and were incorporated by reference into the 1984 Detroit City Code.

Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 day in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

(Code 1984, § 50-9-3; Ord. No. 29-15, § 1(50-9-3), eff. 11-30-2015)

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
No person shall engage in, participate in, aid, form or start any march or parade, unless a parade permit shall have been obtained from the Chief of Police and approved by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(Code 1964, §§ 38-1-8, 58-1-19; Code 1984, § 50-9-16; Ord. No. 29-15, § 1(50-9-16), eff. 11-30-2015)

†Cross reference—Licenses generally, Ch. 28.

CD43:50

laws.title: Application
Standards for issuance
Alternative
laws.content:
When denying an application for a parade permit, the City Council shall be empowered to authorize the conduct of the march or parade on a date, at a time, or over a route different from that named by the applicant. An applicant desiring to accept an alternate permit shall file a written notice of acceptance with the Chief of Police within three days after notice of the action of the City Council. An alternate parade permit shall conform to the requirements of, and shall have the effect of, a parade permit under this division.

(Code 1984, § 50-9-20; Ord. No. 29-15, § 1(50-9-20), eff. 11-30-2015)

laws.title: Contents
Duties of permittee
laws.content:
A permittee under this division shall comply with all permit directions and conditions, with this Code, and with all applicable state and federal law. The march or parade chairperson, or other person heading or leading such activity, shall carry the parade permit upon their person during the conduct of the march or parade.

(Code 1984, § 50-9-22; Ord. No. 29-15, § 1(50-9-22), eff. 11-30-2015)

laws.title: Revocation
laws.content:
The Chief of Police shall have the authority to revoke a parade permit issued under this division upon application of the standards for issuance as set forth in Section 43-11-23 of this Code.

(Code 1984, § 50-9-23; Ord. No. 29-15, § 1(50-9-23), eff. 11-30-2015)

Secs. 43-11-29—43-11-50. Reserved.

CD43:52

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

laws.title: Applicability of article
laws.content:
The provisions of this article shall not be applicable to governmental agencies, or to the owner, occupant, or lessee who, by means of a motor-driven device, removes snow from the sidewalks contiguous to the owner, occupant or lessee’s premises, provided, that no person shall use any snow removal equipment of a scraper or plow-type operated by a motor-driven vehicle upon the sidewalks of the City except during a declared snow emergency.

(Code 1984, § 50-8-16; Ord. No. 364-H, § 1(58-7-1), eff. 1-17-1980; Ord. No. 376-H, § 1(58-7-1), eff. 2-25-1980)

CD43:53

laws.title: Specifications
laws.content:
(a) Generally. Compliance with street and sidewalk vehicle specifications may be waived by the Director of the Department of Public Works upon the declaration of a snow emergency by the Mayor. Such a waiver shall be effective only for the duration of the declared snow emergency. The Department of Public Works shall establish specifications for sidewalk snow removal equipment that may be operated upon the sidewalks during such a declared snow emergency.

(b) Sidewalks. No person shall operate, upon the sidewalks of the City, any snow removal equipment operated by a motor-driven vehicle that is of a gross weight in excess of 4,000 pounds, that is not equipped with pneumatic tires, that is of an overall width greater than the width of the public sidewalk or in any case wider than six feet, and that is not equipped with a revolving-type brush.

(c) Streets. No person shall operate, upon the streets of the City, any snow removal equipment which does not comply with equipment specifications established by the Department of Public Works and placed on file at the Department of Public Works and the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center.

(Code 1984, § 50-8-17; Ord. No. 364-H, § 1(58-7-2), eff. 1-17-1980; Ord. No. 376-H, § 1(58-7-2), eff. 2-25-1980)

laws.title: Occupant not relieved of duty to remove snow or ice from sidewalks
laws.content:
The provisions of this article shall not abrogate the duties of an occupant to remove snow or ice from the sidewalks contiguous to the premises where such occupant is the owner or lessee, as provided by this Code.

(Code 1984, § 50-8-26; Ord. No. 364-H, § 1(58-7-11), eff. 1-17-1980)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
It shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the Department of Public Works, and the Police Department to enforce the provisions of this article.

(Code 1984, § 50-8-27; Ord. No. 364-H, § 1(58-7-12), eff. 1-17-1980)

laws.title: Transportation innovation zone
laws.content:

laws.title: City Treasurer to enforce payment of taxes
Definitions
laws.content:
For the purposes of this article, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this section:

*Adjusted gross receipts* means the gross receipts less winnings paid to wagerers.

*Board* means the Michigan Gaming Control Board.

*Casino* means a building in which gaming is conducted.

*Casino licensee* means a person who has been licensed to operate a casino gambling operation within the City by the Board in accordance with the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, being MCL 432.201 et seq.

*Department* means the Office of Chief Financial Officer.

*Gambling game* means any game played with cards, dice, equipment or a machine, including any mechanical, electro-mechanical or electronic device, which shall include computers and cashless wagering systems, for money, credit, or any representative of value, including, but not limited to, Faro, Monte, Roulette, Keno, Bingo, Fan Tan, Twenty One, Blackjack, Seven And A Half, Klondike, Craps, Poker, Chuck A Luck, Chinese Chuck A Luck (Dai Shu) Wheel of Fortune, Chemin De Fer, Baccarat, Pai Gow, Beat the Banker, Panguingui, Slot Machine, and banking or percentage game, or any other game or device that is approved by the Michigan Gaming Control Board in accordance with the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, being MCL 432.201 et seq.

*Gambling operation* means the conduct of authorized gambling games in a casino.

*Gaming* means to deal, operate, carry on, conduct, maintain, or expose or offer for play any gambling game or gambling operation.

*Gross receipts* means the total of all sums including valid or invalid checks, currency, tokens, coupons, vouchers, or instruments of monetary value whether collected or uncollected, received by a casino licensee from gaming, including all entry fees assessed for tournaments or other contests, less a deduction for uncollectible gaming receivables not to exceed the uncollectible amounts owed as a result of wagers placed at or through a gambling game or four percent of the total gross receipts, whichever is less. The licensee shall not receive the deduction unless the licensee provides written proof to the State Treasurer of the uncollected gaming receivables and had complied with all rules promulgated by the Board regarding the issuance of credit and collection of amounts due under a credit extension.

*Municipal services fee* means the charge imposed pursuant to Section 44-1-4 of this Code.

*Person* means an individual, corporation, limited liability company, association, partnership, limited liability partnership, trust, entity, or other legal entity.

*Cross reference—Casinos, Ch. 10.*

*State law reference—Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, MCL 432.201 et seq.*

CD44:9
$\S 44-1-2$

DETROIT CITY CODE

*Wagerer* means a person who plays a gambling game that is authorized by the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, being MCL 432.201 *et seq.*

*Wagering tax* means the tax imposed pursuant to Section 44-1-3 of this Code.

*Winnings* means the total cash value of all property or sums including currency, tokens, or instruments of monetary value paid to wagerers as a direct result of wagers placed at or through a gambling game.

(Code 1984, § 18-14-2; Ord. No. 23-99, § 1(18-14-2), eff. 8-3-1999)

**Sec. 44-1-3. Imposition of the wagering tax.**

(a) A wagering tax is hereby imposed as an excise tax upon the adjusted gross receipts of a casino licensee.

(b) The wagering tax that is imposed pursuant to this section shall be equal to 9.9 percent of the adjusted gross receipts which are received by a casino licensee and subject to tax under Subsection (a) of this section.

(c) The wagering tax that is imposed pursuant to this section shall be applied against all adjusted gross receipts received in 1999 and each year thereafter in which a casino licensee is licensed by the Board to conduct a gambling operation within the City.

(Code 1984, § 18-14-3; Ord. No. 23-99, § 1(18-14-3), eff. 8-3-1999)

**Sec. 44-1-4. Imposition of the municipal services fee.**

(a) An annual municipal services fee is hereby imposed upon a casino licensee.

(b) The annual municipal services fee that is imposed pursuant to this section shall be equal to the greater of the following amounts:

(1) 1.25 percent of the adjusted gross receipts received by a casino licensee that are subject to tax under Subsection (a) of this section; or

(2) $4,000,000.00.

(c) The municipal services fee that is imposed pursuant to this section shall be calculated on the basis of the adjusted gross receipts which are received in the 12-month period commencing on the day that a casino licensee began a gambling operation within the City and in each 12-month period thereafter.

(Code 1984, § 18-14-4; Ord. No. 23-99, § 1(18-14-4), eff. 8-3-1999)

**Sec. 44-1-5. Method of payment.**

(a) Revenues, as defined in Section 17-10-5 of this Code, shall be remitted daily by each casino licensee to the custodian, as defined in Section 17-10-5 of this Code, by electronic funds transfer for so long as the Collateral Agreement, entered into pursuant to Section 17-10-21, is in effect.

(b) Every casino licensee which is subject to the wagering tax that is imposed pursuant to Section 44-1-3 of this Code shall file, on or before the 15th day of each month, a return for the preceding calendar month on a form prescribed by the Department which shows:

(1) The adjusted gross receipts that have been received in the preceding calendar month which are subject to tax;

(2) Any deduction for uncollectible gaming receivables that have been allowed under the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act, being MCL 432.201 *et seq.*, in the calculation of adjusted gross receipts;

(3) A copy of any written proof of uncollected gaming receivables that have been filed with the State Treasurer;

(4) The amount of tax for which the casino licensee is liable; and

(5) Any other information as may be required by the Department.

A balance of any revenues, as defined in Section 17-10-5 of this Code, that is due to the City for the period covered by the monthly return shall be remitted to the custodian, as defined in Section 17-10-5 of this Code, by electronic funds transfer in the manner required by Subsection (a) of this section on the date that the return is filed for so long as the Collateral Agreement, entered into pursuant to Section 17-10-21 of this Code, is in effect. The monthly return shall be signed by the casino licensee or the casino licensee’s duly authorized agent and, if prepared for the casino licensee by any other person, the return shall so state by providing such person’s name, address, and employer, if any, and be signed by such person.

(c) On the date the casino licensee begins a gambling operation within the City, and within 20 days after each anniversary of the date on which the casino licensee began a gambling operation during all or any portion of that ensuing year, the casino licensee shall remit to the City the minimum municipal services fee that is due under Section 44-1-4 of this Code.

Any amount required to be paid by a casino licensee under this article shall be deemed a debt that is owed by the casino licensee to the City, and deemed delinquent from the date due until paid. The wagering tax and the municipal services fee, together with any interest and penalties imposed thereon, shall be a lien in favor of the City in the same manner or form, with the same attachment and duration as provided for liens of state taxes under Section 29 of the Michigan Revenue Division of the Department of Treasury Act, being MCL 205.29.

laws.title: Liabilities applied to refund amount; order of priority
laws.content:
(a) Where a casino licensee claims a refund that the Department determines to be valid and the Department identifies any liability described in Subsection (b) of this section, the Department shall first apply the amount of the refund in the manner provided for by this section and, if any, the excess shall be refunded to the casino licensee or credited, at the casino licensee’s request, against any current or subsequent liability under this article.

(b) The amount of a refund that is described in Subsection (a) of this section shall be applied in the following order of priority:
