laws.title: Same—Income and profits to which tax applicable
laws.content:
(a) *Income of residents.* The tax under this article shall apply on the following types of income of a resident individual to the same extent and on the same basis that the income is subject to taxation under the Internal Revenue Code:

(1) On a salary, bonus, wage, commission, and other compensation;

(2) On a distributive share of the net profits of a resident owner of an unincorporated business, profession, enterprise, undertaking, or other activity as a result of work done, services rendered and other business activities wherever conducted;

(3) On dividends, interest, capital gains less capital losses, income from estates and trusts, and net profits from rentals of real and tangible personal property; and

(4) On other income of a resident individual.

(b) *Income of nonresidents.* The tax under this article shall apply on the following types of income of a nonresident individual to the same extent and on the same basis that the income is subject to taxation under the Internal Revenue Code:

(1) On a salary, bonus, wage commission, and other compensation for services rendered as an employee for work done or services performed in the City, except that income which the nonresident taxpayer receives as the result of a disability and after exhausting all vacation pay, holiday pay, and sick pay is not compensation for services rendered as an employee for work done or services performed in the City. Vacation pay, holiday pay, sick pay, and a bonus paid by the employer are considered to have the same tax situs as the work assignment or work location and are taxable on the same ratio as the normal earnings of the employee for work actually done or services actually performed;

(2) On a distributive share of the net profits of a nonresident owner of an unincorporated business, profession, enterprise, undertaking or other activity as a result of work done, services rendered and other business activities conducted in the City; and

(3) On capital gains less capital losses from sales of and on the net profits from rentals of real and tangible personal property where the capital gains arise from property located in the City.

(c) *Corporate profits.* The tax under this article shall apply on the taxable net profits of a corporation doing business in the City, being levied on such part of the taxable net profits as is earned by the corporation as a result of work done, services rendered and other business activities conducted in the City, as determined in accordance with this article. No deduction shall be allowed for:

(1) Net operating losses and net capital losses sustained prior to the effective date of the tax; and

(2) The City income tax imposed by this article, provided, that a corporation may deduct income, war profits, and excess profits taxes imposed by a foreign country or a possession of the United States, allocable to income included in taxable net income, any part of which would be allowable as a deduction in determining federal taxable income under the applicable provisions of the Internal Revenue Code.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-21; Code 1984, § 18-10-5; Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-5), eff. 12-11-1998)

*Case law annotation—The lump-sum early retirement payment that employee received from employer was not "compensation for services," within meaning of City's nonresident income tax ordinance. Wyckoff v City of Detroit, 233 Mich App 220; 591 NW2d 71 (1998). (This case construed similar language in this section contained in the 1984 Code).*

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.612.*

laws.title: Determination and payment of tax due from unincorporated businesses, professions, and other activities
laws.content:
(a) *Liability for tax.* An unincorporated business, profession, or other activity conducted by one or more persons subject to the tax under this article as either a sole proprietorship or partnership shall not be taxable as such. The persons carrying on the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity are liable for income tax only in their separate and individual capacities and on the following basis:

(1) A resident proprietor or partner is taxable upon such resident proprietor's or partner's entire distributive share of the net profits of the activity regardless of where the activity is conducted;

CD44:17
$\S 44-2-10$

DETROIT CITY CODE

(2) A nonresident proprietor or partner is taxable only upon such resident proprietor’s or partner’s distributive share of the portion of the net profits of the activity which is attributable to the City under the allocation methods provided in this article; and

(3) In the hands of a proprietor or partner of an unincorporated activity, the character of any item of income taxable under this article is determined as if such item were realized by the individual proprietor or partner directly from the source from which it is realized by the unincorporated activity. In computing the taxable income for a taxable year of a person who is required to file a return, such person shall include therein such person’s taxable distributive share of the net profits for any partnership year ending within or with such person’s taxable year.

(b) Annual return. An unincorporated business, profession, or other activity owned by two or more persons shall file an annual information return setting forth:

(1) The entire net profit for the period covered by the return and the taxable portion of the net profit attributable to the City; and

(2) The names and addresses of the owners of the unincorporated activity and each owner’s taxable distributive share of the total net profit and each nonresident owner’s share of the taxable net profit attributable to the City.

(c) Computation and payment of owners’ tax by business.

(1) At the election of an unincorporated business, profession or other activity, the entity may compute and pay, on behalf of the owners, the tax due with respect to each owner’s share of the net profit of the activity after giving effect to exemptions to which each owner is entitled. This election is available to all unincorporated business entities having two or more owners regardless of the residence of the owners. The tax paid by the entity shall constitute all tax due with respect to each owner’s distributive share of the net profits of the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity.

(2) If the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity elects under this section to file a return and pay the tax on behalf of its owners, the election and filing are deemed to meet the requirements of this article for the filing of a return for each owner who has no other income subject to the tax, provided, that a return is required from any such owner having taxable income other than such owner’s distributive share of the net profits of the entity. In such case the entire income subject to the tax shall be included in the return and credit taken thereon for the tax paid in such owner’s behalf by the unincorporated activity.

(3) If the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity elects to pay the tax on behalf of the owners, the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity assumes the status of a taxpayer and is liable to interest and penalty if payment is not made by the due date in accordance with the calendar or fiscal year used by the unincorporated business, profession, or other activity.

(d) Procedure when profits not derived entirely from business in City. When the entire net profit of a business subject to the tax is not derived from business activities exclusively within the City, the portion of the entire net profit earned, as a result of work done, services rendered or other business activity conducted in the City, shall be determined under Subsections (1), (2) or (3) of this section.

(1) Separate accounting method. The taxpayer may petition for and the Administrator may grant approval of, or the Administrator may require, the separate accounting method. Where such method is petitioned for, the Administrator may require a statement explaining the manner in which the apportionment will be made, in sufficient detail, to determine whether the net profits attributable to the City will be apportioned with reasonable accuracy.

(2) Business allocation percentage method. The business allocation percentage method shall be used where such taxpayer is not granted approval to use the separate accounting method of allocation. The entire net profits of such taxpayer earned as a result of work done, services rendered, or other business activity conducted in the City shall be ascertained by determining the total “in-City” percentages of property, payroll, and sales. “In-City” percentages of property, payrolls and sales, separately computed, shall be determined as follows:

a. First, the taxpayer shall ascertain the percentage which the average net book value

CD44:18

laws.title: Taxation
laws.content:
§ 44-2-10

of the tangible personal property owned and the real property, including leasehold improvements, owned or used by the taxpayer in the business and situated within the City during the taxable period is of the average net book value of all of such property, including leasehold improvements owned or used by the taxpayer in the business during the same period wherever situated. Real property shall include real property rented or leased by the taxpayer, and the value of such property shall be deemed to be eight times the annual gross rental thereon. The term "gross rental of real property" means the actual sum of money or other consideration payable, directly or indirectly, by the taxpayer for the use or possession of real property and includes, but is not limited to:

1. An amount payable for the use or possession of real property, or any part thereof, whether designated as a fixed sum of money or as a percentage of sales, profits, or otherwise;

2. An amount payable as additional rent or in lieu of rent such as interest, taxes, insurance, repairs, or other amount required to be paid by the terms of a lease or other arrangement.

b. Second, the taxpayer shall ascertain the percentage which the total compensation paid to employees for work done or for services performed within the City is of the total compensation paid to all the taxpayer's employees within and outside the City during the period covered by the return. For allocation purposes, compensation shall be computed on the cash or accrual basis in accordance with the method used in computing the entire net income of the taxpayer. Where an employee performs services within and outside the City, the following examples are not inclusive but may serve as a guide for determining the amount to be treated as compensation for services performed within the City:

1. In the case of an employee compensated on a time basis, the proportion of the total amount received by such employee, which is working time within the City, is of such employee's total working time;

2. In the case of an employee compensated directly on the volume of business secured by such employee, such as a salesperson on a commission basis, the amount received by such employee for business attributable to such employee's efforts in the City;

3. In the case of an employee compensated on other results achieved, the proportion of the total compensation received which the value of such employee's services within the City bears to the value of all such employee's services.

c. Third, the taxpayer shall ascertain the percentage which the gross revenue of the taxpayer derived from sales made and services rendered in the City is of the total gross revenue from sales and services wherever made or rendered during the period covered by the return.

1. For the purposes of this subsection, the term "sales made in the City" means all sales where the goods, merchandise, or property is received in the City by the purchaser or by a person or firm designated by such purchaser. In the case of delivery of goods in the City to a common or private carrier or by other means of transportation, the place at which the delivery has been completed is considered as the place at which the goods are received by the purchaser. The following examples are not inclusive but may serve as a guide for determining sales made in the City:

(i) Sales to a customer in the City with shipments to a destination within the City from a location in the City or an out-of-City location are considered sales made in the City;

(ii) Sales to a customer in the City with shipments to a destination within the City directly

CD44:19
$\S 44-2-10$

DETROIT CITY CODE

from the taxpayer's in-City supplier or out-of-City supplier are considered sales made in the City;

(iii) Sales to a customer in the City with shipments directly to the customer at such customer's regularly maintained and established out-of-City location are considered out-of-City sales;

(iv) Sales to an out-of-City customer with shipments or deliveries to the customer's location within the City are considered sales made in the City; and

(v) Sales to an out-of-City customer with shipments to an out-of-City destination are considered out-of-City sales.

2. In the case of public utilities, or businesses furnishing the transportation services, the term "gross revenue" for the purposes of this section may be measured by such means as operating revenues, vehicle miles, revenue miles, passenger miles, ton miles, tonnage or such other methods as shall reasonably measure the proportion of gross revenue obtained in the City by such business.

3. In case the business of the taxpayer involves substantial business activities other than sales of goods and services, such other method of allocation shall be employed as shall reasonably measure the proportion of gross revenue obtained in the City by such business.

d. Fourth, the taxpayer shall add the percentages determined in accordance with Subsections (d)(2)a., b. and c. of this section and divide the total by three, and the result so obtained is the business allocation percentage. In determining this percentage, a factor shall be excluded from the computation only where the factor does not exist anywhere insofar as the taxpayer's business operation is concerned and,

in such case, the total of the percentages shall be divided by the number of factors actually used. The business allocation percentage shall be applied to the entire net profits, wherever derived, of the taxpayer subject to the tax to determine the net profits allocable to the City.

(3) Alternate accounting method. An alternative method of accounting shall be used where the taxpayer or the Administrator demonstrates that the net profits of the taxpayer allocable to the City cannot be justly and equitably determined under the separate accounting method or the business allocation percentage method or where undue expense to the taxpayer would result from complying therewith because of the taxpayer's manner of operations and methods of accounting. In such case, the Administrator, upon application of the taxpayer or upon such Administrator's own initiative, may approve or specify factors or methods of determination as will effect a just, nondiscriminatory, and reasonable result. Application to the Administrator to substitute other factors in the formula or to use a different method to allocate net profits shall be made in writing and state the specific grounds on which the substitution of factors or use of a different method is requested and the relief sought. No specific format need be followed in making the application. Once a taxpayer has filed under a substitute method, such taxpayer shall continue to file under such method until given permission by the Administrator to change.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-22; Code 1984, § 18-10-6)

State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.615 et seq.

laws.title: Taxation of capital gains and capital losses
laws.content:
(a) Capital gains and capital losses other than gains and losses on securities issued by the United States government shall be included in income only to the extent of that portion of the gains or losses which occur after the effective date of this division, which was January 1, 1965. In determining the amount of gain or loss, the taxpayer may use net proceeds from the sale or exchange less fair market value as of the effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965. The fair market value of property shall be determined by an appraisal or similar reliable evidence. The fair market value of a security shall be the last quoted price on the last business day prior to the

CD44:20

laws.title: Taxation
laws.content:
§ 44-2-13

effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965. For a security traded over the counter, the last quoted price shall be the last bid price on the last business day prior to the effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965. The taxpayer may determine the gain or loss on a transaction in the same manner as for federal income tax purposes taking into account only that portion thereof which occurs after the effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965. The portion of that gain or loss includable in computing taxable income will be the same proportion of the total gain or loss as the period of time the property was held after the effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965, bears to the total time the property was held.

(b) Where capital losses exceed capital gains in a taxable year, the unused portion may be utilized to the same extent and on the same basis as under the Internal Revenue Code.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-23; Code 1984, § 18-10-7)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.626.*

laws.title: Taxation of income from estates and trusts
laws.content:
(a) An estate or trust is not subject to tax under this article, provided, that the estate or trust shall be treated as a nonresident individual for purposes of Section 44-2-8 of this Code to the extent income of the estate or trust described in Section 44-2-9 of this Code is not includable in the return of a resident individual as income from estates and trusts. A resident individual shall include "income from estates and trusts" in such resident individual's income subject to tax under this article without regard to the situs of the estate or trust. For this purpose, the term "estate" means the estate of a deceased person during the period of administration or settlement, and the term "trust" means an *inter vivos* or testamentary trust created by an individual for the benefit of one or more persons.

(b) The term "income from estates" means "income" as defined in Section 643(b) of the Internal Revenue Code, properly paid, credited or distributed but not in excess of the resident individual's share of the distributable net income of the estate decreased by the amount of depreciation or depletion allowed the resident individual as a deduction under Section 642 of the Internal Revenue Code. The exceptions hereinafter set forth with respect to trusts are also applicable to income from estates. The term "income from trusts" means the amount of "income" as defined in Section 643(b) of the Internal Revenue Code distributed or required to be distributed under Section 652(a) or 662(a)(1) of the Internal Reve-

nue Code decreased by the amount of depreciation or depletion allowed the resident individual as a deduction by Section 642 of the Internal Revenue Code with the following exceptions:

(1) Dividends on stock of state and national banks and trust companies; and

(2) Interest from obligations of the United States, the states, or subordinate units of government of the states.

(c) Income received by a resident individual from a fiduciary shall retain the character it held in the hands of the fiduciary. With respect to trusts where the income is taxed to the grantor or some other person under Subpart E of Subpart J of the Internal Revenue Code, the grantor or other person shall include in such resident individual's return all items of income and deductions allowed by this article.

(d) An individual shall include "income from estates and trusts" in such individual's return in the same year as provided for in the Internal Revenue Code with respect to distributions of income from estates and trusts. The amount of income included in the return for the first tax year of a resident individual shall be computed, with respect to estates and trusts, as though the tax year of the estate or trust for federal income tax purposes began on the effective date of this article, which was January 1, 1965, and ended with the end of the tax year of the estate or trust for federal income tax purposes which ends next following the effective date of article, which was January 1, 1965.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-24; Code 1984, § 18-10-8)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.627, 141.628.*

laws.title: Exemptions
Deductions from gross income
Returns procedure
laws.content:
(a) *Filing of return required.* Every corporation doing business in the City, and every other person having income taxable under this article in any year, shall make and file with the City an annual return for that year on a form furnished or approved by the City, on or before the last day of the fourth month for the same calendar year, fiscal year or other accounting period, as has been accepted by the Internal Revenue Service for federal income tax purposes for the taxpayer. A married couple may file a joint return and, in such case, the tax liability is joint and several.

(b) *Contents of return.* The annual return shall set forth:

(1) The number of exemptions, place of residence, place of employment, and other pertinent information as shall reasonably be required;

(2) The aggregate amount of compensation, dividends, interest, net profit from rentals, capital gains less capital losses, net profits from business, and other income subject to the tax;

(3) The total amount of the tax imposed by this article;

(4) The amount of the tax previously withheld or paid;

(5) Credits provided for in this article; and

(6) The balance of the tax due or to be refunded.

(c) *Remittance of tax due or claim for refund.*

(1) A balance of the tax that is due the City at the time of filing an annual return shall be paid with the return, unless the balance is less than $1.00, in which case payment is not required. Where the annual return reflects an overpayment of the tax, the declaration of the overpayment on the return constitutes a claim for refund.

(2) Subject to Subsection (c)(5) of this section, where the City agrees that a claim for refund is valid,

CD44:23
§ 44-2-15

DETROIT CITY CODE

the City shall apply the overpayment first to a delinquent tax liability owed to the City by the taxpayer under this article. The City shall apply any remaining overpayment against a subsequent City income tax liability or, at the election of the taxpayer, and where indicated on the return, shall refund the overpayment. However, the City shall not pay refunds of less than $1.00.

(3) Where a valid claim for refund of taxes due is filed for the taxable year 1992, or any taxable year after 1992, interest at the rate established in MCL 205.30 shall be added to the refund, beginning 45 days after the claim is filed or 45 days after the date established under this article for the filing of the return, whichever is later. This does not apply to any refund under the Section 44-2-16(b)(2) of this Code.

(4) If the claim for refund is reflected on a joint tax return, the Administrator shall allocate to each joint taxpayer such taxpayer’s share of the refund. The amount allocated to each taxpayer shall be applied to such taxpayer’s respective liabilities under this article.

(5) Where the Administrator determines that all or a portion of the refund claimed on a joint tax return is subject to application to a liability of an obligated spouse, the Administrator shall notify the joint taxpayers by first class mail sent to the address shown on the joint return. The notice shall be accompanied by a non-obligated spouse allocation form. The notice shall state all of the following:

a. That all or a portion of the refund claimed by the joint taxpayers is subject to interception to satisfy a liability of one or of both spouses;

b. The nature of the liability, and the name of the obligated spouse;

c. That a non-obligated spouse may claim such spouse’s share of the refund by filing a non-obligated spouse allocation notice with the City not more than 30 days after the date the notice was mailed; and

d. A statement of the penalties under Subsection (c)(8) of this section.

(6) A non-obligated spouse who wishes to claim such spouse’s share of a tax refund shall file with the City a non-obligated spouse allocation form. The non-obligated spouse allocation form shall be in a form specified by the Administrator, and shall require each spouse to state the amount of income or other tax base, and all adjustments to income or other tax base, including all subtractions, additions, deductions, credits, and exemptions stated on the joint tax return, that are the basis for the claimed refund, and an allocation of those amounts between the obligated and non-obligated spouse. In allocating these amounts, all of the following apply:

a. Individual income shall be allocated to the spouse who earned the income, and joint income shall be allocated equally between the spouses;

b. Each spouse shall be allocated the personal exemptions that such spouse would be entitled to claim had each spouse filed separate federal returns, except that dependency exemptions shall be prorated according to the relative income of the spouses;

c. Adjustments resulting from a business shall be allocated to the spouse who claimed income from the business; and

d. Ownership of other assets relevant to the allocation shall be disclosed upon request of the Administrator.

(7) A non-obligated spouse allocation form shall be signed by both joint taxpayers, provided, that where the signature of the obligated spouse cannot be obtained, the form may be submitted without such spouse’s signature. The non-obligated spouse shall certify that such spouse has made a good faith effort to obtain the signature of the obligated spouse, and shall state the reason that the signature was not obtained.

(8) A person who knowingly makes a false statement on a non-obligated spouse allocation form is subject to a penalty of $25.00, or 25 percent of the claim for such spouse’s share of the refund, whichever is greater, along with other penalties that are provided for in this article.

(9) A non-obligated spouse, to whom the Administrator has sent a notice under Subsection (c)(5) of this section and who fails to file a non-obligated spouse allocation form within 30 days after the date the notice was mailed, shall be barred from commencing any action against the

CD44:24

laws.title: Taxation
laws.content:
§ 44-2-16

City to recover an amount withheld to satisfy a liability of the obligated spouse to which a joint tax refund is applied under this section. The payment by the City of any amount applied to a liability of a taxpayer under this section shall release the City from all liability to the obligated spouse, the non-obligated spouse, and any other person having or claiming any interest in the amount paid.

(d) Return based on federal income tax return. Where total income, total deductions, net profits or other figures are derived from the taxpayer’s federal income tax return, any item of income not subject to the City income tax and unallowable deductions shall be eliminated in determining net income subject to the City tax. The fact that a taxpayer is not required to file a federal income tax return does not relieve the taxpayer from filing a City tax return.

(e) Consolidated return. For the purpose of determining net profit allocable to the City under this article, a corporate taxpayer may elect to file a consolidated return, including any subsidiaries whose voting stock is more than 50 percent owned by the taxpayer, where such return will more properly reflect the net profits and activities of the taxpayer in the City. Where necessary, the City may require a consolidated return to properly determine net profits of the taxpayer allocable to the City.

(f) Amended return. An amended return shall be filed on a form obtainable from the City where necessary to report additional income and pay an additional tax due, or to claim a refund of tax overpaid. Within 90 days after final determination of a federal tax liability that also affects the computation of a taxpayer’s City income tax liability, the taxpayer shall prepare and file with the City an amended City income tax return showing income subject to the City tax based upon the final determination of federal income tax liability, and pay any additional tax shown due on the return, or make a claim for refund of an overpayment. A taxpayer shall not change the method of accounting or apportionment of net profits after the due date for filing the original return, or any extensions for filing of the original return.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-26; Code 1984, § 18-10-11; Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-11), eff. 12-11-1998)

State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.641 et seq.

laws.title: Collection of tax
laws.content:
(a) Withholding by employer; amount to be withheld.

(1) An employer, doing business or maintaining an establishment within the City, shall withhold from each payment to the employer’s employees, on and after the effective date of this section, which was July 1, 1981, the tax on their compensation subject to the tax, after giving effect to exemptions, as follows:

a. Residents.

1. At a rate equal to the rate set in this article, but not to exceed three percent of all compensation paid to an employee who is a resident where the employee is not subject to withholding in any other city levying an income tax; or

2. At a rate equal to the percentage rate of tax on resident individuals as set forth in this article, less the percentage rate of income tax levied by any other city where the employee works, on all compensation earned by the resident in such city.

b. Nonresidents. At a rate equal to the rate set forth in this article on nonresidents, but not to exceed 1.5 percent of compensation paid to the employee for work done or services performed in the City designated by the employee as the employee’s predominant place of employment. The withholding rate shall be applied to the percentage of the employee’s total compensation equal to the employee’s estimated percentage of work to be done or services to be performed in the City for that employer, but no withholding shall be required where the estimated percentage of work is less than 25 percent.

(2) Withholding by employer; employer as trustee for the City. An employer withholding the tax is deemed to hold such tax as a trustee for the City.

(3) Withholding by employer; liability. An employer who is required to withhold and who fails or refuses to deduct and withhold is liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld. The liability shall be discharged upon payment of the tax by the employee, but the employer is

CD44:25
§ 44-2-16

DETROIT CITY CODE

not relieved of penalties and interest that are provided for in this article for such failure or refusal.

(4) Withholding by employer; income not subject to withholding. Employers shall not withhold any tax from the following payments:

a. Compensation paid to domestic help;

b. Compensation paid to a person who is not an employee, including an independent contractor;

c. An amount allowed and paid to an employee as reimbursement for expenses necessarily and actually incurred by the employee in the actual performance of such employee’s services, which is deductible by the employer; and

d. Compensation paid or income derived by a qualified taxpayer.

(5) Withholding by employer; failure of the employer to withhold or pay City. Where the tax is not withheld, an employee is not excused from filing a return and paying the tax on such employee’s compensation. Where the tax is withheld, but an employer fails to pay the tax to the City, the employee is not liable for the tax so withheld.

(6) Withholding by employer; withholding certificates.

a. Filing and contents. An employee with compensation subject to tax shall file with such employee’s employer a form upon which the employee states the number of exemptions claimed, the city or township of residence, the predominant place of employment, whether or not the employee claims status as a qualified taxpayer of a Renaissance Zone, and the percentage of work done, or services performed, at the predominant place of employment. The percentage shall be expressed as "less than 25 percent," "40 percent," "60 percent," "80 percent," or "100 percent." The employer shall retain the form and rely upon the information therein for withholding purposes, unless directed by the City to withhold on another basis, and where the employee claims status as a qualified taxpayer based on residence in a Renaissance Zone, the employer shall forward a copy of the form to the City. Where information submitted by the employee appears not to be true, correct and complete, the employer shall advise the City of the same.

b. Revised certificates; qualified taxpayer within a Renaissance Zone. Except as provided in Subsection (a)(2) of this section, an employee shall file a revised form with their employer within ten days after the number of exemptions decreases, or when a change in residence from or to a taxing city occurs. In addition, the employee may file a revised form when the number of the employee’s exemptions increases. An employee shall file a revised form by December 1st of each year where such employee’s predominant place of employment, or estimate of the percentage of work done or services to be rendered in the City, or status as a qualified taxpayer of a Renaissance Zone, will change for the ensuing year. Revised withholding certificates shall not be given retroactive effect.

c. Refusal of employee to file. Where, upon the request of an employer, an employee refuses to furnish a withholding certificate, the employer shall withhold a percentage of the employee’s total compensation that is equal to the percentage rate of tax on resident individuals as set forth in this article, and the employer shall report and pay the withholding on the basis of the best information in the possession of the employer.

(7) Withholding by employer; determination of amount to be withheld.

a. Withholding tables. The City shall provide withholding tables establishing the amounts to be withheld for various tax rates, wage brackets, numbers of exemptions, and pay periods. An employer who uses the tables fully discharges the employer’s duty to withhold. An employer may elect not to use the tables, but in doing so to discharge fully such employer’s duty to withhold, the employer shall withhold the applicable percent of taxable compensation after provision for exemptions.

CD44:26

laws.title: Taxation
laws.content:
§ 44-2-16

b. Amount to be withheld from the first compensation after the effective date of the tax levy. The first compensation paid an employee on or after the effective date of the tax levy is subject to withholding, at the option of the employer, on either of the following bases:

1. On the full amount of compensation paid; or

2. On the proportion of compensation paid for work done or services performed on or after the effective date of the levy.

(8) Withholding by the employer; over-withheld tax; refund. Where an employer withholds more than the apparent tax liability of an employee due to an increase in the number of exemptions claimed during the year, or due to the actual percentage of work performed in the City by a nonresident being less than the estimated percentage, or due to a change of residence during the year to or from a taxing City, or due to any reason other than the employer’s error, the employer shall neither refund the excess to the employee nor offset the excess by under-withholding in a subsequent period. The employee shall claim a refund from the City on the employee’s annual return. Correction of an over- or under-withholding as a result of an employer’s error shall be made as follows:

a. Where the error is discovered in the same quarter in which it is made, the employer shall make the necessary adjustment on a subsequent pay and include only the corrected amount on the quarterly return;

b. Where the error is discovered in a subsequent quarter of the same calendar year, the employer shall make the necessary adjustment on a subsequent pay and report the error on the quarterly return; or

c. Where the error is discovered in the following calendar year or if the employer-employee relationship has terminated, the procedure shall be as follows:

1. The employee or former employee shall apply to the City for a refund in case of an over-withholding. Upon proper verification, the City shall refund to such employee, or former employee, the amount of the over-withholding; or

2. If a deficiency is discovered, the employer shall notify the City and the employee, or former employee, who shall pay the City the additional tax due in such employee’s, or former employee’s, annual tax return.

(b) (1) Employer’s returns; filing quarterly return. An employer shall file a return, furnished by or obtainable upon request from the City, and pay to the City the full amount of the tax withheld on or before the last day of the month following the close of each calendar quarter, except, that where, during any calendar month other than the last month of a calendar quarter, the amount withheld exceeds $100.00, the employer shall deposit the amount withheld with the City Treasurer before the end of the next calendar month.

(2) Employer’s return; annual reconciliation of quarterly return. An employer shall file a reconciliation of quarterly returns on or before the last day of February, following each calendar year in which the employer has withheld from an employee’s compensation. A deficiency is due when the reconciliation is filed. Where the employer made monthly or quarterly payments, or both, in excess of the amount withheld from an employee’s compensation, the City shall refund, upon proper verification, the excess to the employer.

(3) Information return. In addition to the reconciliation, the employer shall file an information return for each employee from whom the City income tax has been withheld and each employee subject to withholding under this article, setting forth the employee’s name, address and social security number, the total amount of compensation paid the employee during the year, and the amount of City income tax withheld. The information return shall be on a copy of the federal W-2 form, or on a form furnished or approved by the City. A copy of the information return shall be furnished to the employee.

(4) Filing of returns upon cessation of business. Where an employer goes out of business or otherwise ceases to be an employer, reconciliation forms

CD44:27
§ 44-2-16

DETROIT CITY CODE

and the information return forms shall be filed with the City by the date the final withholding return and payment are due.

(c) (1) Declaration of estimated tax; who is required to file; filing date. A person who anticipates taxable income from which the City income tax will not be withheld shall file a declaration of estimated tax on a form furnished by or obtainable on request from the City. A calendar year taxpayer shall file a declaration on or before each April 30th. A taxpayer on a fiscal year basis, or other accounting period, shall file a declaration within four months after the beginning of each fiscal year or other accounting period.

Where a taxpayer has not previously been required to file, the declaration shall be filed on or before the first date for making a quarterly payment which occurs after the taxpayer becomes subject to the requirement to file a declaration. A taxpayer shall file a declaration for the same calendar year, fiscal year, or other accounting period that has been accepted by the Internal Revenue Service for federal income tax purposes. A declaration by an individual or unincorporated entity is not required, where the total estimated tax, less any credits applicable to the tax, does not exceed $100.00. A declaration by a corporation is not required where the total estimated tax, less any credits applicable to the tax, does not exceed $250.00. A declaration by or on behalf of an estate or trust is not required.

(2) Declaration of estimated tax; computation of estimated tax. A taxpayer’s annual return for the preceding year may be used as the basis for computing a declaration of estimated tax for the current year, or the taxpayer may use the same figures used for estimating federal income tax adjusted to exclude any income or deductions not taxable or permissible under this article.

(3) Declaration of estimated tax; payment. The estimated tax may be paid in full with the declaration or in four equal installments on or before the last day of the fourth, sixth, ninth, and 13th months after the beginning of the taxable year.

(4) Declaration of estimated tax; amendment. An amended declaration may be filed when making a quarterly payment, and the unpaid balance shown due thereon shall be paid in equal installments over the remaining payment dates.

(d) Annual return. The filing of a declaration of estimated tax does not excuse the taxpayer from filing an annual return even though there is no change in the declared tax liability. An annual return shall be filed by the end of the fourth month of the year following that for which the declaration was filed. Upon written request of a taxpayer, the Administrator may extend the time for filing the annual return for a period not to exceed six months. The Administrator may require a tentative return and payment of the estimated tax. A penalty or interest shall not be assessed where the return is filed, the final tax paid within the extended time and all other filing and payment requirements of this article are satisfied, and the estimated tax paid equals 70 percent or more of the tax shown due on the final return or 70 percent or more of the tax shown due on the taxpayer’s return for the immediately preceding taxable year.

(e) Credit for taxes paid to other municipalities. An individual who is a resident of the City and received:

(1) Net profits from a business, profession or rental of real or tangible personal property;

(2) Gains from the sale or exchange of real or tangible personal property; or

(3) Salaries, wages, commissions or other compensation for work done or services performed or rendered;

in each case outside the City, and who is subject to and has paid an income tax on this income to another municipality, shall be allowed a credit against the City income tax for the amount paid to the other municipality. The credit shall not exceed the amount of taxes which would be assessed under this article on the same amount of income of a nonresident.

(f) Renaissance Zone; deductions from gross income. A qualified taxpayer within the boundaries of a Renaissance Zone, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, shall be entitled to certain deductions from gross income as provided for in Section 44-2-17(a) of this Code.

(g) Business; sale of; disposition of assets. Where a person liable for the tax imposed under this article sells a business or the stock of goods of a business, or quits a business, the person shall make a final return to the City within 15 days after the date the business or stock of goods is sold or the person quits the business. The pur-

CD44:28

laws.title: Taxation
laws.content:
§ 44-2-17

chaser, or succeeding purchasers, if any, who purchase a going or closed business or stock of goods of a going or closed business shall escrow sufficient money to cover the amount of taxes, interest and penalties that may be due and unpaid until the former owner produces a receipt from the Administrator, which shows that the taxes due have been paid, or a certificate, which states that taxes are not due.

(h) *Business; waiver of confidentiality.* Where an owner of a business subject to the tax imposed under this article provides a written waiver of confidentiality, the Administrator may release to a purchaser a business’s known tax liability, for the purposes of establishing an escrow account for the payment of taxes.

(i) *Business; purchaser; personal liability.* Where the purchaser or succeeding purchasers of a business or stock of goods of a business fails to comply with the escrow requirements of this section, the purchaser is personally liable for the payment of the taxes, interest, and penalties accrued and unpaid by the business of the former owner. The purchaser’s, or succeeding purchaser’s, personal liability is limited to the fair market value of the business, less the amount of any proceeds applied to balances due on secured interests that are superior to any lien provided for in this article.

(j) *Corporation; personal liability of corporate officers.* Where a corporation that is liable for the tax imposed under this article fails for any reason to file the required returns, or to pay the tax due, any officers of the corporation who have control or supervision of, or who are charged with the responsibility for, making the returns or payments are personally liable for the failure to file or pay. The signature of any corporate officer on a return or negotiable instrument submitted in payment for a tax is *prima facie* evidence of the officer’s responsibility for making the returns and payments.

(k) *Corporation; dissolution; continuing liability.* The dissolution of a corporation does not discharge an officer’s liability for a prior failure of the corporation to make a return or remit a tax due. The sum due for a liability may be assessed and collected under this article.

(l) *Fractions of a cent.* In withholding the tax under this article, a fractional part of a cent shall be disregarded, unless it amounts to one-half cent or more, in which case it shall be increased to one cent. For tax years after the 1996 tax year, where any amount other than a whole dollar amount is used, the Administrator shall disregard the fractional part of the dollar unless the fractional part amounts to $0.50 or more, in which case the amount shall be increased by $1.00.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-27; Code 1984, § 18-10-12; Ord. No. 460-H, § 1(21-8-27), eff. 7-1-1981; Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-12), eff. 12-11-1998)

laws.title: Renaissance Zones
laws.content:
(a) *Gross income; deductions.* Notwithstanding any other provision of this article, and to the extent and for the duration provided in the Michigan Renaissance Zone Act, being MCL 125.2681 *et seq.*, for the 1997 tax year and each tax year thereafter, in determining income subject to tax hereunder a qualified taxpayer, to the extent a deduction is applicable, may deduct from gross income an amount equal to one of the following for the specified types of taxpayers:

(1) *Qualified taxpayer—Individual.*

a. For a qualified taxpayer—individual, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, except as provided for in Subsections (a)(2) and (a)(3) of this section, income subject to the tax that is earned or received in the tax year during the period of time that the taxpayer was a qualified taxpayer.

b. Capital gains subject to the tax that is received during the tax year for the period of time that the taxpayer was a qualified taxpayer. The deduction allowed under this subsection shall be pro-rated based on the percentage of time that the asset was held by the taxpayer while the taxpayer was a qualified taxpayer.

c. Income received by the qualified taxpayer from winning:

1. An online lottery game sponsored by the State of Michigan where the date of the drawing for that game is after the date on which the taxpayer became a qualified taxpayer of a Renaissance Zone; and/or

2. An instant lottery game sponsored by the State of Michigan, where the taxpayer was a qualified taxpayer of a Renaissance Zone on the validation date of the lottery ticket for that game.

laws.content:
§ 44-2-17

shall not use any portion of income subject to tax under this article that is derived from illegal activity, whether conducted in a Renaissance Zone or elsewhere within the City, to calculate the deduction allowed under this section. For a qualified taxpayer—individual, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, who is an individual, any portion of income subject to tax under this article that is derived from illegal activity conducted anywhere shall not be used to calculate the deduction allowed under this section.

(c) Income; casino activities. For a qualified taxpayer—corporation or unincorporated business, profession and other activities, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, any portion of the taxpayer’s tax liability that is attributable to business activity related to the operation of a casino, and business activity that is associated or affiliated with the operation of a casino, including, but not limited to, the operation of a parking lot, hotel, motel or retail store, shall not be used to calculate a credit under this section.

(d) Income; calculation for this purpose only. Income used to calculate a deduction under any other section of this article shall not be used to calculate a deduction under this section.

(e) Residency requirements; tax year.

(1) Residency requirements completed before end of tax year following residency. Where a taxpayer becomes a qualified taxpayer, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code before the end of the tax year in which the qualified taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone, the qualified taxpayer may claim the deduction allowed under this section for that tax year.

(2) Residency requirements completed subsequent to tax year following residency. Where a taxpayer becomes a qualified taxpayer, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, in a year subsequent to the tax year in which the qualified taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone, the following apply:

a. If a qualified taxpayer completes the residency requirement in a tax year subsequent to the tax year in which the taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone, and before the date for filing the annual return under this article for the tax year in which the taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone, the taxpayer may claim the deduction under this section for the tax year in which the taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone.

b. If a qualified taxpayer completes the residency requirement in a tax year subsequent to the tax year in which the taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone and after the date for filing the annual return under this article for the tax year in which the taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone, the qualified taxpayer may claim the deduction allowed under this section for the tax year in which the residency requirement is completed on the annual return for the tax year in which the residency requirement is completed, and may claim the deduction for the tax year in which the qualified taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone by filing an amended return for that tax year in which the qualified taxpayer first resided in the Renaissance Zone.

(f) Eligibility; annual return. To be eligible for the deduction provided for in this section, a taxpayer shall file an annual return under this article.

(g) Eligibility; withholding form. A qualified taxpayer shall file a withholding form prescribed by the City with such taxpayer’s employer after the date the taxpayer becomes a qualified taxpayer, as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code or, at the option of the City, for taxpayers who claim to be qualified taxpayers under Subsection (1) of the definition of the term "qualified taxpayer" in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, the taxpayer shall file with the City a form prescribed by the City after the date the taxpayer completes the requirements under Subsection (a) of this section. Where the City verifies the information on the form, the City shall issue a certificate of qualification to the taxpayer, which the taxpayer shall file with such taxpayer’s employer. Where a taxpayer who filed a form under this subsection is no longer a qualified taxpayer as defined in Section 44-2-6 of this Code, the taxpayer shall send a written notice of that change in status to the City not more than ten days after the change in status occurs.

(h) False claim; interest and penalties. Where the Administrator finds that a taxpayer has claimed a deduction under this section to which the taxpayer is not entitled, the taxpayer is subject to the interest and penalty provisions under this article.

(i) Deduction; continuation after expiration of Renaissance Zone designation. The deduction allowed under this section continues through the tax year in which the Renaissance Zone designation expires.

(j) Change of status. Where a taxpayer who was a qualified taxpayer during the tax year changes status, and is not a qualified taxpayer or vice versa, income subject to tax under this article shall be determined separately for income in each status.

laws.title: Transfer of portion of City income tax revenues to Police Department budget
laws.content:

laws.title: Information to remain confidential; penalty
laws.content:
(a) *Confidential information.* Any information gained by the Administrator, City Treasurer, or other City official, agent or employee as a result of a return, investigation, hearing, or verification required or authorized by this article is confidential, except for official purposes in connection with the administration of the article and except in accordance with a proper judicial order.

(b) *Divulging information; penalty.* Any person who divulges any confidential information delineated in Subsection (a) of this section, except for official purposes, is subject to issuance of a misdemeanor violation and, upon conviction, is subject to receiving a fine of up to $500.00, to being sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, in the discretion of the court, for each offense. In addition, any City employee who divulges this confidential information is subject to discharge for misconduct.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-31; Code 1984, § 18-10-16; Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-16), eff. 12-11-1998)

laws.title: Enforcement
laws.content:
(a) *Penalties and adjustments.*

(1) *Interest; tax years prior to 1992.* All taxes imposed upon taxpayers in a taxable year before the 1992 taxable year, and moneys withheld by employers under this article and remaining unpaid after the taxes or money withheld are due, bear interest from the due date at the rate of 0.5 percent per month until paid.

(2) *Interest; 1992—1996 tax years.* For the 1992 taxable year and each subsequent taxable year before the 1997 taxable year, all taxes imposed upon a taxpayer and money withheld by an employer under this article, and remaining unpaid after the taxes or money withheld are due, bear interest from the due date at the current monthly rate of one percentage point above the adjusted prime rate per annum per month until the tax or money is paid.

(3) *Interest; 1997 tax year forward.* For taxable years after the 1996 taxable year, where the amount of a tax paid is less than the amount that should have been paid, or an excessive claim for credit has been made, the deficiency and interest on the deficiency at the current monthly interest rate of one percentage point above the adjusted prime rate per annum from the time the tax was due and until paid, are due and payable after a final assessment as provided in Subsection (c)(2) of this section.

(4) *Deficiency; interest on.* A deficiency in an estimated payment required by this article shall be treated in the same manner as a tax due, and is subject to the same current monthly interest rate of one percentage point above the adjusted prime rate per annum from the time the payment was due until paid.

(5) *Interest; term "adjusted prime rate" defined.* The term "adjusted prime rate" shall mean the average predominant prime rate quoted by not less than three commercial banks to large businesses, as determined by the Michigan Depart-

CD44:33
$\S 44-2-36$

DETROIT CITY CODE

ment of Treasury. For tax years before the 1997 tax year, the adjusted prime rate is to be based on the average prime rate charged by not less than three commercial banks during the 12-month period ending on September 30th. One percentage point shall be added to the adjusted prime rate, and the resulting sum shall be divided by 12 to establish the current monthly interest rate. The resulting current monthly interest rate based on the 12-month period ending September 30th, becomes effective on January 1st of the following year. For tax years after the 1996 tax year, the term "adjusted prime rate" means that term as defined in and determined under Section 23 of the Michigan Revenue Act, being MCL 205.23.

(6) Penalties. A person who fails to file a return, pay the tax, or remit withholding when due, is liable, in addition to interest, to a penalty of one percent of the amount of the unpaid tax for each month or fraction thereof, not to exceed a total penalty of 25 percent of the unpaid tax. Where a return is filed, or remittance is paid, after the time specified, and it is shown to the satisfaction of the City that the failure was due to reasonable cause, and not to willful neglect, the penalty shall be waived by the Administrator. If the total interest, or interest and penalty to be assessed, is less than $2.00, the Administrator shall instead assess a penalty in the amount of $ 2.00.

(7) Amended return resulting from federal audit. Interest or a penalty shall not be imposed on an additional tax assessment where, within 90 days from final determination of a federal tax liability which also affects the computation of the taxpayer's City income tax liability, the taxpayer prepares and files an amended City income tax return that shows income subject to the City tax based upon the final determination of federal income tax liability, and pays the additional tax shown due thereon or makes claim for refund of an overpayment. Interest shall not be allowed on a refund of the City income tax resulting from a final determination of federal tax liability.

(8) Underestimation of tax on declaration. Interest and a penalty shall not be imposed for underestimating the tax where the total amount of the tax withheld and paid by declaration equals at least 70 percent or more of the tax shown due on the final return, or 70 percent or more of the tax shown on the taxpayer's return for the preceding taxable year.

(9) Liability of employee for noncompliance of employer. An employee shall not be penalized because of the failure of their employer to report or pay tax withheld from the employee when, in fact, the employer has withheld the proper amount of tax.

(10) Penalty; negligence without intent to defraud. Except as provided in Subsection (a)(11) of this section, where any part of the deficiency or an excessive claim for credit is due to negligence but without intent to defraud, a penalty shall be added in the amount of $10.00 or ten percent of the total amount of the deficiency in the tax, whichever is greater, plus interest as provided in Subsections (a)(1) through (a)(4) of this section. The penalty becomes due and payable after a final assessment is issued as provided in Subsection (b)(2) of this section. Where a taxpayer subject to a penalty under this subsection demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Administrator that the deficiency or excess claim for credit was due to reasonable cause, the Administrator shall waive the penalty.

(11) Penalty; intentional disregard of article; no intent to defraud. Where any part of the deficiency or an excessive claim for credit is due to intentional disregard of this article but without intent to defraud, a penalty shall be added in the amount of $ 25.00 or 25 percent of the total amount of the deficiency in the tax, whichever is greater, plus interest as prescribed by Subsections (a)(1) through (a)(4) of this section. The penalty becomes due and payable after a final assessment is issued as provided in Subsection (b)(2) of this section. Where a penalty imposed under this subsection is successfully disputed by the taxpayer, the Administrator shall not impose a penalty prescribed by Subsection (a)(10) of this section to the tax otherwise due.

(12) Penalty; fraudulent intent. Where any part of the deficiency or an excessive claim for credit is due to a fraudulent intent to evade the tax imposed under this article, or to obtain a refund for a fraudulent claim, a penalty of 100 percent of the deficiency, plus interest as provided in Sub-

laws.title: (3) Assessment final when no protest to proposed assessment is filed
laws.content: Where a protest is not filed in response to a proposed assessment, a taxpayer or employer is deemed to have received a final assessment 30 days after receipt of the proposed assessment.

laws.title: (c) No assessment required
laws.content: Where any employer or a taxpayer files a return showing the amount of tax or withholding due the City but fails to pay the amount to the City Treasurer, the Administrator is not required to issue a proposed assessment or a final assessment. The Administrator shall issue a ten-day demand for payment and, where no payment or satisfactory evidence of payment is made within the ten days, the Administrator may recover the tax with interest and penalties thereon in the name of the City in any court of competent jurisdiction as other debts are recoverable, or prosecute for violation of this article under Section 44-2-7 of this Code, or both.

Where the Administrator believes that collection of the tax withheld from an employee’s compensation, as imposed under this article, will be jeopardized by delay, the City shall immediately assess the tax and interest and additions provided by this article, whether or not the time otherwise prescribed by this article for making the return and paying or depositing the tax has expired. The tax, interest, and additions thereupon shall become immediately due and payable and the City shall make an immediate notice and demand for payment notwithstanding when the withheld tax is otherwise due and payable.

Where the Administrator finds that a person liable for the tax administered under this article intends to depart from the City quickly, or remove property from this City, or conceal the person or the person’s property in the City, or to do any other act tending to render, wholly or partly, ineffectual proceedings to collect the tax unless proceedings are brought without delay, the Administrator shall give notice of the findings to the person together with a demand for an immediate return and immediate payment of the tax. A warrant or warrant-notice of levy may issue immediately upon issuance of a jeopardy assessment. When the warrant or warrant-notice is issued, the tax shall become immediately due and payable. Where the person is not in default in making a return, or paying a tax prescribed by this article, and furnishes evidence satisfactory to the Administrator that the return will be filed, and the tax to which the finding relates will be paid, the tax shall not be payable before the time otherwise fixed for payment.

(e) Collection of unpaid taxes and refund of overpaid taxes.

(1) Time for payment of deficiencies. A tax deficiency, as finally determined, and interest or penalties thereon, shall be paid within 30 days after receipt of a final assessment where no appeal is made.

(2) Time limitation; assessments or refunds. Except in case of fraud, failure to file a return, failure to comply with the withholding provisions of this article or omission of substantial portions of income subject to the tax, an additional assessment shall not be made after four years from the date the return was due, including extensions thereof, or the tax was paid, whichever is later. An omission of more than 25 percent of gross income is considered a substantial omission of income. A declaration of estimated tax is not considered a return under this section.

(3) Time limitation; waiver of the federal statute of limitations. Where the Internal Revenue Service and a taxpayer execute a waiver of the federal statute of limitations as to a taxable year, the expiration of the period within which an additional assessment may be made by the Administrator, or a claim for refund filed by the taxpayer for such taxable year for City income tax purposes, shall be six months from the date of expiration of the waiver.

(4) Time limitation; tax erroneously paid. Except as otherwise provided for in this article, a tax erroneously paid shall not be refunded, unless a claim for refund is made within four years from the date the payment was made, or the original final return was due, including extensions thereof, whichever is later, unless the Administrator and the taxpayer mutually agree to extend the time for assessment of refund. A declaration of estimated tax is not considered a return under this section. Upon denial of a refund, a taxpayer may follow the same procedure for appeal as provided for in the case of a deficiency assessment.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-32; Code 1984, § 18-10-17; Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-17), eff. 12-11-1998)

laws.title: Appeal of Income Tax Board of Review decision to Michigan Tax Tribunal
laws.content:
A taxpayer or employer aggrieved by a final assessment, denial, decision, or order of the Income Tax Board of Review may appeal the assessment, denial, decision, or order to the Michigan Tax Tribunal not more than 35 days after the final assessment, denial, decision, or order is issued. The uncontested portion of a final assessment, order, or decision shall be paid as a prerequisite to appeal. An appeal under this subsection shall be perfected as provided under the Michigan Tax Tribunal Act, being MCL 205.701 et seq., and rules promulgated under that Act for the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Not more than 35 days after a final order of the Michigan Tax Tribunal, the taxpayer, employer or other person shall pay the City the taxes, interest and penalty found due to the City, and the City shall refund to the taxpayer, employer or other person any amount found to have been overpaid by the taxpayer or other person.

(Code 1964, § 21-8-37; Code 1984, § 18-10-22(b); Ord. No. 43-98, § 1(18-10-22), eff. 12-11-1998)

laws.title: Judicial determination of appeal
laws.content:
(a) Appeal from the Tax Tribunal. If a taxpayer, employer, person or City is aggrieved by a decision of the Michigan Tax Tribunal, the aggrieved party may take an appeal by right from the decision to the Court of Appeals. The appeal shall be taken on the record made before the Michigan Tax Tribunal. The taxpayer, employer, other person, or City may take further appeal to the Michigan Supreme Court in accordance with the court rules governing appeals to that court.

(b) Finality of assessment. An assessment is final, conclusive, and not subject to further challenge 90 days after the issuance of the final assessment, decision, or order of the Administrator. No person shall be entitled to a refund of any tax, interest, or penalty paid pursuant

**ARTICLE III. IMPROVEMENTS AND SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS***

**DIVISION 1. GENERALLY**

**Sec. 44-3-1. Public improvement reserve fund—Established.**

There is hereby created and established a public improvement reserve fund, for acquiring, extending, altering, enlarging or repairing capital cost public improvements which the City may be authorized, by the Charter or the general laws of the state, to acquire, extend, alter, enlarge or repair.

(Code 1964, $\S 21-1-8$ ; Code 1984, $\S 18-12-1$ )

**Sec. 44-3-2. Same—Certain money and credits to be credited to fund.**

All money and credits appropriated for capital cost improvements, except as provided for in this section, shall hereafter be credited to the public improvement reserve fund, and such money and credits accumulated in such fund shall not be transferred, encumbered or otherwise disposed of except for the purpose of acquiring, extending, altering, enlarging or repairing such capital cost public improvements. Such other money, credits and miscellaneous revenue as are not otherwise pledged, appropriated or encumbered may be authorized to be transferred and credited to such fund by resolution of the City Council, provided, that money and credits appropriated for capital cost improvements from revenues, the use of which is restricted by statute, the Charter, or this Code to special purposes shall not be credited to the public improvement reserve fund, provided further, that capital cost appropriations for equipment shall not be credited to such fund, but to the fund and purpose for which the same was raised or appropriated.

(Code 1964, $\S 21-1-9$ ; Code 1984, $\S 18-12-2$ )

**Sec. 44-3-3. Local improvements not to be made in districts where unpaid taxes equal 20 percent or more of total tax assessment; exceptions.**

No local improvement of any kind, nature or description shall be undertaken by the City or be contracted for in any districts where the amount of unpaid general City taxes equals 20 percent or more of the total tax assessments in such district or where the amount of delinquent special assessments in such district amount to 20 percent or more of the total special assessments therein; provided, that where a portion of the cost of the local improvement is paid for by federal funds, the City Council, upon the recommendation of the Director of the Department of Public Works may waive this requirement. It shall be the duty of the Department of Public Works having charge of such improvement to file a written statement with the City Council showing the amount of general taxes and special assessments assessed against such district and the amount of unpaid general taxes and delinquent special assessments thereon before any action is taken by the City Council relative to such improvement, provided, that this article shall not apply to improvements of streets when made pursuant to the provisions of the resolution adopted February 5, 1946, providing for the preparing of unpaved streets by laying stone and drainage of same and requiring deposits to be made therefor.

(Code 1964, $\S 21-10-1$ ; Code 1984, $\S 18-12-3$ )

**Sec. 44-3-4. Districts to be defined where none exist.**

If no definite district exists in connection with a local improvement, the Department of Public Works having charge of the local improvement shall make a written report to the City Council, defining the section or district in which such local improvement is contemplated, includ-

laws.title: Advanced payments based on tentative assessment roll; refund or payments where sufficient prepayment is not made
laws.content:
The Board of Assessors shall transmit the tentative assessment roll to the City Treasurer, who shall proceed to collect in advance not less than 25 percent of the City’s estimated cost of the proposed improvement, except that this advance payment shall not be required where the City Council has by resolution directed the construction of a lateral sewer, as provided in Chapter 48, Article II, of this Code, provided, that any property abutting on the improvement, which is owned by any public authority and is subject to final assessment for the improvement,

shall not be subject to the 25 percent advance payment. In calculating the amount of the 25 percent payment for all other property abutting the improvement, the City Treasurer shall not include the frontage of such public property. Where such 25 percent or more is not paid within 60 days after the receipt of the tentative roll from the Board of Assessors, the City Treasurer shall report such deficiency to the City Council. The City Council may order the improvement cancelled and the deposits refunded by the City Treasurer to the persons making such deposits. If the 25 percent or more of the City’s estimated cost of the improvement is collected by the City Treasurer within 60 days after the City Treasurer shall have received the tentative roll, the City Treasurer shall notify the City Council to that effect and the City Council may direct, in its discretion, the Department of Public Works to proceed in accordance with the provisions of the Charter and this Code, provided, that the City Treasurer shall not accept from any person more than the total amount shown on the tentative assessment roll levied against the property actually owned by such person.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-4; Code 1984, § 18-12-6)

laws.title: Payment of costs upon completion of improvement
laws.content:
Upon the completion of the improvement and its acceptance by the City Council, the assessable cost of the improvement shall be paid by the City Treasurer out of funds collected in advance through the tentative assessment. The balance, if any, shall be paid from a revolving fund to be created by the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-5; Code 1984, § 18-12-7)

laws.title: Certification of total costs of improvement; preparation of assessment roll; assessment roll to be in four or more annual installments
laws.content:
Upon the completion and acceptance of the improvement by the City Council, the Department of Public Works in charge of such improvement shall certify to the Chief Financial Officer the total cost of such improvement, together with the City’s cost of intersections or sewer arms. Thereupon, the Chief Financial Officer shall furnish the Board of Assessors with a copy of such certification and the Board of Assessors shall proceed to prepare an assessment roll for such improvement as provided for by the Charter and this Code. The assessment roll shall be in four or more annual installments.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-6; Code 1984, § 18-12-8)

**Sec. 44-3-9. Application of money collected through tentative assessment roll to be applied to regular special assessment roll.**

Upon receipt of the assessment roll, the City Treasurer shall apply all moneys collected upon the tentative roll to the regular special assessment roll. All funds received from the special assessment roll shall be credited to the revolving fund as created by the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-7; Code 1984, § 18-12-9)

**Sec. 44-3-10. Refund of overpayments.**

If any person has paid more than the total cost of the improvement, as provided in the assessment roll, the City Treasurer shall certify such overpayment to the City Council which shall direct a refund of the same.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-8; Code 1984, § 18-12-10)

**Sec. 44-3-11. Article not applicable to certain improvements.**

Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to apply to any street widening proceeding now pending in court, any local improvement already commenced, the laying or installation of water pipes, mains or aqueducts as authorized by Section 48-1-21 *et seq.*, of this Code, or any emergency work which, in the opinion of the City Council, is necessary for the peace, health, and safety of the People of the City.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-9; Code 1984, § 18-12-11)

**Sec. 44-3-12. Assessment rolls to be made in four to ten parts.**

Assessment rolls to provide for the cost of any lateral sewer or drain, paving, repaving or resurfacing of alleys or any other local improvement shall be made in four or more equal parts, not to exceed ten, and such parts of the assessment roll shall be numbered consecutively.

(Code 1964, §§ 21-10-10, 21-10-11; Code 1984, § 18-12-12)

**Sec. 44-3-13. Reassessment.**

Whenever any lots or premises were, or hereafter shall be, legally liable to be assessed for the costs and expenses of any paving or other public work or improvement, and it is made to appear that, for any cause, the amount originally assessed upon such lots or premises was not sufficient to pay in full the costs and expenses of such improvements, the City Council may order a new or reassessment to be made upon such lots or premises for the amount of such deficiency, provided, that in all cases where the deficiency arises or has arisen on account of the assessment of lots or premises not legally liable to such assessment, or improperly included in the assessment district created to defray the costs and expenses of any public improvement, the amount of such legal assessment, if paid, may be repaid, by a two-thirds vote of all the members-elect of the City Council, out of the contingent fund, and the new or reassessment to collect such money from the lots or premises legally liable to pay the same shall be credited to, and, when collected, paid into the contingent fund of the City.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-12; Code 1984, § 18-12-13)

**Sec. 44-3-14. Special assessment debt retirement fund.**

Whenever the City Council shall have authorized the issuance of special assessment bonds to defray the cost of any local improvements, as authorized under the laws of the state and the Charter, a special fund shall be created, to be known as the "special assessment debt retirement fund," into which all collections on assessment rolls against which such bonds have been issued shall be paid. If such fund is for the payment of more than one issue of bonds, such collections shall be allocated on the books and records of the City between the various issues in accordance with the amounts collected therefor, and such bonds and interest thereon shall be paid in accordance with this allocation, provided, that all interest and penalties accruing upon such special assessments, as above provided, shall be paid in and credited to such fund. Any cash balance in the special assessment debt retirement fund may be invested.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-13; Code 1984, § 18-12-14)

**Sec. 44-3-15. Conflicting provisions.**

Where the provisions of this division conflict with or differ from the provisions within any other division of this article, the provisions of the other division shall control.

(Code 1984, § 18-12-15; Ord. No. 09-15, § 1(18-12-15), eff. 4-28-2015)

**Secs. 44-3-16—44-3-30. Reserved.**

**DIVISION 2. NOTICE OF SPECIAL ASSESSMENT HEARINGS**

**Sec. 44-3-31. Applicability.**

The requirements of this division shall apply to any special assessments that are proposed under Divisions 3 through 7 of this article.
