laws.title: Notice of hearings in special assessment proceedings; service on owners or parties appearing on last local tax assessment records; statement that appearance and protest at hearing required for appeal; personal appearance; filing appearance or protest by letter; record of parties appearing to protest
laws.content:
(a) For each special assessment made against property, notice of all hearings in the special assessment proceedings shall be given as provided in this division in addition to any notice of hearings to be given by publication or posting as required by statute, the Charter, or this Code. Notice of hearings in special assessment proceedings shall be given to each owner of or party in interest in property to be assessed whose name appears upon the last local tax assessment records by mailing by first class mail addressed to that owner or party at the address shown on the tax records at least ten days before the date of the hearing. The last local tax assessment records means the last assessment roll for *ad valorem* tax purposes that has been reviewed by the local board of review, as supplemented by any subsequent changes in the names or the addresses of the owners or parties listed on that roll.

(b) The notice of hearing shall include a statement that appearance and protest at the hearing in the special assessment proceedings is required in order to appeal the amount of the special assessment to the Michigan Tax Tribunal and shall describe the manner in which an appearance and protest shall be made.

(c) An owner or party in interest, or his or her agent may appear in person at the hearing to protest the special assessment, or shall be permitted to file his or her appearance or protest by letter and his or her personal appearance shall not be required.

(d) The governing body shall maintain a record of parties who appear to protest at the hearing. If a hearing is terminated or adjourned for the day before a party is provided the opportunity to be heard, a party whose appearance was recorded is considered to have protested the special assessment in person.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-31; Code 1984, § 18-12-73)

*State law reference—Special assessment notices and hearings, MCL 211.741.*

laws.title: Tax assessment records; filing of names; changes of names and addresses
laws.content:
Where any person claims an interest in real property whose name and correct address do not appear upon the last City tax assessment records, the person shall be obligated to file immediately his or her name and address with the tax assessing officer. This requirement shall be deemed effective only for the purpose of establishing a record of the names and addresses of those persons entitled to notice of hearings in special assessment proceedings. It shall be the duty of each tax assessing officer to immediately enter on the City’s tax assessment records any changes in the names and addresses of owners or parties in interest filed with the officer and at all times to keep such tax assessment records current and complete and available for public inspection.

*State law reference—Special assessment notices and hearings, MCL 211.742.*

laws.title: Notice of hearings; mailing
laws.content:
Any assessment officer whose duty it is to give notice of hearings in special assessment proceedings may rely upon the last City tax assessment records in giving notice of hearing by mail. The method of giving notice by mail as provided in this division is declared to be the method that is reasonably certain to inform those to be assessed of the special assessment proceedings.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-31; Code 1984, § 18-12-73)

*State law reference—Special assessment notices and hearings, MCL 211.743.*

laws.title: Invalidation of assessment; reassessment
laws.content:
Any failure to give notice as required in Section 44-3-31 of this Code shall not invalidate an entire assessment roll but only the assessments on property affected by the lack of notice. A special assessment shall not be declared invalid as to any property if the owner or the party in interest thereof has actually received notice, has waived notice, or has paid any part of the assessment. Where any assessment is declared void by court order or judgment, a reassessment against the property may be made.

*State law reference—Special assessment notices and hearings, MCL 211.744.*

laws.title: Notice of hearings; validation of previously held hearings
laws.content:
Each special assessment hearing heretofore held is validated insofar as any notice of hearing is concerned, if notice was given by mail to the owners or parties in interest whose names appeared at the time of mailing on the last City tax assessment records. Any such special assessment hearing is also validated as to any owner or

laws.title: Statement of right to file written appeal

laws.title: Payment of contractors
laws.content:
Payment shall be made to the contractors for the assessed portion of the contract only from special assessments levied for such purpose; or from payments made into the City Treasury in behalf of the benefited district to provide for the cost of the improvement; or from the proceeds of the sale of special assessment bonds; and the payment for the City’s portion shall be paid from the street and alley intersection fund within the general fund. laws.title: Notice to public service corporations, City departments and real estate owners to lay cables, conduits, pipes, wires, and the like; cutting of pavement after paving completed

After the pavement shall have been completed, it shall not be cut for any purpose or by any person, firm, corporation or department, during the first year thereafter, unless there be paid, in advance, treble the estimated cost of the restoration of such pavement, and during the second year thereof, double the estimated cost thereof, and thereafter the estimated cost. (Code 1964, § 21-10-28; Code 1984, § 18-12-50)

**Sec. 44-3-102. Approval or rejection of petition; petition required for certain improvements.**

A petition of at least 51 percent of the property owners within the proposed assessment district under this division, providing such 51 percent represents at least 51 percent of the proposed assessments, shall be approved or rejected as to sufficiency by the City department, board or commission in charge of such improvement and shall be filed with the City Council. Such petition shall be required for all local improvements initiated by owners within the proposed special assessment district and no local improvements shall proceed without such petition, provided, that such petition shall not be required for vehicle parking facilities initiated by the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-30; Code 1984, § 18-12-72)

**Sec. 44-3-103. Determination of district to be benefited; confirmation of proposed district; reports on amount of delinquent taxes and assessments within district.**

The City Council shall order the Board of Assessors to make a written report to the City Council defining the district or the lot or parcels of land as will be benefited, in the opinion of the Board of Assessors, by an improvement under this division and stating whether the assessment shall be on a frontage basis or an area basis. The City Council shall confirm such proposed district. Together, with the report from the Board of Assessors, the City department, board or commission having charge of such improvement shall file a written statement with the City Council showing the amount of delinquent general taxes and special assessments within such district, provided, that, if the amount of delinquent general taxes and special assessments is 20 percent or more, such improvement shall not proceed and, provided further, that, in determining such delinquency, special assessments being retired in installments annually shall not be considered delinquent if each annual installment is paid when due.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-32; Code 1984, § 18-12-74)

**Sec. 44-3-104. Preliminary plan of improvement and cost thereof.**

The City Council shall direct the City department, board or commission in charge of an improvement under this division, in consultation with the Corporation Counsel, to provide a preliminary plan of the improvement, showing the estimated cost thereof and its recommendations as to the desirability of the proposed improvement and recommending the portion of the cost to be assessed against the land within the assessment district and the portion to be paid out of general funds. Upon approval by the City Council, such report shall be forwarded to the Board of Assessors for the purpose of preparing a plan of the proposed assessment against the property within the assessment district. The Board of Assessors shall report their findings to the City Council.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-33; Code 1984, § 18-12-75)

**Sec. 44-3-105. Advance payments required; refund of payments when improvement cancelled.**

The Board of Assessors shall transmit the tentative assessment roll under this division to the City Treasurer. The City Treasurer shall proceed to collect, in advance, ten percent or more of the assessable cost of the proposed improvement, provided, that such advance payment of ten percent or more of the assessable cost of the proposed improvement shall not be required when parking facilities are initiated by the City Council without petition and, further provided, that the City Treasurer shall not accept from any person more than the total amount shown on the tentative special assessment roll against the property actually owned by such person. If such ten percent or more is not paid within 60 days after the receipt of the tentative special assessment roll from the Board of Assessors, the City Treasurer shall report such deficiency to the City Council. The City Council may order the improvement cancelled and the deposits refunded by the City Treasurer to the persons making such deposits. If the ten percent or more of the assessable cost of the improvement is collected by the City Treasurer within 60 days after the City Treasurer shall have received the tentative special assessment roll, the City Treasurer shall notify the City Council to that effect.

(Code 1964, § 21-10-34; Code 1984, § 18-12-76)

**Sec. 44-3-106. Council may order improvement made; appropriation of sufficient funds for City’s portion of expenses.**

The City Council may order, in its discretion and by resolution, the improvement made by the City department, board or commission in charge of such local improvement, in accordance with the provisions of the Charter and this Code. If the improvement is so ordered, the Council shall appropriate sufficient funds to defray the City’s portion of the improvement and the assessable cost of the improvement shall be paid by the City Treasurer out of funds collected in advance through the

laws.title: Petition sponsored by a designated neighborhood improvement organization
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with this division, a designated neighborhood improvement organization may sponsor, on behalf of the neighborhood or community it represents, a petition for the creation of a special assessment district to provide for services within its geographic boundaries. Where a group of residents wishes to circulate a petition under this division, they may form a designated neighborhood improvement organization solely for the purpose of petitioning to create a special assessment district under this division and administering the contracts for services. The geographic boundaries of a proposed special assessment district need not be contiguous, but may be composed of only the area or portion thereof constituting the designated neighborhood improvement organization’s specific geographic boundaries.

(b) Where a designated neighborhood improvement organization desires to sponsor more than one service at a time, it may combine the information related to all proposed services on one petition. laws.title: Form of petition; information to be provided with petition
Special assessment roll; confirmation or revision of special assessment roll; endorsement; notice of assessment and collection of assessed amounts; appealing to the Michigan Tax Tribunal
laws.content:
(a) After preparing the tentative special assessment roll pursuant to Section 44-3-211 of this Code, the Board of Assessors shall file the roll with the City Clerk, who shall forward the roll to the City Council for confirmation. Immediately after the public hearing described in Section 44-3-213(a)(10) of this Code, the City Council may confirm the special assessment roll as prepared by the Board of Assessors. Where the special assessment roll is inconsistent with the terms of the special assessment district as stated in the City Council’s resolution pursuant to Section 44-3-213 of this Code, the City Council may request that the Board of Assessors revise the special assessment roll to correct any such inconsistency.

(b) Once the City Council confirms the special assessment roll, the City Clerk shall endorse on the special assessment roll the date of the confirmation, and shall deliver a copy of the assessment roll to the Board of Assessors, Treasurer, and sponsoring designated neighborhood improvement organization. The Treasurer shall proceed to collect the special assessment, and shall continue to do so annually during the term of the special assessment district. The Treasurer may invoice the record owners directly for the special assessment, or the Treasurer may include the special assessment as a separate item on the summer or winter tax bill. Where the nature of a service is such that a periodic redetermination of cost will be necessary without a change in the special assessment district boundaries, the Treasurer shall include with, or send contemporaneously with, the invoice or property tax bill a statement that the cost redeterminations may be made without further notice to record owners or parties in interest in the property subject to the limitations in Section 44-3-215(b) of this Code.

(c) Upon confirmation of the special assessment roll, all assessments on the assessment roll are final and conclusive. An aggrieved person may appeal the assessment by filing a petition with the Michigan Tax Tribunal pursuant to the requirements of the Michigan Tax Tribunal Act, being MCL 205.701 through 205.779, but only if the person protested the assessment at the hearing held for the purpose of confirming the special assessment roll described in Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1984, § 18-12-133; Ord. No. 07-14, § 1(18-12-133), eff. 6-9-2014)

The Administering Department shall make a report of such accounting and estimates to City Council and the sponsoring designated neighborhood improvement organization. After considering the report,

the City Council shall ask the Board of Assessors to prepare a new special assessment roll for the special assessment district for the following year. laws.title: Divisions or combinations of land; changes in exempt status
laws.content:
(a) Where, after a special assessment on the tax parcel is confirmed and before a special assessment is collected, a tax parcel is divided into two or more tax parcels, or two or more tax parcels are combined into one tax parcel, payment of the current year’s tax parcel shares for the original tax parcels shall be due immediately as a condition to the combination or division. For each subsequent year of the term, each resultant tax parcel shall be assessed a tax parcel share as if the resultant tax parcel were in existence at the initial assessment.

(b) Pursuant to Section 44-3-217 of this Code, the exempt status of a tax parcel shall be determined as of tax day as that term is defined in Section 2(2) of the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.2(2). laws.title: Continuation of special assessment district upon expiration of term
laws.content:

laws.title: Provision of services under this division not to reduce provision of general City services

laws.title: Contracting for services
laws.content:
(a) Section 5i of the Michigan Home Rule City Act, being MCL 117.5i, requires that the services under this division be provided by private contractors. The City prefers to enter into a contract with the designated neighborhood improvement organization for the services with the exception that the designated neighborhood improvement organization will enter into one or more subcontracts with the service providers. Where the designated neighborhood improvement organization desires to administer the special assessment district services, and the Administering Department determines that the designated neighborhood improvement organization is qualified, the Administering Department shall negotiate a contract with the designated neighborhood improvement organization in form satisfactory to the Law Department for administering the special assessment district. The contract shall address the methods by which the designated neighborhood improvement organization shall solicit and obtain bids from potential providers of the services for which the special assessment district was established, and the awarding of subcontracts for such services, the procedures for requesting and obtaining prompt payment from the City, which shall include invoices from private contractors that a designated neighborhood improvement organization has contracted with for the provision of services within a special assessment

Where the designated neighborhood improvement organization does not desire to administer the contract for services, the Administering Department may identify another entity to administer the contract for services, or may elect to contract directly for such services in accordance with standard City procedures. Where both the designated neighborhood improvement organization and the Administering Department decline to administer the contract for the services, and the Administering Department is unable to identify another entity to administer the contracts, the special assessment shall be canceled.

(b) The contract shall contain provisions requiring the designated neighborhood improvement organization and all subcontractors to provide in a timely manner all information needed for redetermining costs in accordance with Section 44-3-215 of this Code.

(c) The contract shall terminate upon acceptance of a discontinuance petition pursuant to Section 44-3-222 of this Code, and shall contain a provision so stating.

(3) The Board of Review must conduct its meetings in compliance with the Open Meetings Act. When hearings are held through online video conferencing, the City may not use any function designed to exclude members of the public from the online platform, such as the "waiting room" function. However the Board can take steps to prevent disruption, for example, by not allowing individuals to unmute their microphones until the Board is calling their case.

(h) As required by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, being MCL 15.261 et seq., all Board of Review deliberations must occur at a meeting open to the public. If the Board of Review does not conduct its deliberations and make a determination directly following a hearing, the Board must notify the complainant of the date and time of the public meeting where the Body will deliberate, vote, and issue a final determination on the appeal.

(i) During the first meeting of the year, the Board of Review shall select a chairperson and vice-chairperson from among its members. A majority of the Board members serving shall constitute a quorum to conduct business, but a lesser number may adjourn and may cause the secretary of the Board to notify each absent member to return to the meeting. After notification to appear, said member shall return to the meeting without delay. A majority vote of Board members present shall decide all questions.

(j) The Board of Review shall appoint special subcommittees to review and submit recommendations to the Body regarding poverty exemptions from taxation. Property valuation appeals and property classification appeals may be heard by the full Board. The Board may separate into three committees composed of three members to conduct valuation and classification hearings.

(k) All decisions made by the Board of Review relative to assessment, valuation, and property classification exemptions under property tax laws are subject to review by the Michigan Tax Tribunal in accordance with Section 31 of the Michigan Tax Tribunal Act, being MCL 205.731.

(l) The Board of Review must issue a decision letter for each petition filed with the Board, which shall include the reason for granting, denying, or partially granting or denying each petition. The decision letter must include a statement of the Petitioner's appeal rights to the Michigan Tax Tribunal and provide the deadline to file an appeal with the Michigan Tax Tribunal. In addition, the Board must issue a written response, which provides an explanation for a petition that the Body is without authority or jurisdiction to review.

(m) In accordance with Sections 2-110 and 2-111 of the Charter, the Board of Review shall promulgate its rules of procedure and policy, which are consistent with the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.1 et seq. Such rules of procedure and policy must be published on the Board of Review's page on the City's website.

(n) In accordance with Section 4-104 of the Charter, the City Council President, or the President's designee, shall have administrative responsibility on behalf of, and oversight pertaining to, operation of the Board of Review.

(o) The Board of Review shall comply with provisions of Chapter 2, Article V, of this Code, Ethics.

(p) The Board of Review shall establish an electronic filing system for parties appealing a property tax assessment which shall:

(1) Include a docket-search function that allows the public to search all of the cases submitted to the Board;

(2) Include a hearing calendar available to the public identifying all the cases that the Board will hear each day; and

(3) Substantially conform to the systems used by the State of Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs for the Michigan Tax Tribunal's Small Claims Division.

(q) The City of Detroit's website must include a brief description of the duties of the Board of Review and include a page listing the members of the Board of Review, the date that each Board member's term began and expires, the number of terms that each member has served, the name of the City Council members who voted to appoint the member to the Board, the Board member's resume, and the Board member's City of Detroit email address.

laws.title: Correction and confirmation of assessment roll
laws.content:
(a) The Board of Review shall hear and determine all appeals in a summary manner and correct any errors which the Body may discover in the assessment roll, shall place thereon the names of any persons and the descriptions of any property not already assessed and assess the same, and may increase or diminish any assessment as the Body sees fit, provided, that the Board of Review shall not increase any assessment without giving a reasonable opportunity to persons owning or having charge of the same, if known, to appear and object thereto. Hearings on appeals shall be held at such time, date, and place as the Board of Review shall specify as soon as practicable after the appeal has been filed. The Board of Review may adopt, change, or amend the same assessment roll in whole or in part.

(b) After due consideration thereof, such roll shall, on or before the first Monday in April, or such other date as may be subsequently required by law, be fully and finally confirmed by the Board of Review, and shall remain as the basis, according to property valuation, of all taxes to be levied and collected in the City until another assessment shall have been made and confirmed as provided for in this division. (c) The secretary shall keep a permanent record of the proceedings of the Board of Review and all resolutions and decisions of the Board. The record shall be filed with the City Clerk following the final meeting of the Board specified in Subsection (b) of this section.

(d) The City of Detroit must adhere to the State Tax Commission’s guidance in depreciating the value of real residential property. If the Assessor deviates from the Commission’s standard depreciation recommendations to recognize extremely exceptional or poor maintenance, the Assessor must state the decision clearly in the "Notes" portion of the property record card.

laws.content:
(a) Whenever it shall appear to the satisfaction of the City Council that any individual tax assessment or class of tax assessment is unjust or placed upon any property not owned by the person to whom it is assessed, the Council may repay, by a majority vote of all the members-elect, the same, if collected, out of the contingent fund or, if not collected, vacate the assessment, in whole or in part, and fix upon an amount to be received in full of such tax or assessment.

(b) Where any tax assessment is found to be unjust or placed upon property not owned by the person to whom it is assessed, the City Council shall authorize and direct the Chief Financial Officer to issue a warrant and to provide for a refund of such taxes to the person paying the same if such taxes have been collected.

(c) No action had under this section shall in any way affect or invalidate any other tax or assessment assessed, levied, or collected in the City.

There is no discretion with the City Council as to the refund of illegal assessments which were not voluntarily paid. *Blanchard v City of Detroit*, 253 Mich 491; 235 NW 230 (1931).

**Sec. 44-4-9. Same—Illegal assessments.**

(a) Whenever it shall appear to the satisfaction of the City Council that any City tax has been illegally assessed or collected, the City Council may direct, by a vote of two-thirds of all members elected, and cause such tax or assessment, if collected, to be repaid, in whole or in part, to the person from whom collected, out of the contingent fund. If such tax or assessment has not been collected, the City Council may direct, by a like vote of two-thirds, and cause the same to be vacated or stricken from the rolls. When so vacating any tax or assessment, the City Council may require, as a condition precedent, the payment to the City Treasurer of a sum to be fixed by the City Council. Any sum so paid shall be credited to the same fund into which such tax or assessment would have been paid if collected in full.

(b) No action under this section shall in any way affect or invalidate any other tax or assessment assessed, levied or collected in the City.

(Code 1964, § 21-7-7; Code 1984, § 18-9-9)

**Sec. 44-4-10. Appraisal required for residential property.**

(a) An appraisal of all residential property in the City shall be completed every five years beginning January 1, 2025, and every five years thereafter.

(b) The reappraisal required under Subsection (a) of this section shall be completed in two years and shall be the basis of the annual assessment required under Section 10 of the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.10, the year following the year the appraisal is completed.

(c) The appraisal required under Subsection (a) of this section shall establish the true market value of the property and be completed by utilizing a combination of Remote Data Verification, which shall involve the use of aerial and street level imagery, and the physical inspection of the subject property.

(d) The City may contract with a private appraisal firm to perform the appraisals required under Subsection (a) of this section.

(Ord. No. 2020-28, § 1, eff. 8-21-2020)

**Sec. 44-4-11. Independent Evaluator to advise City Council; duties of Assessment Division.**

(a) City Council may hire, through the City’s procurement process, an Independent Evaluator to complete an assessment ratio study each year.

(b) Every year, the Assessment Division must provide the Independent Evaluator with all of its sales data no later than February 1st following Tax Day as deemed in Section 44-4-1 of this Code. The Independent Evaluator must use this data to conduct an assessment ratio study. The assessment ratio study must include the average assessment ratio for each sales decile and for each Economic Condition Factor, as drawn by the City’s Assessment Division for the current tax year. An assessment ratio is a property’s assessed value divided by its sales price. A sales decile refers to a division of all arms-length sales into ten groups based on sales price. The assessment ratio study must calculate the following:

(1) Coefficient of Dispersion, which is a measure of uniformity based on the average percentage deviation of the ratios from the median and expressed as a percentage of the median. Higher values indicate less uniformity;

(2) Price-Related Differential, which is a measure of regressivity (also known as vertical equity) calculated by dividing the mean sales ratio by the price-weighted mean ratio. Higher values of Price-Related Differential indicate greater regressivity;

(3) Coefficient of Price-Related Bias, which is a regression-based measure that estimates the relationship between the sales ratio and a given proxy for actual property value determined by giving equal weight to sale price and assessed value. It measures the change in the assessment ratio that can be expected to result from a 100 percent change in this value proxy. Lower (more negative) values of price-related bias indicate greater regressivity; and

(4) The percentage of properties where the assessed value exceeds 50 percent of the market value, in violation of the 1963 Michigan Constitution and the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.1 *et seq.*, within each sales decile.

(c) The Independent Evaluator’s study results, the formula and code used to conduct its analysis, and the data used to reach its determination shall be submitted to the City Council no later than the Tuesday following the second Monday in March of each year.

laws.title: Assessment factors; City Council resolution
laws.content:
(a) City of Detroit assessments should have:

(1) A Coefficient of Dispersion between 5.0 and 15.0;

(2) A price-Related Differential between 0.98 and 1.03;

(3) A price-Related Bias between -0.05 and 0.05; and

(4) A statistically insignificant number of properties where the assessed value exceeds 50 percent of the market value, in violation of the 1963 Michigan Constitution, within each sales decile.

(b) Each year, City Council must review the assessment ratio study and adopt a resolution to do one of the following:

(1) Take no action; or

(2) Request that the Board of Review use its authority under Section 30(4) of the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.30(4), to individually review every residential property in any subset or class of real residential properties that the assessment ration study identifies as not falling within the guidelines established in Subsection (a) of this section.

(c) The City Council request may attach the Independent Evaluator data and the report to City Council identified in Section 44-4-11 of this Code as evidence that the Board of Review can consider in determining the property’s assessed value.

(d) The Board of Review may rely on data from the property’s record card, the Economic Condition Factor’s sales study, the Independent Evaluator’s study, and any evidence presented by any person aggrieved by the assessment to make an assessed value determination.

laws.title: Acceptance by City Treasurer
laws.content:
The City Treasurer shall accept partial payments of personal property taxes, real property taxes, and special assessments, both current and delinquent, and shall credit such payments on account on the tax rolls in the manner provided for in this division.

Whenever possible, such amounts upon past due taxes and assessments shall be paid in $10.00 units or multiples thereof. laws.title: Payments at certain banks; dates allowed for same
laws.content:
Upon approval of the Chief Financial Officer, the first payment, second payment or full payment of regular City real and personal property taxes that are levied by the City each fiscal year may be paid at any bank that is selected in accordance with Chapter 17, Article V, of this Code, Purchases and Supplies, as follows:

(1) The first payment taxes for each fiscal year may be paid at the main offices and branches of such banks on banking days from July 1st to August 15th, inclusive;

(2) The second payment taxes for each fiscal year may be paid at the main offices and branches of such banks on banking days from November 15th to January 15th, inclusive;

(3) The full year’s taxes for each fiscal year may be paid at the main offices and branches of such banks on banking days from July 1st to August 31st, inclusive; and

laws.title: Amounts payable; banks not liable for bad checks
laws.content:
The banks named in this division shall receive payments for only the full amount of the tax or the first half or second half tax, respectively, as stated in the City tax bill issued by the City Treasurer. Such banks shall mark out on the original and duplicate bills the part of the stated tax that is not paid, being either the one-half City tax or the full amount of the City tax. If payment under this division is made to any of such banks otherwise than by a cash payment, and the instrument by which payment is made proves to be uncollectible or credit is otherwise erroneously given, such tax payment shall be cancelled by the City and the bank taking such payment shall be reimbursed and relieved of liability to the City for the amount of such tax payment.

(Code 1964, § 21-7-33; Code 1984, § 18-9-73)

laws.title: Disposition of money collected
laws.content:
All tax money paid under this division to the banks named in this division shall be accepted by such banks as deposits to the credit of the City. The banks shall deposit such money in an account designated by the City Treasurer.

(Code 1964, § 21-7-34; Code 1984, § 18-9-74)

laws.title: Reports by banks to City Treasurer
laws.content:
Each bank shall give, on the next banking business day after the receipt by them of payments of tax money under this division, to the City Treasurer all duplicate paid tax bills for which they have received payment, together with a duplicate deposit slip for the full amount of taxes paid on the preceding banking business day. Likewise, each bank shall send to the City Treasurer a list showing the tax bill item number appearing on each paid tax bill and the amount paid for which such tax receipt was issued.

(Code 1964, § 21-7-35; Code 1984, § 18-9-75)

laws.title: Compliance with division

laws.title: Amount generally
laws.content:
All delinquent personal property taxes, real property taxes, or special assessments shall have added thereto interest computed at the rate of 0.5 percent per month to be added the first day of each month from the time that such tax or special assessment became due and payable.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-37; Code 1984, § 18-9-89)

laws.title: Personal and real property taxes—No addition for interest when taxes paid before August 31st
laws.content:
No addition for interest shall be made to personal property taxes or real property taxes paid on or before August 31st. Interest in the amount of 1.5 percent of every unpaid tax shall be added thereto on September 1st, and an additional 0.5 percent of such tax shall be added on the first day of each succeeding month, until such tax is paid in full.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-38; Code 1984, § 18-9-90)

laws.title: Same—Half payments allowed with no addition of interest
laws.content:
Whenever any person liable for the tax on any personal or real property shall pay one-half thereof on or before August 15th of the year in which such tax is assessed and the remaining one-half on or before January 15th of the succeeding year, such person shall have the right to do so without any addition of interest.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-39; Code 1984, § 18-9-91)

laws.title: Same—Failure to pay second half of taxes
laws.content:
Failure to pay the second half of personal property taxes or real property taxes on or before January 15th of the year following that in which the tax is due and payable shall subject the property to all the provisions of state law, the Charter and this Code relating to delinquent taxes the same as if the first half had not been paid, provided, that no interest or penalty shall be charged against that portion of the tax that is paid.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-40; Code 1984, § 18-9-92)

laws.title: Same—Effect of partial payment of tax; when tax considered paid
laws.content:
Payment of any portion of a tax shall not in any manner affect, prejudice or destroy the tax lien on the property for which such tax was assessed and partially paid. The persons liable for a tax under the provisions of state law, the Charter, and this Code shall be liable for the full amount of the tax and such tax shall not be considered "paid" until paid in full.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-41; Code 1984, § 18-9-93)

laws.title: Real and personal property taxes; penalty—Amount generally
laws.content:
All delinquent City taxes levied upon real property and against persons with respect to personal property shall have added thereto a penalty computed at the rate of one percent per month, to be added the first day of each month from the time that such tax became due and payable.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-42; Code 1984, § 18-9-94)

laws.title: Same—When penalty due
laws.content:
No addition for penalty shall be made to City taxes levied on real and personal property paid on or before August 31st. A penalty in the amount of one percent of every unpaid tax shall be added thereto on September 1st and an additional one percent of such tax shall be added on the first day of each succeeding month, until such tax is paid in full, not to exceed a total penalty of 25 percent of the unpaid tax.  
(Code 1964, § 21-7-43; Code 1984, § 18-9-95)

laws.title: Same—Half payment generally

Whenever any person liable for the City tax on any real or personal property shall pay one-half thereof on or before August 15th of the year in which such tax is assessed and the remaining one-half on or before January 15th of the succeeding year, such person shall have the right so to do without an addition of a penalty.

laws.content:
Those housing projects, which are currently exempt from taxation and are already making pilot service charge payments, shall not be affected or the terms of their tax exemption and pilot payments changed by reason of enactment of this division.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-14; Ord. No. 09-90, § 1(18-9-14), eff. 7-20-1990)

laws.title: Duration
laws.content:
The tax exempt status of a housing project approved for such status by resolution of the City Council shall remain in effect and shall not terminate so long as the mortgage loan for such housing project remains outstanding and unpaid, or for such period as the Authority or other governmental entity has any interest in the property.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-16; Ord. No. 09-90, § 1(18-9-16), eff. 7-20-1990; Ord. No. 23-93, § 1(18-9-16), eff. 11-24-1993)

Secs. 44-4-118—44-4-130. Reserved.

laws.title: Informational brochure
laws.content:
(a) If an informational brochure is utilized, it shall contain the following information:

(1) The property tax payment deadlines for the City and the consequences for nonpayment of taxes;

(2) A summary of the current tax foreclosure laws in plain English;

(3) A list of resources available to qualified taxpayers including, but not limited to, principal residence credit, hardship exemption, payment options, and deferments; and

(4) A list of organizations that may provide assistance to qualified taxpayers, including, but not limited to: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services, Michigan Legal Services, United Community Housing Coalition, Legal Aid and Defender, Association, Veteran’s Trust, and the Salvation Army.

(b) The informational brochure shall be updated as necessary based on program or provision changes.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-125; Ord. No. 18-05, § 1(18-9-125), eff. 5-23-2005)

laws.title: Community outreach and education programs
laws.content:
(a) The following outreach efforts may be utilized by the City to educate the public on current taxation and foreclosure legislation, current tax collection procedure, the City agencies responsible for levying and collecting taxes as well as the programs available to assist qualified taxpayers. The City may:

(1) Utilize local outlets such as local cable stations, City publications, and public service announcements to notify taxpayers of property tax deadlines and resources;

(2) Advertise using media sources, such as local television stations and general circulation newspapers, resources, and programs available to qualified taxpayers;

(3) Distribute information including, but not limited to, the informational brochure detailed in Section 44-4-135 of this Code to public places, such as City recreation centers, police precincts and mini-stations, other City offices, Michigan Department of Health and Human Services offices, libraries, churches, barbershops, beauty salons, and grocery stores; and

(4) Coordinate a City-wide volunteer campaign to notify taxpayers of owner-occupied residences that they may be in jeopardy of property tax delinquency.

(b) The provisions contained in this section shall supplement and not replace current efforts within the City to educate taxpayers.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-126; Ord. No. 18-05, § 1(18-9-126), eff. 5-23-2005)

Secs. 44-4-137—44-4-150. Reserved.

CD44:72

laws.title: Ownership and occupancy required
laws.content:
The applicant must be an owner and occupy as a principal residence the property for which the exemption is requested. This applicant shall affirm this ownership and occupancy status by completing and filing a form provided by the State Tax Commission with the Office of the Assessor.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-132; Ord. No. 36-18, § 1(18-9-132), eff. 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, eff. 12-1-2021)

laws.title: Annual application required; time of submission
laws.content:
(a) Except as otherwise provided by Section 7u(6) and (8) of the Michigan Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.7u(6) and (8), the applicant must submit a new application each year to qualify for the exemption provided for in the Homeowners Property Exemption.

(b) The application for an exemption shall be filed after January 1st but prior to the last day of the December Board of Review.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-133; Ord. No. 36-18, § 1(18-9-133), eff. 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, eff. 12-1-2021)

laws.title: Application for Homeowners Property Exemption Program; availability
laws.content:
(a) Homeowners Property Exemption applications, as prescribed and provided by the State Tax Commission, shall be available to the general public at the Office of the Assessor, City of Detroit Recreation Centers, Department of Neighborhood Offices, and on the City’s website under all web pages that reference property taxes or the payment of property taxes. In addition:

(1) The Office of the Assessor shall post a notice near the Homeowners Property Exemption applications and on the Property Assessment Documents Page, which advises residents that the applicant may speak with a representative of the Board of Review if they have any questions about the application; and

(2) The Board of Review shall maintain and provide, upon request, a resource list of organizations that will assist in the completion of the Homeowners Property Exemption application.

(b) An application for Homeowners Property Exemption made pursuant to Section 7u of the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.7u, shall be made by the property owner on a form that is provided by the State Tax Commissioner as set forth in Subsection (a) of this section.

(c) The applicant shall produce with the application:

(1) A deed, land contract, or any other recorded proof of ownership, including, but not limited to, a probate court order or judgment of divorce;

(2) A valid driver’s license, or any unexpired government issued identification so long as the official document includes the applicant’s photograph and address; and

(3) Complete federal and state income tax returns, including schedules, for all adults for the current year, provided, that tax returns are not required for a person residing in the principal residence if that person was not required to file a federal tax return in the tax year in which at the exemption is claimed or in the immediately preceding tax year. In the alternative, an affidavit on a form provided for by the State Tax Commission may be accepted.

(d) The applicant shall not be required to provide utility bills to support the claim of occupancy of the subject property.

(e) In the instance of physical impairment, the Board of Review may be contacted to pick up the application.

Supp. No. 4

DETROIT CODE

(f) The application packet shall include a document checklist of all items needed for the application to be considered by the Board of Review and contain language strongly encouraging the applicant to apply as soon as possible.

(g) No later than August 31, 2024, the Board of Review shall implement a software program that permits applicants to electronically complete and submit applications. This software must:

(1) Allow applicants to complete all portions of the application electronically;

(2) Allow applicants to upload and submit all necessary documents electronically;

(3) Retain all applicant data and documents in a secure database;

(4) Make a preliminary determination whether an applicant is eligible for the property tax exemption; and

(5) Generate a preliminary determination letter explaining whether an applicant’s exemption is granted or denied and, if denied, the particular reason for denial.

(Code 1984, § 18-9-134; Ord. No. 36-18, § 1(18-9-134), eff. 12-10-2018; Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, eff. 12-1-2021; Ord. No. 2023-45, § 1, eff. 12-19-2023)

laws.title: Guidelines
laws.content:
(a) City Council shall determine and make available to the public the policy and guidelines that the City uses for the granting of exemptions. Such guidelines shall be posted on the City of Detroit Board of Review’s page on the City’s website. (b) The guidelines must include, but are not limited to, the specific income and asset levels of the claimant and total household income and assets to qualify for property tax exemption for the applicant: (1) Qualifying levels of household income shall be computed based on the following table:
Household Size Full Exemption 100% Partial Exemption 50% Partial Exemption 25%
1 138% of federal poverty level 159% of federal poverty level 179% of federal poverty level
2 123% of federal poverty level 138% of federal poverty level 152% of federal poverty level
3 108% of federal poverty level 120% of federal poverty level 131% of federal poverty level
4 104% of federal poverty level 114% of federal poverty level 124% of federal poverty level

6 100% of federal poverty level 108% of federal poverty level 115% of federal poverty level
7 100% of federal poverty level 107% of federal poverty level 113% of federal poverty level
8 or greater 100% of federal poverty level 106% of federal poverty level 112% of federal poverty level
(2) For purposes of this section, “federal poverty level” means the most recently available release of the federal poverty guidelines applicable to the State of Michigan that are published and adjusted annually by the United States Department of Health and Human Service; and. (3) The maximum value of asset levels of the claimant established by the guidelines shall not be less than $12,000.00, provided, that assets do not include the value of the property for which the applicant is seeking an exemption or the value of any food or medical benefits, or other public assistance. (c) The Board of Review shall submit the proposed guidelines to City Council by October 15th for consideration and adoption via resolution for the next tax year. (d) The policy and guidelines shall include the appeal process for applicants that are denied relief. (e) The policy and guidelines must describe, in clear language, the conditions that qualify applicants for a multi-year exemption as described in Section 7u(6) and (8) of the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.7u(6) and (8). (f) As provided for in the Michigan General Property Tax Act, being MCL 211.1 et seq., the Board of Review shall follow the policy and guidelines of the City in granting or denying an exemption. (Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, eff. 12-1-2021; Ord. No. 2023-45, § 1, eff. 12-19-2023) Editor’s note—Ord. laws.title: Relief
laws.content:
(a) If a person claiming an exemption is qualified based on the guidelines referenced in Section 44-4-155 of this Code, the Board of Review shall grant an exemption in whole or in part.

(b) Exemptions may be granted in the following levels:

(1) A full exemption equal to a 100 percent reduction in taxable value for the tax year in which the exemption is granted; or

(2) A partial exemption equal to one of the following:

(a) A 50 percent or 25 percent reduction in taxable value for the tax year in which the exemption is granted; or

(b) Any other percentage reduction in taxable value as approved by the State Tax Commission for the tax year in which the tax exemption is granted to be applied in the form and manner prescribed by the State Tax Commission.

(Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, eff. 12-1-2021)

*Editor’s note—Ord. No. 2021-48, § 1, effective December 1, 2021, repealed § 44-4-156 and enacted a new § 44-4-156 as set out herein. Former § 44-4-156 pertained to guidelines and derived from § 18-9-136 of the 1984 Detroit City Code and Ord. No. 36-18, § 1(18-9-136), effective December 10, 2018.*

laws.title: Penalty for certain violations of article
Imposition; amount; basis
laws.content:
(a) Subject to the exclusions, adjustments and exemptions herein provided, a City utility users tax set in increments of 0.25 percent, which shall not exceed five percent for the hiring and retention of police officers, is hereby imposed on and shall be paid by the utility user.

(b) The first $45,000,000.00 of revenue generated from this tax shall be used exclusively to retain and hire police officers.

(c) Where the amount of revenue collected in a fiscal year is in excess of $45,000,000.00 and where the amount of excess funds collected equals or exceeds five percent of $45,000,000.00, the City shall comply with one of the following:

(1) The rate of tax imposed for the following fiscal year shall be lowered in decrements of 0.25 percent for each full five percent collected in excess of $45,000,000.00. By August 1st of a fiscal year following a fiscal year in which the amount of revenue collected was in excess of $45,000,000.00, the City shall notify by certified mail each collector of the tax subject to this article and the State Commissioner of Revenue of the rate of tax to be applied. The rate shall become effective for bills issued beginning October 1st of a fiscal year following a fiscal year in which the amount of revenue collected was in excess of $45,000,000.00. If the tax expires, an adjustment shall not be made for an excess or deficiency in collections for a fiscal year or other period not already adjusted pursuant to this section.

(2) The amount collected in excess of $45,000,000.00 shall be used exclusively to hire and retain additional police officers over the level of police officers employed on November 1, 1984. The hiring and retaining of additional police shall be limited to police officers, investigators, and police sergeants. The City shall not intentionally lay off any police officers in anticipation of rehiring the officers with the additional revenue from this tax nor shall the general fund contribution towards the police budget be reduced from the prior year. If the City fails to comply with Subsection (c)(1) or (2) of this section by August 1, 1985, or any fiscal year following a fiscal year in which the amount of revenue is in excess of $45,000,000.00, the State Commissioner of Revenue shall implement the provisions of Subsection (c)(1) of this section.

(d) Notwithstanding Subsections (b) and (c) of this section and as authorized by Section 2 of the Michigan City Utility Users Tax Act, being MCL 141.1152, the City shall pay $12,500,000.00 annually to the Public Lighting Authority from the proceeds of the tax authorized under this article. Nothing in this subsection shall obligate the City or any trustee to remit to the Public Lighting Authority more than is collected from taxes levied under this article.

(e) This tax shall be measured by the amounts paid, not including any existing or hereafter enacted taxes, including, but not limited to, federal, state, City and other local taxes, directly added to or directly passed on in the users' billing, paid by users for the public utility services as hereinafter provided, billed or ordinarily billable to locations within the taxing City:

(1) The tax shall be imposed on all intrastate telephone communication services, furnished by a public utility. The term "intrastate telephone communication services" shall not include any telephone service originating or terminating outside the state, telephone services by coin-operated installations, directory advertising proceeds, telephone services not taxable under 26

USC 4251 as of December 31, 1969, as amended, centrex and multiline key switching systems, mobile telephone service and any types of services or equipment, furnished by telephone companies subject to public utility regulation, during any period in which such services or equipment are in competition with services or equipment furnished by or available from persons other than telephone companies subject to public utility regulation.

(2) The tax shall be on all electrical energy and steam provided by a public utility or a resale customer. The term "electrical energy and steam provided" shall include amounts paid for metered energy and steam, and minimum charges for service, including user charges, service charges, demand charges, standby charges and annual and monthly charges. The term "electrical energy and steam provided" shall not include electrical energy or steam sold to or exchanged with for resale by another public utility, or used or consumed in the conduct of the business of an electric or steam public utility or a combination gas and electric utility.

(3) The tax shall be on all gas, natural or artificial, provided by a public utility or a resale customer. The term "gas, natural or artificial, provided" shall not include any gas sold for use in the generation of electrical energy by a public utility, any gas sold to or exchanged with, for resale by another gas public utility, or any gas used or consumed in the conduct of the business of a gas public utility or a combination gas and electric utility.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-3; Code 1984, § 18-11-3; Ord. No. 325-H, § 1, eff. 7-1-1979; Ord. No. 332-H, § 1(21-11-3), eff. 7-6-1979; Ord. No. 458-H, § 1(21-11-3), eff. 8-30-1981; Ord. No. 607-H, § 1(21-11-3), eff. 12-20-1984)

State law reference—Similar provision, MCL 141.1152, 141.1163.

laws.title: Billing; deemed debt until paid; when due and payable; examination of records
laws.content:
(a) The taxes imposed under this article shall be billed by the public utility or resale customer as provided in Section 44-5-4 of this Code, and they may imprint upon the face of the bill the amount of the tax and the name of the taxing City, commencing with the first regular billing period applicable to that person which starts on or after the date this article is made operative for the taxing City, and shall be paid by the user along with the amounts billed for public utility services furnished.

(b) Any tax required to be paid by a user under this article shall be deemed a debt owned by the user to the taxing City, and deemed delinquent from the time due until paid.

(c) Subject to extensions which may be granted for good cause shown, and to a utility collection fee of one percent of the tax amounts involved, all tax amounts under this article billed by the public utility or resale customer in a given month shall be remitted to the taxing City on or before the last day of the following month, along with a return in such form as may be prescribed by the taxing City, showing such information as may be necessary for the proper administration of this article provided, that tax amounts based on billing shall be subject to adjustment for tax money not actually collected by the public utility or resale customer. Any such tax amounts not so remitted shall be deemed delinquent. An annual return for each year shall be filed by the public utility and resale customer on or before the end of the fourth month following the end of the tax year.

(d) A taxpayer, public utility or resale customer desiring a special ruling on a matter pertaining to this article or rules shall submit in writing to the Administrator all the facts involved and the ruling sought. A taxpayer, public utility or resale customer, aggrieved by a special ruling may appeal as provided in Section 44-5-16 of this Code.

(e) The Administrator or such Administrator’s duly authorized agent may examine the books, papers and records of any person, public utility, resale customer, taxpayer or the agent or representative of such person, public utility, resale customer or taxpayer, for the purpose of verifying the accuracy and completeness of a return filed, or if no return was filed, to ascertain the tax, penalties or interest due under this article.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-4; Code 1984, § 18-11-4)

State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1164, 141.1165.

laws.title: Duties of Administrator and City Treasurer
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the Administrator may promulgate administrative rules relating to the administration and enforcement of this article, but not in conflict with the article.

(b) The Administrator shall enforce this article and the rules. The Administrator shall prepare, adopt and make available to taxpayers and other persons all forms necessary for compliance with this article.

(c) The City Treasurer shall collect all taxes and payments due under this article and deposit them in a designated City depository.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-5; Code 1984, § 18-11-5)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1165.*

laws.title: Investigation information deemed confidential; exception; penalty for violation
laws.content:
(a) Information gained by the Administrator, or any other City official, agent or employee as a result of a return, investigation, hearing or verification required or authorized by this article is confidential, except for official purposes in connection with the administration of the article and except in accordance with a proper judicial order.

(b) Any person who divulges this confidential information, except for official purposes, is guilty of a violation of this article and subject to a fine not exceeding $500.00 or imprisonment for a period not exceeding 90 days, or both, for each offense. In addition, an employee of the City who divulges this confidential information is subject to discharge for misconduct.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-6; Code 1984, § 18-11-6)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1166.*

laws.title: Procedure for authorized investigation
laws.content:
(a) A person shall furnish, within ten days following a request of the Administrator or such Administrator’s duly authorized agent, the means, facilities and opportunity for making such reasonable examinations and investigations as are authorized by this article, and shall present themselves for examination under oath when so ordered by the Administrator. The request or order of the administrator or such Administrator’s duly authorized agent may be made verbally unless the person requests that the request or order be addressed to such person in writing.

(b) Refusal by any person to submit to such examination or investigation, when requested or ordered by the Administrator, is a violation of this article, punishable by such penalties as are provided in this article.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-7; Code 1984, § 18-11-7)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1167.*

laws.title: Penalties for delinquent taxes
laws.content:
(a) All delinquent tax amounts shall be subject to interest from the due date at the rate of 0.5 percent per month or fraction thereof until paid.

(b) A user failing to pay the tax, or any public utility or resale customer failing to remit money billed and due the City, when due, or file a return when due, is liable, in addition to the interest, to a penalty of one percent of the amount of the unpaid tax, or moneys unremitted, for each month or fraction thereof, not to exceed a total penalty of 25 percent of the unpaid tax. The Administrator may abate the penalty or a part thereof for just cause. If the total interest or interest and penalty to be assessed is less than $2.00, the Administrator, in lieu thereof, may assess a penalty in the amount of $2.00. Interest, interest and penalty, or the minimum charge shall be computed separately for each month or billing period.

(c) Interest and penalties applicable to users shall not be subject to public utility or resale customer billing procedures but shall be recovered only by the City directly from users.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-8; Code 1984, § 18-11-8)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1168.*

laws.title: Administrator to propose assessment for unpaid taxes; notice; protest
laws.content:
(a) Where the Administrator determines that a user has failed to apply the full amount of the tax due under this article, such Administrator may, or if such Administrator determines that a public utility or resale customer has failed to remit the amount of tax money received from users, and due the City, such Administrator shall issue a proposed assessment showing the amount due and unpaid, together with interest and penalties that may have accrued thereon. The proposed assessment shall be served upon the user, public utility or resale customer in person, or by mailing by registered or certified mail to the last known address of such user, public utility or resale customer. Proof of mailing the proposed assessment is *prima facie* evidence of a receipt thereof by the addressee.

Supp. No. 4

CD44:79
$\S 44-5-11$

DETROIT CODE

(b) A user, public utility or resale customer has 30 days after receipt of a proposed assessment within which to file a written protest with the Administrator, who shall give the user, public utility or resale customer or the duly authorized representative of the user, public utility or resale customer an opportunity to be heard and present evidence and arguments in their behalf.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-9; Code 1984, § 18-11-9)

**Case law annotation**—(1) Upheld validity of City administrative rule governing utility users tax, but remanded for determination whether retroactive application of rule was permissible, and (2) City had authority under Act to start collection action, based on Commissioner of Revenue’s order which found valid City administrative rule requiring utility to bill customers for whom it only transported gas customers would have paid for gas had they purchased gas from utility. *City of Detroit v General Motors Corp*, 233 Mich App 132; 592 NW2d 732 (1998). (This case construed similar language in this section contained in the 1984 Detroit City Code).

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1169.

**Sec. 44-5-12. Issuance of final assessment.**

(a) After the hearing the Administrator shall issue a final assessment setting forth the total amount found due in the proposed assessment and any adjustment such Administrator may have made as a result of the protest. The final assessment shall be served in the same manner as a proposed assessment. Proof of mailing of the final assessment is *prima facie* evidence of a receipt thereof by the addressee.

(b) If a protest is not filed in respect to a proposed assessment, a user, public utility or resale customer is deemed to have received a final assessment 30 days after the receipt of the proposed assessment.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-10; Code 1984, § 18-11-10)

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1170.

**Sec. 44-5-13. Administrator’s action upon user’s refusal to pay tax due.**

If the public utility or resale customer determines and reports to the Administrator that a utility user has refused to pay the tax due, the public utility or resale customer is relieved of the obligation to rebill the tax amount involved. In this event the Administrator may, but is not required to, issue a proposed assessment or a final assessment against the user. The Administrator may issue a ten-day demand for payment, and if no payment or satisfactory evidence of payment is made in the ten days, such Administrator may thereafter recover the tax with interest and penalties thereon in the name of the City in any court of record as other debts are recoverable, or prosecute for violation of this article under Section 44-5-3 of this Code, or both.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-11; Code 1984, § 18-11-11)

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1171.

**Sec. 44-5-14. Three-year limit on additional assessment; exception.**

Except in case of fraud, failure to file a return, or omission of substantial portions of tax due on a return under this article, an additional assessment shall not be made after three years from the date the return was due, including extensions thereof, or the tax was paid, whichever is later.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-12; Code 1984, § 18-11-12)

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1172.

**Sec. 44-5-15. Three-year limit on refund of erroneously paid tax.**

(a) Except as otherwise provided in this article, a tax erroneously paid shall not be refunded unless a claim for refund is made within three years from the date the payment was made to the City or the annual return was due, including extensions thereof, whichever is later. Upon denial of a refund a taxpayer may follow the procedure for appeal as provided in Section 44-5-16 of this Code.

(b) A tax deficiency as finally determined and interest or penalties thereon shall be paid within 30 days after receipt of a final assessment where no appeal is made.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-13; Code 1984, § 18-11-13)

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1173.

**Sec. 44-5-16. Appeal by aggrieved person; results of final order.**

Any person aggrieved by a rule adopted by the Administrator, denial, in whole or in part, of a claim for refund, or a special ruling, may file a timely appeal therefrom to the State Commissioner of Revenue in such form and manner as the Commissioner shall prescribe. Within 30 days after a final order of the Commissioner upon the appeal, such person shall pay the City the taxes, interest and penalty found due to the City, and the City shall refund any amount found to have been overpaid.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-14; Code 1984, § 18-11-14)

**State law reference**—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1174.

Supp. No. 4

laws.title: Appeal payments to be made from general fund
laws.content:
If a person is found entitled by a decision on an appeal to recover any sum paid and no further appeal has been taken within the time limited, the sum shall be paid from the general fund of the City.

(Code 1964, § 21-11-16; Code 1984, § 18-11-16)

*State law reference—Similar provisions, MCL 141.1176.*

laws.title: Approval of uniform video service local franchise to Rocket Fiber LLC
laws.content: Secs. 45-3-24—45-3-30. Reserved.

laws.title: Misdemeanor violation; continuing violation; penalties for conviction thereof
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to violate any provision of this article.

(b) Any person who violates this article may be issued a misdemeanor violation for each day that the violation continues.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-6(c); Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-5), eff. 5-12-1981)

laws.title: Franchise required for operation
laws.content:
No person shall operate or participate in the operation of a cable communication system within the City without first obtaining a permit under Article II of this chapter and a franchise granted by the City through enactment of an ordinance under Article III of this chapter. For the purposes of this chapter, a cable communications system shall not include a system that serves only subscribers in multiple-unit dwellings under common ownership, control or management which does not use City rights-of-way.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-1; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-1), eff. 5-12-1981)

laws.title: Risks assumed by franchisee
laws.content:
Nothing in this chapter shall affect the right of a private person to require that the franchisee agree to provide reasonable indemnification to an owner, agent, or representative from damage or liability for damages caused by the installation, operation, maintenance, or removal of cable communication facilities.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-3; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-7), eff. 5-12-1981)

laws.title: Censorship prohibited
laws.content:
(a) The City shall not prohibit or limit any program or type of program or otherwise censor the communications or signals by the franchisee or other parties over the cable communications system, other than programs on the designated government access channel or channels, and shall not promulgate any regulation or condition which would interfere with the exercise, via cable television, of any rights protected by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution.

(b) The City, the franchisee whose facilities are used to transmit a program produced by a party other than the franchisee pursuant to the provisions of the franchise, or applicable state or federal law or regulations, or the officers, directors or employees of the franchisee, shall not be liable for damages arising from any obscene or defamatory statements or actions or invasions of privacy occurring during any program when the City or franchisee does not originate or produce such a program.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-4; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-9), eff. 5-12-1981)

laws.title: Reselling service prohibited
laws.content:
No person shall resell, without the express written consent of both the franchisee and the City, any cable service, program, or signal transmitted by a franchisee operating under a franchise granted by the City.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-5; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-5), eff. 5-12-1981)

laws.title: Theft of services and tampering
laws.content:
(a) No person, whether or not a subscriber to a cable system, shall willfully, maliciously or otherwise damage or cause to be damaged any wire, cable, conduit, apparatus, or equipment of the cable communication system, or commit any act with intent to cause such damage, or to tap, tamper with, or otherwise connect any wire or device to a wire, cable, conduit, apparatus, appurtenance or equipment of such system, with the intent to obtain a signal or impulse from the cable system without authorization from or compensation to the franchisee, or to obtain cable television or other communications service with intent to cheat or defraud the franchisee of any lawful charge to which it is entitled.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to tap, monitor, or arrange for the tapping or monitoring of any cable, line, signal input device or subscriber outlet or receiver for any purpose whatsoever without the specific written authorization of the subscriber or pursuant to a court order.

(c) The rights reserved by the City herein are in addition to all other rights and remedies the City may have under the franchise or any other law and are not intended to be exclusive.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-6; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-8), eff. 5-12-1981)

**Sec. 45-1-7. Protection of property permitted.**

Nothing in this chapter shall affect the right of a private person to require that the cable communications system facilities conform to applicable law and regulations or which may reasonably be necessary to protect safety, function, appearance and value of premises or the convenience of persons or property.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-7; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-6), eff. 5-12-1981)

**Sec. 45-1-8. Interference with right to receive cable service prohibited.**

Neither the owner of any multiple-unit residential dwelling nor the owner’s agent or representative shall interfere with the rights of any tenant or lawful resident thereof to receive cable communication service, cable installation, or maintenance from a franchisee regulated by and lawfully operating under a valid and existing communication franchise granted by the City.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-8; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-2), eff. 5-12-1981)

**Sec. 45-1-9. Gratuities and payments to permit service prohibited.**

Neither the owner of any multiple-unit residential dwelling nor the owner’s agent or representative shall ask, demand or receive any payment, service or gratuity in any form as a condition for permitting or cooperating with the installation of a cable communication service to the dwelling unit occupied by a tenant or resident requesting service.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-9; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-3), eff. 5-12-1981)

**Sec. 45-1-10. Penalties and charges for service prohibited by owner of multiple-unit building.**

Neither the owner of any multiple-unit residential dwelling nor the owner’s agent or representative shall penalize, charge or surcharge a tenant or resident or forfeit or threaten to forfeit any right of such tenant or resident, or discriminate in any way against such tenant or resident, who requests or receives cable communication service from a franchise granted by the City.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-1-10; Ord. No. 437-H, § 1(61A-1-4), eff. 5-12-1981)

**Secs. 45-1-11—45-1-30. Reserved.**

**ARTICLE II. USE OF PUBLIC WAYS BY TELECOMMUNICATIONS PROVIDERS***

**Sec. 45-2-1. Purpose.**

The purpose of this article is to regulate the access to, and ongoing use of, public rights-of-way by telecommunications providers for the telecommunications facilities while protecting the public health, safety, and welfare and exercising reasonable control of the public rights-of-way in compliance with the Michigan Metropolitan Extension Telecommunications Rights-of-Way Oversight Act, being MCL 484.3101 *et seq.*, and other applicable laws, and to ensure that the City qualifies for distributions under the Act by modifying the fees charged to providers and is in compliance with the Act.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-5-1; Ord. No. 21-02, § 1(9.5-5-1), eff. 11-1-2002)

**Sec. 45-2-2. Conflicts.**

Nothing in this article shall be construed in such a manner as to conflict with the Michigan Metropolitan Extension Telecommunications Rights-of-Way Oversight Act, being MCL 484.3101 *et seq.*, or other applicable law.

(Code 1984, § 9.5-5-2; Ord. No. 21-02, § 1(9.5-5-2), eff. 11-1-2002)

**Sec. 45-2-3. Definitions.**

For the purpose of this article, the following words and phrases shall have the meaning respectively ascribed to them by this section:

*Act* means the Michigan Metropolitan Extension Telecommunications Rights-of-Way Oversight Act, being MCL 484.3101 *et seq.*

*Authority* means, as likewise defined in Section 2 of the Act, being MCL 484.3102, the metropolitan authority created under the Michigan Local Community Stabilization Authority Act, being MCL 123.1341 *et seq.*

*Broadband internet access transport service* means the broadband transmission of data between an end-user and the end-user’s internet service provider’s point of interconnection at a speed of 200 or more kilobits per second to the end-user’s premises.

*State law reference—Michigan Metropolitan Extension Telecommunications Right-of-Way Oversight Act, MCL 484.3101 *et seq.*
