laws.title: Insurance requirements
laws.content:
(a) Prior to the issuance of a license to operate a commercial quadricycle for hire, the licensee shall file a certificate of insurance that is signed by a duly authorized officer of a company, which is authorized to write insurance in this state, to the effect that a policy of insurance has been issued and is in full force and effect to the licensee and that the premium has been paid as required thereon, together with a true copy of the policy contract or certificate of insurance.

(b) Such policy of insurance shall insure the licensee against loss resulting from liability imposed by law for bodily injury and property damage with a minimum combined single limit of $2,000,000.00 for all persons injured or for property damage.

(c) The policy of insurance shall name the City as an additional insured party.

(d) The policy of insurance shall contain a provision for a continuing liability thereunder to the full amount thereof, notwithstanding any recovery thereon, and that until the policy is revoked, as provided in Subsection (e) of this section, the insurance company shall not be relieved from liability on account of nonpayment of premium, failure of the commercial quadricycle owner to renew the City business license at the end of the term, or any act or omission of the named insured.

(e) Any insurance company whose policy has been so filed pursuant to this section may file a notice with the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department of its intention to terminate and cancel such policy and give notice thereof to the named licensee, whereupon after ten days from filing, the licensee or owner shall cease to operate, or cause such commercial quadricycle not to be operated, within the City, and the license issued therefor shall be automatically revoked and liability on such policy shall cease and terminate, provided, that the liability of the insurance company therefor for any act or omission of the licensee or owners occurring prior to the effective date of cancellation shall not be discharged or impaired.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-25; Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-25), eff. 12-28-2016)

laws.title: Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to take action upon application
laws.content:
Upon compliance with Sections 47-3-21 through 47-3-25 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall issue an annual license for a business in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-22(b); Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-22(b)), eff. 12-28-2016)

laws.title: Expiration and renewal
laws.content:
All licenses issued under this division shall expire on March 31st of the year following the year of issuance and shall be renewable for each year thereafter.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-26; Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-26), eff. 12-28-2016)

laws.title: Suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal
laws.content:
A license that is issued under this division may be suspended, revoked, or denied renewal in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-27; Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-27), eff. 12-28-2016)

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a commercial quadricycle within the City without having a valid public driver's license from the Police Department in accordance with Article IX of this chapter.

CD47:37

DETROIT CITY CODE

(b) Each licensee shall comply with the laws of this state and shall have been certified by the Police Department as an authorized person to transport passengers in a commercial quadricycle in the City.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-31; Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-31), eff. 12-28-2016)

laws.title: Additional qualifications
laws.content:
In addition to the requirements in Section 47-9-3 of this Code, an applicant for a public driver license to operate a commercial quadricycle must meet the following requirements:

(1) Be able to satisfactorily establish that he or she is currently in sufficient physical condition to master the handling, control, and safe and proper transportation of a fully-occupied commercial quadricycle; and

(2) Have knowledge of the routes, hours of operation, pickup and passenger discharge locations approved and designated by the City.

(Code 1984, § 58-9-32; Ord. No. 41-16, § 1(58-9-32), eff. 12-28-2016)

Secs. 47-3-43—47-3-50. Reserved.

laws.title: Unauthorized access to Detroit People Mover System
laws.content:
No person shall enter onto the property of the Detroit People Mover System or onto any of the Detroit People

laws.title: Transportation for Hire
laws.content:
§ 47-4-12

Mover System vehicles, or shall get on, under or between such vehicles or onto the guideways, except in the ordinary transaction of business.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-2; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-2), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Impeding or hindering employees of the Detroit Transportation Corporation
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to impede or hinder an employee of the Detroit Transportation Corporation in the performance of such employee’s duties.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-3; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-3), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Unlawful to vandalize Detroit People Mover System property
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to tamper with, deface, destroy, disfigure or vandalize any property of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-4; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-4), eff. 6-19-1987)

*State law reference—Malicious mischief generally, MCL 750.377a et seq.*

laws.title: Unlawful to obstruct guideways or property of the Detroit People Mover System
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to place or cause to be placed any obstruction on or over the Detroit People Mover System guideways or property or in any way inhibit or endanger the operation of the Detroit People Mover.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-5; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-5), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Unlawful use of missiles, projectiles, and objects
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to throw, shoot or drop any missile, projectile or object at or from any part of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-6; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-6), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Smoking and spitting prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to smoke, carry lighted tobacco, or spit within any vehicle or station area of the Detroit People Mover System, except that smoking or carrying of lighted tobacco may be permitted within designated smoking areas of the station.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-7; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-7), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Eating, drinking, and use of intoxicants or controlled substances prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful to eat or drink, or carry an open container of food or beverage, on any Detroit People Mover System vehicle or in any area of a station.

(b) No person in a visibly intoxicated state or visibly under the influence of a controlled substance shall utilize the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-8; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-8), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Playing radios and other electronic devices prohibited; exception
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to play any musical instrument, or any radio or other electronic audio or video playback device, without using earphones or earbuds, within any Detroit People Mover System vehicle or area of any station.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-9; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-9), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Animals prohibited; exception
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to bring, carry or transport any animal on a Detroit People Mover System vehicle or in any area of the system, with the exception of a service animal as defined in Section 47-4-1 of this Code.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-10; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-10), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Disposal of solid waste and deposit of bodily discharge prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful to dispose of solid waste, as defined in Section 42-1-1 of this Code, including, but not limited to, garbage, papers, refuse, or other forms of trash within the Detroit People Mover System, except in receptacles provided for such purpose.

(b) No person shall deposit, blow, or spread any bodily discharge on any part of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-11; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-11), eff. 6-19-1987)

*State law reference—Littering, MCL 324.8901 et seq.*

laws.title: Refusal to pay fare
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to refuse to pay the established fare, evade payment of fare, remain in a vehicle for longer than one trip on the Detroit People

§ 47-4-12

DETROIT CITY CODE

Mover without paying another fare, or enter onto the system through exit doors or emergency exits of any part of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-12; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-12), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: False reports or threats prohibited
laws.content:
(a) It shall be unlawful to make a false report to any person regarding the conduct of another person concerning the operation of the Detroit People Mover System.

(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to make a threat concerning the Detroit People Mover System or its employees or agents.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-13; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-13), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Forgery and counterfeit items prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to make, possess, use, offer for sale, sell, barter, exchange, pass or deliver any forged, counterfeit or falsely altered pass, permit, fare card, master key, token, identification card, or other authorization purporting to be issued by or on behalf of the Detroit Transportation Corporation.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-14; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-14), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Explosives and fireworks prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to carry, transport or ignite any explosive, fireworks, acid or flammable liquid anywhere on the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-15; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-15), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Equipment cabinets, unauthorized access prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to enter any equipment cabinet of any vehicle.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-16; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-16), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Safety lines, unlawful to cross
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to cross a safety line on a Detroit People Mover System station platform except to enter or exit a vehicle.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-17; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-17), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Equipment use
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized individual to operate any Detroit People Mover System equipment except:

(1) Where such equipment is designed for use by the public; or

(2) When necessary in an emergency situation.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-18; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-18), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Detroit Mover vehicle doors
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to interfere with the operation of a Detroit Mover vehicle doors.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-19; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-19), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Order to leave vehicle or Detroit People Mover System facilities
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person to refuse to leave a Detroit People Mover System vehicle or any other part of the Detroit People Mover System upon proper direction or order of an employee of the Detroit Transportation Corporation.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-20; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-20), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Soliciting or carrying on business
Commercial photography or recording
laws.content:
No person, unless authorized in writing by the Detroit Transportation Corporation, shall take still, motion, or sound motion pictures or sound records or

CD47:40

laws.title: Transportation for Hire
laws.content:
§ 47-4-27

recordings of voices or otherwise for commercial, training or educational purposes, other than news coverage, anywhere in the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-22; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-22), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Building construction and improvements
laws.content:
No person, unless the environmental, operational, safety, security, and structural integrity impacts on the Detroit People Mover System have been reviewed and approved in writing by the Detroit Transportation Corporation, shall construct or cause to be constructed any permanent or temporary buildings or structures, including signs, utility connections, or any improvements, modifications, or additions to any such buildings or structures, or any pavings, excavations, removal of oil or fill material anywhere within 50 feet of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-23; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-23), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Advertising
laws.content:
No person, unless authorized in writing by the Detroit Transportation Corporation, shall post or distribute commercial signs, advertisements, literature, circulars, pictures, sketches, drawings, handbills, or any other form of printed or written commercial matter or material anywhere within the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-24; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-24), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Vending in public areas
laws.content:
No person shall vend services, including, but not limited to, amusements and food and beverages, anywhere within 75 feet of the Detroit People Mover System, unless authorized in writing by the Detroit Transportation Corporation.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-25; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-25), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Signs
laws.content:
No person, unless authorized in writing by the Detroit Transportation Corporation, shall construct or install any sign or device anywhere on the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-26; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-26), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Solicitation of contributions and distribution of materials—Generally
laws.content:
(a) No person shall solicit alms or contributions of money or other articles of value for religious, charitable or any other purpose, or conduct or participate in any speech-making, distributing of pamphlets, books or other written or graphic materials anywhere on the Detroit People Mover System without having delivered a written notice to the Executive Director, or the Director’s designee, of the intent to do so at least ten days prior thereto so that the Detroit Transportation Corporation may be fully informed of the activity proposed and take adequate precautions to protect the public health, safety, welfare and order, to ensure the efficient and orderly use of the Detroit People Mover System for its primary purpose and function, and to ensure appropriate opportunity for the freedom of expression to others.

(b) The written notice required herein shall provide:

(1) The full name, address, and mailing address if different, telephone number of the person furnishing the notice, and if an organization, the name, address and telephone number of a responsible local officer thereof and the title of such officer;

(2) The purpose or subject of the proposed activity and a description of the means and methods intended to be used in conducting the same. If the proposed activity includes the solicitation of alms, donations or contributions of money or of other articles of value, the notice shall contain the verified statement of a responsible local officer of the organization furnishing the notice that it is a tax-exempt organization under existing federal laws and regulations and that donations and contributions made to such organization may lawfully be included as charitable deductions on a donor’s federal income tax return for the year in which made; and

(3) The date, hours and location desired for the proposed activity and the maximum number of persons proposing to participate therein at any one time or period of time, together with a form of identification card, authenticated copies of which shall be displayed on the outer clothing of each individual participating in the particular activity proposed. Such identification cards shall contain the name of the organization furnishing

CD47:41
§ 47-4-27

DETROIT CITY CODE

the notice, the legal name of the individual bearing the card, the signature and title of the official of such organization and the date issued.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-27; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-27), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Same—Regulations
laws.content:
Persons having given such written notice shall be permitted to conduct their activities in or on the Detroit People Mover System with the number of persons, at the time, for the purpose, in the manner, and with the identification card, all as set forth in their respective written notices subject only to such restrictions as may be prescribed from time to time by the Detroit Transportation Corporation, provided, that any such restrictions shall be reasonable and appropriate and shall be prescribed only after a finding by the Detroit Transportation Corporation that the restrictions are necessary to avoid injury, or the likelihood of injury, to persons or property, or to ensure the safe, peaceful, and orderly use of the system by the public, and such restrictions shall be applied equally and without discrimination as to all persons who have given such written notice. A copy of any such restrictions and any explanatory diagrammatic attachments shall be furnished those persons affected.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-28; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-28), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Same—Interference prohibited
laws.content:
(a) While engaging in the activities provided for herein, no person shall:

(1) Prevent or interfere with access to or egress from entrances or exits, fare gates, change or token machines, platforms, vehicles, stairways, escalators, or elevators;

(2) In any manner assail, coerce, threaten or physically disturb any member of the public, any Detroit Transportation Corporation employee, or any other person for any reason; or

(3) Prevent, impede, interfere with, hamper or curtail the conduct of ordinary business on the Detroit People Mover System.

The activities provided for herein shall not intrude upon or take place in any location or area reserved or zoned for a particular use including, but not limited to Detroit Transportation Corporation offices and reception areas, Detroit People Mover System stations, and within any vehicle.

(b) No individual engaged in the proposed activity shall solicit any donation or engage a member of the public as a prospective donee without first identifying the organization such individual represents in connection with such prospective donation.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-29; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-29), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Same—Posting of written or graphic matter prohibited
laws.content:
While engaging in the activities provided for herein, no person shall affix any written or graphic matter to any Detroit People Mover System structure or facility, or leave any such matter unattended at any location anywhere within the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-30; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-30), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Same—No sales
laws.content:
While engaging in the activities provided for herein, no person shall:

(1) Sell any material whatsoever to a member of the public;

(2) Tender or transfer any material whatsoever to a member of the public in return for a fixed sum of money or other specific thing of value agreed upon in advance of such tender or transfer; or

(3) After the transfer of such material, require or demand any sum of money or other specific thing of value including the item transferred, from any member of the public.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-31; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-31), eff. 6-19-1987)

laws.title: Modification of restrictions
laws.content:
The Detroit Transportation Corporation is empowered to restrict or modify, wholly or partially, the activities provided for herein as needed or as determined in the best interest of the Detroit People Mover System or in the event of emergencies, including, but not limited to, strikes, accidents, riots, civil disturbances, power failures, tornadoes, or other conditions tending to disrupt the normal operation of the Detroit People Mover System.

(Code 1984, § 58-7-32; Ord. No. 18-87, § 1(58-7-32), eff. 6-19-1987)

Secs. 47-4-33—47-4-50. Reserved.

CD47:42

laws.title: Exemption for concession at Belle Isle
laws.content:
The concession at Belle Isle shall be exempt from the provisions of this article.  
(Code 1984, § 58-3-2)

laws.title: Rates
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department is authorized to establish, with the approval of the City Council through adoption of a resolution, the amount to be charged and collected for the use of an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage by one or more passengers.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the schedule of permitted rates shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk;

(3) Conspicuously displayed at all times upon a sign provided by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, which shall be permanently affixed to the vehicle; and

(4) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) No direct or indirect charge of any kind shall be made to a passenger for any reason other than the charges permitted by law.  
(Code 1964, §§ 60-3-8, 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-3; Ord. No. 29-13, § 1(58-3-3), eff. 11-22-2013)

laws.title: Card frame for license and inspection card
laws.content:
A card frame shall be permanently and conspicuously affixed to each electric carriage and horse-drawn carriage at the forward part of the passenger compartment and made visible to all passengers. Such card frame shall contain at all times the current electric carriage or horse-drawn carriage driver’s license and the Police Department inspection card.  
(Code 1964, § 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-4)

laws.title: Records to be kept by owner
Designated routes
laws.content:
After leaving its designated starting point, an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage may pick up and discharge passengers only at specified locations and only on a prescribed route. Such stops and routes shall be designated by the Director of the Department of Public Works, in cooperation with the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, the Police Department, the Detroit Department of Transportation, and the Planning and Development Department.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-16; Code 1984, § 58-3-6; Ord. No. 29-13, § 1(58-3-6), eff. 11-22-2013)

laws.title: Advertising matter on carriage prohibited
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful for any person, owning or operating an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage for hire, to permit advertising matter to be affixed to or installed in or on such electric carriage or horse-drawn carriage for hire.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-14; Code 1984, § 58-3-7)

Cross reference—Advertising generally, Ch. 4.

laws.title: Number parked at one stop
laws.content:
No more than two electric carriages or horse-drawn carriages shall be allowed to stand parked at any one stop at any one time.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-17; Code 1984, § 58-3-8)

laws.title: Time of operation
laws.content:
No electric carriage or horse-drawn carriage shall operate from 6:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. on weekdays.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-15; Code 1984, § 58-3-9)

laws.title: Hours of use for each horse
laws.content:
No owner of a horse-drawn carriage shall permit any one horse to be driven more than ten hours in any 24-hour period. Where more than one driver is assigned to the same horse in any continuous 24-hour period, the records shall indicate the time each driver and horse left and returned to the stable.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-10)

laws.title: Care of horses
laws.content:
All carriage horses shall be treated in a humane manner. All carriage horses shall also be properly diapered. An owner shall be responsible for the humane care and treatment of such owner’s carriage horse, when it is under such owner’s direct supervision and control. At all other times, the owner is required to take all necessary and reasonable steps to ensure the humane care and treatment of such owner’s horses while under the direct supervision and control of a licensed driver.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-11)

laws.title: Marking of horse
laws.content:
Each carriage horse shall be plainly and conspicuously marked by a different number, three-fourths of an inch high, permanently branded onto its left front hoof.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-12)

laws.title: Inspections
laws.content:
(a) Each electric carriage and horse-drawn carriage, and the harness and traces of each horse-drawn carriage, shall be clean, in good working condition and shall be inspected at least once daily by the licensee.

(b) Each electric carriage and horse-drawn carriage shall be available for inspection by the Police Department as required by Subsection (c) of this section.

CD47:44

laws.title: Transportation for Hire
laws.content:
§ 47-5-18

(c) The Police Department shall cause all licensed electric carriages and horse-drawn carriages to be inspected at least once every four months. The date of such inspection and the signature of the person making the inspection shall be recorded upon the inspection card in the spaces provided therefor.

(Code 1964, §§ 60-3-6, 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-13)

laws.title: Repairs and alterations
laws.content:
Each licensee of an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage shall make repairs and alterations to the electric carriage or horse-drawn carriage as may be required by the Police Department or as is necessary to maintain proper standards of comfort and safety.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-14)

laws.title: Duties of drivers
Prohibitions for drivers
Suspension of operations by Chief of Police
laws.content:
The Chief of Police shall have the authority to temporarily suspend the operation of electric carriages and horse-drawn carriages on the streets of the City when conditions for such operations become unsuitable or unsafe.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-18; Code 1984, § 58-3-17)

laws.title: Promulgation of administrative rules; prescription of forms
laws.content:
The Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department may promulgate admin-

CD47:45
$\S 47-5-18$

DETROIT CITY CODE

istrative rules in accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, and prescribe such forms as are necessary to carry out the provisions of this article.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-11; Code 1984, § 58-3-18; Ord. No. 282-H, § 1, eff. 11-3-1978; Ord. No. 29-13, § 1(58-3-18), eff. 11-22-2013)

Secs. 47-5-19—47-5-30. Reserved.

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to operate for hire an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage in the City without first having obtained a license from the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to operate such business.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-2; Code 1984, § 58-3-31)

laws.title: Application; information required
Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee
laws.content:
(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 6-503(13) of the Charter for the processing and issuance of a license under this division. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

*Cross reference—Licenses generally, Ch. 28.

CD47:46

laws.title: Transportation for Hire
laws.content:
§ 47-5-36

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department at least once every two years.

(c) A fee shall be charged each new licensee, any current licensee who applies to renew an existing license, or a current licensee applying for a license at another location.

(d) Prior to the expiration of a current license, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay an annual fee for the renewal of a license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation of the business for the location until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

laws.title: Ownership prerequisite to issuance
laws.content:
No license shall be issued under this division without first establishing ownership of an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage.

(Code 1964, § 60-3-3; Code 1984, § 58-3-32)

laws.title: Inspection prerequisite to issuance
laws.content:
(a) A vehicle shall be licensed as an electric carriage or as a horse-drawn carriage only after the vehicle, and the horse for a horse-drawn carriage, have been examined and inspected, and found to comply with all the requirements of the vehicle and traffic laws of the state, and shall have been certified by the Police Department as being safe and properly equipped to operate. The Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall refuse a license to, or, where already issued, suspend the license of any electric carriage, or horse-drawn carriage or horse, found to be unfit for operation.

(b) The Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department shall prescribe an appropriate form of inspection card for electric carriages and horse-drawn carriages and the manner that such card and the electric carriage or horse-drawn carriage driver’s identification card shall be displayed.

(Code 1964, §§ 60-3-5, 60-3-7; Code 1984, § 58-3-33; Ord. No. 29-13, § 1(58-3-33), eff. 11-22-2013)

laws.title: Insurance prerequisite to issuance
laws.content:
(a) Before the issuance of a license to operate an electric carriage or a horse-drawn carriage for hire, the owner shall file a certificate of insurance signed by a duly authorized officer of a company authorized to write insurance in this state to the effect that a policy of insurance has been issued and is in full force and effect to the licensee and that the premium has been paid as required thereon, together with a true copy of the policy contract or certificate of insurance.

(d) Such policy of insurance shall contain a provision for a continuing liability thereunder to the full amount thereof notwithstanding any recovery thereon, and that until the policy is revoked, as herein provided, the insurance company will not be relieved from liability on account of non-payment of premium, failure to renew license at the end of the year, or any act or omission of the named assured.

**Sec. 47-5-38. Investigation by Office of Chief Financial Officer required to confirm no City tax or assessment arrearage.**

(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by this division shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessments are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

**Sec. 47-5-39. License plate and date tab.**

(b) The license plate issued to the licensee may be, at the discretion of the Director of the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department, a plate of a permanent nature with a replaceable date tab attached thereto, indicating the expiration date of the plate during each license year and the issuance of such a plate with such date tab to a person possessing such a plate, shall be deemed issuance of a license plate. Such license plate and the replaceable date tab to be issued from year to year to be attached thereto, shall be of such material, form, design and dimension, and set forth such distinguishing number or other identification marks as the Director shall prescribe.

The failure to affix or display such date tab in a manner prescribed by the Director shall constitute a violation of this section.

(d) In the event of the loss, mutilation or destruction of any license plate or date tab issued hereunder, the owner may file such statement and proof of facts as the Director shall require with a fee adopted in accordance with Section 47-5-33 of this Code at the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center, and the Business License Center shall issue a duplicate or substitute license plate or date tab.

(Code 1964, §§ 60-3-4, 60-3-13; Code 1984, § 58-3-36; Ord. No. 29-13, § 1(58-3-36), eff. 11-22-2013)

**Sec. 47-5-40. Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center to take action upon application.**

Upon compliance with Sections 47-5-31 through 47-5-39 of this Code, the Buildings, Safety Engineering, and Environmental Department Business License Center shall issue an annual license for a business in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, Licenses.

**Sec. 47-5-41. Non-transferable.**

All licenses issued under this division are not transferable to another individual, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity.

laws.title: Required
laws.content:
(a) Each driver of a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, a sightseeing bus, a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw shall be licensed as a public driver.

(b) No person shall permit any employee to operate a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, a sightseeing bus, a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw within the City without first obtaining a public driver’s license from the City.

(c) No licensee of a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, a sightseeing bus, a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw shall permit an unlicensed driver, or any driver whose public driver’s license has been suspended or revoked, to operate said vehicle for hire in the City.

laws.title: Application; qualifications of drivers
laws.content:
(a) Each applicant for a public driver’s license must:

(1) Be 18 years of age or older;

(2) Be in good physical condition, have good eyesight, and not subject to epilepsy, to vertigo, to heart trouble, to any other infirmity of the body or of the mind, or to the chronic use of prescription drugs or medication, which might render the applicant unfit for the safe operation of a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, a sightseeing bus, a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw;

(3) Be able to sufficiently read, write, speak and understand the English language to carry out the duties of a driver;

(4) Be clean in dress and in person;

(5) Not be addicted to alcoholic liquor, a controlled substance, or an illegal drug;

(6) Possess a valid Michigan driver license;

(7) Not be liable, either criminally or civilly, for more than four traffic violations within any 12-month period;

(8) Know the geography of the City;

(9) Have knowledge of the traffic regulations under Chapter 46 of this Code, Traffic and Vehicles;

(10) If applicable, present proof of eligibility either to be employed or to be self-employed in the United States in accordance with federal law and rules promulgated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services;

(11) Produce certificates of good character, on forms provided by the Police Department, from two reputable citizens who have known the applicant personally and observed such applicant’s conduct during one month prior to the date of such application; and

(12) Upon a form provided by the Police Department, complete a statement giving the applicant’s full name, residence, place of residence for five years previous to moving to such applicant’s present address, age, height, color of eyes and hair, place of birth, length of time such applicant has resided in the City, whether such applicant is a citizen of the United States, places of previous employment, whether such applicant has ever been convicted of a felony or misdemeanor and, if convicted, the nature of the crime and the date and place of conviction, whether such applicant has previously been licensed as a driver or chauffeur and, if so, when and where, and whether such applicant’s license has ever been revoked and for what cause, which statement shall be signed and sworn to by the applicant in the presence of a notary public and filed as a permanent record with the Police Department.

(b) The investigation of all applications for a public driver’s license under this article shall be conducted by the Police Department and, when such investigation is completed, the application shall be forwarded by the inspecting police officer to the Chief of Police, who shall

**Sec. 47-9-4. Photograph of driver to accompany application.**

Each applicant for a public driver's license must file with such applicant's application three recent photographs of themselves, showing a reasonable likeness of the applicant, that are of a size that may be attached easily to the license. One shall be attached to such license when issued, one shall be attached to the card, and the third shall be attached to the application and filed with the Police Department. The photograph shall be affixed to the license so that it cannot be removed and another photograph substituted without detection.

(Code 1984, $\S$ 58-8-33; Ord. No. 23-06, $\S$ 1(58-8-33), eff. 7-28-2006; Ord. No. 41-16, $\S$ 1(58-9-33), eff. 12-28-2016)

**Sec. 47-9-5. Establishment, approval, publication, and payment of annual fee.**

(a) A non-refundable fee shall be charged and collected in accordance with Section 28-1-7 of this Code for the processing and issuance of a license under this article. Based upon the cost of issuance and administration of the licensing regulations, the Chief of Police shall establish this fee, which is subject to approval by the City Council through adoption of a resolution.

(b) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the fees that are provided for in Subsection (a) of this section shall be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Police Department and at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the Chief of Police at least once every two years.

(c) A fee shall be charged each new licensee, any current licensee who applies to renew an existing license, or a current licensee applying for a license at another location.

(d) Prior to the expiration of a current license, a licensee shall submit an application for renewal and pay an annual fee for the renewal of a license. Submission of an application for renewal and payment of the license fee before the expiration date of the license shall allow for the continued operation of the business for the location until such time that the license renewal application is denied, or the license is suspended or revoked.

(Code 1984, $\S$ 58-8-34; Ord. No. 23-06, $\S$ 1(58-8-34), eff. 7-28-2006; Ord. No. 41-16, $\S$ 1(58-9-34), eff. 12-28-2016)

**Sec. 47-9-6. Examination of applicants.**

Each applicant for a public driver's license shall be examined by a person designated by the Police Department, as to such applicant's knowledge of the provisions of this article and traffic regulations and, if the result of the examination is unsatisfactory, such applicant shall be denied a license. Where required by the Police Department, each applicant must demonstrate the skill and ability to safely handle the charter bus, inter-city bus, intra-city bus, sightseeing bus, commercial quadricycle, electric carriage, horse-drawn carriage, pedal-cab, or rickshaw by driving said vehicle through a crowded section of the City accompanied by an examining police officer designated by the Police Department.

**Sec. 47-9-7. Investigation by Office of Chief Financial Officer required to confirm no City tax or assessment arrearage.**

(a) Upon application and before any license that is required by this article shall be issued or renewed, it shall be the duty of the Police Department to refer such application to the Office of Chief Financial Officer, which shall cause an investigation to be completed in accordance with Section 2-113 of the Charter to determine whether any property tax, income tax, personal tax or special assessments are unpaid, outstanding or delinquent to the City.

(b) A license shall not be issued or renewed by the Police Department until the Chief Financial Officer has given written confirmation that the applicant is not in arrears to the City for taxes or assessments that are delineated in Subsection (a) of this section.

**Sec. 47-9-8. Form; defacing, of licenses prohibited.**

(a) Upon satisfactory fulfillment of the requirements of this article, the applicant shall be issued a public driver's license, which shall be in such form as to contain the photograph and signature of the licensee.

laws.content: Upon compliance with Sections 47-9-4 through 47-9-8 of this Code, the Police Department shall issue an annual license under this article in accordance with Chapter 28 of this Code, *Licenses*, which contains an endorsement of the type of vehicle that the driver will operate.

Display of license in certain vehicles
laws.content: Every licensed public driver of a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw shall conspicuously display such driver’s license, together with such driver’s photograph, on the inside of such driver’s vehicle for hire, with a light shining upon it at night, so that it may be seen easily both during the day and night by passengers of the vehicle for hire.

laws.title: Expiration dates and renewal requirements
laws.content:
(a) A license that is issued under this article for the driver of a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, or a sightseeing bus, shall expire on December 31st of each year.

(b) All applications for renewal of a license for a driver of a charter bus, an inter-city bus, an intra-city bus, or a sightseeing bus, shall be filed before January 1st of each year.

(c) A license that is issued under this article for the driver of a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw shall expire on March 31st of each year.

(d) All applications for renewal of a license for a driver of a commercial quadricycle, an electric carriage, a horse-drawn carriage, a pedal-cab, or a rickshaw shall be filed before April 1st of each year.

(e) Unless renewal has lapsed as provided for in Subsection (g) of this section, the Police Department may renew a public driver’s license from year to year by appropriate endorsement by the Police Department either upon the application for renewal or, where deemed necessary, through reexamination.

(f) When applying for renewal of a public driver’s license, such driver shall make such application upon a form to be furnished by the Police Department, entitled “Application for Renewal of License,” which shall be filled out with the full name and address of the applicant together with a statement of the date upon which such driver’s original license was granted and the number thereof.

**Sec. 47-10-3. Responsibility for violations.**

(a) Except as otherwise expressly stated in this article, any violation of any provision of this article arising from or related to a particular shared electric personal mobility device, including, but not limited to, its technical features, operation, parking, or abandonment, shall be the responsibility of the owner of such shared electric personal mobility device.

(b) Nothing in this article shall assign to any particular individual or entity the responsibility for the violation of any law not set forth in this article, including, but not limited to, violations of Chapter 46 of this Code, *Traffic and Vehicles*, which, through Section 46-3-1 of this Code, adopts and incorporates by reference the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.1 *et seq.*

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-4. Violations; administrative remedies permitted.**

(a) The Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to revoke, suspend, restrict, or reduce the authorized fleet size or otherwise modify a shared mobility permit issued to any owner based upon a finding that such owner’s violation of any provision of this article constitutes a detriment to the public peace, health, safety, and welfare in the City or any portion thereof. The Director is further authorized to prohibit, suspend, or restrict the operation of an electric personal mobility device based upon a finding that the involvement of such electric personal mobility device in the violation of any provision of this article constitutes a detriment to the public peace, health, safety, and welfare.

(b) In accordance with Chapter 3 of this Code, *Administrative Hearings and Enforcement*, and *Administrative Appeals*, Article IV, *Administrative Appeals*, as well as the rules of procedure promulgated thereunder, any appeal of an administrative decision made pursuant to Subsection (a) of this section shall be made to the Department of Appeals and Hearings.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-5. Registry and reporting of alleged violations.**

(a) The Director of the Department of Public Works shall accept and investigate complaints and other allegations of violations of any provision of this article, whether identified by the Department of Public Works, referred by another department of agency of the City, or received from a member of the public, regarding electric personal mobility devices or their owners or operators. The Director shall maintain a registry of all such alleged violations, which must include for each entry, to the extent that such information is available:

(1) Date, time, and location of the alleged violation;

(2) Owner of the electric personal mobility device involved in the alleged violation;

(3) Brief description of the nature of the alleged violation;

(4) Citation to the provision of this article subject to violation;

(5) Source of the alleged violation; and

(6) Findings, if any, by the Department upon investigation into the alleged violation.

(b) No later than December 1st of each year, the Director shall prepare reports of all alleged violations that have occurred in the previous 12 months and are associated with each owner. The Director shall transmit each report to the owner associated therewith and provide not less than 30 days for each owner to provide responses to the alleged violations included in such report. The Director shall include all such responses in the registry.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-6. Abandonment, obstruction, removal, storage, and disposition.**

(a) An electric personal mobility device must not be abandoned or subject to any circumstances providing for the presumption of abandonment.

(b) An electric personal mobility device may be presumed by the Department of Public Works to be abandoned if left unattended in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The electric personal mobility device is located in a public place and in an inoperable condition for a period of at least 48 hours;

(2) The electric personal mobility device is located for any period of time on private property without the consent of the owner of such property;

(3) The electric personal mobility device is placed and allowed to remain for any period of time in a public river, stream, fountain, or other body of water, whether natural or artificial;

(5) The electric personal mobility device is located for any period of time in a public place in such a manner as to create an imminent danger to public health or safety; or

(6) The electric personal mobility device is located for any period of time in a grassy or otherwise vegetated portion of a public place.

(c) An electric personal mobility device may constitute an obstruction for purposes of Section 43-8-2 of this Code in any of the following circumstances:

(1) The electric personal mobility device is parked in a public place in violation of Section 47-10-60 of this Code;

(2) The electric personal mobility device is a shared electric personal mobility device for which the owner does not hold a valid shared mobility permit, except when expressly authorized in this article to be operated without such permit; or

(3) The electric personal mobility device satisfies any one or more of the circumstances set forth in Subsection (b) of this section that the device may be presumed to be abandoned.

(d) An electric personal mobility device that obstructs a public place or a public right-of-way in violation of Section 43-8-2 of this Code may be subject to removal in accordance with Section 43-8-7 of this Code, except that:

(1) Notwithstanding Section 43-8-7(a) of this Code, the Department of Public Works may issue notice of removal of an abandoned electric personal mobility device up to, but not more than, 24 hours after such removal; and

(2) For purposes of Section 43-8-7(b), the Department’s service of its notice of removal of a shared electric personal mobility device may be made by means of the contact information printed or otherwise affixed to the device.

(e) An electric personal mobility device that has been removed by the Department is subject to storage and disposition in accordance with Section 43-8-8 of this Code and the owner of such device is subject to all fees authorized therein.

laws.title: Permit required
laws.content:
It shall be unlawful to make available for hire a shared electric personal mobility device for operation in any public place unless its owner has been issued and currently holds a valid shared mobility permit from the City and is in compliance with the terms and conditions of such permit.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

laws.title: Permit fee
laws.content:
(a) The Department of Public Works shall require payment of a fee from each applicant for a shared mobility permit to defray the Department’s costs to administer and enforce the provisions of this division. Such fee shall be due upon submission of each shared mobility permit application and shall be non-refundable, except when a refund is expressly authorized by this division.

(b) In accordance with Section 9-507 of the Charter, the Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to establish fees, subject to approval by resolution of the City Council, based on its anticipated costs to administer the review of shared mobility permit applications and enforce compliance with the provisions of this division. The Department may establish distinct fees based on the size of the shared fleet for which the permit is applied.

(c) After adoption of a resolution by the City Council and approval of the resolution by the Mayor, the schedule of fees must be:

(1) Published in a daily newspaper of general circulation and in the Journal of the City Council;

(2) Made available at the Office of the City Clerk; and

(3) Reviewed by the City Council at least once every two years.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

laws.title: Permit term, effective date, and expiration
laws.content:
(a) A shared mobility permit issued under this division may be valid for a period not to exceed two years commencing on the date of its issuance by the Department of Public Works.

laws.title: Promulgation of parameters and minimum requirements for evaluation of shared mobility permit applications
laws.content:
(a) In accordance with Section 2-111 of the Charter, the Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to periodically promulgate parameters for purposes of evaluating shared mobility permit applications, including minimum requirements for each such parameter.

(b) The Director’s promulgation of parameters and associated minimum requirements must be based on the recommendations of the Office of Mobility Innovation and, in its sole discretion, may be based on consultation with other City departments or agencies and private stakeholders.

(c) Parameters must relate to specific issues that are reasonably related to the effective, efficient, and equitable deployment and operation of shared fleets in the City. Parameters and associated minimum requirements may include, but need not be limited to, the following:

(1) Shared fleet size for small and large shared fleets;

Digital platform

Each owner of a shared fleet must maintain, and must make available to current and prospective operators of its shared electric personal mobility devices, a digital platform through which operators can locate and access shared electric personal mobility devices, submit payments for their use, and provide feedback and other communications with the owner, among other functions necessary for their effective operation of a shared electric personal mobility device. Digital platforms for dockless shared electric personal mobility devices must be available via a mobile application. Digital platforms for docked

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-32. Customer support services.**

(a) Each owner of a shared fleet shall establish a public customer support service through which the owner can accept and respond to questions, comments, complaints, and other inquiries from current or prospective operators of its shared electric personal mobility devices. At a minimum, the owner’s customer support service must be able to accept reports that one of its shared electric personal mobility devices is defective, damaged, inoperable, being improperly operated or parked, or has been involved in an accident, whether or not resulting in injury to any person or damage to any property.

(b) The owner’s customer support service must be accessible through the owner’s website, mobile application, and the telephone number provided on its shared electric personal mobility devices in accordance with Section 47-10-53(3) of this Code.

(c) The owner’s customer support service must be available 24 hours per day and seven days per week for the entire duration of its shared mobility permit.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-33. Identification, maintenance, and repair.**

(a) Each owner of a shared fleet shall assign a unique identification number for each shared electric personal mobility device within its shared fleet.

(b) Each owner of a shared fleet shall perform regular preventive maintenance of all shared electric personal mobility devices within its shared fleet to keep them in good working order and free of defects. Upon completion of such maintenance, a shared electric personal mobility device must be, at a minimum, in compliance with all technical standards set forth in Division 4 of this article.

(c) No shared electric personal mobility device may be made available for hire if inoperable or otherwise in need of repair. Each owner shall maintain standard procedures to promptly identify shared electric personal mobility devices within its shared fleet that are in need of repair, remove such devices from public places, and perform all necessary repairs.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-34. Deployment.**

Each owner of a shared fleet shall be responsible for the periodic deployment of its shared electric personal mobility devices in public places. Such deployment shall occur on a daily basis unless another period is stated in the terms of the owner’s shared mobility permit. Each owner shall undertake such deployment in accordance with all applicable terms of its shared mobility permit and the parking standards set forth in this article.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

**Sec. 47-10-35. Geofencing.**

(a) Each owner shall establish geofences around certain public places, public rights-of-way, or portions thereof, in which operation of a shared electric personal mobility device would be unsafe or otherwise should be restricted.

(b) The Department of Public Works may identify, in the terms of a shared mobility permit, certain areas to be geofenced on a permanent basis. The Department must identify the same areas in the terms of all shared mobility permits that have been issued at any particular time. Each owner must geofence all areas identified in its permit and maintain such geofencing at all times during the term of its shared mobility permit.

(c) The Department of Public Works may identify at any time certain areas to be geofenced on a temporary basis. Reasons for temporary geofencing may include repaving or other construction activities, street fairs or other pedestrian-oriented special events, and other circumstances that render operation of a shared electric personal mobility device unsafe, whether for the operator or for pedestrians and vehicles in the area. The Department shall provide to all shared mobility permit holders not less than 24 hours advance notice of any temporary geofencing, including the area subject to geofencing, the duration of the geofencing, and the reason for the geofencing. Each owner shall implement such geofencing within 24 hours and maintain such geofencing for the area and duration specified in the Department’s notice.

(d) Each owner of a shared fleet shall remotely incapacitate a shared electric personal mobility device within its shared fleet immediately upon demand by the Department in response to an emergency situation or other circumstances in which continued operation of the shared electric personal mobility devices could present an unacceptable risk to the safety of its operators or of the general public.

laws.title: Interference with other shared mobility permittees
laws.content:
Each owner of a shared fleet shall refrain from taking any action, and shall refrain from authorizing, enabling, encouraging, or facilitating operators of its shared electric personal mobility devices, to interfere with the normal operations of any other owner of a shared fleet or its shared electric personal mobility devices. Examples of such prohibited interference include, but are not limited to:

(1) Damaging, disabling, tampering with, or rendering inoperable a shared electric personal mobility device;

(2) Concealing, hiding, or otherwise rendering inaccessible a shared electric personal mobility device; and

(3) Placing a shared electric personal mobility device in non-compliance with applicable parking standards or otherwise rendering the shared electric personal mobility device in violation of this article.

(Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023)

laws.title: Operator education; community engagement; participation in mobility initiatives
laws.content:
(a) Each owner of a shared fleet shall provide, through its digital platform, mobile applications, docking stations and other comparable means, educational communications to operators of its shared electric personal mobility devices to facilitate their compliance with applicable provisions of this article. Specific topics may include technical specifications of electric personal mobility devices, best practices for safe operations, applicable traffic safety requirements, and applicable parking requirements. (b) The Department of Public Works may host, from time to time, community outreach and engagement activities for various mobility-related purposes, such as promoting the use of electric personal mobility devices, increasing accessibility of electric personal mobility devices and other mobility alternatives, or providing operator and traffic safety education. Such activities may include town hall meetings, meetings with neighborhood organizations, attendance at neighborhood special events, and direct communications to residents. Each owner shall participate, upon request by the Department, in such activities. The Department shall provide the owner reasonable advanced notice of any such activities and other information necessary to enable the owner's meaningful participation. (c) The Department of Public Works may conduct, from time to time, surveys for various mobility-related purposes, such as better understanding residents' transportation preferences. Such surveys will be in digital format and may be distributed through various means, among others, the City's website, email, and social media. Each owner of a shared fleet shall promote, upon request by the Department, such surveys, for example by providing access to such surveys via its digital platform, website, or other means. The Department shall provide the owner reasonable advanced notice of any such survey, including links to access the survey and other information necessary to enable the owner's compliance with this subsection. (d) The Department of Public Works may develop, from time to time, pilot programs and other special initiatives to demonstrate various mobility-related technologies or policies involving electric personal mobility devices. Each owner of a shared fleet shall participate, upon request by the Department, in such initiatives. The Department shall provide the owner reasonable advanced notice and other information necessary to enable the owner's meaningful participation. The owner's deployment of shared electric personal mobility devices as part of such an initiative are not subject to, and may not be counted against, any fleet size limits set forth in its shared mobility permit and will not impact the number of electric personal mobility devices, which it is authorized to deploy as part of its normal operations. (c) The City and the owners of shared fleets shall each be responsible for their own costs and expenses of participation in any community outreach and engagement activities, pilot programs, or other initiatives authorized by this section. (d) The owner of a shared fleet will have no obligation to participate in any community outreach and engagement activities, pilot programs, or other initiatives authorized by this section if, based on the information provided by the Department, the owner can reasonably Supp. No. 4 CD47:77 $\S 47-10-37$ DETROIT CODE demonstrate that its participation would be impractical for reasons other than the incurrence of reasonable costs arising from such participation. (Ord. No. 2023-11, § 1, eff. 3-1-2023) **Sec. 47-10-38. Data sharing.** (a) Each owner of a shared fleet shall share its complete data regarding usage of its shared electric personal mobility devices and other data pertinent to its operations with the Department of Public Works. The Department shall enumerate in the owner’s shared mobility permit the specific metrics for which the owner must provide data as well as the frequency by which such data must be shared. Examples of specific metrics for which the Department may require data sharing include, but need not be limited to: (1) Utilization volumes; (2) Membership volumes; (3) Trip volumes; (4) Trip origins, destinations, distances, and routes; (5) Geographic distributions of periodic re-deployments; (6) Real-time scooter locations and availability, based on the General Bike Share Feed Specification (GBFS); (7) Parking violation reports; (8) Theft and vandalism reports; (9) Maintenance reports; (10) Operator complaint reports; and (11) Accident and injury reports. (b) All data must be anonymized so as to exclude any data that reveal the identity of an individual operator or other person, or that otherwise contain personally identifiable information. (c) Unless otherwise directed by the Department, the owner shall share all data through an application programming interface that is compatible with the current version of the mobility data specification. (d) In exchange for acceptance of a permit issued pursuant to Section 47-10-14 of this Code, each owner of a shared fleet shall grant to the "City of Detroit" a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and non-exclusive license to possess and utilize all data that the owner provides to the Department pursuant to Subsection (a) of this section for purposes of the administration or enforcement of this article as well as for purposes of general mobility planning and policy-making activities. Each such license must further authorize the City to sublicense all subject data to its vendors, partners, and collaborators, as well as to other governmental agencies, as may be reasonably necessary in furtherance of the purposes stated in this section, except that no such license must authorize the City to sublicense data provided by one owner of a shared fleet to any other owner of a shared fleet. laws.title: Indemnification
laws.content:
(a) Each owner of a shared fleet shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless, and shall include in its terms of service applicable to all operators of any electric personal mobility device within its shared fleet the requirement that such operators shall indemnify and hold harmless the City against and from any and all liabilities, obligations, damages, penalties, claims, costs, charges, losses and expenses, including, without limitation, fees and expenses for attorneys, expert witnesses and other consultants, that may be imposed upon, incurred by, or asserted against the City or its departments or agencies, officers, employees, or agents by reason of any of the following occurring during the term of its shared mobility permit with respect to the owner or its associates:

(1) Any negligent or tortious act, error, or omission attributable in whole or in part to the owner or its associates, or the operator of an electric personal mobility device owned by the owner or its associates;

(2) Any failure by the owner or its associates to comply with the provisions of this article; and

(3) Any injury to the person or damage to the property of an employee of the City where such injury or damage arises out of the activities of

the owner or its associates, or by the activities of an operator of an electric personal mobility device owned by the owner or its associates.

(b) Each owner of a shared fleet shall further defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City and its elected or appointed officials, employees, agents, and volunteers from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, expenses, fines, penalties, judgments, demands and defense costs, including, without limitation, actual, direct, out-of-pocket costs and expenses, and amounts paid in compromise, settlement or judgment, and reasonable legal fees arising from litigation of every nature or liability of any kind or nature, including civil, criminal, administrative or investigative, arising out of, in connection with, or which are in any way related to, the owner's operations under a permit issued pursuant to this article, the business conduct and operations of the owner or any of its associates, any violation of any laws by the owner or any of its associates, or any bodily injury including death, or damage to property arising out of or in connection with any use, misuse, placement, or misplacement of any of the owner's electronic personal mobility devices or its associated equipment, except such claim caused by the willful misconduct or gross negligence of the City. This indemnity includes, but is not limited to, personal injury sustained by an operator arising from defects or unsafe conditions on City's streets, sidewalks, or other public areas unless caused by the sole, willful misconduct of the City. The owner will conduct all defenses at its sole cost and expense, and the City shall reasonably approve selection of the counsel to represent the City as proposed by the owner. This indemnity shall apply to all claims and liability regardless of whether any insurance policies of the owner, its affiliates, or any other parties are applicable thereto. The policy limits of any insurance of the owner, its affiliates or other parties are not a limitation upon the obligation of the owner, including, without limitation, the amount of indemnification to be provided by the owner.

(c) The provisions of this section shall survive the expiration or termination of any permit issued pursuant to this article.

(d) For purposes of this section, the term "associates" includes the owner's parent corporation and subsidiaries and any of their officers, managers, employees, agents, contractors, and volunteers as well as affiliates of the owner, its parent corporation, or its subsidiaries.

laws.title: Operation in compliance with traffic laws and other safety requirements
laws.content:
(a) Operation of a shared electric personal mobility device shall comply at all times with all applicable traffic laws governing the operation of vehicles and bicycles as set forth in Chapter 46 of this Code, Traffic and Vehicles, which, through Section 46-3-1 of this Code, adopts and incorporates by reference the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.1 et seq., including Sections 656, 657, 658, 660, 660d, 661, and 662, being MCL 257.656, 257.657, 257.658, 257.660, 257.660d, 256.661, and 257.662. If any provision of Chapter 46 of this Code conflicts with a provision of this article, the provision of this article controls.

(b) In accordance with Section 658(3) of the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.658(3), an electric personal assistive mobility device or an electric skateboard shall not be operated to carry more than one person at a time. Any other type of shared electric personal mobility device, such as an electric bicycle, shall not be operated to carry at a time more than the number of persons specified in the shared mobility permit authorizing its operation, or one person if no number is specified in such permit.

(c) In accordance with Section 658(4) of the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.658(4), an electric skateboard shall not be operated by an individual who is less than 19 years of age and fails to wear a crash helmet on his or her head at all times during such operation.

Supp. No. 4

CD47:82

§ 47-10-60

(d) In accordance with Section 658(9) of the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.658(9), an electric skateboard shall not be operated on a public highway or street by an individual who is less than 12 years of age.

(e) In accordance with Section 661 of the Michigan Vehicle Code, being MCL 257.661, an electric personal mobility device shall not be operated by an operator carrying any package, bundle, or article that prevents him or her from keeping both hands upon the handlebars or otherwise maintaining control of the electric personal mobility device at all times.

(f) Operation of a shared electric personal mobility device shall at all times adhere to all applicable traffic control lights, signals, and signage governing the operation of vehicles and bicycles.

(g) A shared electric personal mobility device shall be operated only for its intended purpose and shall not be operated in any manner constituting disorderly conduct in violation of Section 31-5-1 of this Code.

(h) A shared electric personal mobility device shall not be operated while under the influence of an alcoholic liquor or marijuana, an illegal drug, or a controlled substance.

(i) The Director of the Department of Public Works is authorized to designate reduced speed limits for shared electric personal mobility devices in any public place or public right-of-way where the Director determines:

(1) Congested pedestrian traffic is present or is likely to be present;

(2) Without a speed limit, a significant speed differential would exist between pedestrians or non-motorized traffic and electric personal mobility devices; or

(3) Without a speed limit, the presence of electric personal mobility devices traffic could endanger public health and safety.

zoning requirement for landscaped areas to be irrigated with readily-available water supply, § 50-14-328.

(c) Any person who is found guilty of violating any provision of this article shall be convicted of a misdemeanor for each violation that is issued and, in the discretion of the court, may be fined up to $500.00 and sentenced up to 90 days in jail, or both, for each misdemeanor violation that is issued.

**Sec. 48-1-2. Service connections—To be authorized by Board of Water Commissioners; costs to be charged against property owner.**

(a) Whenever it is necessary to make connections from water mains to lot lines, the same shall be authorized in a manner as set forth by the Board of Water Commissioners and the cost thereof shall be the responsibility of the owner of the property to which the service connection runs.

(b) Whenever it is necessary to make disconnections from water mains to lot lines, the same shall be authorized in a manner as set forth by the Board of Water Commissioners and the cost thereof shall be the responsibility of the owner of the property to which the service connection runs.

(c) The cost of service rendered pursuant to Subsection (a) or Subsection (b) of this section is to be paid for in terms to be established by the Board of Water Commissioners.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-1; Code 1984, § 56-2-1; Ord. No. 2023-24, § 1, eff. 6-15-2023)

**Sec. 48-1-3. Same—Costs to constitute lien on property; enforcement of collection of costs.**

If any person for whose benefit water main taps or connections are made refuses to pay the cost provided for in Section 48-1-2 of this Code within the time specified, the charge may become a lien on the property and the Board of Water Commissioners may enforce collection of any such bill in the manner provided by law.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-2; Code 1984, § 56-2-2)

**Sec. 48-1-4. Same—To be run to inside of areaways between water mains and lot lines.**

If there is an areaway intervening between any water main and lot line, the water service connection shall cease on the inside of the areaway.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-3; Code 1984, § 56-2-3)

**Sec. 48-1-5. Same—Repairs.**

Whenever any repairs are necessary to any service connection between the lot line and the water main, the Board of Water Commissioners shall immediately cause the same to be repaired without cost to the property owner or person responsible.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-4; Code 1984, § 56-2-4)

**Sec. 48-1-6. Conservation of water during emergencies; notice through enactment of emergency ordinance; violation thereof.**

(a) Whenever the Board of Water Commissioners determines that the amount of pumpage of water from its distribution system has reached a volume that, unless restricted, the public health, safety and general welfare is likely to be endangered, the Board may act to conserve the water supply during such emergency by requesting that, in accordance with Section 4-116 of the Charter, the City Council pass an emergency ordinance for a specific period of time:

(1) To prohibit the outdoor use of water throughout the City; or

(2) To prohibit the outdoor use of water for even-numbered addresses on even-numbered days and for odd-numbered addresses on odd-numbered days.

(b) After the emergency ordinance is passed by City Council, approved by the Mayor, and becomes effective upon publication, it shall be unlawful for any person to violate Subsection (a) of this section.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-5; Code 1984, § 56-2-5)

**Sec. 48-1-7. Reports of leaks or defects found in public water pipes while making excavations.**

Any person who, while excavating in any public street or alley in any manner, may have contributed to create a leak or discover any leak or defect in any of the public water pipes of the City or in any service pipe connected therewith, shall forthwith give notice to the contractor, superintendent or overseer of the work in process of excavation, who shall forthwith give notice by telephone to the Director of the Water and Sewerage Department as soon as possible. No person shall fill up such excavation or permit or cause the same to be filled up until such pipe is repaired and such leak stopped.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-6; Code 1984, § 56-2-6)

*Cross reference—Excavations generally, § 43-9-1 et seq.*

**Sec. 48-1-8. Opening without permit or obstructing fire hydrants prohibited.**

(a) No person shall open any fire hydrant or use any water from the same without first obtaining a permit from the Board of Water Commissioners.

(b) No person shall in any manner obstruct the use of any fire hydrant in the City or have, place or allow to be placed any material or thing in front thereof or connect or tie thereto any object, animal or thing. Any material found as an obstruction may be removed by the employees of the Water and Sewerage Department, at the risk, cost, and expense of the owner or claimants.

(Code 1964, § 65-1-7; Code 1984, § 56-2-7)

*Cross reference—Fire prevention and protection generally, Ch. 18.*

**Secs. 48-1-9—48-1-20. Reserved.**

**DIVISION 2. CONSTRUCTION OF WATER MAINS**

**Sec. 48-1-21. Petition by property owner; resolution of Board of Water Commissioners.**

In any district within the City which is not adequately served by water pipes, mains or aqueducts, one or more owners of real property within such district may present a petition to the Board of Water Commissioners requesting the Board of Water Commissioners to lay and install, for the purpose of serving such district, water pipes, mains, or aqueducts. Such petition shall be accompanied by a sum of money equal to the petitioner’s *pro rata* share of the total cost of such improvement, which share shall be determined in accordance with the lineal footage of real property of such petitioner fronting upon the street or alley where such main or aqueduct is to be laid; or, the Board of Water Commissioners, without such petition, in its discretion, may, and whenever deemed necessary, shall lay or install water pipes, mains or aqueducts fronting upon such property with a like assessment to the owner of real property fronting upon such property. Following receipt of such petition or without such petition, the Board of Water Commissioners may adopt, in its discretion, a resolution authorizing the laying and installation of pipes, mains, or aqueducts and specifying the streets and alleys through which it shall be found necessary to lay the same in order to adequately serve such property.

(Code 1964, § 65-2-1; Code 1984, § 56-2-19)
